title: The 2026 Rams have eleven captains
summary: For the Rams, it's just as easy to list the players who aren't captains as it is to list those who are.
full_text: For the Rams, it's just as easy to list the players who aren't captains as it is to list those who are. The team has announced a whopping eleven captains for 2026 . They are: quarterback Matthew Stafford, running back Kyren Williams, receiver Davante Adams, tight end Tyler Higbee, center Coleman Shelton, defensive end Myles Garrett, defensive tackle Kobie Turner, linebacker Nate Landman, cornerback Trent McDuffie, defensive back Quentin Lake, and long snapper Joe Cardona. Few if any teams have ever had that many captains. For whatever reasons, the Rams have decided to have that many players with a "C" on their jerseys. Conspicuous in their omission are defensive tackle Aaron Donald, who is returning after a two-year retirement, and receiver Puka Nacua, one of the best receivers in the NFL.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jets plan to stick with Cade Klubnik as their backup QB
summary: The Jets did not claim a quarterback off of waivers on Monday and it doesn't sound like they plan to make a move to acquire one via another avenue.
full_text: The Jets did not claim a quarterback off of waivers on Monday and it doesn't sound like they plan to make a move to acquire one via another avenue. Rookie Cade Klubnik made the cut to the 53-man roster as the only backup to Geno Smith and head coach Aaron Glenn said at a Monday press conference that the team plans to stick with the fourth-round pick as their No. 2 at the position. "He's our backup quarterback and he'll do a good job," Glenn said. Klubnik was 21-of-34 for 190 yards and an interception in his preseason action. He was a three-year starter at Clemson, but landed in the fourth round after his production dropped in his final college season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Steelers GM Omar Khan: We hope Joey Porter Jr. finishes his career here
summary: The Steelers activated cornerback Joey Porter Jr. from the physically unable to perform list on Sunday, which clears the way for Porter to practice with the team and play in Week 1 even though he has not received the contract extension he's been looking for all offseason.
full_text: '' The Steelers activated cornerback Joey Porter Jr. from the physically unable to perform list on Sunday, which clears the way for Porter to practice with the team and play in Week 1 even though he has not received the contract extension he's been looking for all offseason. There has been no sign that such a deal is imminent, but General Manager Omar Khan made it clear on Monday that the team is planning to have Porter on the practice field. “Not just Joey but anyone we feel is healthy and available to us, we expect them to practice," Khan said, via multiple reporters. Khan confirmed that the Steelers will not budge from their organizational philosophy of cutting of contract talks at the start of the regular season and said that he still hopes "Joey finishes his career here" while declining to delve into any details of where things stand on the negotiating front.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Four other teams put in a claim for CB Darrell Luter
summary: The Raiders had the top waiver priority over the weekend and used it to pick up cornerback Darrell Luter.
full_text: '' The Raiders had the top waiver priority over the weekend and used it to pick up cornerback Darrell Luter. It turns out they were far from the only team interested in the former 49er. Per Field Yates of ESPN, the Titans, Dolphins, Cowboys, and Colts also put in a claim for Luter. But because the Raiders were first in line, they were the team to get him. Yates notes no other player had more than two teams put in a claim for him. A fifth-round pick in 2023, Luter has appeared in 27 games with three starts over the last three seasons. In 2025, he appeared in all 17 games with three starts, recording 28 total tackles with one pass defensed and one fumble recovery.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Joe Burrow on Super Bowl goals: "If you don’t talk about it, I don’t know how you can do it.”
summary: Not many teams that have missed the playoffs for three straight seasons are viewed as a team of destiny.
full_text: Not many teams that have missed the playoffs for three straight seasons are viewed as a team of destiny. That isn't stopping Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow from attempting to speak a Super Bowl win into existence. “ I’ve never understood why people are scared to say it ,” Burrow told Albert Breer of SI.com. “I guess people get scared of how the media will portray them or their team in a certain way. But you have to set expectations with yourself, your teammates, your organization. Everybody says they want to win the Super Bowl, you talk about it every day, you set that expectation every day, you go and work for it every single day. I mean, I don’t know the answer to that for everybody, but that’s what I want to do, that’s what I’m trying to do, that’s what I do this for. “I won the championship in college, and there’s no freaking better feeling than that. And if you don’t talk about it, I don’t know how you can do it.” He's right about that. He's also right about the other 31 teams having the same goal. Whether they talk about it or not, they enter each season at 0-0 and with high hopes. For Burrow, he's basing his belief on something tangible. He's comparing the vibe at the 2026 Bengals to the sense he had at LSU, seven years ago. “I don’t know, it just felt inevitable,” Burrow told Breer. “We finished stronger the year before. I knew how good Justin [Jefferson] was. I didn’t quite know how good Ja’Marr [Chase] was going to be yet because his superpower is after the catch, and in practice you can’t really see that. He was getting open and making plays. Obviously, that’s what he does, but what makes him one of one is after the catch. I realized that somewhere in the early 2019 season. “But, yeah, I just knew how things felt around the building. I knew how practices were going. I knew that offense fit my skill set more so than any one I had been in. It just made sense to me. As I said, there was just a feeling around the building that it was inevitable.” Burrow's confidence in the Bengals is bolstered by the other side of the ball. “The vibe of the defense is really good right now,” Burrow said. “Our defensive line is so deep this year. The depth of that unit was a weak point last year, [but] now we have nine or 10 guys that we feel good about putting out there in five-down sets. Obviously, Dexter [Lawrence II] plays a big role in that. Jonathan Allen plays a big role in that. And those guys have been vocal leaders for us to start this out, which is something that we needed." Whatever happens, the stakes are high. A fourth straight year with no postseason appearance will likely spark a coaching change. And it could make Burrow, after seven years in Cincinnati, look for a place where it will seem even more inevitable that he'll be smoking a locker-room cigar in one or more of the remaining Februarys of his career.
author: Mike Florio

title: Steve Sarkisian: Bumping players for NFL transfers is "wrong"
summary: As a time when Lane Kiffin is ready to pounce on as many former NFL players as he can, a former USC colleague of Kiffin's has a far different viewpoint.
full_text: As a time when Lane Kiffin is ready to pounce on as many former NFL players as he can, a former USC colleague of Kiffin's has a far different viewpoint. "The fact that somebody out there is going to take a player off of an NFL roster and tell somebody who's been doing it for nine months to go kick rocks, that doesn't sit well with me," Texas coach Steve Sarkisian said Monday, via David Eckert of 247sports.com. "I think that's wrong. That, morally, is wrong ." It's hardly uncommon, especially in the NFL. On Monday, players who spent the entire offseason, training camp, and preseason in the building will lose their brand-new roster spots to newcomers claimed on waivers or signed as free agents. The dynamic has become relevant in college football, for this year only, because of the NCAA's new five-year rule. The NCAA didn't realize, or didn't care, that the change would unlock an effort by players who had only four years at the college level to get another season. All due respect to Sarkisian, but football coaches will say whatever it takes to justify whatever they want. Sarkisian, like Oregon's Dan Lanning, doesn't want any of the available former NFL players. that makes it easier for them to get on a soapbox when it comes to embracing players who were released by their NFL teams.
author: Mike Florio

title: The Shilo Sanders bankruptcy trial gets started (and doesn't start well)
summary: Shilo Sanders, the son of Deion and a member of the Buccaneers during the 2025 offseason program and preseason, hopes to discharge an $11.89 million civil judgment through the federal bankruptcy laws.
full_text: '' Shilo Sanders, the son of Deion and a member of the Buccaneers during the 2025 offseason program and preseason, hopes to discharge an $11.89 million civil judgment through the federal bankruptcy laws. The trial on that specific question began on Monday. So far, it's not going well. Brent Schrotenboer of USA Today has the recap . The question is whether injuries Shilo inflicted on John Darjean in 2015 were "willful and malicious." If not, the debt will go away. If so, he'll still be on the hook for it. Multiple witnesses testified via prerecorded video about the incident. One saw Shilo hit Darjean with an elbow in the throat before punching him twice. Another saw Shilo punch Darjean in the face, "unprovoked." Another said Shilo's conduct was "aggressive" and "volatile." Shilo's lawyers claim that he had been "overpowered" by Darjean during the altercation. Obviously, they'll need to introduce evidence that overcomes the initial witnesses presented by Darjean. Darjean worked as a security guard at Shilo's school. The incident happened after Darjean tried to confiscate Shilo's phone. Meanwhile, Deion posted a video on Monday expressing support for Shilo. "Praying for my baby . . . that people see what really transpired,” Deion Sanders said, per Schrotenboer. To any who doubt Shilo's version that he was acting in self-defense, Deion said, “We going to forgive you for your judgment." The problem for Shilo is that he didn't show up for the trial of the personal injury case, resulting in a default judgment and a massive verdict. Deion will testify remotely on Friday, if (and only if) Shilo's lawyers open the door to potential testimony from Deion regarding the reason(s) for Shilo not wanting to lose access to his phone. The case will be decided by the presiding judge, not a jury. Which means that, in the end, the judge will have to decide whether the full scope of the evidence does or doesn't point to "willful and malicious" behavior by Shilo. The stakes for Shilo are considerable. If Shilo prevails, he can move forward with his life unfettered by an eight-figure financial obligation to Darjean. If Shilo loses, he will constantly be faced with efforts to collect on the obligation, with statutory interest constantly being added to the unpaid amounts.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cowboys waive QB Joe Milton
summary: The Cowboys kept three quarterbacks on their initial 53-man roster, but they dropped to two on Monday, They have waived Joe Milton, which leaves Sam Howell as the only backup to Dak Prescott.
full_text: The Cowboys kept three quarterbacks on their initial 53-man roster, but they dropped to two on Monday, They have waived Joe Milton, which leaves Sam Howell as the only backup to Dak Prescott. Milton could return to the practice squad if he clears waivers. Milton was 29-of-43 for 378 yards and three touchdowns during the preseason and his play earned good reviews from head coach Brian Schottenheimer, so another team might take the chance to add Milton to their roster with the hope of continuing his development. Running back Emari Demercado was claimed off of waivers from the Chiefs, which necessitated another roster move to make space for him in Dallas.
author: Josh Alper

title: Vikings to waive QB Max Brosmer
summary: The Vikings came out of cut-down day with four quarterbacks on their 53-man roster.
full_text: The Vikings came out of cut-down day with four quarterbacks on their 53-man roster. Now, they'll be going down to three. Per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Minnesota is waiving Max Brosmer. The Vikings needed a roster spot after claiming a pair of players off waivers. Brosmer entered the league as an undrafted free agent last year after five collegiate seasons with New Hampshire and one with Minnesota. He appeared in seven games with two starts as a rookie, completing 66.2 percent of his passes for 328 yards with no touchdowns and four interceptions. Brosmer could be brought back on Minnesota’s practice squad if he clears waivers. The Vikings still have Carson Wentz and J.J McCarthy behind starting quarterback Kyler Murray on their roster.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Joe Burrow plans to play for as long as he can
summary: Joe Burrow turns 30 on December 10.
full_text: Joe Burrow turns 30 on December 10. As he gets deeper into his NFL career, he has decided to let it ride for as long as he can. “I used to think I didn’t want to play very long," Burrow told Albert Breer of SI.com, "and now I’m like, 'I’m just going to go until I can’t do it anymore. This is fun to do. What the hell else would I do?' I used to want to go and maybe play a different sport after a couple of Super Bowls, but now I’m like, ‘I’m just going to play until I can’t .'" Injuries have kept him from playing as much as he would have liked during the first six years of his career. His plan for Year 7 includes managing the game to reduce the chances of more absences, based on lessons he learned last year after returning from toe surgery. “It’s where there’s a free runner in the pocket and I just dirt it, or a keeper and I get pressure, and I just throw it away, where normally my physical ability would have let me make that guy miss and go make a play; last year I couldn’t,” Burrow said. “I had to get rid of the ball and live to see another down a little bit. Not being able to move around, I had to tailor my game to that. And so, as I said, I can play quarterback a lot of different ways. When it’s needed in the fourth quarter, I can go and do that. . . . I can mitigate risk early in the game until it’s needed.” And the desire to stay healthy isn't just about pursuing a championship. Burrow knows from experience that being able to play is dramatically better than the alternative. “Two out of the last three seasons, I’ve missed extended time," Burrow told Breer. "I’ve put a lot of work into this. When that happens, that sucks, quite frankly. So I’m just excited to play. When you’re hurt, you’re away from the team, you’re away from the guys. You’re not going through it like they are. It’s a lonely process." For now, the loneliness has been replaced with anticipation and optimism. That all potentially changes once the games start. And the reality for the Bengals is that, after a Super Bowl appearance and an AFC title game in back-to-back years, the playoff drought is at three straight seasons. The overriding focus entering 2026 is to put that to an end, convincingly.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyle Shanahan: George Kittle's passing everything, didn't mean to say he had a setback
summary: The 49ers remain hopeful that Kittle will play in Week 1 against the Rams.
full_text: 49ers tight end George Kittle is practicing this week and he's moving into team drills in the days leading up to their trip to Australia, so any worries that his return from a torn Achilles hit a snag should be put to rest. Kittle's status for Week 1 against the Rams remains up in the air, but head coach Kyle Shanahan said on Monday that last week's press conference comment that Kittle had " taken a step back " was not meant to express that his timeline for returning to the lineup had changed. “I don’t know exactly what I said there, but it was probably just me not speaking right ," Shanahan said. "George has been great. He’s passing everything. We’re just getting him out with the team these three days and anytime when you come back out and practice with the team going against people and stuff — I hope there’s not a setback in that way. That has nothing to do with his injury or anything, that has to do with his coming back and practicing these three days. There was nothing that I meant to say that people looked into. If I did say that, it was an accident.” The 49ers will practice the next three days before traveling to Melbourne to resume preparations for the opener. Shanahan said it wasn't necessary to know if Kittle will play before leaving, but that it wouldn't be a bad thing. "I think if we didn't think he was going to play and it was looking that way, it would much nicer to make the decision before we left," Shanahan said. The team also plans to have defensive end Nick Bosa on the practice field this week and they'll be hoping both players look like they're ready to contribute against their division rivals to kick off the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Passports for practice squad signings are a logistical challenge for 49ers and Rams
summary: Every team in the league is in the process of calling players to ask them to join the practice squad, but the Rams and 49ers have another question: "Do you have a passport?"
full_text: Every team in the league is in the process of calling players to ask them to join the practice squad, but the Rams and 49ers have another question: "Do you have a passport?" Because the Rams and 49ers will open the season in Australia, those teams need to know that any new additions to the team will be able to get into a foreign country. Players who have been with the teams all offseason have been preparing for international travel, but 49ers General Manager John Lynch says making sure new additions to the team can get into Australia is a logistical challenge. "We're bringing practice squads from the outside. I've never asked a potential practice squad, 'Do you have a passport?' Those are questions we have to ask now," Lynch said. "One guy who's coming into town, his parents are next daying it, because it was at the house. So there's a lot of little logistics like that that are complicated by this, but we're embracing it, we're having a plan for everything, and we're getting it done." Lynch said the 49ers' staff behind the scenes has had to work overtime to get the team ready for the longest road trip in NFL history. "There's a lot, and I think it's an opportune time to give a shout out to our staff," Lynch said. "Everything from getting visas, which is much more complicated than I knew, they've been outstanding. They've worked in conjunction with the league but most of the work has been done on our part and hats off to those guys for pulling off a monumental task, and it's not done yet. There's a lot."
author: Michael David Smith

title: John Lynch: Aaron Donald makes the Rams better, but we're pretty good, too
summary: The 49ers are preparing to face Donald next week in Australia.
full_text: If Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald is ready to go following a two-year retirement, he'll play against the 49ers in Australia next week. 49ers General Manager John Lynch says that just makes the rivalry more intense. Lynch has long subscribed to a philosophy he attributes to legendary UCLA basketball coach John Wooden: "Don't lose sleep over what other teams are doing; let them lose sleep over what you're doing." Lynch was asked if he still feels that way when it comes to Donald returning to the Rams. "The guy's different," Lynch said of Donald. "He's an exceptional player. One of the greats. I do subscribe to that. I think we're pretty good, too. They got better, certainly, with him deciding to come out of retirement." Lynch said he believes Donald will arrive in top shape. "There's time away, but I know that guy trains like a madman," Lynch said. "I ran into him in a hotel somewhere a while back and we had some fun chatter back and forth. Never thought he'd do it, but he's doing it, so we better get ready for it." The Rams have not said whether Donald will be active for Week One, but the 49ers are preparing as if they're going to face the three-time defensive player of the year in his first game in two and a half years.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Odell Beckham Jr.: I have an opportunity to rewrite the last chapter
summary: Wide receiver Odell Beckham experienced something new while waiting for the Giants to set their initial 53-man roster for the 2026 season.
full_text: Wide receiver Odell Beckham experienced something new while waiting for the Giants to set their initial 53-man roster for the 2026 season. Beckham was on the roster bubble since returning to the team this spring and said on Monday that "it was a different feeling" to be unsure about whether he'd wind up making the cut ahead of Week 1. Beckham said it created some pressure to feel "I have to go and get it" after years of being on the top of depth charts and that making it to the regular season was "an honor and a privilege" he wants to take full advantage of moving forward. "I have an opportunity to rewrite some of the last bit of the chapter," Beckham said, via a transcript from the team. "Don't know, last year, whatever it is, I just know I'm going to give my all. But definitely had that moment where it was like you could let out some of the pain that I feel like I went through. It was just very healing, very emotional, something I was very happy about." Beckham making it through final cuts was a nice story, but it will be less resonant if it isn't followed by meaningful contributions to the team during the season. It's been a while since the wideout has made that kind of an impact, so it remains to be seen just how different the final chapter will wind up looking.
author: Josh Alper

title: Howie Roseman: Zach Ertz one of the greatest tight ends, but love what we have
summary: Word in early August was that tight end Zach Ertz has been cleared for all football activities after tearing his ACL last December, but the veteran remains a free agent with the start of the regular season a little over a week away.
full_text: Word in early August was that tight end Zach Ertz has been cleared for all football activities after tearing his ACL last December, but the veteran remains a free agent with the start of the regular season a little over a week away. One possible path back to the field that's been bandied about has been a return to the Eagles. Ertz spent his first eight-plus seasons with the team and helped them win a Super Bowl before moving on to Arizona in a 2021 trade. The Eagles have Dallas Goedert, Johnny Mundt, E.J. Jenkins, and second-round pick Eli Stowers on the 53-man roster with Grant Calcaterra on injured reserve. On Monday, General Manager Howie Roseman was asked about the possibility of a reunion with Ertz. "First, I'd say what an unbelievable player, what an unbelievable person, tremendous respect for him," Roseman said, via a transcript from the team. "At the same time, love what we have going in our tight end room, too. I would say, have talked to Zach over a period of time, obviously rehabbing his ACL and the relationship, just like a lot of our former players who've been here. But like anything else, wouldn't get into any conversations about anything other than from a big picture perspective. In my opinion, one of the greatest tight ends to play the game and just tremendous respect for him, and also excited about the tight ends that we have here." Ertz had 116 catches for 1,158 yards and 11 touchdowns in 30 games for the Commanders the last two seasons, so he remained a productive offensive piece before his injury. If Roseman decides the Eagles are a little short at tight end, he could get a chance to finish out his career where it started.
author: Josh Alper

title: Aaron Donald's absence from Monday's practice "part of the plan all along"
summary: Aaron Donald officially came out of retirement and practiced with the Rams on Sunday, but the three-time defensive player of the year was not on the field with the team on Monday.
full_text: ' Aaron Donald officially came out of retirement and practiced with the Rams on Sunday, but the three-time defensive player of the year was not on the field with the team on Monday. Rams head coach Sean McVay said that Donald's absence had nothing to do with anything that happened during his first practice with the team. McVay said it was "part of the plan all along" for the defensive tackle and that the team will see where that plan takes them as they move toward their Week 1 game against the 49ers in Melbourne. "I wouldn't rule anything out yet," McVay said, via the team's website. "Sometimes when you put unnecessary parameters or guidelines on something, you can skew things. But what I think what's really good for us is if he's able to go, great, if not, that's kind of how we've been operating as is, and guys have done an excellent job of being able to do some really cool stuff in the meantime. So, if he's not ready, and that's not what's best for him and for the team, (we) absolutely wouldn't have him play in Australia." Donald's participation as well as that of defensive end Myles Garrett will continue to be closely monitored as the football world waits to find out when we'll see the duo on the field at the same time.
author: Josh Alper

title: Nnamdi Madubuike doing "more and more," but Ravens uncertain about Week 1
summary: Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike did not go on injured reserve while the team set its initial 53-man roster, which means that the team does not think he will miss the first four games of the season as he continues working his way back from the neck injury that kept him out for most of last year.
full_text: '' Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike did not go on injured reserve while the team set its initial 53-man roster, which means that the team does not think he will miss the first four games of the season as he continues working his way back from the neck injury that kept him out for most of last year. That doesn't mean Madubuike is going to be playing in Week 1 against the Colts, however. Madubuike did not take part in 11-on-11 work during training camp and head coach Jesse Minter declined to say at a Monday press conference if that will happen this week. "I don't see him obviously missing that many games," Minter said, via the team's website. "I think the path that's been all along, he's progressing more and more. So we'll kind of evaluate these next couple weeks." Minter did say that Madubuike is in "a good position" and the Ravens will continue to monitor his workload to determine when he's ready to move up to full participation in both practices and games.
author: Josh Alper

title: SEC explores "extreme measures" against LSU — including expulsion
summary: The SEC hopes to grab the Tigers by the tail.
full_text: '' The SEC hopes to grab the Tigers by the tail. Ross Dellenger of Yahoo Sports reports that the conference is exploring various ways to address LSU's plan to add former NFL players to its team, including " extreme measures ." The possibilities reportedly include boycotting competition against the school, probation, or expulsion. The SEC also is considering filing a federal lawsuit on the issue. It was a federal lawsuit against Texas Tech from the Big 12 that prompted the Red Raiders to abandon the plan to allow quarterback Brendan Sorsby to play this year, after he won an injunction against the NCAA's gambling suspension. No decision is expected before Thursday's hearing on whether the pending TRO will become a preliminary injunction. The conversations are reportedly "serious," and "[t]ensions are high." The possibility of giving LSU the boot and replacing it with another team is on the table. It's nothing more than an effort to bully LSU to back down, along with a not-so-subtle unwillingness to accept the eventual ruling from the court that issued the TRO, if the court doesn't reverse its decision and allow the SEC rule prohibiting conference members from adding former NFL players to play for their programs. Through it all, the ongoing agitation keeps the story alive, with the obvious goal of getting Congress to give college football (and the other sports) the coveted antitrust exemption through the Protect College Sports Act. For now, the SEC is experiencing the chaos it deserves. The issue is a byproduct of the reckoning that followed decades of exploiting players through the creation of a govening body that prevented any of them from getting anything more than a free education, regardless of the real value of the services they provide to their schools.
author: Mike Florio

title: Patrick Herbert, brother of Justin Herbert, joins Chargers' practice squad
summary: After spending the last year in Jacksonville, Patrick Herbert will join his brother in Los Angeles.
full_text: Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert will be practicing with his brother for the first time since they were teammates at Oregon in 2019. Patrick Herbert, a tight end who was cut by the Jaguars on Sunday, signed with the Chargers' practice squad on Monday. The 25-year-old Patrick, who is three years younger than Justin, signed with the Jaguars as an undrafted free agent last year and spent the season on their practice squad. He remained with the Jaguars throughout this offseason. Patrick spent six seasons at Oregon, playing there from 2019 through 2024. As a freshman he got on the field for two games, while Justin was leading the Ducks to a 12-2 record that culminated in winning the Rose Bowl. During his college career, Patrick caught 31 passes for 388 yards and four touchdowns.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Eagles to add RB Jaydon Blue to their practice squad
summary: Running back Jaydon Blue, who the Cowboys waived on Sunday, is signing with the Eagles' practice squad, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
full_text: '' Running back Jaydon Blue, who the Cowboys waived on Sunday, is signing with the Eagles' practice squad, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. The Cowboys drafted Blue in the fifth round in 2025, but he was a healthy scratch for 12 games as a rookie. He totaled 38 carries for 129 yards and a touchdown. Coach Brian Schottenheimer noted Blue's growth in maturity in 2026, though it was not enough to keep his roster spot. The Eagles have Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley on their 53-player roster at the position.
author: Charean Williams

title: Locker-room attack put TCU receiver in hospital for three days
summary: Football is premised in many respects on controlled violence.
full_text: '' Football is premised in many respects on controlled violence. The emotions of the game can lead to uncontrolled violence, and that can create a major problem for players and teams. At TCU, a locker-room fight earlier this month resulted in the dismissal of safety Jacob Fields. It also resulted in very serious injuries for TCU receiver Dozie Ezukanma. Via Shambhavi Rimal of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram , Ezukanma spent three days in a hospital with a concussion and a brain bleed after the August 13 attack. The delayed transport of Ezukanma to the hospital apparently made the situation worse. After multiple brain scans and with treatment (including medication), doctors finally got the situation under control. Fields was charged on Sunday with aggravated assault for allegedly punching and kicking Ezukanma in the head. The assault was reported to TCU police on August 14. Fields was expelled from the team the next day, and the move was announced three days later. Fields, after the incident, said the following in a text message: “I made an emotional decision cause how I felt I played the last few practices. . . . I’ll pay every hospital bill and then some to make this right.” He'll be facing far greater consequences than that, and if he did what he's accused of doing, he should.
author: Mike Florio

title: Can the Rams get Aaron Donald ready for Week 1?
summary: Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald returned to the team on August 30.
full_text: Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald returned to the team on August 30. They play the 49ers in Australia on September 10. The most immediate question is whether he'll play and, if so, the number of snaps he'll take. Several weeks ago, it was believed that the target for Donald would be 30 to 40 snaps. That was based on Donald returning in time to have a sufficient ramp-up process for the first game. While it took a little longer than originally expected, there's an apples-to-apples comparison. In 2018, Donald held out until August 31. And the Rams played their first game on Monday, September 10, against the Raiders. In that game, the Rams had 70 defensive snaps. Donald participated in 62 of them. Although Donald is eight years older than he was in 2018 (as we all are), 30-40 doesn't seem ridiculous. Regardless, the clock is ticking. And Donald is practicing. He'll eventually be playing. Whether that's Week 1 against the 49ers or Week 2 against the Giants remains to be seen.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jesse Minter expresses confidence in Tyler Loop
summary: Ravens kicker Tyler Loop missed field goals of 58 and 51 yards in the preseason finale.
full_text: Ravens kicker Tyler Loop missed field goals of 58 and 51 yards in the preseason finale. He finished the preseason 5-of-8 as he tries to rebound from the 44-yard miss that ended the Ravens' season in Week 17. Baltimore kept Loop on the roster, but signed Jake Moody to the practice squad on Monday. "I have a lot of confidence in Tyler still," Jesse Minter said, via Jamison Hensley of ESPN. "He's had a great training camp. I expect him to be our kicker going into [the Sept. 13 season opener in] Indianapolis. title: Aaron Donald sits out practice: Rams admit returning star might not play Week 1 in Australia
summary: A day after officially coming out of retirement, Donald missed Monday's practice and his Week 1 status remains unclear
full_text:
Aaron Donald has only been back with the Los Angeles Rams for two days, and he's already missed his first practice. The three-time Defensive Player of the Year practiced on Sunday after officially announcing his return , but he sat out Monday's session and there's a chance that he might not be on the field for the Rams' season opener in Australia against the San Francisco 49ers .
Rams coach Sean McVay said that the team is trying to ease Donald back into action, which is why the defensive tackle didn't practice on Monday.
"Aaron not being out there was part of the plan all along, so that was par for the course," McVay said after practice.
Donald spent the past two months working out on his own, but the 35-year-old is still working his way into football shape, which is why the Rams are still trying to figure out how much he can handle right now.
"I know it is annoying as hell just saying, 'We're taking it a day at a time.' But it is a unique thing," McVay said. "This has never been done before. I think him being able to help guide us and then being able to trust [Senior Vice President of Sports Medicine and Performance Reggie Scott] and what we think is best for the ramp up is what we're going to do."
With Donald sitting out practice, McVay was asked about the possibility of the defensive tackle missing the opener and the Rams coach admitted that could happen.
"Oh, yeah, absolutely. That could be a possibility," McVay said of Donald not playing in Week 1. "I wouldn't rule anything out yet. I think sometimes when you put unnecessary parameters or guidelines on something it can skew things."
The Rams will be heading to Melbourne, Australia, at some point next week, and the team will likely want to make a decision on his status before they get on the plane so Donald doesn't take an unnecessary 15-hour flight if he's not going to be active.
"If he's not ready and that is not what is best for him and for the team, absolutely wouldn't have him play in Australia unnecessarily," McVay said.
The Rams coach said the team wants to see Donald on the practice field before making any decisions about Week 1. Donald spent the past two years in retirement and hasn't played in an NFL game since January 2024.
"The first step was, 'all right, if you're coming back let us do that, let us get you out on the practice field,'" McVay said Sunday. "'Let us get you acclimated to your teammates to your coaches,' and then we'll see what that ramp up period looks like whether or not he is available or whether or not we think it is best to be able to play him in Australia."
As for Donald, he was also non-committal about playing in Week 1.
"I need to be at the level that I want to play at and that's all I can do," Donald said Sunday. "Ain't rushing [anything]. Like I said, just continue to stack them days and see where we [are] at."
Donald's revised contract with the Rams seems to take into account the fact that he might not be out on the field in Week 1. The 10-time Pro Bowler signed a one-year, $30 million deal that includes $10 million in bonus money that's tied to whether he's on the active roster each week. That specific bonus will pay out at a rate of $666,667 per game for a maximum of 15 games, so if Donald misses Week 1 or sits out Week 18 because the Rams are resting their starters, it won't impact his ability to make the full $10 million in bonus money.
Donald's Week 1 status seems to be genuinely up in the air, and the Rams will have to make a decision soon. The 49ers are leaving for Australia on Sept. 2, but the Rams won't be leaving until next week, so McVay and Donald will have a few more days to decide if he's ready enough to play.
author: John Breech

title: Odell Beckham Jr. earns spot on Giants 53-man roster, discusses chance to 'rewrite history'

full_text:

On Sunday, NFL teams narrowed down their teams for the upcoming season, needing to be at 53 players by 6 p.m. ET. This means a total of 1,184 players will be released by their teams.
Beckham is not one of those players .
Beckham discussed being in a new position of having to fight for a roster spot, rather than being an automatic in, calling it a "different feeling." He said making the roster was "an hour and a privilege."
"I have an opportunity to rewrite some of the last bit of the chapter," Beckham said. "Don't know, last year, whatever it is, I just know I'm going to give my all. But definitely had that moment where it was like you could let out some of the pain that I feel like I went through. It was just very healing, very emotional, something I was very happy about."
Beckham signed with the Giants this offseason, looking not only for a reunion with his old team but also with his former coach. Beckham worked with current Giants head coach John Harbaugh when they were both with the Baltimore Ravens in 2023.
He may now also get a reunion with his old number, 13. Wide receiver Jalin Hyatt currently wears No. 13 for the Giants.
"I think we all know what that means to me, and there definitely will be some conversations. I'll just say we'll see what happens, but like I said, it would be an honor and a privilege to put that back on," he said on potentially putting on a No. 13 jersey again.
Harbaugh complimented Beckham's efforts as the 33-year-old was working to make the roster. Earlier this week, Harbaugh added that this was OBJ's "best week" at training camp.
"Yes, he has done enough to make an NFL roster, for sure," Harbaugh said. "He's played well. He's gotten better as camp's gone along. He deserves credit for that. He's done a really good job with it."
Beckham has some unfinished business with the Giants and feels like he has more to give on the football field, and gets his chance this year with the Giants when they kick off their season on Sept. 13 at home against division rival Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football.
The Giants' starting quarterback is Jaxson Dart , with Jameis Winston backing him up. The wide receiver room also includes Malik Nabers , rookie Malachi Fields , Darius Slayton and Darnell Mooney .
"It would mean everything to me if I made it," Beckham said earlier this week. "... I feel like I gave everything I've had. Super grateful for the opportunity. ... I know that I have a good feeling about myself. I feel like there is ball to be played, plays to be made. Right now, I'm just truly grateful for that opportunity and experience."
His journey has included many bumps in the road, injuries, team changes and up-and-down play.
Beckham last saw an NFL regular-season game as a member of the Miami Dolphins in 2024. He was eventually waived in December of the same year. Ahead of the release, he appeared in nine games, finishing with nine receptions for 55 yards.
In October of 2025, Beckham was suspended for six games for violating the league's performance-enhancing drug policy. He would not play a single snap all season, making his last in-game appearance on December 8, 2024, against the New York Jets , where he had one reception for one yard.
OBJ spent the first five years playing for the Giants, recording memorable moments like the one-handed catch and racking up four 1,000-plus-yard receiving seasons, and earning all three of his Pro Bowl selections during his time with the team.
He was one to watch from the beginning, winning the NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2014, but after a solid first year with the Browns , an ACL injury impacted his stat line and playing time in Cleveland. His time with the Browns was not without drama: he played for them in 2019, 2020 and six games in 2021 before joining the Los Angeles Rams in November of 2021.
Beckham played eight games for the Rams, recording 27 receptions for 305 yards on the Super Bowl-winning team. OBJ was sidelined for the majority of the big game after scoring the first touchdown of the contest against the Cincinnati Bengals due to an ACL injury. He didn't get to play the entire game, but he did get his ring.
He didn't end up signing with a team for the following season, sitting out all of 2022 before joining the Ravens for one season in 2023 and Miami in 2024, bringing us to his latest venture.
Beckham discussed having to sit out two full seasons in his career and the decision to keep playing, even with some roadblocks.
"It was a tough couple years, taking a step back and deciding whether to move forward with life. Are you done? The mental battles that we go through and just push through, persevere and overcome adversity ..." Beckham said.
In his career, Beckham has played 119 games, with 97 starts, totaling 7,987 receiving yards and 59 touchdowns in the air.

title: Aaron Donald is back: What NFL history says about his super duo with Myles Garrett
summary: Donald's return gives the Rams two generational pass rushers with five Defensive Player of the Year awards between them
full_text:
He's back. Aaron Donald is officially returning after two years of retirement to complete the Rams ' super team, which includes Matthew Stafford , Kyren Williams , Puka Nacua , Davante Adams , Myles Garrett , Aaron Donald, Trent McDuffie and more, with Sean McVay at the controls.
What about the dynamic duo of Donald and Garrett, then? If super teams don't usually live up to the hype, what about a super duo? These are two of the best defensive players of all time. They are the first pair of teammates with multiple Defensive Player of the Year awards in NFL history. Yet, we don't know if they are joining forces at the height of their powers. I assume Garrett will be a monster this year, but is Donald going to be the same game wrecker at age 35 after two years out of the league?
It's fun to dream, but probably premature to put them in the same company of some of the best defensive pairs (Ray Lewis/Ed Reed, Lawrence Taylor/Carl Banks, Warren Sapp/Derrick Brooks) or defensive line duos (Alan Page/Carl Eller, Merlin Olsen/Deacon Jones, Richard Dent/Dan Hampton) of all time. If they played together for a while in their prime, sure. But they haven't even taken a snap together.
There's no denying this is maybe the most decorated duo ever on paper, though. So instead of comparing them to the duos above, pairs that were teammates for extended periods in their primes (Marvin Harrison and Reggie Wayne come to mind) or two ships passing in the night (Steve Young didn't become "Steve Young" until Joe Montana was out of the picture), I scoured league history for superstars joining forces later in their careers.
I like to call them super duos. They have a checkered history and can provide a picture of some potential outcomes for Donald and Garrett.
Let's start with the reason we are talking about this in the first place. The numbers surrounding Donald and Garrett are mind-blowing. Collectively, they have the most first-team All-Pro selections (13) by a defensive line duo ever (entering a season). The last DL duo with at least five All-Pro selections each was Alan Page and Carl Eller, who made up half of the "Purple People Eaters" on the 1978 Vikings .
They are the first duo to enter a season with 100+ career sacks each since Derrick Thomas and Leslie O'Neal for the 1999 Chiefs .
Donald averages the most sacks per game (0.72) by a defensive tackle all-time and has the most sacks in a season by a DT (20.5), while Garrett averages the most sacks per game (0.94) in NFL history (at any position) and is coming off a single-season record total (23.0) in 2025.
The ceiling is out of this world. They could replicate a season from any of the best DL duos ever, or perhaps become the first tandem in league history to combine for 40+ sacks in a season. Or, maybe Garrett gets hurt or Donald proves to be a step slower.
Julio Jones and Mike Evans are a cautionary tale. Jones signed with the Buccaneers during training camp in 2022 after one season with the Titans where he had 434 receiving yards in 10 games. His prime was already over, so this came with less fanfare, but the name still had some value next to another future Hall of Famer in Mike Evans. Jones' decline continued as he didn't even eclipse 300 yards in his only season with Tampa Bay, who went one-and-done in the playoffs.
This is the closest example, in my opinion, and probably a good test case for what the Rams can get out of Donald and Garrett. We've already seen Donald pair up with a beast off the edge. Von Miller was a three-time first-team All-Pro and Super Bowl MVP with over 100 career sacks when he was traded to the Rams at the deadline in 2021. Donald and Miller combined for 19.0 sacks in 12 games together after Miller's midyear debut, including 4.0 in the Super Bowl (where Donald had the game-sealing play). Los Angeles would obviously be thrilled to get this type of production from their new super duo as the season progresses.
Terrell Owens and Chad Johnson were a reality show's dream (maybe not an offensive coordinator's) when they joined forces on the 2010 Bengals. Owens was near the end of his decorated career at age 37 and coming off 829 yards in 2009 with Buffalo. Johnson (who went by Ochocinco at the time) was 32 and coming off a seventh career 1,000-yard season. The show-stopping duo didn't produce many fireworks in Owens' last NFL season and Johnson's last in a Bengals uniform. The Bengals were awful (4-12 with Carson Palmer at quarterback), Owens had a quiet 983 receiving yards (222 in one game) and Johnson also fell below 1,000 yards.
Junior Seau and Zach Thomas are two of the best linebackers in NFL history. Seau was near the end of a Hall of Fame career when he was traded to the Dolphins in 2003, while Thomas was in the middle of his. They combined for nearly 250 tackles and Miami was third in scoring defense in 2003, but ultimately the pairing didn't get Miami to the playoffs and Seau was hurt much of his last two years with the Dolphins.
In terms of the team and players' pedigrees, I love this comp for Donald and Garrett. The GOAT Jerry Rice signed a four-year deal with the Raiders in 2001 (who had just made the AFC title game) to team up with Tim Brown.
"I'm living a dream right now. A situation like this doesn't happen that often. After 16 years in the league, to come to a team of this magnitude, I'm excited about the possibilities," Rice told ESPN's John Clayton back in 2001.
Rice and Brown were both top 10 all-time in receiving yards entering 2001 with Rice as the all-time leader. They became the oldest duo in league history with 1,000 receiving yards apiece (both were 35+) in 2001, and they helped Oakland reach the Super Bowl with another productive season in 2002.
Now this was a true "dream team." Washington had Deion Sanders, Darrell Green, Champ Bailey and Bruce Smith on its defense in 2000. Sanders and Green were about as decorated as you could find at the cornerback position, and they helped Washington finish as one of the best defensive units in football. It still wasn't good enough to make the playoffs, though.
Leslie O'Neal and Derrick Thomas were two of the best pass rushers of the nineties when O'Neal signed with Kansas City in 1998. They didn't do much damage in two seasons as teammates, which amounted to both of their final two years in the league. Thomas tragically passed away in 2000 following a car accident.
Kevin Greene and Chris Doleman both had 100 career sacks when they teamed up for the 1997 49ers and became the oldest duo in league history with 10+ sacks in a season. They helped San Francisco make an NFC title game near the end of its dynasty.
The 49ers dynasty attracted a lot of stars, including Richard Dent and Rickey Jackson, who had the most career sacks by any duo entering a season (239.5) when they got together in 1994. The 49ers won a Super Bowl that year, but Dent only played two games due to injury.
Well, Marcus Allen and Eric Dickerson were two of the best backs of the eighties, but they didn't have much left in the tank by the time they were teammates in 1992. In fact, there was so much tension from the running back room that it created a rift between Al Davis and Allen. This was Allen's last season with the silver and black and Dickerson's last year in the league.
The Dolphins had a super duo during their perfect 1972 season. They claimed former MVP quarterback Earl Morrall off waivers for $100 that offseason to back up future Hall of Fame signal caller Bob Griese. They could not have scripted it any better because Morrall had an All-Pro year after Griese broke his leg. Though he did return to start and win the Super Bowl.
Bottomline. The Donald-Garrett pairing could go either way. But, I think they'll be more Donald/Miller or Rice/Brown than some of the sob stories on this list.

Then 2025 was an unmitigated disaster as the Chiefs opened the year with back-to-back losses, rallied back to 5-3 by midseason and then lost eight of their last nine games as well as Patrick Mahomes to an ACL tear late in that skid. Now Mahomes is in a battle with the clock to be ready for Week 1 while the defense will have to overcome the departure of multiple cornerbacks in order to get back to the top of a competitive conference.

The Chiefs sitting +160 to win the division during the Patrick Mahomes era isn't unprecedented -- they were around the same price at the beginning of the 2022 season before rattling off three straight trips to the Super Bowl -- but they'll have their longest odds to win the Super Bowl heading into a season since Mahomes' first taking over as starting quarterback.
