title: Ravens Roundtable: Reactions to UDFA QB Joe Fagnano making 53-man roster
summary: The Baltimore Ravens finalized their initial 53-man roster on Sunday and one of the biggest decisions they made was keeping Joe Fagnano. Fagnano, an undrafted free agent out of Connecticut, is the first UDFA quarterback in Ravens’ franchise history to make the 53-man roster. Fagnano was a standout performer in the preseason and evidently played […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - AUGUST 22: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Joe Fagnano (12) warms up before the NFL preseason game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Minnesota Vikings on August 22nd, 2026, at U.S. Bank in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens finalized their initial 53-man roster on Sunday and one of the biggest decisions they made was keeping Joe Fagnano. Fagnano, an undrafted free agent out of Connecticut, is the first UDFA quarterback in Ravens’ franchise history to make the 53-man roster. Fagnano was a standout performer in the preseason and evidently played well enough to earn himself a roster spot. Here are the Baltimore Beatdown staff’s reactions to the move. There was almost no thought that the Ravens would keep three quarterbacks entering this spring and summer. However, no one foresaw Joe Fagnano performing at such a high level in the preseason. He put together three good exhibition performances and demonstrated the ability to run Declan Doyle’s offense well. Fagnano is a good developmental quarterback to have in the farm system, and evidently the Ravens felt risking him to other teams was not worth it. With how he played in the preseason, Fagnano may very well have been scooped up by another team. The Ravens now have more insurance behind Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley, and another potential long-term backup option. — Frank Platko Going into the preseason, I thought there was absolutely no world in which the Ravens would keep three quarterbacks on the 53-man roster, but Fagnano’s excellent performance across three games changed my opinion completely. Fagnano’s poise in the pocket and ability to work through his reads and deliver accurate passes on time was something you rarely see from a rookie quarterback, let alone an undrafted one with barely any practice reps under his belt entering the preseason. The risk of him making it through waivers to land on Baltimore’s practice squad was a risk they weren’t willing to take in the end — Dustin Cox Joe Fagnano earned his spot on the roster and absolutely deserves it. I am shocked the Ravens kept a third, developmental, quarterback who should hopefully never see the field on a championship hopeful roster but I’m glad they managed it. I could absolutely see Fagnano developing into the backup quarterback of the future and making either him or Huntley a tradable asset soon. — Zach Canter

full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 27: Keleki Latu #83 of the Buffalo Bills against the Pittsburgh Steelers during a pre-season game at Highmark Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images Everyone tells you what they believe in, but actions speak louder than words. In 2012, a film called “Would You Rather” released in select theaters. An independent psychological horror film, the movie focuses on a dinner party conducted by a wealthy “philanthropist” Shepard Lambrick who organizes a set of games to test how far his financially-strapped guests would be willing to go to obtain the money they so desperately need. In one notable scene, Lambrick tests the convictions of vegetarian character Iris (played by Brittany Snow) by offering her $5,000 to eat a steak and foie gras. When Iris (who attended the party to try to acquire money to help her ill brother) declines on principle, Lambrick ups the ante to $10,000. Iris caves, taking the money and eating the meat. Overall, I felt the strong premise of the film was damaged by the leaning towards gore and inconsistent character logic. However, it does do an excellent job of outlining the idea that people’s principles are far more fluid and situational than they will vocally acknowledge. The Buffalo Bills have their initial 53-man roster and practice squad set. General Manager/VP of Football Operations Brandon Beane and Head Coach Joe Brady have spent a lot of time discussing their vision for the team since their promotions were announce early this year. Ultimately, none of that matters. What they actually did says far more about their principles than whatever they said. And principle spoke loudest above all when the dust settled: the Bills picked organizationally perceived talent over traditionally perceived roster quotas. Armaj Reed-Adams. Kani Walker/Toriano Pride Jr. Ben VanSumeren. Mike Danna. In all three of these circumstances, players who the regime felt were roster-worthy players pushed the organization towards making a decision that pushed rigid positional numbers to the back burner. Offensive Line Reed-Adams played well in the preseason as a seventh-round pick, but as the likely 10th offensive lineman and a guard-only backup, traditional thinking would have meant he was destined for waivers and a practice squad spot. But the Bills decided to go heavy on the offensive line to keep him on the active roster and not expose him to other teams (an unorthodox stance for a player taken in the last 15 picks of the draft). Given the Bills have two players on expiring contracts that just finished a battle for the starting left guard position in Alec Anderson and Austin Corbett, having a cost-controlled player who’s been in the building developing as a potential option for a starting guard position in 2027 may be on the team’s mind as they elect to carry Reed-Adams. Cornerback Kani Walker and Toriano Pride Jr. were neck-and-neck when I most recently evaluated the positional battle. Where I (and others) got it wrong is in the assumption that there must be an outside CB4 from the two of them. Many, including myself, expected that for all actual logistical purposes, Dee Alford was your CB4. There was little change of having a situation come up on the field where Dee Alford would be in the nickel defender spot, Walker/Pride Jr. would be at outside corner, and second-year offseason star Jordan Hancock would be on the bench. In actuality, Alford would take on the outside corner spot if necessary and Hancock (who may be the team’s preferred dime defender) would slide in to play the nickel. But surely after all that talk from Beane about cornerback depth being a concern post-draft (as reasoning for the surprise second-round selection of Davison Igbinosun out of Ohio State), they wouldn’t have just five corners, right? They would, because talk is cheap, and they didn’t feel like Walker or Pride Jr. were rosterable NFL players at this time. Fullback Joe Brady said he wasn’t going to keep a fullback just to keep a fullback. He apparently meant it. The team released undrafted rookie Jackson Acker a few weeks ago, leading the roster down the path of “if they keep one, I guess VanSumeren.” They didn’t keep one, despite the Bills highly-ranked rushing attack featuring the league’s rushing yards leader employing a fullback in 2025. Despite the Sean Payton offenses historically (of which Joe Brady calls himself of “protege”) using the position. Despite the league-wide trend towards heavier personnel having the position (along with second and third tight ends) get a larger snap share than it did in the 2010s. The Bills didn’t think VanSumeren was a roster-worthy player, so they didn’t roster him (he has since signed to the Chiefs practice squad, so they didn’t secure him there either); positional checkmarks be damned. The Bills elected to keep fourth tight end Keleki Latu (inarguably more effective player than VanSumeran as exhibited throughout both of their respective careers) and already had a very strong tight end room in the 1-3 spots on the depth chart in another move toward maximizing the perceived talent on the roster. Edge Rusher The Bills elected to keep six edge rushers, including May signee Mike Danna. For comparison, Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard’s former team (the Denver Broncos) currently has four edge rushers on their active roster. The Baltimore Ravens have five, the New England Patriots have four, The Los Angeles Rams have five, and the Green Bay Packers have four (not counting All-Pro Micah Parsons, currently on the Physically Unable to Perform list). Danna performed well this preseason after coming aboard later in the spring and has been a paid starter for a high-level defense in Kansas City previously, but the numbers weren’t in his favor as the team was always likely to keep Gregory Rousseau, 2026 free agent signee Bradley Chubb, 2nd round pick T.J. Parker, and Michael Hoecht coming off an Achilles injury but trending towards active roster status. Those four may have been where teams may have stopped, but Javon Solomon plays special teams and is a better fit in this defense than the previous one under former head coach Sean McDermott, so he had a chance if they kept five. Danna, like Reed-Adams and Latu already mentioned, appeared to be the victim of the numbers game. But the Bills decided the best way to win the game was to not play in 2026. Danna proved to be a roster-worthy player, so he made the roster. What seems so simple to many is actually a slap in the face on more traditional roster construction philosophies. This isn’t some magical or unique thing that Brady and Beane are doing, but it happened in multiple circumstances across the roster and creates a theme worth mentioning here. Time will tell if Beane and Brady made the right calls in each of these situations. That’s why I specifically used the word “perceived” in the premise of this article. The organization thinks they picked player talent over traditional position allocations. Does it work? No idea. Does it even stand or do the Bills make a set of roster moves in the next week that completely blow this entire premise to smithereens? No clue. But it’s something to put in the back of our minds as we have to partially reset our opinions of this partially new Bills regime. …and that’s the way the cookie crumbles. I’m Bruce Nolan with Buffalo Rumblings. You can find me on Twitter and Instagram @BruceExclusive and look for new episodes of “The Bruce Exclusive” every Thursday on the Rumblings Cast Network — see more in my LinkTree!

summary: The Buffalo Bills have put the finishing touches on their first practice-squad roster of the 2026 NFL season, with the news official now revealing a group of 17 players having signed contracts on August 31. By rostering defensive lineman Travis Clayton (who is part of the NFL’s International Player Pathway program), the Bills are able […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - JANUARY 17: Shaq Thompson #45 of the Buffalo Bills leads a huddle prior to an NFL divisional playoff football game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on January 17, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills have put the finishing touches on their first practice-squad roster of the 2026 NFL season, with the news official now revealing a group of 17 players having signed contracts on August 31. By rostering defensive lineman Travis Clayton (who is part of the NFL’s International Player Pathway program), the Bills are able to include a 17th player on the practice squad this season. Ryan Talbot was among the first to share the names of 13 players sticking with Buffalo , confirming that wide receiver Greg Dortch is among those heading to One Bills Drive. Dortch was released by the Arizona Cardinals over the weekend. He brings a dynamic element as a receiver after the catch and as a potential punt returner. Additionally, the Bills are bringing back inside linebacker Shaq Thompson via the practice squad, per a report by Jay Skurski. Widely considered the team’s best linebacker last season, Thompson played a key role with Buffalo in 2025, highlighted by his elite leadership intangibles. Interestingly, fan-favorite running back Ian Wheeler is not part of the team’s initial practice squad plans , per Ryan Talbot. Reportedly, Wheeler turned down an offer to join the Bills’ practice squad , per a report by Greg Gabriel. Among other notable initial absences are cornerback Tre’Davious White, wide receiver Brandin Cooks, and linebacker Matt Milano. IT remains to be seen if any of those three find their way back to One Bills Drive later this season. The Bills defeated the Jaguars 27-24. [Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union] | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Bills hadn’t signed any holdovers from the previous regime to their practice squad… until now. As clubs around the league are filling out their practice squad on Monday evening, Buffalo News’ reporter Jay Skurski tweeted the following about Shaq Thompson set to return to Orchard Park: The Bills have a deal in place to bring a familiar face back to the organization. According to a league source, the team is signing linebacker Shaq Thompson to the practice squad. — Jay Skurski (@JaySkurski) August 31, 2026 Thompson played admirably for the Bills in 2025, his first with the team after a long tenure in Carolina. He played on 42.4% of Buffalo’s defensive snaps a season ago and made 56 tackles, six tackles for loss, two pass breakups, one sack, and one forced fumble. Thompson made 13 tackles, two tackles for loss, and snagged an interception — against the Jaguars — in the Bills two playoff games in January. Now 32, the longtime veteran is part of Buffalo’s practice squad to provide experienced depth behind Terrel Bernard, Dorian Williams, Kaleb Elarms-Orr, and Joe Andreessen at inside linebacker in Jim Leonhard’s scheme. What’s most intriguing about this addition — it appears as though Thompson was picked over Matt Milano on the practice squad.

title: Buffalo Bills hit homerun with practice-squad signing of Greg Dortch
summary: It seemed painfully obvious during the Buffalo Bills preseason — the team had returner problem, and they may have just solved it after NFL cutdown day. According the Talbots, Damon and Ryan, the Bills are expected to sign veteran receiver and return man Greg Dortch to their practice squad: I cannot stress enough how much […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 23: Greg Dortch #4 of the Arizona Cardinals runs the ball past Andrew Wingard #42 of the Jacksonville Jaguars during the second half of the game at State Farm Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Glendale, Arizona. The Jaguars defeated the Cardinals 27-24 in overtime. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images It seemed painfully obvious during the Buffalo Bills preseason — the team had returner problem, and they may have just solved it after NFL cutdown day. According the Talbots, Damon and Ryan, the Bills are expected to sign veteran receiver and return man Greg Dortch to their practice squad: Can confirm. #BillsMafia https://t.co/dLVpgG9ubM — Ryan Talbot (@RyanTalbotBills) August 31, 2026 I cannot stress enough how much I’m in favor of this transaction for the Bills. Dortch has 99 punt returns and 75 kick returns in his NFL career to date. So that solves the returner problem. Even though Dortch does have six fumbles on those 174 returns, he’s undeniably a veteran returner. A season ago, Dortch finished 11th in the NFL in average return yards on punts at 11.6, which represented the fourth-consecutive season in which he upped his punt-return average and the first time he raised that average to double-digit yardage. Secondly, Dortch is, of course, a receiver, and that’s still a position group I felt the Bills had room to add talent to ahead of the beginning of the regular season. In 2022, Dortch played on 42.5% of the Cardinals snaps and was respectably productive, amassing 467 yards on 52 receptions with a pair of receiving touchdowns. He failed to reach 40% of Arizona’s offensive snaps in any of the following three seasons and averaged 34 snags for 313 yards and three touchdowns per year. Dortch has proven to be relatively sure-handed as a twitchy, underneath option. He’s dropped just four passes on 184 targets as a professional. And, for a 5’7”, 175-pound receiver, Dortch’s 40% contested-catch win rate is rather impressive. But for me, a longtime believer in the importance of YAC in the modern NFL, what Dortch has proven to be capable of with the ball in his hands is most tantalizing about the addition for the Bills when considering his receiver profile. Last season, on just 29 receptions, Dortch forced 12 missed tackles. That’s absurd. For perspective, Jameson Williams forced the same amount of missed tackles on 65 catches (in the regular season). And the 2025 season wasn’t an outlier for Dortch. In 2024, on a mere 37 catches, he forced 13 missed tackles, the same number as Ladd McConkey forced on 82 receptions. The dude is a YAC machine… he’s a receiver that cornerbacks, safeties, and linebackers do not want to see in space. Roughly two-thirds of Dortch’s career snaps have come from the slot, which could spark more pre-snap alignment flexibility for Khalil Shakir who’s appeared inside on over 70% of his snaps in each of the past three regular seasons with the Bills. And he’s someone who plays with a noticeable “edge” that the Bills have seemingly been looking to acquire all offseason. He plays with no fear and oftentimes his urgency with the ball in his hands, or when he’s leaping to make a catch in traffic, surprises defenders because he’s small playing with unbridled tenacity. That inner-aggression on the field dates back to Wake Forest — and likely earlier. Dortch accumulated exactly 1,800 receiving yards on 142 receptions with 17 touchdowns in his two seasons with the Demon Deacons and regularly outmuscled cornerbacks on jump balls or powered through arm-tackle attempts in the ACC. The cherry on top? Dortch, who’s 28 years old, spent 2021-2025 with Bills special teams coordinator Jeff Rodgers in Arizona. I hope this article doesn’t read as though I believe the Bills have just signed an All-Pro to their practice squad with Dortch. But he checks all the boxes for what the team needed at (punt) returner. And he adds experienced depth — with a specialized skill (YAC!)— to a receiver group that indisputably was ripe for an infusion of veteran talent. Dortch will (oh, and he was born in Rochester, New York)

title: Buffalo Bills awarded no players on waivers, rookie claimed by Browns
summary: The NFL has announced the waiver claims by all teams after roster cutdown day, and it was reasonably uneventful for the Buffalo Bills — they were not awarded any players. However, rookie seventh-round pick Toriano Pride Jr. was claimed by the Browns. This is not the first time during the Brandon Beane era a Bills […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 22: Toriano Pride Jr. #32 of the Buffalo Bills walks off the field prior to a preseason game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on August 22, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The NFL has announced the waiver claims by all teams after roster cutdown day, and it was reasonably uneventful for the Buffalo Bills — they were not awarded any players. However, rookie seventh-round pick Toriano Pride Jr. was claimed by the Browns. This is not the first time during the Brandon Beane era a Bills rookie was claimed by another team after spending only one summer in Orchard Park. Pride Jr. joins the likes of guard Jack Anderson, cornerback Alex Austin, guard Nick Broeker, tackle Luke Tenuta who were claimed before Week 1 by another team after one training camp and preseason with the Bills. Buffalo selected Pride Jr. with its first of three seventh-round picks this past April after an illustrious career at Missouri and a blistering 4.32 time in 40-yard dash at the 2026 NFL Combine. The 5’11”, 188-pounder missed a whopping three tackles on 100 snaps during the preseason and allowed nine catches for 50 yards with one touchdown on 11 targets in his coverage area. He was also credited with a pass breakup. And now he’s a Cleveland Brown. (This of course means, Kani Walker remains on the Bills practice squad.)

title: Injured players Buffalo Bills will avoid in first month of the season
summary: With NFL cutdown day also comes injury designations for a small collection of players on each team around the league. The Buffalo Bills placed rookie Zane Durant on IR designated to return, Phidarian Mathis on the suspension list, Dorian Strong on the Non-Football Injury list, and Tyrell Shavers on the Physically Unable to Perform list. […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - DECEMBER 04: Brian Branch #32 of the Detroit Lions defends in coverage during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at Ford Field on December 4, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images With NFL cutdown day also comes injury designations for a small collection of players on each team around the league. The Buffalo Bills placed rookie Zane Durant on IR designated to return, Phidarian Mathis on the suspension list, Dorian Strong on the Non-Football Injury list, and Tyrell Shavers on the Physically Unable to Perform list. Which players on the rosters of Buffalo’s first four opponents — IR has the shortest return timeline at four weeks — found themselves on these lists to begin the season? Check below. Week 1 – Houston Texans WR Tank Dell WR Jayden Higgins EDGE Dylan Horton Dell is still working back from a devastating knee injury he suffered late in the 2024 campaign. Higgins tore his ACL in a joint practice just a few weeks ago. The latter was an early second-round pick in 2025 and had 41 catches for 525 yards with six touchdowns during the regular season as a rookie, including four grabs for 38 yards and a score against the Bills. Horton tore his Achilles this summer after he generated 16 pressures on 146 pass-rush snaps in 2025 in his third season with the Texans. Week 2 – Detroit Lions S Brian Branch S Kerby Joseph OC Cade Mays Branch and Joseph, when healthy, are in the running for the best safety tandem in the NFL. Branch tore his Achilles in Week 14 last season, and is still recovering. Joseph was signed to a monster extension before the 2025 season, played through a knee injury, and reaggravated the injury late last season. He was placed on IR on December 20. Both Brian and Joseph will start the season on the PUP list for Detroit. Mays has over 1,700 snaps on his NFL resume to date — all of which came in Carolina — and he inked a three-year, $25 million deal this offseason to be the Lions starting center but broke a bone in his wrist this summer and will miss a large chunk of the upcoming season. Week 3 – Los Angeles Chargers OC Tyler Biadasz Biadasz worked his way into the starting lineup in Dallas across four seasons before spending the past two with Dan Quinn in Washington as the full-time center. The Chargers signed him to a three-year, $30M deal in March but he tore his ACL this summer. Week 4 – New England Patriots EDGE Harold Landry The veteran edge rusher was placed on PUP to begin the Patriots season, meaning he’ll miss the Week 4 showdown with the Bills. The former second-round pick has strong ties to Mike Vrabel from their time together in Tennessee. In 2025 with the Patriots, Landry registered 52 pressures on 435 pass-rush snaps — including playoffs — including a whopping seven on 36 opportunities in New England’s win over the Bills in Orchard Park.

title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 12 Days Remaining
summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA - JANUARY 18: Wide receiver Muhsin Muhammad #87 of the Carolina Panthers quiets the Philadelphia Eagles fans after catching a touchdown pass in the second quarter during the NFC Championship game on January 18, 2004 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Brian Bahr/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #12. Muhsin Muhammad The Carolina Panthers took Muhammad in the second round of the 1996 NFL Draft. The big-bodied receiver out of Michigan State only played nine games his rookie year due to a lingering hamstring issue, but brought in over 400 yards receiving and one touchdown. The run-first offense in 1996 combined with the heavy reliance on Wesley Walls and Mark Carrier made it tough for Moose to break out. It wasn’t until the 1998 season, his third in the league, that he finally started to blossom. He started all 16 games for the Panthers, bringing in 68 catches for 941 yards and six touchdowns. The following season was Muhammad’s first Pro Bowl selection, which was well earned. He hauled in 96 passes for 1,253 yards and eight touchdowns, leading the team in the former two categories and finishing third in the latter. Muhammad eclipsed the 100 catch mark for the first and only time in his career during the 2000 season, finishing with just under 1,200 yards and six scores. He ended up leading the entire NFL in catches that year with 102. The 2001 season was disappointing for the entire franchise, and Muhammad was no different. He missed five games due to injuries, yet still finished second in catches and yards, which really hammers home just how bad the offense was in 2001. The 2001 Draft changed the Panthers franchise forever in many ways, including giving Muhammad a true running mate on the outside. Steve Smith Sr came into the league as mainly a returner, but by 2002 the Panthers had their dynamic duo at wide receiver. Smith and Muhammad shared similar target shares and success those two seasons. The 2003 season was a magical one for Muhammad and the Panthers, making a surprising run to the Super Bowl. Muhammad still owns the record for the longest receiving touchdown in Super Bowl history, and 85-yard bomb from Jake Delhomme. 2004 was Muhammad’s best individual season, which was good timing for him since he was in a contract year. An injury to Steve Smith left Muhammad as the main viable receiving threat, and he absolutely thrived. He caught 93 passes for a career high 1,405 yards and a still Panthers record 16 receiving touchdowns. He cashed in that offseason, signing a six-year, $30 million contract with the Chicago Bears. That may sound paltry by today’s standards, but in 2005 it was the equivalent of getting about $15 million per year in today’s cap. He never came close to living up to his contract, however, scoring fewer touchdowns in three seasons with the Bears than he did in just the 2004 season in Carolina. He returned to the Panthers in 2008 after the Bears released him, and he bounced back a bit, falling just short of the 1,000 yard receiving mark. He retired following the 2009 season. Muhammad has been around the team since, occasionally dropping in for color commentary on local broadcasts. He was inducted into the Panthers Hall of Honor in 2023 along with Hall of Famer Julius Peppers. To this point, Moose is the second best receiver in Panthers history, literally. He ranks second in franchise history in all major receiving categories: catches, yards, touchdowns, 100-yard games. His constant appearance in the record books and high performance on the biggest stage lands him at No. 12 on our countdown.

full_text: CANTON, OHIO - AUGUST 06: Akayleb Evans #29 of the Carolina Panthers looks on during the first quarter of the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame Game against the Arizona Cardinals at Tom Benson Hall Of Fame Stadium on August 06, 2026 in Canton, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The end of the offseason is here. All NFL teams were required to cut their 90-man preseason rosters down to 53 players by Sunday evening. Carolina Panthers gneral manager Dan Morgan and head coach Dave Canales (+3300 to win AP NFL Coach of the Year per FanDuel ) had their work cut out for them. The roster announcement coming an hour late not withstanding, there is plenty of suspense left for the Panthers roster. Look no further than fan favorite wide receiver Ja’seem Reed, who is currently subject to waivers. The Panthers have a surprising amount of talent they may want to bring back into their fold. Doing so to either their 53-man roster or practice squad requires following the rules of the NFL waiver wire. Waiver claims Corey Bullock, center, Baltimore Ravens Former Panthers claimed by other teams Trevin Wallace, linenacker, New York Jets Nick Samac, C, Minnesota Vikings How does the waiver wire work? Teams have until 1 PM ET the day after roster cuts—that’s Monday, August 31st for those following along at home—to file a waiver claim. That’s just 19 hours after cuts are finalized. The NFL will then review claims and assign players to teams in order of their waiver wire priority. What is waiver wire priority? Waiver wire priority follows, for the first three weeks of the NFL season, the pre-trade NFL draft order. That order then adjusts to a record-based order, essentially the next year’s projected draft order. The Carolina Panthers are currently 19th in the waiver wire priority order. The full list is as follows: Las Vegas Raiders New York Jets Arizona Cardinals Tennessee Titans New York Giants Cleveland Browns Washington Commanders New Orleans Saints Kansas City Chiefs Cincinnati Bengals Miami Dolphins Dallas Cowboys Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Tampa Bay Buccaneers Indianapolis Colts Detroit Lions Minnesota Vikings Carolina Panthers Green Bay Packers Pittsburgh Steelers Los Angeles Chargers Philadelphia Eagles Jacksonville Jaguars Chicago Bears Buffalo Bills San Francisco 49ers Houston Texans Los Angeles Rams Denver Broncos New England Patriots Seattle Seahawks

full_text: Nov 10, 2019; Chicago, IL, USA; A detailed view of the Chicago Bears helmet before the game against the Detroit Lions at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Mike DiNovo-USA TODAY Sports The Chicago Bears have begun signing players to their initial 2026 practice squad, but the list will be fluid, and we’ll update it throughout the year. Here are the first 11 signed players per the NFL transaction wire, but a couple of others were reported earlier today and are listed in our tracker . There will be other players added to the practice squad tomorrow. Caden Barnett, OG Kyle Hergel, iOL Salvon Ahmed, RB Scotty Miller, WR Kaden Davis, WR J.P Richardson, WR Stephen Carlson, TE Wayne Matthews, LB Marlen Sewell, S Deantre Prince, CB Marcus Davenport, DE Here are the qualifications for practice squad eligibility and some rules to remember. A 17th player is permitted as long as he qualifies for the NFL’s International Pathway Program. Players with no accrued seasons (rookies) and those with fewer than nine regular-season games in their lone accrued season. A maximum of ten players are allowed who have earned no more than two accrued seasons. Up to six players with unlimited accrued seasons are permitted on the practice squad. However, the number of players in the last two categories cannot exceed 10 total players. Teams can elevate up to two practice squad players for each game, but they can still only have 48 players active on game day. After the game, the elevated player(s) will revert to the practice squad. A player can be elevated up to three times, but if he’s needed after that, the team would be required to sign him to the 53-man active roster. Players on practice squads are free agents who can be signed to another team’s active roster. A player’s current club can’t block him from leaving; they can only make a counteroffer to keep him. Ultimately, it’s the player’s decision. If a player is signed away, his new team must keep him on its 53-man roster for three weeks, but if he’s released, he’ll revert to his previous team. Players signed to another active roster are also guaranteed three weeks’ salary. A practice squad player can’t sign with his team’s upcoming opponent unless he does so six days before the upcoming game or ten days prior if his team is on its bye week.

title: 2026 Chicago Bears Practice Squad Rules and Rumor Tracker
summary: The NFL’s cut-down deadline is later today at 5:00 pm (CT), but several teams have already gotten an early start in whittling their offseason roster down to 53 players. Clubs can’t establish their 16-man practice squads until the claiming period for players placed on waivers expires at Noon (CT) tomorrow (8/31), but plenty of rumors […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - DECEMBER 04: Marcus Davenport #92 of the Detroit Lions rushes the passer during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at Ford Field on December 4, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL’s cut-down deadline is later today at 5:00 pm (CT), but several teams have already gotten an early start in whittling their offseason roster down to 53 players. Clubs can’t establish their 16-man practice squads until the claiming period for players placed on waivers expires at Noon (CT) tomorrow (8/31), but plenty of rumors about players teams want back will be floating around before then. If you want to catch up on any Chicago Bears news, you can check out our 53-Man Roster Transaction Tracker . Here are the qualifications for practice squad eligibility. A 17th player is permitted as long as he qualifies for the NFL’s International Pathway Program. Players with no accrued seasons (rookies) and those with fewer than nine regular-season games in their lone accrued season. A maximum of ten players are allowed who have earned no more than two accrued seasons. Up to six players with unlimited accrued seasons are permitted on the practice squad. However, the number of players in the last two categories cannot exceed 10 total players. Teams can elevate up to two practice squad players for each game, but they can still only have 48 players active on game day. After each game, the elevated player(s) will revert to the practice squad without having to pass through waivers. A player can be elevated up to three times a season, but a fourth would require him to be signed to the 53-man active roster. If they want to place him back on the practice squad, they’d need to release him and have him clear waivers. If that happens, the club could elevate him three more times. Another point to keep in mind about the practice squad is that all these players are free agents. They can negotiate and sign to another team’s active roster without being blocked by their current employer. The current club can make a counteroffer, but if the practice squadder wants to leave, he’s gone. If a player is signed away, his new team must keep him on its 53-man roster for at least three weeks; if he’s released before then, he reverts to his previous team. Players signed to another active roster are also guaranteed three weeks’ salary. Also, a practice squad player can’t sign with his team’s upcoming opponent unless it’s done six days before the upcoming game or ten days prior if his team is on its bye week. title: Bears betting big on Jordan van den Berg
summary: There had been rumors for months, largely fanned by Fox’s Jordan Schultz, that the Chicago Bears were looking to move Gervon Dexter. Over the weekend, those rumors materialized as there were reports that Dexter was on the move and headed to the Atlanta Falcons. The trade makes some sense. Dexter’s in the last year of […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Chicago Bears defensive tackle Jordan van den Berg (96) makes a tackle against Cincinnati Bengals running back Kentrel Bullock (31) during the second quarter at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There had been rumors for months, largely fanned by Fox’s Jordan Schultz, that the Chicago Bears were looking to move Gervon Dexter. Over the weekend, those rumors materialized as there were reports that Dexter was on the move and headed to the Atlanta Falcons. The trade makes some sense. Dexter’s in the last year of his deal and the Bears have never really made any indication that they were planning on giving him a second contract. Ian Cunningham is now the GM in Atlanta, and he was a big part of the Dexter draft selection a few years ago. And the Bears receive CB Clark Phillips (and a 5th round pick) in return, and the Bears secondary is certainly a mess right now. But for all the reasons that it makes sense, there’s one reason it makes no sense: the Bears need all the talent they can get on the defensive line. It’s no secret that their defensive line is the weakest position group on the team. After Montez Sweat, there are some has-beens, some never-wases, and some hopeful prospects, but there certainly isn’t much in terms of established help for Sweat. Dexter was that guy. He certainly had weaknesses in his game, largely against the run, but he was able to get some interior pressure, and his play was consistently better than many others in that room. So why make a weak position group even weaker? Enter Jordan van den Berg. Van den Berg has had an excellent training camp and has turned heads with some of his preseason highlights. His play has certainly been inconsistent, but that should be expected for a rookie 6th-round pick. The fact that the Bears traded two sevenths to move up to get him shows that they spent almost zero draft capital on this player, and he could be a contributor in year one. But that’s a key word there. He could be a contributor in year one; we don’t necessarily know if he will be. But the Bears think they do know, and they think he will be. . @ChicagoBears @Titans @JordanvandenB12 @StaceyDales Some guys just know how to play the game….And with a maniac's intensity. He was born to be a Bear. #dabears #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/ELi5BzKOvm — Brian Baldinger (@BaldyNFL) August 30, 2026 When Brian Baldinger starts highlighting a player like this, people should listen. But are the Bears betting too much on a 6th-round rookie? You can certainly make that case. The Bears have opened up a Super Bowl window, many of us think if the Bears aren’t a true Super Bowl contending team this year, the defensive line is going to be the reason why they are not. The Bears just took their most consistent defensive tackle and traded him away because they are betting on a 6th-round rookie being just as reliable, if not more so than what Dexter has been. Now, from a roster building exercise, if you can get draft capital for a player you don’t see fitting into your longterm plans, it certainly makes sense to get something for them. But when you are as thin at a position as the Chicago Bears are, trading away a player is certainly risky business. But Dexter is gone, and it’s van den Berg time. I think there’s no question that van den Berg is going to be a fan favorite. We will see van den Berg jerseys at Soldier Field sooner rather than later. We are going to see the rookie make some splash plays from time to time. But will the rookie have the learning curve and ability to be consistent and not either be wildly successful or wildly dominated during a series (something we saw in preseason). The Bears believe they have found a diamond in the rough and that made Dexter expendable. Time will tell if the Bears scored something special with this year’s sixth round pick. They are betting on it. As Bears fans, we are certainly hoping they are correct.

full_text: You know what they say: turn your weaknesses into bigger weaknesses . Well, I’ve never heard that, but that’s what the Chicago Bears are ostensibly doing after trading starting defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Sr. to the Atlanta Falcons for Clark Phillips and a fifth-round pick. The former Bears second-round pick from the 2023 NFL Draft has been rumored to be on the trading block for much of the offseason and goes to reunite with Ian Cunningham, the assistant general manager who was part of bringing him to Chicago. While the move isn’t a total surprise, nor is it crazy in a vacuum, the concept of making the league’s worst run defense and pass rush demonstrably worse on paper is…a choice, to be sure, especially given how relatively little Chicago did in the offseason to address their defensive front. But if there are three things you can take away from this move, here’s what I’d say they are. 1. Keeping Dexter simply wasn’t worth it The NFL can be an unsentimental business. And the cold reality for Dexter was this: the Bears had no reason to keep him long-term based on what he’s done on the field. While posting a solid showing in 2024 under the previous regime, he simply didn’t seem to fit Dennis Allen’s vision for a quick, explosive 3-technique (55.6 overall grade). Retaining him beyond this year would’ve necessitated extending him to the tune of something like $15-20 million a season. The Bears are in no financial state to do this. So Poles and the Bears weighed the value of him being on the field providing mediocre play on a potentially expensive contract versus recouping what value they could for him in a swap and leaning on what they already have. Which leads us to… 2. The Bears think Jordan van den Berg is ready for a bigger role We were all thinking it, right? The sixth-round pick out of Georgia Tech has arguably been the biggest winner of the Bears’ preseason slate, popping repeatedly on film with a combination of top-flight athletic traits and an always-hot motor that makes him hard to miss. Now, doing this against another team’s starting offensive line versus feasting on backups will be something to watch. But one doesn’t need to be a first-round pick to be effective in the NFL, and van den Berg clearly fits the archetype of what Allen wants—an aggressive, athletic gap-shooter who beats offensive linemen to the spot and doesn’t allow them to block linebackers. It’s a risky move given that veteran Grady Jarrett is the only player in that position group with a track record of success, and Neville Gallimore and Kentavius Street are little more than depth pieces. That means the rookie will have to learn on the job fast, especially on early downs. But if the kid is as relentless against the starters as he looks against backups, one can understand making room for him rather than parking him behind a veteran in Dexter that you know isn’t part of the future. 3. This is the offense’s team now To be clear, the Bears don’t want to give up 30 points a game. One imagines the expectation for this year is no different than any other: get stops, keep teams out of the end zone. But in practical terms, this defense is leaving a lot to good execution and takeaway luck, which they benefited a ton from last season. The reality: they’re probably going to give up some points this season. It’s going to be the offense’s job to pick up the slack. They have the horses to do it. That much is for sure. Caleb Williams will continue his ascension into being one of the NFL’s best quarterbacks this season. The likes of Colston Loveland and Luther Burden III are primed to become stars. And Ben Johnson’s balance of creative passing concepts and dedication to pounding opposing defenses into the ground with his run game has proven for several years in a row now to be successful. (The latter, in particular, will be important to saving the defense’s stamina.) Poles, Johnson, and Allen have no doubt discussed the full-team implications of sending Dexter out of town and how they’re going to work around it. If the Bears are able to control the football effectively on offense, opposing offenses will have fewer chances to expose the defense. Plus, adding cornerback depth for a team with several injury question marks at the position, as well as future draft ammo, is useful. Hopefully, they’re right and that this skeleton crew is enough to get them to more home playoff games.

title: Bengals Tuesday Trenches: 53-man roster is set
summary: Training camp and the preseason are finished, and the Cincinnati Bengals have trimmed their roster down to the 53 men required to start the regular season, which begins in about a week and a half. Between now and then, it’s possible the Bengals add someone or move a few things around, but what we have […]
full_text: Aug 28, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Dohnte Meyers (81) makes a catch against the Philadelphia Eagles during the first quarter at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Training camp and the preseason are finished, and the Cincinnati Bengals have trimmed their roster down to the 53 men required to start the regular season, which begins in about a week and a half. Between now and then, it’s possible the Bengals add someone or move a few things around, but what we have right now is likely pretty close to what we’ll see in Week 1. There weren’t a ton of HUGE surprises, but there were a few. Here are some thoughts on the Bengals’ 53-man roster: I was happy to see Landon Robinson make the final 53, but I don’t think there was ever much doubt that he would. He’s the kind of kid you love to root for, and I have a feeling we’ll be seeing a lot of him, even though the Bengals’ defensive tackle rotation is very deep. I waffled back and forth over the last few days on what would happen with Tanner Hudson. It’s not that he didn’t deserve a spot; I just didn’t know if the Bengals would keep five tight ends, and I was confident he’d be the first one out the door if they chose to keep only four. In the end, I was right and wrong. They kept him initially, then dropped him to pick up offensive tackle Myles Hinton. The biggest surprise came at wide receiver. I was pretty shocked to see Ke’Shawn Williams make it over Mitchell Tinsley and Charlie Jones. I figured the final wide receiver spot would go to either Jones, because of his ability as a return specialist, or Tinsley, who turned a lot of heads last season. In the end, it went to neither. That means Williams is the new return specialist. I was also somewhat surprised to see Jones clear waivers and not even sign with a practice squad (as of this writing). Tinsley, meanwhile, was quickly claimed by the Texans. Josh Newton’s addition is likely a result of Ja’Sir Taylor being placed on IR with a designation to return because of a hamstring issue. Newton spent much of the preseason in the doghouse, but now he has at least the next four weeks to prove he belongs on the roster for good. Speaking of IR, it’s great news that Shemar Stewart avoided it. It’s not that there was much conversation about him being placed there, but it was still a relief knowing that, even if he isn’t ready for Week 1, we won’t automatically be waiting until Week 5 to see him. What is the thinnest position now that the roster is set? I’d have to go with linebacker and running back. What say you? Is there anything the Bengals can realistically do about either position right now? I’m not sure there’s anyone sitting around who could help them in a meaningful way. Bobby Wagner is still out there, but I feel like if that were going to happen, it probably would have happened by now. So, for the most part, I think this roster is set. Still , even with the lack of depth at running back and linebacker, I am very excited about this team. Offensively, the Bengals are a massive bomb ready to explode at any moment. There isn’t a defense in the NFL that can completely shut this offense down. There’s just too much talent. Sure, you can slow down Ja’Marr Chase, but then you have Tee Higgins to deal with. Take those two away, and there’s Mike Gesicki, Andrei Iosivas and the running backs. And, of course, Joe Burrow is the guy pulling the trigger. Good luck. And I’m just as excited about the defense. I wish they would have done more at linebacker, and I wouldn’t have complained about another veteran cornerback, but I think this has a chance to be the Bengals’ best defense since the 2021 and 2022 seasons. The defensive line is going to be so much better, and that improvement will trickle all the way back to the safeties. A defensive back’s best friend is a quarterback who doesn’t have time to throw. Remember how things worked when DJ Reader was soaking up blockers in the middle of the defensive line? It should be like that again. There are still plenty of variables. Health is a huge one, and there is little anyone can do to control that. A couple of key injuries can change the trajectory of an entire season overnight. Usually, when we reach this point in the offseason, I’m disappointed. I’ve almost always felt like the Bengals didn’t do enough to improve. That they left obvious holes unfilled. That they were counting too heavily on young players developing or injured players staying healthy. That too much was being left up to chance. I don’t feel that way right now. They took some big swings this offseason. They addressed major weaknesses. They added legitimate difference-makers. Are there still holes? Absolutely. But any complaints I have about this roster as it stands today feel more like nitpicking than legitimate grievances. For once, I’m not looking at the roster and thinking about what the Bengals should have done. I’m looking at what they actually did. And I like it. There’s a 14-3 team in that 53-man roster. Hopefully we get to see it. Relative Song Lyrics: 🦋 ‘Cause I can see the light of a clear blue morning I can see the light of a brand new day I can see the light of a clear blue morning Oh, and everything’s gonna be all right It’s gonna be okay

title: Bengals announce 11 practice squad moves
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are moving steadily through the process of filling out their practice squad. NFL teams can officially have 17 players on the practice squad (if one of them is part of the International Pathway Program), but most of them are just 16 men strong. The Bengals have officially announced 11 members of their […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 28: Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Isaiah Foskey #51 rushes the passer during the pre season game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Cincinnati Bengals on August 28th, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals are moving steadily through the process of filling out their practice squad. NFL teams can officially have 17 players on the practice squad (if one of them is part of the International Pathway Program), but most of them are just 16 men strong. The Bengals have officially announced 11 members of their practice squad, but it is not hard to guess where one more might come from. Here are the 11 that have been announced by the Bengals RB Kentrel Bullock QB Sean Clifford DT Howard Cross III DE Isaiah Foskey LB Joe Giles-Harris LB Shaka Heyward CB Bralyn Lux HB Kendall Milton WR Jordan Moore WR Noah Thomas S Russ Yeast These are all players who spent time with the Bengals during training camp. It isn’t hard to imagine that the 12th one should be. See, Cincinnati claimed Philadelphia Eagles offensive tackle Myles Hinton. That means they had to release a player who made the initial 53-man roster. Well, the released tight end is Tanner Hudson. He probably wants to return, as much as the Bengals would like to have him on their practice squad. Otherwise, the players they have kept here are either players who have been here for a while, or guys who impressed in camp. The Bengals can call up any of these guys to be activated on game day up to three times before they have to make room for them on the 53-man roster officially. Also, if a player goes on injured reserve for any period, they can call these guys up. So it is not only a way to keep developing these guys in your building, but it is actually a vital part of roster building since the rules around it changed during the COVID season to allow veteran players on it beyond those who have only played for two seasons or less. Given that Cincinnati has seen some of their more talented players they cut move on to other teams, these are the players they were looking to keep from their own guys before they went out and added from other teams. We will see if they can land any interesting players that could show up on a couple of Sundays.

title: 3 things we learned from the Bengals’ opening day 53-man roster
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals’ final roster cuts had some surprises but nothing too shocking. The main takeaway is that Zac Taylor and the front office put together a group of players who fit what the Bengals do, not one built on high upside or promise.  Here’s what we learned.  They like their tight ends Five tight […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - AUGUST 22: Dohnte Meyers #81of the Cincinnati Bengals runs with the ball while defended by Malik Muhammad #24 of the Chicago Bears during the preseason game at Paycor Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals’ final roster cuts had some surprises but nothing too shocking. The main takeaway is that Zac Taylor and the front office put together a group of players who fit what the Bengals do, not one built on high upside or promise. Here’s what we learned. They like their tight ends Five tight ends is a lot. But Taylor and offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher often feature multiple tight-end looks and even keep them on the field as fullbacks. Mike Gesicki is the starting-caliber receiving tight end. Erick All Jr. is superbly talented and needs to stay healthy. Drew Sample made his name as a blocker. Tanner Hudson has shown up as a receiver in the regular season. And Jack Endries gave us some splash plays in the preseason. It’s not hard to see why all five were retained. The focus is on the present The Bengals let Charlie Jones go, even though he was a fourth-round pick just in 2023 and, as Paul Dehner Jr. pointed out , the only NFL player with at least one return for a touchdown in each of the last three seasons. Cincinnati also released McKinnley Jackson, a talented third-round pick in 2024 who had yet to put it all together. In other words, they’re letting past production or unrealized potential be deciding factors. They want guys who are performing right now , this offseason. And that’s how Landon Robinson made it over Jackson and Dohnte Meyers, Colbie Young, and Ke’Shawn Williams made it over Jones. It’s a different mindset and one that is fitting for a team with Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, Dexter Lawrence, and only a few more years for that group to win a championship together. They want fighters This year’s roster is filled with inspiring stories, from Robinson, taken in the seventh round, to Meyers, a zero-star recruit who worked DoorDash until 3 AM to fund his NFL dream. Then there’s the undrafted Jacob Bayer and Swayze Bozeman. "This is just the beginning." pic.twitter.com/2q0j92paQM — Cincinnati Bengals (@Bengals) August 30, 2026 As Dehner Jr. wrote : Those are the types of players who build winning chemistry rather than tear it apart. There will be games this year when each of these players will be counted on to do a job or help a teammate do a job. There will be no doubt in their ability to do so or desire to do anything that helps the team win. The writer for The Athletic contrasted that with the players we’ve seen in the past who “you couldn’t say that about, whether it be staying out of trouble off the field, maintaining conditioning, knowing the playbook or, you know, showing up for stuff.” So the takeaway from all this is that the Bengals know who they are and what they want to accomplish. They’re no longer justifying decisions in their minds. They’re going with what they see on the field and maintaining a sense of urgency.

title: Bengals’ biggest 53-man roster surprises
summary: The preseason is over, and now we just need to wait two weeks until the Cincinnati Bengals take the field for the first time in a game that matters. Until then, though, there is still plenty to discuss. On Sunday, the Bengals announced their final 53-man roster. They made their cuts, and now they’ll prepare […]
full_text: Aug 28, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ke'shawn Williams (12) celebrates his touchdown catch against the Philadelphia Eagles during the second half at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The preseason is over, and now we just need to wait two weeks until the Cincinnati Bengals take the field for the first time in a game that matters. Until then, though, there is still plenty to discuss. On Sunday, the Bengals announced their final 53-man roster. They made their cuts, and now they’ll prepare to put together their practice squad. Before we get to that, though, here are some guys that made the roster that may surprise some. Ke’Shawn Williams We all knew the Bengals were going to have to make some tough decisions at the bottom half of the wide receiver position. Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and Andrei Iosivas were always going to be locks, but four guys were vying for the last three spots. Most thought the Bengals would either keep Jones or Tinsley, considering Jones is an accomplished return specialist, and Tinsley scored two touchdowns during last year’s regular season. That ended up not being the case, though. Instead, they opted for Williams, who caught seven passes for 81 yards and a touchdown. Jones and Tinsley combined for seven receptions. The decision to keep Williams likely stemmed from his comfort as both a return specialist and a receiver. Josh Newton Newton spent the vast majority of the preseason in the coach’s “ doghouse , “ but it appears as if his time chained up outside could be over. It could have been his performance on Friday night, which included an athletic pass breakup down the left sideline. Ja’Sir Taylor, who was placed on IR, was brought to Cincinnati as a free agent addition to the secondary on a one-year deal this offseason. The Bengals selected Tacario Davis in the third round of the draft, and he’ll join five other corners on the 53-man roster. Now the only corner on the roster the Bengals didn’t draft is Jalen Davis. PJ Jules Daijahn Anthony might be the better safety, but Jules made the roster because of what he does on special teams. Neither Jules nor Anthony would get a ton of snaps at safety—those will go to Bryan Cook and Jordan Battle. Special teams is a big deal, though, and it’s often the best way to sneak onto a roster. Jacob Bayer Guard Brian Parker II would have landed on the 53-man roster, but ended up on IR with Taylor instead. His spot went to Bayer, who played well this preseason, especially as a pass blocker. Hopefully he, along with the rest of the backup offensive linemen, isn’t called upon out of necessity. This is also a position the Bengals could address in free agency now that teams are making their final cuts. What players, if any, surprised you by making the Bengals’ 53-man roster? Sound off!

title: Browns: Rookie QB working to be more than just a physical threat
summary: Cleveland Browns rookie quarterback Taylen Green is a hard man to miss on the practice field. That is what happens when you are 6-foot-6 and anywhere from three to seven inches taller than the other quarterbacks standing next to you. But Green also stands out as arguably the most athletic of Cleveland’s four quarterbacks, a […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 27: Taylen Green #15 of the Cleveland Browns warms up prior to a preseason game against the New England Patriots at Huntington Bank Field on August 27, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Cleveland Browns rookie quarterback Taylen Green is a hard man to miss on the practice field. That is what happens when you are 6-foot-6 and anywhere from three to seven inches taller than the other quarterbacks standing next to you. But Green also stands out as arguably the most athletic of Cleveland’s four quarterbacks, a skill he flashed in last week’s preseason game against the New England Patriots when he turned a busted play in his own end zone into a 30-yard run. His ability to turn disaster into something positive certainly helped when head coach Todd Monken and general manager Andrew Berry selected the initial 53-man roster on Sunday. There was fear that Green already had a one-way ticket to the practice squad, since no team would ever consider carrying four quarterbacks on its roster. (Just don’t look at the Minnesota Vikings, Philadelphia Eagles, or Atlanta Falcons, because that ruins the narrative.) But Dillon Gabriel came down with an opportune back injury that landed him on injured reserve and opened up a roster spot for Green, a sixth-round draft pick who called making the squad “a dream come true.” Much of the attention placed on Green throughout the summer has focused on his athletic ability and whether or not the Browns will create “a package of plays” featuring Green to stun opposing defenses this fall. How realistic that is, or how much practice time Monken can devote to such a thing, is debatable and remains to be seen. It also, at least on a smaller level, boxes in Green as nothing more than someone who can just use his size to get a yard or two, as opposed to a quarterback who might bring more to the field as he develops. Taylen Green Every dropback from his NFL preseason debut pic.twitter.com/5vQ0WNPsCK — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) August 28, 2026 Green and Monken both had media time before practice today, and there were two things that stood out from their comments, both relating to the work Green has been putting in this summer. With practice reps limited, and about to get even more scarce with the regular season on the horizon, Green shared how he works on his game away from the practice facility : “Normally after we get out of practice, I normally take like 30 minutes to 45 minutes to myself. No football or nothing, watch some TV, eat something. Then after that, I normally go to my whiteboard; we have our script up and go through every single play and write it until I can’t get it wrong. After that, I do a mini walkthrough in my room. Just doing that, and then I got to call wifey. She helps me prepare for the next day. I continue to do that day in and day out, and in the morning, we have a walkthrough period as well, so just continue to do that.” That extra work has not gone unnoticed by Monken, who continues to make it clear that he likes a quarterback who thinks and studies the game : “(Taylen’s) very diligent. He’s a diligent note taker; you look at his notes, and so is Dillon. But Taylen, he stands back there even in the walks, and I can see him mentally going through the reps. So, I think that’s the biggest thing, looking at film, mentally going through the reps. Maybe not getting the physical reps, but he gets the mental part of it, and then some of his athleticism that ends up taking over.” Is that enough to get Green on the field this season? Probably not, as he is still pretty raw as a passer and was selected in the sixth round for a reason. But this is still the Browns, a team that has made a habit of playing numerous quarterbacks during a season, so ready or not, Green may find himself in the huddle one Sunday afternoon this fall. And if he does, no one can accuse him of not putting in the work, even if he has to go a long time without getting any first-team reps.

summary: The initial Cleveland Browns 53-man roster has given way to the next Cleveland Browns 53-man roster quite quickly. On top of that, the Browns first practice squad is taking shape and, reportedly, will not include preseason phenom WR Luke Floriea. As always in Cleveland, and really around the NFL, the quarterback continued to be the […]
full_text: Aug 28, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Dallas Cowboys quarterback Joe Milton III (10) runs with the ball during the game between the Cowboys and the Saints at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The initial Cleveland Browns 53-man roster has given way to the next Cleveland Browns 53-man roster quite quickly. On top of that, the Browns first practice squad is taking shape and, reportedly, will not include preseason phenom WR Luke Floriea . As always in Cleveland, and really around the NFL, the quarterback continued to be the big story. The Browns got… a little help… when QB Dillon Gabriel ended up with a back injury that will sideline him for the first four weeks of the season. That has allowed the team to not have to part ways with any of their four quarterbacks , for now. Just like Cleveland, the Dallas Cowboys continued their roster juggling on Monday, waiving QB Joe Milton , who many believed would be the team’s primary backup to QB Dak Prescott . As our SB Nation’s Blogging the Boys noted, Milton’s potential departure was eye-opening: The move comes as a pretty big surprise given the events of training camp and specifically the preseason. It seemed like Milton was a lock to be Dak Prescott’s primary backup this season, but even if you disagreed with that the idea of him not making the roster at all seemed a bit farfetched. Again, Milton played extremely well over the course of the preseason. He led the NFC in third-down passing across the exhibition period at large. This isn’t anything to really write home about given that it was the preseason, but you get the point that Milton played well in the opportunities that he had. Milton, much like Browns rookie Taylen Green , came out of college as an athletic marvel with a big arm. The third-year pro played in one game as a rookie with the New England Patriots, completing 76% of his passes for 241 yards and a touchdown. Last year, after being traded to the Cowboys, Milton played in four games, completing 15 of 24 passes (63%) with one touchdown and two interceptions. In his five career contests, Milton has also run for 66 yards. Milton’s rushing talent, along with his big arm, has made him a preseason highlight reel, including this year with Dallas. According to Marcus Mosher, who also covers the Cowboys, the team values a backup quarterback who does not need practice snaps or development , which led to their decision to hold on to QB Sam Howell and release Milton. With the Browns having a high waiver claim (6th) spot for the first four weeks of the 2026 season, it will be interesting to see which players they bring in. Given Milton’s athletic ability and big arm, he fits HC Todd Monken’s traits for a quarterback. While Cleveland could choose to claim Milton and waive a player at another position, that seems unlikely. Instead, the addition of Milton would likely lead to the departure of either Shedeur Sanders or the rookie Green. With Milton’s experience and Green entering his first season, Sanders seems like the odd man out if the Browns were to claim Milton. Given Cleveland’s history, it is also possible the team keeps four quarterbacks or tries to sneak Green to the practice squad if they acquire Milton. If the Browns decide to pull the ripcord on the Sanders experience in favor of Milton, it is possible that GM Andrew Berry can find a trade partner who is looking for a quarterback to develop and likes Sanders’ upside. Whatever you think about Sanders’ talent, last year he lost a quarterback competition to the aged Joe Flacco and the undersized Gabriel. All three played poorly in 2025. Then, this year with a new coaching staff and added talent around him, Sanders lost a quarterback competition to Deshaun Watson , who hasn’t been good for half a decade and is coming off missing a year and a half of football. None of that screams that the Cleveland organization is high on Sanders. Claiming Milton could just be the final nail in Sanders’ time with the Browns. Do you think the Browns should claim Milton? If so, do you think they should waive Sanders, Green, or keep all 4 QBs on the 53-man active roster? Join the conversation! Mandatory Credit: Jacob Musselman-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Did you get the Cleveland Browns initial 53-man roster memorized? Welp, there is a reason we call it the “initial” roster over and over again because things change quickly. On Sunday, the Browns waived and released a number of players , including WR Luke Floriea . Less than 24 hours later, waiver claims were due at 1 PM, with Cleveland looking to make some upgrades at different spots on the roster, which could include one of the current quarterbacks being replaced by a claimed or signed player. Often, teams looking to build a roster that struggled the previous season will make the most moves, but the Browns claimed just one player: CB Toriano Pride Pride was selected in the seventh round of the 2026 NFL draft by the Buffalo Bills. The 5’10” cornerback spent two years at Clemson and two years at Missouri before being drafted. His draft profile by The NFL Network notes his traits: Pride did an admirable job of holding up outside against solid SEC competition but he’ll be under consideration as a slot corner in the pros. He plays with good zone awareness and average man-cover talent. He’s athletic with agile feet and is feisty at the catch-point, but he might not have the needed speed or length. Toughness is not an issue, but he will be dragged for additional yardage as a run-support tackler. Pride could go late on Day 3, but a lack of traits and explosiveness create an uphill fight for him. Pride did not play a game for the Bills in 2026. Floriea was not among the 29 players claimed on Monday and is now free to join any team and seems likely to sign with the Browns practice squad. The Miami Dolphins claimed seven of the 29 players on Monday. According to a report, Cleveland is releasing DE Julian Okwara to make room for Pride: The #Browns are releasing veteran edge Julian Okwara, source says. A move indicative of roster juggling. — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) August 31, 2026 The team has made those two moves official . Are you surprised the Browns only claimed one player? title: Browns QB room: Decisions around the 4 QBs are and will be complicated
summary: Heading into the NFL season, most teams will carry two quarterbacks on their 53-man roster, with a third on the practice squad who can be called up when needed. With a limited number of roster spots available, teams have to balance their needs across every position group. This is why it is such an interesting choice for the Cleveland Browns to […]
full_text: Heading into the NFL season, most teams will carry two quarterbacks on their 53-man roster , with a third on the practice squad who can be called up when needed. With a limited number of roster spots available, teams have to balance their needs across every position group. This is why it is such an interesting choice for the Cleveland Browns to choose to keep four quarterbacks in their orbit. Dillon Gabriel was put on the IR with a back injury , while Deshaun Watson , Shedeur Sanders , and Taylen Green have all made the initial 53-man roster. It will be difficult to justify keeping four quarterbacks when Gabriel is healthy, when another roster spot could be better used on a player who fills a greater need. Gabriel and Green both proved their value in the final preseason game against the New England Patriots, so the team clearly views them as important assets. With a lot of questions around the play of both Watson and Sanders, it makes sense to keep other options on the roster that you trust. Additionally, the decisions made on the initial 53-man roster aren’t final. If a need arises at another position, the team has the flexibility to adjust its roster and address it accordingly. The fact that Gabriel is on Injured Reserve and doesn’t occupy an active roster spot also made the decision easier. Many felt as though a roster spot could be better used on someone like wide receiver Luke Floriea , who was very impressive during this year’s pre-season. The team likely feels confident it can bring him back to the practice squad and keep him in the organization in some capacity. With Gabriel on IR, the Browns have four game weeks to decide what they will do with their four quarterbacks. title: Browns roster comparison: 2026 initial 53-man roster versus the 2025 version
summary: The more things change, the more they stay the same… that has been true for the Cleveland Browns for quite a few seasons, but not anymore. Now, every year since GM Andrew Berry took over the team in 2020, the Browns roster has seen some changes here and there, but the massive overhaul that started […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NV - SEPTEMBER 29: Defensive end Myles Garrett #95 of the Cleveland Browns, long snapper Charley Hughlett #47, center Ethan Pocic #55, guard Joel Bitonio #75, cornerback Denzel Ward #21, and quarterback Deshaun Watson #4 stand on the sidelines prior to an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders, at Allegiant Stadium on September 29, 2024 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The more things change, the more they stay the same… that has been true for the Cleveland Browns for quite a few seasons, but not anymore. Now, every year since GM Andrew Berry took over the team in 2020, the Browns roster has seen some changes here and there , but the massive overhaul that started in 2025 has taken another step ahead in 2026. So what happens when you compare the newly unveiled 2026 initial 53-man roster in Cleveland to the one the Browns started the 2025 season with? First, it is important to note that we already know how last year’s roster turned out. We are not comparing that roster on the day it was set to Sunday when this year’s roster was put in place. That doesn’t mean we can’t try the exercise anyway. It’ll be quite simple: a list of names from each year, and where it seems to be improved or diminished in talent compared to last year. Quarterback 2025: Joe Flacco, Dillon Gabriel, Shedeur Sanders 2026: Taylen Green, Shedeur Sanders, Deshaun Watson Verdict: Very, very uncertain. Flacco was terrible last year, as were the other two. Maybe a small improvement due to Green’s athletic ability? Running back 2025: Jerome Ford, Dylan Sampson 2026: Michael Burton (FB), Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson, Raheim Sanders Verdict: Much improved. Obviously, things changed quickly in the RB room last year but this exercise is based on initial rosters. Wide receivers 2025: Jerry Jeudy, Cedric Tillman, Jamari Thrash, Gage Larvadain, Isaiah Bond, DeAndre Carter 2026: Isaiah Bond, Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion Jr., Malachi Corley, Jerry Jeudy, Tylan Wallace Verdict: Much improved. Next Tight ends 2025: David Njoku, Harold Fannin, Blake Whiteheart, Brenden Bates 2026: Harold Fannin Jr., Carsen Ryan, Blake Whiteheart Verdict: Diminished. Fannin was the top tight end last year, but Njoku was still a good blocker and had moments where he could make an impact in the passing game. Offensive line 2025: Jack Conklin, Dawand Jones, Cornelius Lucas, KT Leveston, Joel Bitonio, Wyatt Teller Teven Jenkins, Zak Zinter, Ethan Pocic, Luke Wypler 2026: Austin Barber, Parker Brailsford, Spencer Fano, Tytus Howard, Elgton Jenkins, Teven Jenkins, Zion Johnson, Dawand Jones, Luke Wypler, Zak Zinter Verdict: Has to be improved, right?! The starters will either all be new or four out of the five of them, from a line that was putrid last year, besides the now-retired Bitonio. Defensive line 2025: Myles Garrett, Alex Wright, Isaiah McGuire, Joe Tryon-Shoyinka, Cameron Thomas, Mason Graham, Maliek Collins, Mike Hall Jr, Shelby Harris, Adin Huntington 2026: Derek Barnett, Maliek Collins, Kalia Davis, Mason Graham, Mike Hall Jr., Adin Huntington, Isaiah McGuire, Julian Okwara, Jared Verse Verdict: Diminished. One of the easiest calls, sadly, in the roster comparisons. Cleveland is hoping that Verse plus some development from the young guys can offset Garrett’s departure and Wright’s injury. A lot to hope for. Linebacker 2025: Carson Schwesinger, Devin Bush, Mohamoud Diabate, Jerome Baker, Easton Mascarenas-Arnold 2026: Justin Jefferson, Easton Mascarenas-Arnold, Winston Reid, Carson Schwesinger, Quincy Williams Verdict: Some improvement. Williams can replace Bush, and Schwesinger should grow off his Rookie of the Year season. Defensive backs 2025: Denzel Ward, Greg Newsome II, Myles Harden, Cameron Mitchell, Dom Jones, Grant Delpit, Ronnie Hickman, Rayshawn Jenkins, Damontae Kazee, Donovan McMillon 2026: Mekhi Blackmon, Tyson Campbell, Michael Coats Jr., Grant Delpit, Myles Harden, Ronnie Hickman, Donovan McMillon, Emmanuel McNeil-Warren, Daniel Thomas, Denzel Ward Verdict: Slight improvement. The loss of some veteran depth at safety is offset by Campbell for Newsome, some development from the young guys, and the upside of EMW. Special Teams No changes Tabulating up the results: Improved : 5 (RB, WR, OL, LB, DB) Diminished : 2 (TE, DL) Too close to call: 2 (QB, ST) What say you? (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys set their initial 53-man roster on Sunday afternoon and it will undergo a few changes before things are fully finalized and ready for them to begin their Week 1 preparation. While the Cowboys have a final (ongoing) 53-man roster, they also have to put together a practice squad. Some FAQ topics answered regarding an NFL practice squad: NFL teams are allowed to have 16 players and can carry a 17th if the extra is from the league’s International Pathway Program. A maximum of six players on the squad can have NFL experience. Each Tuesday of the season the league can “protect” four of them so that they cannot be poached. Every week the Cowboys (or any NFL team) can promote two players from the squad to their active roster but only three times maximum. Beyond that the player must be a member of the active roster. This post from Hogs Haven covers some of the NFL’s practice squad details more in depth if you are curious. Check out all the NFL odds from our partner FanDuel . They have the Cowboys at +2000 for the Super Bowl, behind 12 other teams. 2026 Dallas Cowboys Practice Squad The Cowboys are bringing back DE Dayo Odeleye, an international player, to the practice squad.
