title: Cowboys news: New addition at RB, possible new starter at RT
summary: The Dallas Cowboys made a surprise roster move at QB on Monday by cutting backup Joe Milton, taking the risk he’ll be able to return to the practice squad. That move corresponded with the team also answering for their initial roster cutdown surprise of only keeping two running backs, adding a third with Emari Demercado. […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys made a surprise roster move at QB on Monday by cutting backup Joe Milton, taking the risk he’ll be able to return to the practice squad. That move corresponded with the team also answering for their initial roster cutdown surprise of only keeping two running backs, adding a third with Emari Demercado. While neither move shakes up the fact the Cowboys are still in position to have the same starting 11 on offense going into week one, their trade over the weekend for Broderick Jones could, as the former Steelers right tackle will reportedly compete with Terence Steele for that starting job. Dallas Cowboys release QB Joe Milton – RJ Ochoa, Blogging The Boys Joe Milton provided an exciting preseason starting all three games, but still will be subject to waivers if he wants to be the primary backup in Dallas to Dak Prescott. Again, Milton played extremely well over the course of the preseason. He led the NFC in third-down passing across the exhibition period at large. This isn’t anything to really write home about given that it was the preseason, but you get the point that Milton played well in the opportunities that he had. Milton obviously made the Cowboys’ initial 53-man roster when it was released on Sunday, and it isn’t uncommon for players who do so to be cut after the fact. Maybe the Cowboys feel like he can clear waivers and specifically chose to execute this move now so that other teams already got their claims in and finalized things. Cowboys add a familiar face for OC Klayton Adams only one day after setting initial 53-man roster – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports The Cowboys found more big-play potential at RB with a familiar face to OC Klayton Adams by signing Emari Demercado on Monday. Demercado, 27, played for the Arizona Cardinals from 2023 to 2025, coinciding with Cowboys OC Klayton Adams for a couple of seasons. Back then, Adams coached the Cardinals offensive line and was known for being a part of a creative run game. That includes Demercado’s most recent rushing touchdown, which happened in a 53-yard play in 2024. Schottenheimer explains Jaydon Blue, RB decisions for Cowboys roster – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys really, really, really like Malik Davis as the incumbent RB2 as well. “I think this is more a testament to a guy like Malik Davis that has just, time in and time out, come back and proven his worth. And the way he’s wired, I know both Jaydon and Phil should and will reach out to Malik, because now they’re unfortunately in a situation like [what Davis has experienced several times in the past]. “But, if you want to learn from a veteran, Malik Davis would be the first call that I would make. The guy went from being on the street, not getting really hardly any looks, even workouts, and he’s back in Oxnard, and now he’s solidified himself as a very, very valuable member of our football team.” Of course this happened. Former Cowboys RB Jaydon Blue, released Sunday, is signing with the Eagles practice squad, per source. pic.twitter.com/iHn4yHDBNS — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 31, 2026 Broderick Jones will compete for the Cowboys’ right tackle job – Josh Alper, Pro Football Talk The Cowboys have been very serious about creating competition for both of their starting tackles this offseason, with their new addition Broderick Jones looking to push Terence Steele on the right side. Jones played both left and right tackle during his time with the Steelers, but Schottenheimer said he will be playing on the right side in Dallas. Schottenheimer said he called Terence Steele to tell him about the impending competition after the Cowboys finalized the trade for Jones. “As you can imagine , Terrence Steele was the ultimate pro,” Schottenheimer said, via the team’s website. Why Broderick Jones Could Work for the 26′ Cowboys? – Cody Warren, Inside The Star Jones comes with experience at both left and right tackle, and the Cowboys will be hoping their coaching makes a difference for a former Steelers draft pick for the second year in a row. The Dallas Cowboys have two offensive line gurus in Klayton Adams and Conor Riley . Adams, in particular, has already worked with another young, athletic first-round tackle from the 2023 draft. Paris Johnson Jr. played right tackle as a rookie in Arizona before being moved to left tackle. His PFF grade jumped from 60.1 in his first year to 80.8 in year 2. I don’t know if Broderick Jones can make that kind of jump, but we have the coaches to help. Cowboys’ injured OLB, rookie CB to miss at least first 4 games of regular season – Todd Brock, The Cowboys Wire Devin Moore and Marist Liufau were both bubble players to make the roster anyway, but due to their injuries the Cowboys are able to stash them for now. The Cowboys placed both players on injured return with “Designated to Return” status as part of Sunday’s cutdown. The move allowed Dallas to fill their spots on the initial 53-man roster yet gives both players an easy path back once they recover from their injuries. They are required to sit out, though, a minimum of four games. And when they are ready to come back, the club will have to make room on the roster by cutting or moving two other players. Daily discussion question: What do you make of the Cowboys’ running back room?

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 13
summary: It is Day 13 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: IRVING, TEXAS - JANUARY 2, 1972: Quarterback Roger Staubach #12 of the Dallas Cowboys pitches the ball to a teammate during the NFC Championship Game against the San Francisco 49ers on January 2, 1972 at Texas Stadium in Irving, Texas. The Cowboys defeated the 49ers 14-3, and went on to win Super Bowl VI. (Photo by James Drake/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Day 13 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. It’s lucky number 13 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit the conference championship victory that put Dallas one win away from finally becoming Super Bowl champions. In a bruising defensive battle, the Cowboys allowed only three points, intercepted John Brodie three times and defeated the San Francisco 49ers to capture their second consecutive NFC title. Sunday, January 2, 1972 — 1:30 p.m. ET Texas Stadium, Irving, Texas Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 14, San Francisco 49ers 3 Dallas, having finished the regular season with an impressive 11-3 record, secured a spot in the championship game by defeating Minnesota 20-12 on Christmas Day. San Francisco, on the other hand, completed a 9-5 season and eliminated Washington 24-20. This highly anticipated rematch marked the rematch of the previous season’s NFC Championship Game, where Dallas had emerged victorious 17-10, propelling them to their first Super Bowl appearance. Dallas finally broke through because of its defense. Veteran defensive end George Andrie intercepted a Brodie screen pass and returned it seven yards to the San Francisco two-yard line. Calvin Hill scored from one yard out shortly afterward, and Mike Clark’s extra point gave the Cowboys a 7-0 lead. That remained the only score through halftime. San Francisco finally responded during the third quarter when Brodie completed a 24-yard pass to Ted Kwalick, helping set up Bruce Gossett’s 28-yard field goal. The 49ers had reduced the margin to 7-3 and later had another opportunity, but Gossett missed from 47 yards. Dallas responded with the game’s defining offensive possession. Roger Staubach completed a 17-yard pass to Dan Reeves late in the third quarter and then connected with Billy Truax for 23 yards early in the fourth. The Cowboys methodically travelled 80 yards in 14 plays, with Duane Thomas finishing the drive on a two-yard touchdown run to make it 14-3. From there, the Doomsday Defense slammed the door. Chuck Howley broke up a fourth-down pass to end one San Francisco possession before Lee Roy Jordan intercepted Brodie on the next. Even when the 49ers blocked a Clark field-goal attempt and received one final opportunity, Cliff Harris intercepted Brodie and allowed Dallas to run out the clock. This was not a game won through spectacular passing numbers. Dallas instead relied on patience and its running game. Staubach himself led the Cowboys with 55 rushing yards, Walt Garrison added 52 and Thomas contributed 44 as Dallas accumulated 172 yards on the ground. The defense was even more impressive. San Francisco was held to only 61 rushing yards and nine first downs, while Brodie was intercepted three times. The 49ers never reached the end zone and managed only Gossett’s third-quarter field goal. This game belongs on the countdown because it was the final hurdle before Dallas changed its reputation forever. The Cowboys had already reached one Super Bowl and lost narrowly to Baltimore, adding to years of criticism that Landry’s teams could not finish championship runs. Beating San Francisco gave Dallas another opportunity, and this time there would be no disappointment. #Cowboys vs #49ers 1971 NFC Championship Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 14, San Francisco 49ers 3 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/lO9IEMQLel — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 31, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game This was the first NFL playoff game at Texas Stadium. title: Dallas Cowboys net results from Pickens, Jones trades with Steelers
summary: The Dallas Cowboys and Pittsburgh Steelers seem quite comfortable with one another. On Saturday evening the teams made a trade which marked a second straight year and season where this was the case. If Broderick Jones has even 10% of the impact on the Cowboys that the former Steeler George Pickens did, then things are […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 10: George Pickens #14 and Broderick Jones #77 of the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrate after Pickens' receiving touchdown in the first quarter of a game against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on November 10, 2024 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys and Pittsburgh Steelers seem quite comfortable with one another. On Saturday evening the teams made a trade which marked a second straight year and season where this was the case. If Broderick Jones has even 10% of the impact on the Cowboys that the former Steeler George Pickens did, then things are going to work out rather nicely. Let me say right now that what we are doing is not meant to be taken in a literal or supremely serious way. Sometimes coincidences happen and therefore things can be looked at through unique prisms and that is what we are about to do here today. Net results from the Pickens and Jones trades Obviously the Cowboys and Steelers did not agree to one composite trade included George Pickens and Broderick Jones; however, the two trades are interestingly tied together by a particular detail in a way that multiple trades between two teams usually are not. With the Broderick trade now completed here are the net results on each side. Cowboys received: George Pickens (Trade 1) Broderick Jones (Trade 2) 2027 4th (Trade 2) Steelers received: 2026 3rd (Trade 1) 2027 3rd (Trade 2) 2027 5th (Trade 1) There is one final thing that each team received, but as noted the interesting thing is that they each received it. During Trade 1 (the Pickens deal) the Steelers sent their 2027 sixth-round pick to the Cowboys. It was a swap as they received Dallas’ 2027 fifth. Trade 2 (the Broderick deal) saw Dallas send that exact same pick back to where it originally started. Again, not every set of trades between teams involves a take-back like that. Once again, this is simply a fun way to look at these two trades because they involved the same two teams. The George Pickens factor makes it hard for the Cowboys to not be viewed as the winners, but obviously that was not a detail that was associated with the most recent deal.

title: 7 surprise cuts from Cowboys 53-man roster
summary: The 2026 Dallas Cowboys are one step closer to being gameday ready, with their roster being trimmed down to 53 players at Sunday’s deadline. We kept track of it all right here, and will continue to do so as there is still potential for shakeups, and building the practice squad remains a work in progress. […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - JANUARY 04: Jaydon Blue #23 of the Dallas Cowboys celebrates a first quarter touchdown against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on January 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 Dallas Cowboys are one step closer to being gameday ready, with their roster being trimmed down to 53 players at Sunday’s deadline . We kept track of it all right here , and will continue to do so as there is still potential for shakeups, and building the practice squad remains a work in progress. It’s been several months on end now when Cowboys fans have been chattering about how different the player acquisition phase of this offseason felt, and roster cuts helped keep this theme going in a lot of ways. A large percentage of the Cowboys cuts came and went without much surprise at all, as Dallas did considerably more work in the offseason to bring in established players worthy of roster spots from the jump. This is especially true for a defense moving on from being one of the worst in franchise history just one season ago, with the only path forward being wiping out as much of the personnel responsible and starting fresh. This blew up, so let me clarify: 17 of the 26 players on the initial 53-man roster last year are not on 53-man rosters right now. 15 are unemployed, 2 are starting the season on PUP (Parsons, Liufau). https://t.co/w3KIm8YIE3 — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 31, 2026 We still have a list of seven surprising cuts below, and they favor Christian Parker’s new-look defense with four names on the list. On offense, the headline that all 11 starters return from 2025 became locked in on Sunday, but the position with the most room for change brought plenty of surprises at cut day, with Dallas going shorter than expected on the final roster at running back. Let’s get into the list. CB Reddy Steward Starting off with a mild surprise, Reddy Steward had a chance to be a rare carryover from that 2025 defense, but ultimately did not make the depth chart at cornerback. What most likely worked against Steward’s chances was the fact his best position is the nickel, where the Cowboys are expected to utilize first-round pick Caleb Downs plenty. There has been some concern about using Downs as just a matchup player in the slot and not using his versatility in the best way possible, but the Cowboys answered for this by also keeping Cobie Durant and Ameer Speed as capable players in this role. Speed came on strong as a special teams player and ultimately this was enough to beat out a player like Steward. Steward also did not have the draft pedigree of a player like Caelen Carson, who similarly had struggles throughout the preseason, but becomes a carryover player Dallas isn’t quite ready to give up on yet under new coaching as he also beat out Steward for a spot. RBs Phil Mafah, Jaydon Blue, Israel Abanikanda The Cowboys cuts at running back came one after another, after another, which is at least one more than anticipated for many fans. With Javonte Williams locked in as the starter, Jaydon Blue, Phil Mafah, Malik Davis, and Israel Abanikanda battled it out for the RB2 role, which Davis ultimately won – apparently in strong enough fashion to push the rest of his competition off the roster entirely. The Cowboys now have a pair of similar backs that are at their best pounding the rock between the tackles, passing on the chance to have more of a dynamic duo by pairing Williams with Blue. All three of these cuts will be candidates to watch for potential signings to the practice squad , where Dallas can still call on them come gamedays. After a balanced share out of the backfield in the preseason opener at the Seahawks, the Cowboys leaned on Blue to get them through the Cardinals game, and then saw Mafah lead them in carries against the Saints – a preseason finale that came and went without feeling like it had much impact on final roster decisions, especially on offense. Knowing how much this team prefers to keep the players they plan on using in the regular season on ice during exhibition season, the tea leaves here pointed to Davis earning the RB2 role. Opting to not have either Blue or Mafah as a RB3 with potential depending on the game plan to rise to RB2 any given week is still a surprise. Another thing the Cowboys showed against the Saints, and Cardinals the week before, is a desire to get in on the trend of multiple tight end usage this season. This offense may still trend towards the middle or bottom of heavy TE personnel usage due to having three receivers that demand to see the field a lot, but when they do, Williams and Davis are the best “no nonsense” backs to keep for these looks. Still, with the Cowboys having only Williams, Davis, and fullback Hunter Luepke on the roster out of the backfield, keep a close eye on how efficient they are in the short passing game as extensions of the run to make or break if moving on from a pair of second-year draft picks was the right decision. LB Sam Williams Back to another mild, or perhaps medium surprise, Sam Williams did not make the final roster of edge rushers. Rashan Gary, Donovan Ezeiruaku, Von Miller, and rookie Malachi Lawrence were four obvious choices on the depth chart here, and the other two spots went to players that flashed more than Williams this preseason, James Houston and Tyrus Wheat. The Cowboys defense obviously has many goals for this season, but an early one to officially move on from last year’s disaster is simply to play as a cohesive unit where all 11 players are on the same page and playing together. Far too many times, both in his previous stint with the team and in this preseason, Williams played out of line with this goal and cost the team with reckless play, penalties, or poor technique. The splash play potential in between these mishaps from Williams always gave him some chance to still make the team, but Dallas opted for players with more consistent rush integrity in Wheat and Houston. How much this group gets home to sack opposing quarterbacks is of course something to watch, especially if the Cowboys offense does what they’re expected to and piles on points to force opponents to play from behind. In more neutral situations and close games against top competition though, the Cowboys outside linebackers must do a better job than they have so far in setting a hard edge and not getting outflanked on the perimeter. Wheat and Houston may not be the first players that will help the defense here, but they are more capable than Williams while also having the speed to finish sacks in obvious pass situations. The team made a clear statement about just how much they value all of these things by leaving Williams off the team going into week one. DTs Jay Toia, Tommy Dunn Sticking with the defense to conclude our list, Jay Toia and UDFA Tommy Dunn are a package deal to make for a roster surprise when it comes to depth on the interior. Both players did not help themselves nearly as much as they could have on Friday night at home against the Saints, but prior to that had strong performances earlier in the preseason. If for nothing else, both Toia and Dunn should be commended for eating up snaps at a position where the Cowboys arguably had the most density of talent riding the bench all preseason, with Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, and Otito Ogbonnia just waiting for the Giants game. Joining these three presumed starters on the roster are veteran Jonathan Bullard and rookie LT Overton. Where Toia was a true nose tackle with little pass rush upside, and Dunn was a bit more of a hybrid player with way more juice as a run stuffer, Bullard and Overton both have the right mix the Cowboys are apparently looking for of pass rush upside and anchoring ability at the point of attack. With this pass rush potential from Bullard and Overton though comes concerns about how well Dallas can defend the inside run when the big…

title: Over half of last year’s Cowboys defenders are off the roster
summary: Roster cuts can be brutal, and it looks like they are especially brutal for players who played on the NFL’s worst defense last year. Nick Harris of the Star-Telegram did a quick check on the Cowboys defense, and found that 17 of the 26 defenders on the 2025 Week 1 roster are unemployed after yesterday’s […]
full_text: Roster cuts can be brutal, and it looks like they are especially brutal for players who played on the NFL’s worst defense last year. Nick Harris of the Star-Telegram did a quick check on the Cowboys defense, and found that 17 of the 26 defenders on the 2025 Week 1 roster are unemployed after yesterday’s final roster cuts. This blew up, so let me clarify: 17 of the 26 players on the initial 53-man roster last year are not on 53-man rosters right now. 15 are unemployed, 2 are starting the season on PUP (Parsons, Liufau). https://t.co/w3KIm8YIE3 — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) August 31, 2026 Harris corrected the number to 15, explaining that two of those 17 players were actually on IR. Here’s a look at the 2025 Week 1 roster for the defense, with the red cells indicating players that do not have a job right now, and the yellow cells marking players on IR: body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 0px 6px !important; } 2025 Week 1 roster – Base 4-3 D POS Starter 2nd 3rd LDE Sam Williams Donovan Ezeiruaku NT Kenny Clark Mazi Smith Jay Toia DT Osa Odighizuwa Solomon Thomas Perrion Winfrey RDE Dante Fowler Marshawn Kneeland (RIP) James Houston WLB Jack Sanborn Shemar James MLB Kenneth Murray Marist Liufau (IR) SLB Damone Clark (IR) Buddy Johnson SS Malik Hooker Markquese Bell FS Donovan Wilson Juanyeh Thomas RCB Kaiir Elam C.J. Godwin (retired) Trikweze Bridges LCB DaRon Bland Trevon Diggs Reddy Steward IR/PUP DeMarvion Overshown, Shavon Revel Jr., Caelen Carson Of the 27 players on the opening-day roster against the Eagles in 2025, 15 are currently without a team, even if that may not last more than a few hours in some cases. Rosters in the NFL churn about 30% each year, so some degree of change can be expected from year-to-year, especially among backups and down-roster players. But five of last year’s starters are also without a team right now, which seems pretty high, but is probably indicative of the quality of those former starters. Jerry Jones opened the press conference following Day 2 of the draft by pointing out the changes made to the defense . “We have been able to, as of right now, rebuild this defense. I think the fact that we put a new newness to the system and coaching staff, and new faces that we’ve added, we’ve changed this defense.” Jones also pointed out that the changes made were not just a reaction to last year, but a “product of 3, 4, 5 years, maybe more, where we ultimately didn’t get to where we were trying to go and be a contender.” If you look closely at the table above, you’ll also notice that the 2026 Cowboys are only returning seven defensive players from last year’s week one roster (plus Marist Liufau on IR). Eight out of 27. That’s a roster churn of 70%. A change of this magnitude is not just unusual, it’s unprecedented for a team like the Cowboys that likes to keep things comfortable and is generally averse to change. But judging by how last year’s players fared with other teams around the league, those changes were absolutely necessary.

Here are our 10 thoughts on the team’s initial roster. 1. Camden survives Fans were on pins and needles about whether the team would carry six wide receivers, with one being undrafted free agent and camp sensation, Camden Brown. Well, we got our answer. Brown started turning heads in camp with amazing catches, and he continued such in the preseason. His quick acceleration and elite contested-catch ability were too good to leave off the roster. 2. Three’s company Whether it was their intentions all along, or the final preseason game sealed the deal, the Cowboys are keeping three quarterbacks. This gives them some flexibility between Joe Milton III and Sam Howell, as one offers some nice upside while the other provides a safe floor. Hopefully, we’ll never find out which the team prefers, but at least they’ll have options if that time comes. 3. Short at RB It seemed as if we knew what was going on at running back based on who played (or didn’t play) in the final preseason game, but the team pulled a fast one on us by releasing their fast one. Jaydon Blue, the team’s fifth-round pick last year, was a surprise release. He’s looked better this year, but the coaches don’t feel comfortable keeping him. With all the backups not named Malik Davis released, the team hopes they can get a couple of them back on the practice squad. 4. Tackle trades The offensive tackle position saw a huge shakeup over the last 24 hours with two trades. On Saturday, the Cowboys traded with the Pittsburgh Steelers to acquire former first-round pick Broderick Jones . The move signaled the end for third-year tackle Nate Thomas, but the team at least got something in return by trading him to the Houston Texans on Sunday. They worked the phones to get a swing tackle upgrade. Fingers crossed it works out. 5. Familiar approach Not only did the Cowboys bring in a new guy they like and trade away a third-year player they have given up on at the last second, but they also kept a developmental guy who clearly wasn’t ready. Fourth-round rookie Drew Shelton survived roster cuts, giving the team more time to work with him. This approach looks very familiar to last year, but they pulled off something similar. 2025 – Outside acquisition (Hakeem Adeniji), develop a rookie (Ajani Cornelius), and trade (Asim Richards) 2026 – Outside acquisition (Broderick Jones), develop a rookie (Drew Shelton), and trade (Nate Thomas) Enter the Biff’s “There’s something very familiar about this” meme. 6. Light in the interior The interior offensive line took a bigger hit than expected. While we were waiting to see who survived between Nick Leverett and Trevor Keegan, the team surprised people by not choosing either of them. They still have T.J. Bass and last year’s development tackle-turned-guard, Cornelius, but they still seem a bit light. The good news is that at least one (if not both) of Leverett and Keegan should make it through waivers to the practice squad. Or the Cowboys may opt to claim an interior lineman who’s been released? 7. Hard work rewarded Both Tyrus Wheat and Alijah Clark have made the roster before, so it shouldn’t be a complete shocker, but many felt their chances were slim because they were stuck in crowded position groups. The Von Miller signing created little room at outside linebacker, but Sam Williams’ release and Marist Liufau’s injury opened up just enough room for Wheat. Clark wasn’t given those same breaks, so he had to make his own luck and force the team to go long at safety. Both guys show relentless effort and are key contributors on special teams, which proves that we must not overlook these details when filling out the roster. Note – Liufau was placed on IR, designated to return. 8. No more room in the middle The Cowboys have completely remodeled their defensive tackle position as all five of the guys selected just completed their first training camp with the team. All of them. With four savvy veterans and one fourth-round rookie, this group looks stout, but it didn’t leave room for either Jay Toai or Tommy Dunn, both of whom flashed in preseason action. 9. The need for Speed Cornerback depth after the first three was a big question for the Cowboys. Caelen Carson made the cut despite being picked on some in preseason action, but the biggest surprise was hanging on to UFL’er Ameer Speed. He’s had a good camp and only allowed one reception across 77 defensive snaps this preseason. Rookie corner Devin Moore was placed on IR, designated to return. 10. Good use of a Day 3 pick Dee Winters made the team! Okay, that’s not a surprise to anyone, but it’s worth pointing out that the fifth-round pick the team traded to the San Francisco 49ers to get him did not. Tight end Justin Joly, taken 152nd overall, was released on Sunday. It’s a friendly reminder that Day 3 picks have low-chance returns, so anytime you can exchange that for a sure-thing contributor, it’s a good move.

title: Jonathon Cooper pleads not guilty at arraignment; has trial scheduled for November
summary: A few days ago, Denver Broncos edge rusher Jonathon Cooper was placed on the NFL commissioner’s exempt list. Per 9News insider Mike Klis, Cooper is expected to miss anywhere from two to six games to start the 2026 regular season. However, he could be subject to further discipline and suspension by the league pending the […]
full_text: Dec 21, 2025; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper (0) before the game at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A few days ago, Denver Broncos edge rusher Jonathon Cooper was placed on the NFL commissioner’s exempt list. Per 9News insider Mike Klis, Cooper is expected to miss anywhere from two to six games to start the 2026 regular season. However, he could be subject to further discipline and suspension by the league pending the outcome of his trial. Yesterday at his arraignment, Cooper plead not guilty to all [five] charges from domestic violence incidents back in June. The trial dates have been set from November 10th to November 13th—with a break on November 11th in observance of Veteran’s Day. The timing of the trial coincides with the Broncos’ Week 10 BYE. After Monday’s practice, Head Coach Sean Payton provided an update on the situation. “We wait on the league. In the meantime, the difference now is he’s in the facility, he’s lifting, he’s in the meetings. He can’t practice, and then we just wait for this process to play out,” stated Payton. In five years with the Broncos, Cooper has played in 81 games with 65 starts. To date, the former seventh-round pick has 266 tackles, 33 tackles for loss, 31.5 sacks, and 63 quarterback hits. With him being sidelined for the foreseeable future, the Broncos will turn to Jonah Elliss, Que Robinson, and Dondrea Tillman to keep their pass rush strong. Over the course of the offseason, the aforementioned trio has received praise from Payton, Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph, as well as General Manager George Paton. The past two seasons, the Broncos’ defense has led the NFL in sacks. In order to make that three in a row, Elliss, Robinson, and Tillman will have to put together the best seasons of their young NFL careers.

title: Horse Tracks: Countdown to MNF begins now
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Training camp is done, preseason is over, and cuts have been completed. The 2026 season is officially here. WooHoo! And that means the Broncos’ two-week countdown to their opening game against the Chiefs on Monday Night Football is officially on the clock. And no one in the locker room, even the […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 16: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs hugs Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos after the game at Empower Field At Mile High on November 16, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Training camp is done, preseason is over, and cuts have been completed. The 2026 season is officially here. WooHoo! And that means the Broncos’ two-week countdown to their opening game against the Chiefs on Monday Night Football is officially on the clock. And no one in the locker room, even the rookies, needs a refresher on what this game will mean. “We know we’re playing a really good football team, a divisional opponent, Monday Night Football ,“ said Sean Payton after the first practice with the official 2026 roster. ”It’s not like Andy [Reid] and I have to go in and give our teams a pep talk.“ But it is still just Week 1, and while the stakes are always high with a division opponent — especially one that had won the AFC Championship in five of seven appearances since 2018 until a 6-11 trainwreck season last year — keeping perspective on the season is important, Payton says. “You really focus on the process leading up to the game,” Payton said, noting the logistics of a Monday night game and an extra practice day that week. “With a Monday night game, I spend more time thinking about the schedule to make sure that we’re ramping up to play our best and it doesn’t get stale because we’re not playing on Sunday, if that makes any sense. But our players will know the significance of the first game, and I think it’s the process and the details.” Veteran offensive tackle Mike McGlinchey knows the significance as well as how important the next two weeks of prep will be. “It’s huge. I think every week is about getting better,” he said. “We’ve done that since we started training camp. This week is no exception. You don’t want to go into a game week next week off of a three-day off day and not feel like you accomplished something the week before or get better at your job.” With two weeks before kickoff, McGlinchey said this week allows the new team to hone in on some details before specifically game-planning for the Chiefs. “I think it’s an incredible opportunity we have for the next three days to go and compete against each other for a couple more times here, hone in on some of the small details, kind of the introductions to what we want to do in the gameplan against Kansas City and then hit the ground running,” he said. “You want to be your best on Week 1, but it’s more important to be your best in Week 18. Every single week, you have to be better than the week before. It’s not going to be perfect when we first go out and start, but it’s about continuing to improve on each rep and each game as the season unfolds.” Back to the grind 💪 pic.twitter.com/Z5BAr08bwt — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) August 31, 2026 Ultimate Fan is back for its 13th year! Get hyped and get ready to sign up for the greatest series on earth (not to be hyperbolic or anything!) This is fair warning that the sign-up post for the season-long series — where YOU, the ultimate fan, get to talk about the upcoming game in a Q&A format — is coming this Friday, so start thinking about which game you’d like to contribute your expert analysis. Not too early to think about Christmas…presents I know, it seems too early. It’s one day into September and the season hasn’t even started yet. So yeah, kinda too soon. But…if you have family members who like Bobbleheads, you’ll want to make sure you get them the Denver Broncos-themed bobblehead advent calendar to help count down the days until the Broncos host the Bills in Week 15 (which also happens to be Christmas Day). FOCO has released three officially licensed Broncos advent calendars for the 2026 holiday season, led by a $100 mascot bobblehead calendar featuring 12 unique, 2-inch Miles figures, with a different version of the Broncos’ mascot hidden behind each door. Two less expensive options include a $50 BRXLZ Christmas tree calendar and a $40 ornament-set calendar . Each offers 12 days of Broncos-themed surprises that can become part of the holiday fun.

title: Denver Broncos announce that they signed 17 players to their 2026 practice squad
summary: The Denver Broncos trimmed their roster from 91 players to 53 players yesterday and made a few surprising cuts. We saw rookie tight end Justin Joly and Red Murdock be waived, as well as running back Jaleel McLaughlin and others. Now, with all these players either passing through waivers or being claimed, they can sign […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL, CO - August 18 : Red Murdock (50) of Denver Broncos is in the training camp at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Tuesday, August 18, 2026. (Photo by Hyoung Chang/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Denver Broncos trimmed their roster from 91 players to 53 players yesterday and made a few surprising cuts . We saw rookie tight end Justin Joly and Red Murdock be waived, as well as running back Jaleel McLaughlin and others. Now, with all these players either passing through waivers or being claimed, they can sign to teams’ practice squads. We learned early on about a few vested veterans who signed to the Broncos’ practice squad prior to waivers, but now we have a complete list. We've signed 17 players to the practice squad. 📰 » https://t.co/O2VbeQfOj1 pic.twitter.com/XQnAKAAnds — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) August 31, 2026 So, with all that said, here are all the reported players signing to the Denver Broncos’ 17-man practice squad at the start of the 2026 NFL regular season. Denver Broncos practice squad players OLB David Agoha (International Pathway Program/17th man) FB Adam Prentice LS Mitchell Fraboni WR Michael Bandy TE Lucas Krull LS Luke Basso EDGE Johnny Walker OL Calvin Throckmorton OT Tyler Miller WR/KR Kolbe Katsis OL Gavin Ortega CB Brent Austin LB Red Murdock S Miles Scott WR Dane Key RB Cody Schrader CB/KR Sean Fresch Jr. The Broncos have signed 17 players to their practice squad, including edge rusher David Agoha, who will serve as their International Pathway Program player and their 17th man on their practice squad. The remaining 16 are all players who were on the Broncos’ 91-man roster this offseason, which continues their trend of not adding any outside players. OLB David Agoha He is a 6-4, 252-pound edge rusher from Nigeria who has spent time with the Las Vegas Raiders and Tennessee Titans. He joined the league in 2023 as an undrafted free agent and spent two seasons with the Raiders before spending time with the Titans last season. Now, he will join the Broncos’ practice squad and continue his development. FB Adam Prentice The veteran fullback was the star of the preseason with multiple touchdowns and first-down conversions on short-yardage plays. He will likely be elevated from the practice squad a maximum of three times before being added to the 53-man roster in Week 4. LS Mitchell Fraboni The veteran long snapper landed on the Broncos’ practice squad to give them some added roster flexibility. Like Prentice, he will be elevated from the practice squad a maximum of three times before potentially being added to the 53-man roster in Week 4. I say potentially because he’s not the only long snapper on the practice squad. WR Michael Bandy The now-veteran wide receiver has spent multiple seasons with the Broncos on their practice squad and lands here again. He clearly has the trust of the Broncos coaching staff and adds depth at the slot receiver position and as a punt returner in a pinch. TE Lucas Krull With rookie Justin Joly being waived and then claimed by the Miami Dolphins, veteran tight end Lucas Krull continues to stick around with the Broncos. He provides depth behind Evan Engram as a pass-catching threat at the tight end position. WR/KR Kolbe Katsis Katsis was one of my favorite undrafted free agents, and he flashed enough talent to stick around on the practice squad. He made some plays throughout camp as a wide receiver and flashed some real kick return potential throughout the preseason. He could be viewed as Marvin Mims’ backup in the return game. LS Luke Basso A second long snapper? I saw the reports yesterday and did not put much stock in them, but here we are. It’s unclear whether the Broncos will go with Fraboni for three games and then Basso for three games before having to make a decision, but time will tell. EDGE Johnny Walker With Jonathon Cooper on the exempt list and only four edge rushers on the 53-man roster, Johnny Walker appears to be the next man up if they need to add some depth at edge rusher. I don’t see him being elevated from the practice squad unless they have an injury at the position. OL Calvin Throckmorton A Sean Payton favorite is back again for another season. The veteran lineman can play all over the offensive line and added center to his list of positions he can play this offseason. He was the starting center for Bo Nix vs. the Packers and will provide some valuable depth on the practice squad. Per reports, he had options elsewhere but decided to stay in Denver with the Broncos. OT Tyler Miller The mammoth 6-9, 335-pound undrafted free agent offensive tackle is back! The Broncos like their tackles B I G, and they don’t get much bigger than Miller. He will likely be a pet project for the Broncos’ offensive line coaches, with the hopes of him making the 53-man roster at some point down the road. OL Gavin Ortega The undrafted free agent is normally a guard, but due to injuries, he played mostly center this summer, which likely helped him stick with the Broncos. He will provide added depth at guard and center while also giving them another young player they can develop with the hopes of earning a spot on the 53-man roster down the road. CB Brent Austin The Broncos have a GREAT track record with undrafted cornerbacks, and Brent Austin is the latest player to join the list. He had a good summer and flashed talent throughout the preseason and will likely replace Taylor Reeses’s role on the practice squad. LB Red Murdock The big one. Many were concerned that the 7th-round rookie would get claimed, but he made it through waivers and signed back to the Broncos’ practice squad. Former undrafted rookies Karene Reid and Jordan Turner will serve as the backups, but rookie Red Murdock will be the next man up if an injury occurs. S Miles Scott The Broncos ‘ 7th-round rookie was likely destined for the practice squad. He transitioned from wide receiver to safety in college and is viewed as an ascending player and will look to continue his development on the practice squad this season. WR Dane Key The younger brother of All-Pro special teams player Devon Key seemed to elevate himself up the depth chart throughout the preseason and was getting some second-team work in the preseason finale. He adds some depth to the wide receiver group that includes Michael Bandy and Kolbe Katsis. RB Cody Schrader The preseason finale star who topped 130 yards in total yards from scrimmage was among the Broncos’ final cuts yesterday, but lands back on their practice squad today. He gives them a tough runner between the tackles and a player who can contribute in the passing game. CB/KR Sean Fresch Jr. The former UFL star returner signed with the Broncos late in the offseason, but showed enough during training camp and the preseason to stick around on the depth chart. He will provide depth at kick and punt return along with WR Kolbe Katsis behind Marvin Mims.

title: Rookie TE Justin Joly and CB Reese Taylor were claimed off waivers by the Miami Dolphins
summary: Waiver claims are in, and the Broncos saw two players they waived yesterday claimed by the Miami Dolphins. As expected, 5th-round rookie tight end Justin Joly was claimed by the Dolphins, as was reserve slot corner Reese Taylor. The Broncos did not claim any players. Joly was a 5th-round pick by the Broncos this past […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - AUGUST 28: Justin Joly (80) of the Denver Broncos stands on the field during the third quarter against the Minnesota Vikings at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Friday, August 28, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Waiver claims are in, and the Broncos saw two players they waived yesterday claimed by the Miami Dolphins. As expected, 5th-round rookie tight end Justin Joly was claimed by the Dolphins, as was reserve slot corner Reese Taylor. The Broncos did not claim any players. Waiver claims! pic.twitter.com/wLbrIJL54j — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) August 31, 2026 Joly was a 5th-round pick by the Broncos this past April and was viewed as a potential pass-catching weapon for them this season and moving forward. However, it just never really worked out this summer. He struggled throughout camp, started a camp scuffle, and consistently played with the third-team offense in the preseason. His lone highlight play came in the finale when he caught a wide-open pass from QB Sam Ehlinger and scored an 88-yard touchdown. Broncos General Manager George Paton told reporters yesterday that Justin is a talented player, but they knew that he was raw. He missed much of the offseason, per Paton, and was behind the rest of the tight ends; the position is typically tough for rookies as is. Paton added that they think he’s going to have a nice career, but they have to make tough decisions to build the best 53-man roster they can. “Justin is a talented player. We knew it when we drafted him. We knew he was raw. We still like the player. He was coming on towards the end of training camp. Tight end position is a tough position for a rookie. He missed a lot of the offseason, just a little bit behind. We wish we had another game or two. We still like the player. We think he’s going to have a nice career. You just have to make tough decisions to build the best 53 you can make.” The team opted to go with 7th-round rookie Dallen Bentley instead on the 53-man roster, and now, Justin Joly is taking his talents to Miami with the Dolphins. As for Reese Taylor, the Broncos wanted to sign him back to their practice squad if he wasn’t claimed, but the Dolphins put in a waiver claim on him, and now he’s headed to Miami with Joly. The former undrafted free agent has served as slot depth for the Broncos since he joined the team back in 2023 and has bounced on and off the roster. He was behind Ja’Quan McMillian and Jahdae Barron on the roster, so his avenue to playing time was blocked. Taylor should find better opportunities for playing time with the Dolphins. With the Broncos becoming one of the league’s top teams, they anticipated that teams would claim some of their players. Paton told reporters that if any of their players get claimed, they will shake their hand, give them a hug, and root for them moving forward. “I think that’s part of it. I told a number of these guys—and I think I just mentioned it—if they get claimed, we’re going to shake their hand, we’re going to give them a hug and root for them. We root for these guys. It’s no different than losing a scout or losing an Assistant GM. You’re rooting for them. You want these guys to do well. These guys have put in a lot of work and dedication. We love these players, and we want them to do well. We hope they are here obviously, but if not here, we wish them the best. You never know what happens here down the road. We like this group. We like this group that is going to be on the waivers tonight. We would love to get a lot of them back, and we’ll just see how it goes. To answer your question, we just wish them well.” Losing players sucks, but it is part of the process when you’re one of the best teams in the league. The Broncos’ search for tight end help will continue with Joly moving on, and we’ll see if undrafted rookie Brent Austin, who is expected to sign to the Broncos’ practice squad, can fill Taylor’s role moving forward.

title: Red Murdock is signing back to the Broncos’ practice squad
summary: Yesterday, inside linebacker Red Murdock was one of the final players waived during the roster cutdown process before the deadline. It was a mild surprise considering how well he played in the preseason and how much Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph praised him throughout training camp. But no worries, Broncos Country. According to 9News insider Mike […]
full_text: Aug 14, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Keelan Marion (85) is tackled by Denver Broncos linebacker Red Murdock (50) in the second quater at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Yesterday, inside linebacker Red Murdock was one of the final players waived during the roster cutdown process before the deadline. It was a mild surprise considering how well he played in the preseason and how much Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph praised him throughout training camp. But no worries, Broncos Country. According to 9News insider Mike Klis, Murdock is back with the Denver Broncos signing a deal to be a part of the team’s 16-man practice squad. Broncos are signing back 7th-round rookie ILB Red Murdock to their practice squad, per source. — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) August 31, 2026 The final pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Mr. Irrelevant , Murdock had an impressive collegiate career at the University of Buffalo. Over four seasons, he played in 42 games with 31 starts. In that timeframe, he racked up an eye-popping 364 tackles, 39.5 tackles for loss, and 9 sacks. Additionally, he broke Khalil Mack’s NCAA forced fumble record with 17. While Murdock’s coverage skills need work, he has a nose for the football and is extremely good when going downhill. Several draft analysts, including The Athletic’s Dane Brugler, had him pegged with a late-fourth to early fifth-round grade. He plays with a lot of toughness and tenacity and it’s great to see the Broncos get him back on the practice squad for further development. Welcome back, Red Murdock!

title: Broncos GM George Paton on the decision to keep 3 QBs: ‘Sam is a big part of this quarterback room’
summary: One of the bigger questions heading into the roster cut deadline was whether or not the Broncos will keep three quarterbacks on their 53-man roster. Last season, they released Ehlinger, but despite reportedly having backup opportunities out there for him, the former Texas star quarterback agreed to sign on to the Broncos’ practice squad. But […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 28: Sam Ehlinger #4 of the Denver Broncos throws a pass during the second quarter against the Minnesota Vikings in a preseason game at Empower Field at Mile High on August 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the bigger questions heading into the roster cut deadline was whether or not the Broncos will keep three quarterbacks on their 53-man roster. Last season, they released Ehlinger, but despite reportedly having backup opportunities out there for him, the former Texas star quarterback agreed to sign on to the Broncos’ practice squad. But would they risk that again this year? The answer is no. Before the cut deadline, it was reported that the Broncos would keep three quarterbacks on their 53-man roster, which meant third-string QB Sam Ehlinger made the team. George Paton said Sam Ehlinger's third preseason game convinced them they needed to keep him. — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 30, 2026 After the preseason finale on Friday, I wrote that it is tough to figure out what from that game mattered and what didn’t. For instance, Justin Joly has an 88-yard touchdown and is later waived. The same goes for Jaleel McLaughlin, who scored a touchdown from QB Sam Ehlinger but was also cut. Well, Ehlinger’s performance mattered and convinced the Broncos to keep him on their 53-man roster. Broncos GM George Paton told reporters, “Sam obviously played great. If we were thinking anything there, that certainly confirmed keeping Sam”. He added that Ehlinger is “a big part of this quarterback room and they felt they would have lost him if they let him go this time around. “We love the quarterback room. We stated that a lot. [QB] Sam [Ehlinger], ‘Stiddy’ (QB Jarrett Stidham), we thought they both had really good offseasons, really good training camps and in the games. Sam is a big part of this quarterback room. We didn’t want to lose him, and we felt we were going to lose him. He’s too important to our team and just didn’t want to risk doing that. Obviously the game he played the other night was outstanding. We love the room. We’re going to keep the room together.” Since being signed to the team, the Broncos have been very vocal about what Ehlinger meant to this team on and off the field. Sure, he might just be a third-string quarterback who hopefully doesn’t play this season, but he’s important to the locker room and, specifically, that quarterback room. One example was this offseason, when Ehlinger and Nix planned an offseason throwing session in Austin, Texas (they love Ehlinger down there), and Broncos wide receiver Troy Franklin added that Ehlinger set up a boat trip for the players during their time there . The coaches love him, the players seem to love him, and he gives the Broncos talented quarterback depth. Does he stay on the 53-man roster all season? That remains to be seen, but in the short-term, he’s on the 53-man roster and the Broncos love their quarterback room.

title: Jonah Elliss and Que Robinson will step into big roles on the Broncos’ defense
summary: It was announced on Sunday that starting outside linebacker/edge rusher Jonathon Cooper would be placed on the Commissioner’s Exempt List and be sidelined for the foreseeable future. As we know, he is dealing with a serious legal matter off the field, and this was simply part of the process. General Manager George Paton told reporters […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - JANUARY 25: Jonah Elliss #52 and Que Robinson #51 of the Denver Broncos celebrate during the first quarter of the AFC Championship game against the New England Patriots at Empower Field At Mile High on January 25, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was announced on Sunday that starting outside linebacker/edge rusher Jonathon Cooper would be placed on the Commissioner’s Exempt List and be sidelined for the foreseeable future. As we know, he is dealing with a serious legal matter off the field, and this was simply part of the process. General Manager George Paton told reporters that they continue to take this matter very seriously and will monitor all legal developments and support Cooper. He added that Cooper has worked very hard to better himself, and he believes it will be good to have him inside the building and simply be part of the team. Yes, in regards to [OLB] Jonathon [Cooper] being placed on the Commissioner’s Exempt list, it’s part of the process. We continue to take this very seriously. We’re going to monitor all the legal developments and continue to support Jonathon. Jonathon’s worked very hard to better himself, and it’ll be good to have him in the building, be in meetings and just be a part of the team”. However, while Cooper is sidelined, the Broncos are going to need to replace him on the field. He was a key starter in their league-leading pass rush unit and will need to be replaced if they want to be the league’s best pass rush unit again this season. Thankfully, the Broncos are deep at edge rusher and have two young and talented players ready to step up. George Paton on the OLB room without Jonathon Cooper: "These guys have all played in games. Big games" "All these guys can play" Gave a shoutout to Que Robinson and how he came on late down the stretch last year "We feel really good about him" — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 30, 2026 Third-year edge rusher Jonah Elliss is expected to replace Jonathon Cooper in the Broncos’ starting lineup. He has flashed real talent during his first two years with the team and now will have an opportunity to shine as a starter. However, don’t sleep on second-year edge rusher Que Robinson. He looked like a future starter last season, according to Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph, and has all the tools to be a 10+ sack guy for the Broncos defense this upcoming season. GM George Paton told reporters that “all these guys can play” and singled out Que Robinson as someone they feel really good about moving forward. He added they like their depth, but will be looking around because “You can never have enough pass rushers.” “These guys have all played in big games and done well. All these guys we feel like can play. We like the depth there. We led the league in sacks the last two years, and these guys were all a part of that. [OLB] Que [Robinson] coming on late. I think you saw what Que did in the New England game late in the season, even the Houston game last year and some of the things he did. Then you watched him in training camp and the games this year. We feel really good about him. Then [OLB] Jonah [Elliss] and obviously ‘Tilly’ (OLB Dondrea Tillman) and [OLB] Nik [Bonitto], these guys have played and have done well. Depth-wise, we’ll be looking a little bit, looking on the practice squad and we’ll be looking around. You can never have enough pass rushers, so we’ll kind of see how that goes.” Jonah Elliss was a standout player throughout camp, but so was Que Robinson. Both have pass rush potential and should see significant snaps moving forward. I am personally a big Que Robinson fan and believe he is a big-time breakout candidate. He looks like a legit pass rusher off the edge. He has the size, length, athleticism, bend, and explosive first step you look for, and he could thrive opposite Nik Bonitto. He was making plays throughout the preseason, and I believe that will continue into the season. Simply, the Broncos will need these two players to step up and play well quickly. Their schedule on paper looks tough, starting the year with an opening-week road game in primetime at Arrowhead, a home game vs. the Jaguars (the only team that truly beat the Broncos last season), and games vs. the Rams, 49ers, Chargers, and the reigning champions, the Seattle Seahawks. They cannot afford their pass rush to take a step back early on, so Elliss and Robinson will really need to step up for the Broncos. I think they will, and the team seems confident that they will. Offenses will be focusing on All-Pro’s Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen while players like Malcolm Roach and Eyni Uwazurike also get after the passer. So, both Elliss and Robinson should have opportunities to thrive in Vance Joseph’s defense this season.

title: Broncos GM George Paton explains their decision to go with Tyler Badie over Jaleel McLaughlin
summary: One of the Broncos’ more noteworthy roster cuts on Sunday was running back Jaleel McLaughlin. The former undrafted free agent made the team as a rookie after a standout performance during the preseason and became a key member of the Broncos’ offense for a period of time. Despite being undersized, McLaughlin ran well between the […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 28: Tyler Badie #28 of the Denver Broncos runs with the football during the first quarter against the Minnesota Vikings in a preseason game at Empower Field at Mile High on August 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the Broncos’ more noteworthy roster cuts on Sunday was running back Jaleel McLaughlin. The former undrafted free agent made the team as a rookie after a standout performance during the preseason and became a key member of the Broncos’ offense for a period of time. Despite being undersized, McLaughlin ran well between the tackles and had some big plays for the team. However, the tide started to turn last season when McLaughlin was inactive for several games prior to the injury to veteran running back JK Dobbins. He did see some late-season action, but struggled to really get anything going on the ground. Jaleel would re-sign on a one-year deal with the Broncos this offseason, but the selection of standout rookie Jonah Coleman in the draft really put his roster spot in danger. Ultimately, McLaughlin played behind Coleman throughout the summer, and the writing appeared to be on the wall when McLaughlin played well into the fourth quarter of the preseason finale. Still, this was a tough cut for the Broncos. McLaughlin was a favorite in that locker room, and General Manager George Paton called McLaughlin the “toughest cut” they had to make at the roster deadline this year. Broncos GM George Paton noted that Jaleel McLaughlin was the "toughest" cut this year at the roster deadline, with Tyler Badie nabbing the RB4 spot. "Yeah, I mean that was really tough. Really all three of those runners, you know, they're all really good runners. They're all… pic.twitter.com/4J64EpsEwI — Andrew Mason (@MaseDenver) August 31, 2026 When asked what went into the decision to keep Tyler Badie over Jaleel McLaughlin, Paton said it was tough, but special teams and third-down ability played into it. “Yes, that was really tough. Really, all three of those runners, they’re all really good runners; they’re all different. A lot goes into it, obviously. [RB] Jaleel [McLaughlin], he’s something else. He was really important to this team- the passion, everything he brings. They have two different skill sets, without going into too much detail. So without getting into details, it was a really hard decision. Obviously, special teams are involved, third-down ability. There’s a lot involved, but that was probably the last decision we made, this fourth runner.” The special teams and third-down ability part is what ultimately mattered here. McLaughlin is a better running back than Tyler Badie; however, Badie offers a lot more as a pass blocker and on special teams. When you’re the RB4 on the roster, those are two things you need to excel at, and that is where Tyler Badie had the edge and is the same reason why he was active over McLaughlin last season. Heading into Week 1, the Broncos’ running back room looks pretty good on paper. Veteran JK Dobbins was among the league leaders in rushing prior to his injury, and if he can stay healthy, he will be a big part of this offense this season. Then you have the pass-catching specialist RJ Harvey, who has great speed and can pop off a big run at any moment and make some big plays in the passing game. He is coming off a 12-touchdown rookie year and will look to repeat that again this season. Then you have impressive rookie Jonah Coleman, who should factor into this backfield right away. He’s a powerful back with good short-area quickness who can pass block and catch passes out of the backfield. Coleman has the makings of a future impact starter. Finally, you have Badie, who could be inactive most weeks, but he offers some running and pass-catching ability and is mostly on the roster for his pass-blocking and special-teams ability. We shall see where Jaleel McLaughlin lands today. Will he be claimed, sign to the Broncos’ practice squad, or start fresh somewhere else and continue his NFL career?

title: Detroit Lions signing versatile offensive lineman to practice squad
summary: The Detroit Lions have made their first external addition since cutting their roster down to 53 players. According to Buccaneers beat writer Greg Auman, the Lions are signing former Tampa Bay offensive lineman Elijah Klein to their practice squad. Klein was drafted by the Buccaneers at the end of the sixth round of the 2024 […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - OCTOBER 20: Tampa Bay Buccaneers guard Elijah Klein (79) walks off of the field at the conclusion of the NFL football game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Detroit Lions on October 20, 2025 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Detroit Lions have made their first external addition since cutting their roster down to 53 players. According to Buccaneers beat writer Greg Auman, the Lions are signing former Tampa Bay offensive lineman Elijah Klein to their practice squad. Klein was drafted by the Buccaneers at the end of the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft—10 picks after the Lions selected starting left guard Christian Mahogany. Over the next two seasons, Klein would make 26 game appearances for Tampa, but just one single start. The Bucs tried Klein out at several different positions throughout his time in Tampa. In his rookie season, he split his preseason playing time at left guard, right guard, and right tackle. In 2025’s preseason, he logged snaps at left guard, right guard, and—primarily—center. This past preseason, he went back to left guard, right guard, and right tackle. His one NFL start came last season, when he played 72 snaps in a Week 3 contest against the New York Jets. While he graded out fantastically as a pass blocker (79.0 PFF grade), he struggled in the run game, earning just a 32.4 grade from PFF. His overall performance this preseason was highly dependent on his position. He earned a 74.2 grade at left guard in preseason Week 1, a 64.0 grade at right guard and right tackle in Week 2, and a 43.4 grade solely at right tackle in Week 3. In that preseason finale, he particularly struggled, allowing three pressures and two sacks over 35 snaps. It will be interesting to see where Klein fits among the Lions’ depth. Beyond Detroit’s five projected starters, they have offensive tackle Larry Borom, backup center Seth McLaughlin, reserver guard Ben Bartch, utility lineman Miles Frazier—with guard Mason Miller and tackle Devin Cochran on the practice squad. While it seems like Klein’s best fit is on the interior, the Lions are a bit thinner at tackle. We’ll see what the Lions have in store for him when he’s officially signed and in the building. You can see the rest of the Lions’ 15-man practice squad (one current vacancy) with our 2026 Detroit Lions practice squad tracker.

title: Discussion: Where is the Detroit Lions’ 53-man roster’s biggest weakness?
summary: Forming a 53-man roster is a never-ending business in the NFL. The Detroit Lions may have settled on an initial 53-man roster and 15 of their 16 practice squad players, but general manager Brad Holmes and the rest of the Lions’ personnel department are not “finished.” The job of an NFL personnel employee is never […]
full_text: Aug 29, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell looks on from the sideline during the first half against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Forming a 53-man roster is a never-ending business in the NFL. The Detroit Lions may have settled on an initial 53-man roster and 15 of their 16 practice squad players , but general manager Brad Holmes and the rest of the Lions’ personnel department are not “finished.” The job of an NFL personnel employee is never done. The search for upgrades at every position continues throughout the entire season. Whether it’s free agency, the waiver wire, the NFL Draft, the trade deadline, or any other time of year, there is a humongous pool of football talent available, and opportunities abound. That job never ends, because no NFL roster is perfect. There are holes, depth issues, injury insurance is needed, and new players who just don’t end up working out. The Detroit Lions are no exception to this. You better believe that this week the Lions will continue to look across the NFL landscape and at hundreds of newly available players to see if they can upgrade their team. But before they do that, they need to evaluate the status of their own roster. So today’s Question of the Day is: Where is the Lions’ 53-man roster (and practice squad) the weakest? My answer: I think my answer is the same as it was when the Lions entered training camp: cornerback. While I’ve certainly been encouraged by the play of starters D.J. Reed and Rock Ya-Sin thus far, I haven’t had that same level of optimism with the depth. Ennis Rakestraw had a very up-and-down camp with more downs than ups. Roger McCreary, who I believed to be a savvy pickup, has had flashes (particularly in the first two preseason games), but has underwhelmed compared to my previous expectations. The most promising player amongst the depth is Nick Whiteside, and Detroit didn’t even believe he played well enough to warrant a spot on the 53-man roster, risking losing him by putting him on waivers before bringing him back to the practice squad. The situation at nickel may be even more dire. While things were trending toward Christian Izien winning the starting job before his injury, that felt more like no one winning the job than anything. McCreary didn’t stand out. Rakestraw was kept on the outside. And rookie Keith Abney is clearly still adjusting to being a full-time nickel after having more success on the outside in college. Not only do I not know who the starter at nickel will be in Week 1, but I’m also not sure who the best possible reserve is, either. I say all of this not to induce panic. I’m actually a pretty big fan of the rest of this roster, and if the Lions can get plenty of healthy playing time out of Reed and Ya-Sin, maybe they’ll hold up at cornerback, too. But if I were Holmes and company, I’d certainly keep my ears and eyes open to upgrading the cornerback room. title: Grading the 2026 Detroit Lions initial 53-man roster
summary: It took some time, but the Detroit Lions eventually established their initial 53-man roster—and yes, they could count to 53 this year! Amid a flurry of unexpected roster moves, the Lions are now poised for their Week 1 tilt versus the New Orleans Saints on September 13. Detroit will have two weeks to ramp up […]
full_text: Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16) practices during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Monday August 17, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It took some time, but the Detroit Lions eventually established their initial 53-man roster —and yes, they could count to 53 this year! Amid a flurry of unexpected roster moves, the Lions are now poised for their Week 1 tilt versus the New Orleans Saints on September 13. Detroit will have two weeks to ramp up their roster, make tweaks to the game plan, and try to put their best foot forward. There is plenty of hope but an equal amount of doubt. Is this the roster that can win the NFC North, the NFC, and the Super Bowl? Let’s grade the 53-man roster that Detroit has put together. Quarterbacks (2) Starter: Jared Goff Depth: Joshua Dobbs I do not think there will ever be a consensus on how good Goff is compared to his peers, but here in Detroit, we are fortunate to have him leading the offense. He won’t wow you with athleticism, but he is as steady as them come—you know what you are getting from Goff. He can air it out when needed or take what is given to him. With a rekindled offensive scheme, perhaps this is the year that he garners league-wide respect for his play. As for the backup spot, the Lions are rolling with just one quarterback. Luke Altmyer had a competitive preseason and impressed considering his undrafted status. However, once Dobbs got settled in, he quickly took control of the quarterback competition. He has the football IQ to be an asset in the film room, the experience to be a worthwhile substitute if called upon, and the athletic ability to do damage through the air or on the ground. Considering the Lions signed Dobbs just days before the first preseason game, I feel pretty satisfied with him as a backup. Grade: A Running backs (5) Starter: Jahmyr Gibbs Depth: Isiah Pacheco, Sione Vaki, Jacob Saylors, Jabari Small We all know who Gibbs is at this point: one of the most electric players in the NFL. The biggest question is surrounding his supporting cast. How large of a role will Gibbs fill in this offense, and when he needs time off, who will step in—and how well? Pacheco should be the top reserve behind Gibbs, but he has rarely been healthy in training camp. That leaves three unknowns to fill in. Vaki is unproven as a running back, and he is more so a special teams ace at this point in his career. Saylors was downright dominant in preseason, but his resume is miniscule—is he ready to take RB2 duties? As for Small, him making the 53-man roster was a shock to begin with, as he has gotten injured nearly every week. I think there is some upside with the depth, but as a whole, it is a step down from David Montgomery. Gibbs really elevates this group. Grade: B+ Wide receivers (4) Starters: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa Depth: Tay Martin The release of Greg Dortch is downright stunning. A player that seemingly had a lock on the WR4 role now hits free agency. That leaves the Lions with St. Brown and Williams, arguably the league’s best receiving duo, atop the depth chart. A lot is to be expected of Isaac TeSlaa going forward—not only is he the WR3 in a potent offense, he is the unchallenged WR3. TeSlaa has had a poor training camp and preseason, so the Lions are really betting on him rising to the occasion. As for Martin, he is somewhat of an unknown factor. He likely made this team for his special teams ability, but can he be relied upon to be WR4? While his stock skyrocketed in camp and preseason, he still only finished with six catches for 46 yards and a touchdown—this doesn’t scream instant contributor. I am fairly concerned about the receiver depth, and I would be surprised if it is not addressed in the near future. Yet much like at running back, the starters do a lot of the heavy lifting for this grade. Also… who will return punts? Grade: B- Tight ends (3) Starter: Sam LaPorta Depth: Brock Wright, Jackson Meeks The answer for who will be WR4 is likely in the tight end group. LaPorta will obviously be an important part going forward, likely third in the receiving pecking order. LaPorta has battled injuries but is still an elite player when healthy, contributing both as a receiver and a blocker. Expect him to see the field often. As for the depth, the Lions surprisingly released Tyler Conklin, leaving just Wright and Meeks on the roster. Wright is a steady reserve, but there was some hope that Conklin would have been an upgrade over him at TE2. Instead, the Lions opted to keep Meeks, the former wide receiver. Meeks has obvious upside as a receiving threat, but his inline ability is still a project. If he is active on game days, the Lions will likely try to use him in passing situations, but I am still skeptical of how well they can run 13 personnel with this trio. Re-signing Conklin to the practice squad would ease some of my worries, but it is nonetheless a group that I wish I had more faith in. Grade: B- Offensive linemen (9) Starters: Penei Sewell, Christian Mahogany, Tate Ratledge, Blake Miller, Juice Scruggs Depth: Larry Borom, Ben Bartch, Miles Frazier, Seth McLaughlin IR: Cade Mays NFI: Giovanni Manu This unit will obviously miss Mays during their first four games, but I am actually cautiously optimistic—normally a rarity when it comes to offensive line depth. Sewell is obviously an All-Pro talent, but I think Ratledge and Miller have a chance to shine over on the right side of the line. Scruggs slots in at center in the meantime, and while he is a below-average starter, that still makes him an above-average backup in the NFL—the Lions could do far worse than him. The biggest question mark is Mahogany, but I am still a believer in his potential. Is this the best offensive line depth that the Lions have had in a decade? Borom is a high-end swing tackle that could reasonably start on a few teams around the league. Bartch has battled injuries, but could also be a starting-caliber player when healthy. As for Frazier and McLaughlin, the Lions have themselves two high-upside reserves. We will see if McLaughlin sticks around when Mays comes back. Grade: A Defensive tackles (5) Starters: Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams Depth: Levi Onwuzurike, Skyler Gill-Howard, Mekhi Wingo McNeill has looked dominant in camp, now over a year removed from his ACL tear. Tyleik Williams looks primed for a big Year 2 jump and has impressed in camp, but he is still classified as an unknown commodity. I am hopeful but cautious. If these two play to their ceilings, it could be a very formidable interior, both in terms of run defense and shrinking the pocket. As for the depth, there was some nervousness regarding Onwuzurike’s roster spot, but the former second rounder stayed aboard the 53. Perhaps most interestingly is that of their depth tackles, all of them are undersized with pass rushing prowess. Gill-Howard turned himself in a roster lock with an outstanding preseason. His play largely overshadowed Wingo given their similar skill sets, but the Lions still kept Wingo on the team as well. Ideally, it would be nice if Detroit had another nose tackle, but they do benefit from both McNeill and Williams being capable at that spot. Plus, Chris Smith is a likely candidate for the practice squad as insurance. Grade: B+ Edge defenders (6) Starters: Aidan Hutchinson, DJ Wonnum, Tyler Lacy Depth: Derrick Moore, Ahmed Hassanein, Eric O’Neill Pass rush was a problem for the Lions in 2025, and they have seemingly revamped the group in just one offseason. Hutchinson is among the league’s best and needs little discussion, but Wonnum should not be forgotten about. He has a chance to be an reliable rotation piece for the Lions. Sprinkle in Moore coming off the edge, and the Lions have some guys capable of crushing the pocket. Add in Lacy at big end, and they aren’t too bad at run defense either. The top four of this group were a given from the start of camp, with Hassanein…
