title: Rams were as surprised for Aaron Donald’s return as anyone
summary: The Los Angeles Rams and their staff made moves for Trent McDuffie, Myles Garrett and more because it was what they thought were the best moves for the team. They apparently did not make these moves thinking Aaron Donald would come out of retirement to join a “super team”. That was an added bonus and […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - JANUARY 14: Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald (99) walks off of the field at the conclusion of an NFL NFC Wild Card playoff football game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Detroit Lions on January 14, 2024 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams and their staff made moves for Trent McDuffie, Myles Garrett and more because it was what they thought were the best moves for the team. They apparently did not make these moves thinking Aaron Donald would come out of retirement to join a “super team” . That was an added bonus and a welcomed surprise . Now, for the past few months and weeks, yes, it was known that AD may be making a comeback, but when the Rams made their initial offseason moves back in the Winter/Spring, Donald was not part of the plan. Donald was happily retired. Once the door opened even a little for AD to make a return, conversations were had, plans were made and actions was taken by L.A. and Donald. Maybe it’s all a lie, and Donald has been orchestrating L.A.‘s offseason this whole time, crafting the team he wanted to play with whether they win it all or not. However, according to the Rams, this all just happened. Funny how life works out sometimes. Trent McDuffie never imagined playing with Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald: ‘Would’ve said you’re lying’ (nfl.com) “A stunning trio of moves that McDuffie would never have predicted. “I probably would’ve said you’re lying, for real,” McDuffie told Andrew Siciliano during an interview that will air during Tuesday’s “The NFL Report”, which streams at 7 p.m. ET on NFL Channel . “There’s no way you can get me. There’s no way you can get Myles. There’s no way you can get A.D. But, hey, hat off to (general manager) Les [Snead]. Hat off to (head coach) Sean [McVay]. Those guys are masterminds and they did it.” Aaron Donald’s absence from Monday’s practice “part of the plan all along” (sports.yah00) “I wouldn’t rule anything out yet,” McVay said, via the team’s website. “Sometimes when you put unnecessary parameters or guidelines on something, you can skew things. But what I think what’s really good for us is if he’s able to go, great, if not, that’s kind of how we’ve been operating as is, and guys have done an excellent job of being able to do some really cool stuff in the meantime. So, if he’s not ready, and that’s not what’s best for him and for the team, (we) absolutely wouldn’t have him play in Australia.” Donald’s participation as well as that of defensive end Myles Garrett will continue to be closely monitored as the football world waits to find out when we’ll see the duo on the field at the same time.“ Rams sign 17 players to initial 2026 practice squad (therams.com) “WOODLAND HILLS, Calif. — The Rams have signed 17 players to their initial practice squad on Monday for the 2026 season following the announcement of their initial 53-man roster on Sunday, utilizing the 17th spot for an international player. Here is Los Angeles’ initial practice squad:” Aaron Donald’s Los Angeles Rams return creates the NFL’s most fascinating experiment, potentially ever (atozsports) “The conversation around Donald’s return inevitably gravitates toward percentages. If he is only 60% of what he once was, how useful is that version of the player? The answer depends entirely on what baseline you are measuring against. Here is where the Rams’ roster construction changes the equation. For the first time in Aaron Donald’s football career, dating back to his days at Pittsburgh and through his entire tenure with the Rams, he will not be the primary target of opposing offensive lines.“ Rams linebackers have an opportunity to prove themselves with all eyes watching (ramblinfan) “That gives LA’s linebackers an opportunity, though. Led by Nate Landman and Omar Speights, the group has an open invitation to take their game to another level, proving to the NFL world that they are far from a weak link. Both Landman and Speights became full-time starters last season, and they are reprising those roles in 2026. Landman proved to be a high-value free-agent signing a year ago, having a career campaign with 132 tackles, eight tackles for loss, 2.5 sacks, and one interception. Speights, a 2024 undrafted signee, added 85 tackles.“ Rams believe in Aaron Donald because they’ve seen this story before (ramblinfan) “Forget what you think you know about the former All-Pro defensive tackle. He doesn’t need to reinstate his prime. Donald merely has to be in the right position to make plays to help the Rams win games. Rams know what Aaron Donald is capable of, and so does he He overcame size concerns to dominate. Draft analysts were brutally harsh in writing up Donald’s profile . Noting his size and weight (just under 6-foot-1 and 285 pounds), they waved off general managers with catch phrases like ‘undersized’ and ‘overpowered’. And yet, Rams GM Les Snead took him with the 13th pick in 2014.“ Fans had jokes about the Rams naming way too many captains (larrybrownsports) “Fans couldn’t help but laugh at the Rams handing out captaincy like cars on that one episode of Oprah. One fan hilariously compared it to a bride being indecisive about which of her friends to name as bridesmaids.” Super Bowl Odds for Every NFL Team in 2026 Season (Rams Enter as Favorites, 14 Teams 20/1 or Better) (si.com) “Last year’s champions – the Seattle Seahawks – are fourth in the odds to win the Super Bowl (+1100), a sign that oddsmakers expect a big season once again from Sam Darnold and Co. Seattle doesn’t have the best odds to win the Super Bowl in its own division, though, as the Los Angeles Rams (+550) enter the season as the favorite to win Super Bowl LXI. The Rams made the NFC title game in the 2025 season before they lost to the Seahawks, and they added two defensive superstars in Trent McDuffie and Myles Garrett (the reigning Defensive Player of the Year) to their roster in the offseason. “ Sean McVay, Kobie Turner, Kyren Williams & more Rams players and coaches join fans at this year’s Kickoff for Charity (therams.com) “Watch a recap of the Los Angeles Rams’ annual Kickoff for Charity event presented by UNIFY Financial Credit Union. Fans watched an exclusive interview between Rams legend Andrew Whitworth and head coach Sean McVay, then met wide receiver Davante Adams, quarterback Matthew Stafford, defensive end Kobie Turner, running back Kyren Williams & more Rams players.” 2026 NFL Preseason Week 3 rookie grades: Ravens punter thriving; did Texans find undrafted gem? (nfl.com) “NFL rookies had some time to get acclimated to their new cities and teammates. Now, we all get to see how these newcomers handle the best competition they’ve ever faced. Below, I’ve graded the performance of one rookie from each of the past week’s 16 preseason contests . Some of these players are well-known to football fans, while others are trying to make names for themselves on the professional gridiron. These evaluations are not predictions of how players will fare in this upcoming season, nor are they long-term career projections. Each mark simply takes stock of how the rookie played in Week 3 of the 2026 preseason.“ Comment of the Day: “Joe Milton was cut by the Cowboys. One of our posters said over and over that we should’ve drafted him because “arm talent is important”. Well, it is, but it’s also important to be a good QB, and Milton ain’t. A good arm is only half the battle….maybe even less. Accuracy, being pocket aware, not locking on to your #1 target, not always throwing rockets….all of these are equally important.“ -JeffinBranson Feedpost of the Day:

title: Rams announce 11 captains, most in Sean McVay era
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are entering the 2026 season with an unprecedented amount of leadership. After finishing their initial 53-man roster Sunday, the Rams announced Monday that their players had voted for 11 team captains. That is the largest captain group of the Sean McVay era, surpassing the nine captains selected in 2020. The Rams […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - OCTOBER 2: Captains of the Los Angeles Rams and the San Francisco 49ers during the coin toss before the game at SoFi Stadium on October 2, 2025 in Inglewood, California. The 49ers defeated the Rams 26-23. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are entering the 2026 season with an unprecedented amount of leadership. After finishing their initial 53-man roster Sunday, the Rams announced Monday that their players had voted for 11 team captains . That is the largest captain group of the Sean McVay era , surpassing the nine captains selected in 2020. The Rams had seven captains in 2025. The group is also notable for its balance. Five captains represent the offense, five represent the defense and Joe Cardona represents special teams. It includes six returning Rams captains and three newcomers to Los Angeles, while Davante Adams and Coleman Shelton are first-time Rams captains. McVay described the group as having as much leadership as the Rams have had during his tenure, and the list certainly backs up that assessment. Introducing our 2026 captains 🫡 pic.twitter.com/breO1uRqWS — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) September 1, 2026 Matthew Stafford Rams captaincy: 6 years | NFL career captaincy: 17 years There is perhaps no bigger captaincy lock on the roster than Matthew Stafford. The veteran quarterback has been selected as a Rams captain every season since arriving in Los Angeles in 2021, making 2026 his sixth consecutive year wearing the “C.” Stafford’s NFL captaincy history is even more impressive. He has been a captain in every season of his career except his rookie year in 2009, giving him 17 captaincies entering his 18th NFL season. Kyren Williams Rams captaincy: 2 years | NFL career captaincy: 2 years Kyren Williams returns as a Rams captain for the second consecutive season. The veteran running back has established himself as one of the team’s most important offensive leaders while also becoming a consistent contributor on the field. His 2026 selection represents his second career captaincy. Davante Adams Rams captaincy: 1 year | NFL career captaincy: 5 years Davante Adams earns his first captaincy as a member of the Rams after being voted a captain four times previously during his career with the Green Bay Packers and Las Vegas Raiders. Adams’ experience and status as one of the NFL’s most accomplished veteran receivers make him a natural addition to a leadership group that McVay believes is particularly strong. Tyler Higbee Rams captaincy: 2 years | NFL career captaincy: 2 years Tyler Higbee returns to the captain group after previously earning the honor in 2023. His 2026 selection marks his second season as a Rams captain and his second career captaincy. Higbee has spent his entire NFL career with Los Angeles and is one of the longest-tenured players remaining from the McVay era. Coleman Shelton Rams captaincy: 1 year | NFL career captaincy: 1 year Coleman Shelton is a first-time captain for both the Rams and his NFL career. The veteran center’s selection gives the Rams another offensive lineman in a leadership role and demonstrates the respect he has earned from his teammates since joining the organization. Kobie Turner Rams captaincy: 3 years | NFL career captaincy: 3 years Kobie Turner has become one of the central leaders of the Rams’ defense. He is entering his third consecutive season as a captain, making 2026 his third career captaincy. Turner’s rise from rookie defensive lineman to one of the team’s most trusted voices has been rapid, and his continued presence among the captains underscores his importance to the defense. Myles Garrett Rams captaincy: 1 year | NFL career captaincy: 3 years Myles Garrett is one of three newcomers to the Rams who earned a captaincy in his first season with the organization. Garrett previously served as a captain for the Cleveland Browns, including in 2024 and 2025. His 2026 selection therefore gives him his third career captaincy. Considering his status as one of the NFL’s premier defensive players, his immediate selection is hardly surprising. Nate Landman Rams captaincy: 2 years | NFL career captaincy: 2 years Nate Landman has earned consecutive captaincies since joining the Rams. After being selected in his first season with Los Angeles in 2025, Landman returns to the group in 2026. That makes this his second Rams captaincy and second NFL captaincy. Trent McDuffie Rams captaincy: 1 year | NFL career captaincy: 1 year Trent McDuffie is another newcomer who immediately earned the trust of his new teammates. The cornerback arrived in Los Angeles after beginning his career with the Kansas City Chiefs and quickly established himself as one of the leaders of the Rams’ defense. His 2026 selection marks his first captaincy at the NFL level. Quentin Lake Rams captaincy: 3 years | NFL career captaincy: 3 years Quentin Lake is back as a captain for the third consecutive season. The safety has become a fixture in the Rams’ leadership group, earning the honor in 2024, 2025 and now 2026. With three captaincies, Lake is tied with Turner for the most among Rams players outside of Stafford. Joe Cardona Rams captaincy: 1 year | NFL career captaincy: 2 years Joe Cardona rounds out the group as the Rams’ special teams captain. The veteran long snapper previously earned a captaincy with the New England Patriots in 2024 before joining the Rams. His 2026 selection gives him his first captaincy in Los Angeles and second in his NFL career. Cardona replaces Ethan Evans as the Rams’ special teams representative after Evans served as a captain in 2025. A Historic Leadership Group The Rams’ 11 captains represent one of the deepest leadership groups McVay has assembled since becoming head coach in 2017. The previous high-water mark came in 2020, when Los Angeles had nine captains, while the 2021 and 2023 teams each had eight. This year’s group is different in another important way: it combines the continuity of established Rams leaders with the immediate influence of several newcomers. Stafford remains the centerpiece, extending his remarkable streak to six straight seasons as a Rams captain. Turner, Lake, Landman and Williams also return, while Garrett and Cardona bring captaincy experience from previous stops. Adams and Shelton provide additional veteran leadership, and Higbee returns to a role he previously held. The Rams record number of captains doesn’t even include Aaron Donald who returned to the team on Sunday . With Super Bowl LXI set to be played at SoFi Stadium, the Rams have made it clear that expectations are enormous for the 2026 season. The decision to name 11 captains reflects just how much leadership the organization believes it has available as it begins its championship pursuit.

title: Rams sign 17 players to practice squad
summary: After finalizing their initial 53-man roster Sunday, the Rams announced Monday that they had signed 17 players to the practice squad, taking advantage of the additional spot available through the NFL’s International Player Pathway program. The official group includes 16 traditional practice-squad players and international punter Jack Bouwmeester. A significant portion of the practice squad […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 1: Dean Connors #33 of the Los Angeles Rams walks off the field during training camp at Loyola Marymount University on August 1, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images After finalizing their initial 53-man roster Sunday, the Rams announced Monday that they had signed 17 players to the practice squad, taking advantage of the additional spot available through the NFL’s International Player Pathway program. The official group includes 16 traditional practice-squad players and international punter Jack Bouwmeester. A significant portion of the practice squad consists of players who have already spent time with Los Angeles. Six players — Tanner Ingle, Cam Lampkin, Elias Neal, Bill Norton, Brennan Presley and Jordan Waters — were on the Rams’ practice squad during the 2025 season. All six signed Reserve/Future contracts with Los Angeles earlier this offseason after spending time on the practice squad last year. Practice Squad (17) RB, Dean Connors S, Nick Andersen DT, Tim Keenan III CB, Cam Lampkin WR/KR/PR, Alex Bachman OL, Austin Blaske P, Jack Bouwmeester DB, Nyzir Fourqueran OL, Blake Hance S, Tanner Ingle DL, Larrell Murchison LB, Elias Neal DL, Bill Norton EDGE, Daryl Peterson III WR, Brennan Presley RB, Jordan Waters TE, Dan Villari The Rams have officially announced their practice squad: pic.twitter.com/iQ3iEgucrr — Blaine Grisak 💭 (@BGMediaOnSI) August 31, 2026 That gives the Rams a strong level of continuity heading into the regular season. Ingle, Lampkin, Neal, Norton, Presley and Waters have already spent considerable time learning Sean McVay’s system and working with the team’s coaching staff. The Rams also have a couple of veterans with previous experience in the organization. Larrell Murchison has spent multiple seasons with Los Angeles, while Alex Bachman originally entered the NFL as a Rams undrafted free agent in 2019. Murchison has played for the Rams in 2022, 2023 and 2025, while Bachman returns to Los Angeles after spending the 2025 season with the Las Vegas Raiders. The remainder of the group provides the Rams with plenty of young talent to develop. Rookie defensive lineman Tim Keenan III, who narrowly missed the 53-man roster, gets another opportunity to remain in the organization, while Austin Blaske, Nick Andersen, Nyzier Fourqurean, Darryl Peterson III and Dan Villari will continue their development. Dean Connors is another notable name returning to the organization after an impressive preseason. The running back produced several strong performances during the exhibition schedule and gives the Rams additional depth at a position where injuries can quickly change the roster. The practice squad can become much more than a collection of reserve players over the course of a season. Players can be elevated for games, promoted to the active roster or eventually earn larger roles. For a Rams team with Super Bowl aspirations, maintaining quality depth behind the initial 53-man roster could prove extremely important.

PFF converted it’s grading scale to a 0-100 system partially because JJ Watt and Donald were breaking the old approach. The new scale applies a dark blue to elite marks, which represents exceptional, game-changing play at the highest positional level . The grades do not take into account strength of competition. title: Rams 53-man roster: Does LA have enough tackles and defensive backs?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams may boast one of the best rosters in professional football history on paper. But margins are extremely thin in the NFL. For every position of strength—like the defensive line with Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald, and others—there is somewhere where LA is hoping people don’t notice just how thin they are running. […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 25: Kamren Kinchens #26 of the Los Angeles Rams talks with Quentin Lake #37 prior to the NFC Championship NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on January 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams may boast one of the best rosters in professional football history on paper. But margins are extremely thin in the NFL. For every position of strength—like the defensive line with Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald, and others—there is somewhere where LA is hoping people don’t notice just how thin they are running . I spy two places that are concerning and could grow even more so should attrition strike: offensive tackle and defensive back. The Rams effectively turned in a roster with three tackles and almost no reserve secondary players. It’s not a nitpick—it’s a reality. Alaric Jackson is still awaiting word from the league that he’s in the clear. Until then, a suspension will linger over his head. David Quessenberry is the next man up at left tackle. That probably isn’t good enough. Rookie Keagen Trost will miss at least the first four games of the season. On the defensive side, the Rams have truly cut out all fat. There’s nothing left at safety or corner. Jaylen Watson and Trent McDuffie are entrenched as starters. McDuffie could play often in the slot, which means Rams fans will probably see more of Emmanuel Forbes on the outside than they realize. Josh Wallace also made the cut but hasn’t played outside much over his tenure in Los Angeles. At safety behind Kamren Curl, Kamren Kinchens, and Quentin Lake is only Jaylen McCollough. McCollough isn’t really a backup—he’s someone who carved out a decent role as a situational contributor a year ago. Running skinny at these positions is a direct relationship to keeping seven receivers, five tight ends, and three quarterbacks. WR#7, TE#5, nor QB#3 are going to keep Matthew Stafford upright or help protect a lead into the playoffs. These are luxuries. We’ve read this book before. 2022 brought intense attrition starting with the offensive line. Stafford shortly followed when the Rams couldn’t block a soul. Before we knew it, half the roster was prematurely calling it a season. Did the Rams not learn their lesson? A weakened secondary would make a great sequel, although it runs the risk of ending the same way.

title: Sean McVay sits starters, Rams win preseason
summary: Sean McVay isn’t the first head coach to sit every starter and important reserve during the preseason, but the L.A. Rams may have perfected the practice. While every key player sat during the preseason, as has been the case since McVay’s second year on the job in 2018, the Rams were still praised for the […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Ty Simpson #15 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on during the first half of a preseason game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sean McVay isn’t the first head coach to sit every starter and important reserve during the preseason, but the L.A. Rams may have perfected the practice. While every key player sat during the preseason, as has been the case since McVay’s second year on the job in 2018, the Rams were still praised for the performances of their two quarterbacks and added Aaron Donald . The Rams have even so far avoided suspension news for Puka Nacua and A.J. Jackson . They’re not out of the woods, but Nacua did return to practice on Sunday after missing a couple of weeks from a joint practice injury against the Cowboys. Although McVay sat over 40 players during the preseason because they were destined to make the final roster, rookie Ty Simpson was praised by the media for his efficient stat line and a high-level touchdown throw in the preseason finale. Compare that to Fernando Mendoza, the Raiders first overall pick who in all likelihood would have been named the Las Vegas starter if he had produced as well as Simpson . TRENDING: Ty Simpson’s BEST PASSES from his first preseason in the NFL. 47/60 (78%), 382 passing yards, 3 TD’s, 0 INT’s, 19 FD’s, 109.9 passer rating 😳🎯 pic.twitter.com/lcUZveANt9 — Rookie Watch (@RookieWatxh) August 28, 2026 It doesn’t matter if one quarterback has a better preseason than another quarterback. It just does not matter . But don’t tell that to Klint Kubiak and Mendoza. They would love to trade Mendoza’s first three games for Simpson’s right now. With a supporting cast that featured almost no players who made the final roster , save for C.J. Daniels, Max Klare, and a couple backup offensive linemen, plus not always having his plays called by McVay, Simpson avoided the rookie yips and the cries of “bust!” that typically come with first appearances. Of course, the Rams didn’t lose in the preseason either (also doesn’t matter) and didn’t turn it over or get sacked. The L.A. Rams succeeded in the preseason, avoided major injuries, got to see their first-round pick have a good first month of game action, kept Matthew Stafford upright, and are even happy with Stetson Bennett. On top of everything else, a future Hall of Famer was willing to reset his eligibility for the Hall of Fame by coming out of retirement. Zachary Pereles of CBS Sports cites the Rams as the biggest winners of the preseason : What more is there to say? After the Rams added one of the best defensive players of all time ( Myles Garrett ) and two cornerbacks ( Trent McDuffie , Jaylen Watson ) to address their biggest need, Aaron Donald officially un-retired on a one-year deal. Donald is now 35, but if he is even 70% of his peak self, he’s still a star. Los Angeles can work him in slowly if they need to. A pass rush with Garrett, Donald, Kobie Turner , Byron Young , Braden Fiske and others is nightmare fuel for opponents. Furthermore, unlike last year, Matthew Stafford has seemingly no back concerns entering the year. And if he should miss time, both Ty Simpson and Stetson Bennett flashed in preseason action. The Rams are even heavier favorites to win the Super Bowl after the preseason than they were before training camp, and they were already heavy favorites . Now comes the proof. "If this team is healthy,… I think it's gonna be hard to keep them within single digits." @danorlovsky7 says a healthy Rams team will reach the Super Bowl 👀 pic.twitter.com/KlMpDoNvRw — First Take (@FirstTake) August 31, 2026 The Rams still start the season with a series of difficult tests, including traveling across the world to face the 49ers, coming home to face the Giants (a slight reprieve), then going on the road in back-to-back weeks to face the Broncos and Eagles, prior to returning to SoFi Stadium to host the Buffalo Bills. Under most circumstances, any team would love to be 3-2 after that. Can the Rams accept less than 5-0? Sure. 3-2 actually would be good. The Rams have often started worse than that. But with as strong as their offseason has been, there’s no telling how good their actual season could be.

title: Puka Nacua back with Rams at Sunday’s practice
summary: Puka Nacua was back at practice on Sunday for the Los Angeles Rams after missing the last several weeks. Nacua’s return bodes well for his availability in Week 1. On the defensive side for L.A., Myles Garrett was still out. Though not a concern, for now, fans and the team would likely like to see […]
full_text: WOODLAND HILLS, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 11: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams runs after the catch during joint practice between the Dallas Cowboys and the Los Angeles Rams at Rams Village at Warner Center on August 11, 2026 in Woodland Hills, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images Puka Nacua was back at practice on Sunday for the Los Angeles Rams after missing the last several weeks. Nacua’s return bodes well for his availability in Week 1. On the defensive side for L.A., Myles Garrett was still out. Though not a concern , for now, fans and the team would likely like to see Garrett back at practice sooner than later. Another major piece of news to come out on Sunday is that Aaron Donld is officially back with the Rams . This isn’t just Rams’ news; this is news that impacts the entire NFL. Now, will Donald be as effective as he once was? Do teams have a plan to use against the Rams that they aren’t ready for? Will the Rams be as good on the field as they look on paper? All fair questions. As it stands, the Rams look like one of the best teams in the NFL without playing a single game. We will see how they look on their opening day against the San Francisco 49ers. Puka Nacua returns to Rams practice, Myles Garrett still out (ramswire) “Nacua has been dealing with a psoas injury. After avoiding being placed on the NFL commissioner’s exempt list before the NFL’s roster cut-down deadline, he appears to be on pace to feature in the team’s season opener against the 49ers in Australia. The Rams were never overly concerned about Nacua’s injury but now that he’s returned to practice, he’s certainly on track to play in Week 1.“ Sources: Aaron Donald unretires, reaches $20M deal with Rams (espn) “Donald, who retired in March 2024 after 10 NFL seasons, is a three-time Defensive Player of the Year, an eight-time first-team All-Pro, a 10-time Pro Bowl selection and the 2014 Defensive Rookie of the Year. But the Rams’ trade for Myles Garrett in June spurred conversation about the possibility of Donald’s return for the chance to play with the reigning Defensive Player of the Year. Since the Rams’ June 1 trade for Garrett, Donald has been putting himself through a “very strict, regimented process that was similar to what he did when he played” to see whether he could return, head coach Sean McVay said.“ Rams Troll Heat Over LeBron James YouTube Video Post After Aaron Donald Signs New Contract (bleacherreport) “The Los Angeles Rams had a hilarious callback on social media after signing Aaron Donald on Sunday. The Rams referenced the Miami Heat’s accidental YouTube livestream link teasing LeBron James’ signing.“ All-time great Aaron Donald comes out of retirement to rejoin stacked LA Rams (theguardian.com) “During a 10-season career with the Rams, who drafted him with the 13th overall pick in 2014, Donald was a three-time defensive player of the year and an eight-time first team All-Pro. He won a Super Bowl with the Rams at the end of the 2021 season before announcing his retirement in March 2024 at the age of 32. The 35-year-old returns to a stacked Rams roster who were already betting favorites to win the Super Bowl this season. The team includes reigning MVP Matthew Stafford at quarterback and the reigning defensive player of the year, Myles Garrett, who Los Angeles acquired in a trade with the Cleveland Browns in June .“ Rams final moves ahead of 2026 53-man roster deadline include trade, three on IR, waived 28 players, five terminated vested veterans, one waived/injured (therams.com) “WOODLAND HILLS, Calif. – The Rams made multiple roster moves ahead of the 3 p.m. deadline on Sunday before ending with their initial 53-man roster for the 2026 season. Los Angeles made one trade by sending tight end Mark Redman to Green Bay in exchange for a 2028 seventh-round pick. The Rams also placed quarterback Matthew Caldwell and offensive linemen Keagen Trost and Justin Dedich on Injured Reserve. The final round of cuts included: 28 players waived, five terminated vested veterans and one waived/injured.“ Tutu Atwell is wearing his 3rd different jersey number with the Rams (ramswire) “Upon arriving in Los Angeles, Atwell learned that his old jersey number, 5, was taken by Kamren Kinchens. The number he wore before that, 15, has also been taken by Ty Simpson. So Atwell had to pivot. At practice, Atwell was spotted wearing his third different jersey number as a Ram, switching to No. 8. Obviously, No. 8 was last worn by Jared Verse, who was traded to the Browns this offseason for Myles Garrett.“ Rams news: Watch Aaron Donald move incredibly at practice (sports.yahoo) “There could not be a better outlook for the Los Angeles Rams than watching Aaron Donald back in action with full force. The star defensive tackle has been showing an impressive level of activity during team practice sessions after making the roster cut once the team finalized its 53-man roster. In a recent video shared by ESPN’s NFL reporter Lindsey Thiry, Donald could be seen performing bag drills and agility work on the field for the first time in years. The outlook is what the Rams fans were hoping for.“ Aaron Donald’s New LA Rams Jersey Just Dropped Online (si.com) “Luckily for fans, Nike and Fanatics wasted no time in turning around one of the new Rams’ jerseys for Donald. Online shoppers can buy the Aaron Donald Los Angeles Rams Nike Game Jersey (Royal) for $149.99 in adult sizes at Fanatics and select retailers.“ Aaron Donald reveals wife’s advice that helped him make decision to come out of retirement and re-join Rams (foxnews.com) “”I think my wife played a huge part of me making this decision period because if the wife wasn’t happy, it wasn’t going to get done. I got to make sure that the household was good, the kids were okay with it all,” he said. “Then having the hard conversations, figuring things out, what I wanted to do. If I was to do it, how would we do it? “My wife was on board. She said, ‘If you want to do this, (I’m) with (you) 100%,’ and there were days when I was like, ‘I don’t know.’ She talked to me enough to be like, ‘You want to do this. Don’t make no decisions faster than what you need to make a decision. Take your time.’ She played a huge part of me figuring this out because it really wasn’t an easy decision. It took a lot of hard work, a lot of long conversations with a lot of different people, but I felt good enough to make the decision to come back and do this.” 2026 NFL roster cuts tracker: All the moves made by all 32 teams on cutdown day (cbssports) “For the first time in 22 years, the NFL decided to hold final cuts on a Sunday, and things definitely got kind of crazy with nearly 1,200 players being released over the weekend. During the preseason, teams are allowed to carry 90 players on their roster, but that number had to be cut to just 53 by the cut deadline at 6 p.m. ET Sunday, which means a total of 1,184 players were released, including Titans QB Will Levis . Now that we have cuts out of the way, each team will still have plenty of opportunities to re-shape their roster, and the first big chance will come this week with the waiver wire . After getting cut, any player with less than four years of NFL experience will hit the waiver wire, where they can be claimed by another team. The waiver order is the same as the 2026 NFL Draft order, so the Raiders will have first dibs on claiming any player who goes on waivers. The deadline for claims is Monday at 1 p.m. ET. After that deadline, teams will be notified by the NFL whether their claim went through (if two teams claim the same player, the player will go to the team with higher priority in the waiver order). Any player with more than four years of experience will officially become a free agent after getting cut, so they won’t hit the waiver wire, and they’ll be eligible to sign with any team as soon as Monday, so we could see a rash of signings starting this week.“ Comment of the Day: “I hope AD can be 75…

title: Why Fernando Mendoza should sit
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders should stick to the plan in place with Fernando Mendoza. Kirk Cousins was brought in to start at quarterback and allow Mendoza to sit until he’s ready. Throughout the preseason, Mendoza has shown he is the real deal; he has also struggled with what he has around him. Pass protection hasn’t […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 27: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders is sacked by Keion White #56 of the San Francisco 49ers in the second quarter of their preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The 49ers defeated the Raiders 18-12. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders should stick to the plan in place with Fernando Mendoza. Kirk Cousins was brought in to start at quarterback and allow Mendoza to sit until he’s ready. Throughout the preseason, Mendoza has shown he is the real deal; he has also struggled with what he has around him. Pass protection hasn’t done him any favors; none of the second-tier wide receivers have separated from the pack or other teams’ defensive backs, for that matter. He has pushed Cousins for the starting role, but here are some reasons why the Raiders need to stay the course. Now do average yards of separation for the wide receivers. The offensive line is the main reason why he should sit. Trying to go through progressions to find wideouts who don’t get open only to get hit anyway will ruin him. https://t.co/KGZGgd3TV0 — Phil Robinson III (@PhilRobinsonIII) August 25, 2026 Offensive line is strike one Cousins has maintained his lead at the top of the depth chart with an emphasis on the short-yardage, quick-passing game. Pass protection issues have plagued the Raiders since the (Derek) Carr Insurance offensive line policy was canceled and disbanded. The Raiders’ team of offensive line coaches has done wonders with what they have, but they aren’t miracle workers. The Raiders’ complete starting offensive line has only taken the field for three series in the entire preseason. Mendoza has yet to take a game snap from Tyler Linderbaum or enjoy blindside protection from Kolton Miller. Meanwhile, the battle at right guard between Jackson Powers-Johnson and Caleb Rogers has yet to be decided with the conclusion of preseason competition. Left guard free-agent acquisition Spencer Burford is a much better run blocker than a pass protector. Yet he is still much better than his backups. The tackle situation is a sturdy foundation rooted in eroding soil. Kolton Miller, one of the last holdovers from the Oakland Raiders, has an extensive injury history and the gap between him and Charles Grant isn’t as large as it used to be. Delmar Glaze is the starting right tackle and like most of his peers, his run blocking in this scheme far exceeds his pass protection. Glaze has maintained his lateral quickness deficiency as best he can. It now takes the more premier defensive ends to completely outclass him. Which wide receiver is number on e Head coach Klint Kubiak called out his entire receiving corps, charging the entire unit with taking a step back during joint practice and the preseason game in Houston. Paramount to the success of any rookie quarterback are trusted and reliable wide receivers. Most importantly, ones who fulfill the obligation of catching the football when targeted, capable of running correct routes, and getting to their landmarks in phase and on time. Receivers who generate separation either coming out of the break or at the top of the route. None of the receivers on the Raiders depth chart have been “wide receiver one” since high school. Former fourth-round pick Tre Tucker has had the best showings of the bunch thus far. Jalen Nailor has been inconsistent throughout his preseason action. Often trading wow plays of opposite extremes and can go from hand-raising to head-scratching on back-to-back plays. Jack Bech has made more plays throwing blocks than he has catching passes. Sixth-round draft pick Malik Benson has been the Cinderella story of camp. However, down the preseason’s home stretch, he has begun to waver against unfamiliar competition. Against the Houston Texans, butterfingers and catch-point disruptors got the better of him. He had a nice sideline grab out of bounds after a San Francisco 49ers defensive back bumped him off his spot and out of bounds. He would draw a flag on that play, but his production has downshifted as his competition has increased. There is no rush Mendoza is the Raiders’ future at quarterback and Kubiak is going to be afforded every opportunity and resource to build a winner around Mendoza. The benefit to Cousins being on the team is not having to rush Mendoza out into adverse situations. Having Aidan O’Connell on this roster provides another sacrificial lamb should the pass protection not keep Cousins upright. Mendoza has had very good play but it’s just not quite jiving the way it’s supposed to. Mendoza has continued to demonstrate an ability to get through all of his reads if necessary. Meaning if he is dropping back and given time to throw, he will find the open guy. He isn’t holding onto the ball for no reason; guys just aren’t getting open. It is still at least a year before the Raiders will either draft or sign in free agency Mendoza’s “wide receiver one” of the future. Not having receivers consistently capable of generating separation and catching the football is too much of a hindrance for a pocket passer. Maybe sometime before the end of the year he’ll actually get a couple of starts and the chance to play with all of the starters instead of some.

title: 5 takeaways from Las Vegas Raiders’ initial 53-man roster
summary: With cutdown day in the books, the Las Vegas Raiders have their initial 53-man roster set. That gives us some information to develop a handful of takeaways and explore a few spots that could still be addressed via an early-season free-agent signing. WR depth is as bad as it gets This isn’t exactly an earth-shattering […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - JANUARY 04: Dont'e Thornton Jr. #10 of the Las Vegas Raiders warms up prior to a game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Allegiant Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images With cutdown day in the books, the Las Vegas Raiders have their initial 53-man roster set. That gives us some information to develop a handful of takeaways and explore a few spots that could still be addressed via an early-season free-agent signing. WR depth is as bad as it gets This isn’t exactly an earth-shattering takeaway since anyone who has been paying attention to the offseason knew the Raiders’ wide receiver room lacked talent heading into training camp. Also, Klint Kubiak called out the position group after the second preseason game, saying that someone needed to step up. However, Dont’e Thornton Jr. making the team after struggling to begin camp and then missing about a month—including all three preseason games—with an injury really highlights how much the group was struggling as a whole. Pair that with an underwhelming rookie season, and it seems like the only reasons the 2025 fourth-round pick has a roster spot are because of his draft slot and lack of other options. On top of that, Dareke Young is occupying a roster spot after having just one catch for 10 yards during the preseason. Granted, Young made it for what he brings on special teams. But he’s one of six receivers on the roster, so that only reinforces that Las Vegas lacks depth at the position. Thus, it’s widely expected the Raiders will be looking for more wideouts throughout the season, meaning Thornton shouldn’t get too comfortable. No market for O’Connell It was a little bit of a surprise to see Kubiak keep Aidan O’Connell. The fourth-year pro is in a contract year while Kirk Cousins is expected to be named the Week 1 starter , and rookie Fernando Mendoza is the quarterback of the future who can also serve as the backup in the interim. So, it seemed like the Raiders were going to try to get a late-round pick or address another position by trading O’Connell at the end of training camp. However, he didn’t play well enough to drum up a market, going 22-for-46 (47.8 completion percentage) for 283 yards and no passing touchdowns (1 rushing TD) during the preseason. Meanwhile, quarterbacks Kyle McCord (Packers to Dolphins) and Quinn Ewers (Dolphins to Jaguars) were dealt on cutdown day. So, other teams were in the market for a backup quarterback, but O’Connell is still in Vegas. Maybe the Raiders plan to keep him as the backup to prevent Mendoza from having to be thrown into a game if Cousins gets injured, or they’re waiting for an injury to try and trade AOC during the season. But right now, it doesn’t seem like the rest of the league is interested in giving anything up for him. Jeanty relatively healthy At the time of writing, we still don’t know the full extent of Ashton Jeanty’s injury. It seemed devastating when the news was first reported, with notes about the team holding a prayer circle and him not being able to put weight on the injured leg. However, the follow-up that Jeanty suffered “just” a sprained ankle was a big sigh of relief considering the alternative. Adding to that, the fact that the coaching staff is only rostering three running backs to begin the year suggests Jeanty won’t have to miss many or any games at all. Hypothetically, had Dare Ogunbowale made the team in some form (i.e., Jeanty getting placed on IR but designated to return, or even if both made it and someone else was cut), that would’ve cast doubt on the 2025 first-round pick’s availability. No UDFAs With a 10-player draft class, it was going to be difficult for any undrafted rookies to make the team this year. Even the last pick of the class—defensive tackle Brandon Cleveland—didn’t secure a roster spot. So, there was always a good chance no UDFAs would make the initial 53-man roster. However, it was somewhat surprising that Cian Slone didn’t make it while Keyron Crawford was placed on season-ending IR . Sure, Patrick Johnson played better during the preseason. But the Raiders only kept four edge defenders when it’s fairly common to see five rostered around the league. Also, Slone received strong reviews during training camp and stood out during the preseason, too. He did clear waivers to be an option on the practice squad, so there’s no harm in him not having a spot initially. But it is worth noting that no rookie UDFAs made it. IOL help needed Along similar lines as wide receiver, the Raiders have a depth problem on the interior offensive line. After trading away Jordan Meredith , the backup center options are Jackson Powers-Johnson and rookie Trey Zuhn III. Powers-Johnson was exclusively playing right guard during training camp and is expected to start there in Week 1. Zuhn moved around throughout camp and only had 17 snaps at center during the preseason, per Pro Football Focus . Meanwhile, Atonio Mafi was a bit of a surprise to make the team. Mafi stood out as a run-blocker but struggled to provide pass protection for Mendoza during the preseason. Guard or center could be another spot that the front office addresses in the beginning of the season, meaning the four-year pro’s seat is still warm.

title: Raiders News: Keyron Crawford will officially miss rookie season
summary: The NFL’s cutdown day has come and gone, meaning the Las Vegas Raiders have their initial 53-man roster set. One player who isn’t on it is rookie third-round pick Keyron Crawford. Crawford was placed on injured reserve after suffering an ankle injury in the Raiders’ final preseason game against the San Francisco 49ers this past […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 27: Keyron Crawford #42 of the Las Vegas Raiders is driven off of the field on a cart after he was hurt on a play against the San Francisco 49ers in the third quarter of their preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The 49ers defeated the Raiders 18-12. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL’s cutdown day has come and gone, meaning the Las Vegas Raiders have their initial 53-man roster set. One player who isn’t on it is rookie third-round pick Keyron Crawford. Crawford was placed on injured reserve after suffering an ankle injury in the Raiders’ final preseason game against the San Francisco 49ers this past Thursday night. The defensive end had to be carted off the field, and while the full extent of his injury is still unknown, the fact that Las Vegas didn’t use one of its two return designations on the Auburn product means it’s significant. The Raiders did designate tight end Carter Runyon to return from IR after Runyon missed the majority of training camp with an undisclosed injury. Crawford likely wasn’t going to get much playing time behind Maxx Crosby, Kwity Paye and Malcolm Koonce in year one, anyway. Of course, practice reps are valuable for a young player’s development down the line, but the rookie being out will have a minimal impact on this year’s defense. Meanwhile, Crawford’s injury likely was the final boost Patrick Johnson needed to make the team. The 28-year-old was arguably the Silver and Black’s best top performer during the preseason, collecting 11 tackles, two sacks and four TFLs over the three games. Baring another move/waiver wire pickup on Monday, the Silver and Black will roll into the 2026 season with Crosby, Paye, Koonce and Crawford at edge defender. In Other Raiders’ Links: Cut tracker: A recap of all the cuts the Raiders made on Sunday. Jordan Meredith traded: “According to NFL Media, the Raiders have traded backup center/guard Jordan Meredith to the New York Jets,” S&BP’s Bill Williamson wrote. “The Raiders are sending a 2029 seventh-round pick to New York with Meredith for a 2027 sixth-round pick.” Laki Tasi waived by Titans: The former fan favorite and IPP/rugby player didn’t make Tennessee’s 53-man roster on cutdown day, via WSMV 4 . (Photo by Lee Coleman/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins cut their roster to the NFL’s 53-man regular-season limit on Sunday, then immediately started making major changes to that “final” roster in Monday’s waiver process. The Dolphins claimed seven players off waivers, the most in the league, as they churn the bottom of their roster and try to find the right combination of players for the 2026 season. Heading into the year, the Dolphins have the league’s youngest roster, and it is not close. The Dolphins’ players average 25. They are almost two years younger than the league average of just under 27. Miami is clearly in a developmental mindset, hoping this group of players will grow together and form the nucleus of the team’s rebuild. The Palm Beach Post’s Joe Schad looked at the Dolphins’ young roster and tied it back to comments from Miami general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan in March – specifically the Dolphins front office trying to shake Miami out of the mediocrity that had settled around the team for years. Nearly half of Miami’s initial 53-man roster is aged 22, 23 or 24. Patience is required. Every or almost every decision general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan has made and will make in the coming months is with a long-term lens. “We can’t live in the middle,” Sullivan forewarned in March. title: Miami Dolphins have NFL’s youngest roster heading into 2026 season
summary: The Miami Dolphins have concluded their preseason slate and have trimmed the roster down to 53 men after a flurry of cuts on Saturday and Sunday. As the dust settled, one thing became clear — the organization and new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan have embraced a youth movement regarding the 2026 version of the Dolphins. […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - AUGUST 14: Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis (2) hands the ball to running back De'Von Achane (28) during the Miami Dolphins preseason game versus the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on August 14, 2026, in Landover, MD. (Photo by Lee Coleman/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins have concluded their preseason slate and have trimmed the roster down to 53 men after a flurry of cuts on Saturday and Sunday. As the dust settled, one thing became clear — the organization and new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan have embraced a youth movement regarding the 2026 version of the Dolphins. The numbers prove it. In a social media post sent out on Monday morning, Joe Schad of the Palm Beach Post compiled a list of the youngest teams in the National Football League — and the Miami Dolphins easily boast the youngest roster in the entire league, with an average age of 25.3 years. The Dolphins have – and it's not even close – the youngest roster in the NFL Patience required Average age of 53-man roster Dolphins 25.3 Browns 25.9 Chiefs 26.1 Patriots 26.2 Lions 26.2 Packers 26.3 Titans 26.3 Jaguars 26.3 — Joe Schad (@schadjoe) August 31, 2026 The Dolphins beat out the Cleveland Browns as the youngest team in the league — with an average age that is 0.6 years younger than the AFC South squad. The Kansas City Chiefs come in third — 0.8 years older than Miami’s average player. Conversely, the Pittsburgh Steelers and Atlanta Falcons have the oldest rosters in the league — with each having an average age of 27.4 years. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers is obviously dragging that number up for Pittsburgh, but that means the age of an average Steelers or Falcons player in 2026 is a whopping 3.1 years older than the average Dolphins player. Oldest 53-man rosters in the NFL Steelers 27.4 Falcons 27.4 Rams 27.3 Broncos 27.2 Commanders 27.2 49ers 27.2 — Joe Schad (@schadjoe) August 31, 2026 So, what does that mean for Miami in 2026? It means that if the squad hopes to compete against a difficult schedule of talented teams, they’ll need to lean on their youth and athleticism, while being coached to their fullest potential by a new coaching staff led by head coach Jeff Hafley. It could be a rocky road ahead for the Dolphins this season, but watching a young team come into their own as the year unfolds should be a rewarding experience — even if that doesn’t translate to a lot of wins in the process.

title: Miami Dolphins news: Dolphins roster cuts and trades
summary: The Miami Dolphins spent the weekend trimming their roster from the 90-man preseason allowance down to the NFL’s 53-man regular-season limit. The league’s cutdown requirements led to nearly 1,200 players being waived, released, or placed on reserve lists. Sunday was a rough day around the NFL and tough decisions had to be made. In Miami, […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 09: Tyrel Dodson #25 of the Miami Dolphins enters the field prior to a game against the Buffalo Bills at Hard Rock Stadium on November 09, 2025 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins spent the weekend trimming their roster from the 90-man preseason allowance down to the NFL’s 53-man regular-season limit. The league’s cutdown requirements led to nearly 1,200 players being waived, released, or placed on reserve lists. Sunday was a rough day around the NFL and tough decisions had to be made. In Miami, one of those tough decisions was veteran linebacker Tyrel Dodson, who was released after recording 129 tackles for the team last season. Dodson was acquired by the Dolphins during the 2024 season when he was claimed off waivers from the Seattle Seahawks. Now he finds himself a free agent. Miami Dolphins on SI’s Alain Poupart took a closer look at the release of Dodson, explaining: The logic behind the move is that Dodson didn’t figure into the team’s long-term plans after the selections of Jacob Rodriguez and Trey Moore in the 2026 draft and sacrificing depth at linebacker was worth the cap savings for GM Jon-Eric Sullivan and head coach Jeff Hafley. If the Dolphins don’t come close to playoff contention in 2026, as most everybody expects, then it’s easy to endorse the move. But they will regret it if somehow they indeed are in contention in the second half of the season and wound up short on linebackers because of injuries. title: Vikings 53-Man Roster: McCarthy Stays, Banks Is the Future, and the Practice Squad Revealed
summary: J.J. McCarthy stays on the Vikings 53 — and the injury story still doesn’t add up. The Minnesota Vikings set their 53-man roster with J.J. McCarthy still on it, then spent Monday shuffling the edges. On The Real Forno Show, Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano unpacked the leak that McCarthy’s ankle is suddenly “week to […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: J.J. McCarthy #9 of the Minnesota Vikings warms up before an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images J.J. McCarthy stays on the Vikings 53 — and the injury story still doesn’t add up. The Minnesota Vikings set their 53-man roster with J.J. McCarthy still on it, then spent Monday shuffling the edges. On The Real Forno Show, Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano unpacked the leak that McCarthy’s ankle is suddenly “week to week,” Ben Goessling’s report that McCarthy himself chose not to play Friday, the Max Brosmer and Dillon Bell cuts, waiver claims of Trevor Keegan and Nick Samac, and a practice squad still taking shape. Forness opened with the elephant in the room: he expected Minnesota to move on from McCarthy before the deadline. Then Adam Schefter said on Pat McAfee that the ankle is a multi-week injury — 10 days after the sprain, after McCarthy practiced fully Monday and Tuesday. “I don’t buy it for a second,” Forness said. “If it really was a multi-week injury… now we’re calling it a week-to-week injury after he goes out and practices in full?” Stefano called a grade-one deltoid sprain “100% playable” and asked why sitting Friday or leaking “week to week” would help trade stock. Forness noted other backups (Quinn Ewers, Kyle McCord) already moved for sixth-rounders, and that waiting only shrinks the market. Goessling reported the sit-out was McCarthy’s call, not the organization’s. “It was him not being comfortable playing in the game,” Forness quoted. “The whole thing just smells rotten.” Monday’s moves were clearer. Minnesota claimed interior linemen Keegan and Samac after trading Walter Rouse, then waived Brosmer and Bell to make room. Forness said if McCarthy can’t go Week 1, Kevin O’Connell will want a third active-roster quarterback because an emergency QB must be on the 53, not the practice squad. They also ran the rest of the roster: four tight ends with T.J. Hockenson in a contract year; Tyler Batty’s torn ACL thinning the edge; Caleb Banks as a long-term “unicorn” pick, not a Year 1 finished product. “You drafted him for ’27, ’29, and ’30,” Forness said. “Trading him now would be incredibly shortsighted.” Key points from the episode: J.J. McCarthy saga : McCarthy practiced fully Monday and Tuesday before sitting out Wednesday. He chose not to play Friday’s preseason finale despite the plan being for him to start the first half. Trade talks reportedly occurred but no deal materialized. Tyler expects a new quarterback added if McCarthy can’t play Week 1. Offensive line : The Vikings claimed Trevor Keegan (fourth-ranked PFF guard) and Nick Samac (top PFF preseason center), both with center versatility. Walter Rouse was traded for a sixth-round pick. Max Brosmer and Dillon Bell were waived. Tight end : Four TEs made the roster—T.J. Hockenson, Josh Oliver, Ben Yurosek, and Gavin Bartholomew. Tyler noted Hockenson is in the final year of his deal. Caleb Banks : Tyler defended the developmental pick: “You’re drafting for ’27, ’29, and ’30. This guy could, if he reaches his potential, be a Chris Jones type wrecking All-Pro.” Edge depth : Tyler Batty tore his ACL and is out for the year. The edge group includes Dallas Turner, Andrew Van Ginkel, Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins, Bo Richter, and Chaz Chambliss. Linebacker : Ivan Pace Jr. showed improvement in coverage. Blake Cashman, Eric Wilson, and Jake Golday round out the group. Special teams : Brett Thorson beat out Johnny Hekker for the punter job, with Tyler citing the international pathway player designation and comparable performance. Practice squad : Da’Veawn Armstead, Kahlef Hailassie, Bangally Kamara, Jahvaree Ritzie, and Cam’Ron Stewart highlight a group Tyler called “pretty solid.” GM Nolan Teasley’s Seattle connections brought in Marshall Lang, Michael Briscoe, and Trayvon Rudolph. title: Are the Minnesota Vikings Super Bowl contenders?
summary: The Minnesota Vikings may not be the betting favorites like some of the teams with more recent playoff success, but they have become one of the more popular dark horse picks among national TV and radio personalities entering the season. One of the advantages of not living in the local market is getting to hear […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 28: Head Coach Kevin O'Connell of the Minnesota Vikings motions on the field before a preseason game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on August 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings may not be the betting favorites like some of the teams with more recent playoff success, but they have become one of the more popular dark horse picks among national TV and radio personalities entering the season. One of the advantages of not living in the local market is getting to hear outside perspectives on the Vikings. I’ve been struggling to get into this season. Maybe it’s life, maybe it’s the lingering disappointment from last season, but for whatever reason, I couldn’t get excited about this season. However, that started to change recently. Every time I turn on an NFL show or listen to a football podcast, someone seems to be talking about the Vikings as a dark horse contender. Why are the Vikings Generating Buzz? The most obvious answer is talent. For a team that recently moved on from its general manager, the roster is surprisingly stacked. The offensive line is stout, the wide receiver group is elite, and the Vikings have two very capable running backs. The biggest question is whether Kyler Murray can take full advantage of those weapons while still providing a threat with his mobility. Brian Flores’ defense is consistently among the league’s most respected units, and he has a track record of maximizing the talent available to him. The team has done well to shed aging talent and continue to develop young players. Dallas Turner is a name on everyone’s tongue as a breakout player. The coaching staff and the addition of Kyler Murray are two more reasons for the optimism surrounding the team. Kevin O’Connell has a knack for developing quarterbacks and winning games even when his teams aren’t receiving elite quarterback play. He has helped multiple quarterbacks step into the system and find immediate success. The timing for Kyler Murray couldn’t be any better for a career revival, and it was only two seasons ago when the team rode Darnold to 14 wins in his first year in purple. Murray has always had the talent, and this might be the team he needs to get the most out of it. The Perfect “Dark Horse” Profile The team has a likable coach with a history of getting veteran quarterbacks comfortable in his system quickly. The roster is very deep and doesn’t depend on one star, but it does have a star in Justin Jefferson. The Vikings are the perfect dark horse pick because they’re talented enough that no one will be surprised if they’re playing meaningful games in January. Kyler Murray for MVP? Vikings QB among top nine dark horse candidates in 2026, @TheDan_Parr writes https://t.co/A3SIZ5AOt1 pic.twitter.com/nbgZdNNnrt — Around The NFL (@AroundTheNFL) June 10, 2026 Final Thoughts The national media is mostly lazy. There isn’t an effort to go in depth on 32 teams. That means national narratives aren’t always the best measuring stick. I don’t know if I’m fully ready to call them Super Bowl contenders, but I do believe they’ll be in the hunt for the division title and a playoff spot late in the season. And once you get in, it’s anyone’s game.

title: What’s Going On with J.J. McCarthy?
summary: It’s been an eventful month of August for J.J. McCarthy and the Minnesota Vikings. The month began with a ‘competition’ for the starting quarterback job with Kyler Murray, in which McCarthy got 50% of the first team reps. The reps quickly shifted toward Kyler Murray and ten days later, following the night training camp practice, […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 28: J.J. McCarthy #9 of the Minnesota Vikings walks on the field after a preseason game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on August 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Broncos won the game 34-6. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s been an eventful month of August for J.J. McCarthy and the Minnesota Vikings. The month began with a ‘competition’ for the starting quarterback job with Kyler Murray, in which McCarthy got 50% of the first team reps. The reps quickly shifted toward Kyler Murray and ten days later, following the night training camp practice, Kyler Murray was named the starting quarterback. McCarthy reportedly spent much of the offseason working on his mechanics and footwork and improving his game but reports of his mechanics looking better in OTAs soon faded and once training camp got underway, McCarthy looked remarkably similar to 2025 training camp. McCarthy’s preseason action didn’t show any progress either, as inaccuracy and his one-speed passing continued to be a problem. So much so that after the second preseason game, speculation about his status as QB2 began to mount, with Carson Wentz being considered the favorite, regardless of position on the depth chart, to come into a game should Kyler Murray suffer an injury. Wentz looked a little smoother and more comfortable running the offense than McCarthy and there was speculation that Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell may trust Wentz more than McCarthy to run the offense should Murray go down. At the same time, speculation mounted that if McCarthy isn’t the backup to Murray, will the Vikings keep him as QB3? That led to some trade speculation as the roster cutdown deadline approached. That week, following the Ravens preseason game, McCarthy suffered what was thought by McCarthy and O’Connell to be a minor ankle injury. McCarthy was asked about it and said he did not expect to miss any games because of it. He practiced twice that week and showed no signs of injury before the Vikings held him out of Wednesday’s practice as a precautionary measure, with Kevin O’Connell saying after the game that he had planned for McCarthy to start and play the first two quarters. But when game day arrived, McCarthy apparently told O’Connell that he wasn’t comfortable playing, according to Vikings beat reporter Ben Goessling . It wasn’t the team, after consulting their doctors, saying it wasn’t safe for McCarthy to play- he had been cleared to play- it was McCarthy saying he wasn’t comfortable playing and essentially taking himself out of the game plan. That is a key point. And that has led to even more speculation about what McCarthy’s motivation was in taking himself out of the game. After all, this was his last opportunity to play for potentially a year, particularly if he is third on the depth chart. There was speculation that McCarthy playing in the final preseason game would be an opportunity for the Vikings to showcase his talents in a trade scenario, but apparently McCarthy was not up for it. One possibility behind McCarthy’s choice is that he doesn’t want to be traded and so not playing the last preseason game takes away an opportunity to showcase his ability to other teams that may be interested in trading for him. The Vikings have reportedly received some trade inquiries that they met ‘with varying degrees of interest’ suggesting the compensation was short of their hope or expectations. Releasing McCarthy means the Vikings would take on the rest of his rookie contract- around $13 million- in dead cap over the next two years and receive nothing in return. Trading him would result (most likely) in a day three draft pick equivalent (or a player) and about $7 million less in salary cap obligations. So there really isn’t much of a motivation for the Vikings to release him and at least some minor benefits to trading him if they’re convinced his development path is not worth keeping him on the roster at this point. But now NFL insider Adam Schefter says he believes McCarthy’s ankle injury is a multi-week injury. It’s unclear if that’s just his view or if that was information he got from either the Vikings or the McCarthy camp, but it wouldn’t be the first time that a seemingly minor McCarthy injury stretches into a multi-week one. And if that is the case, that essentially kills any near-term trade scenario involving McCarthy, at least until he is fully healed. In the meantime, if McCarthy is indeed sidelined for multiple weeks, that makes Carson Wentz the backup and presumably he’ll be getting those reps in practice rather than McCarthy. This is a critical time for backups to get work and reps and McCarthy apparently has chosen to forego that and put himself in a hole when it comes to competing for the QB2 job. My guess is that if Wentz isn’t already the de facto QB2, regardless of what’s on the depth chart, he will be soon and it will be difficult for McCarthy to climb out of the QB3 hole once the season is underway. Looking at all this from McCarthy’s point of view, how does he benefit from not playing the last preseason game and what may be his last opportunity to play in a game until next August, not to mention sabotaging his chances at being QB2 as well? One thing I can think of is that McCarthy, perhaps in consultation with his agent, decided not to play in the last preseason game to avoid being traded- potentially to a team he didn’t like. Not playing in that game and now having a minor ankle injury McCarthy himself said would not keep him out of games turn into a multi-week injury according to Adam Schefter, essentially makes it very difficult for the Vikings to trade McCarthy. It also does him no favors in terms of durability/reliability with the coaching staff. My guess is that there wasn’t much of a trade market for McCarthy to begin with- Will Levis was not claimed on waivers and had better stats than McCarthy and more experience- but McCarthy not playing against the Broncos after a poor game against the Ravens and now yet another injury may have killed whatever market there may have been. And that may suit McCarthy. Perhaps the discussion in the McCarthy camp is let’s not make it easier for the Vikings to trade him and force them to release him which new GM Nolan Teasley may be disinclined to do- risking a backlash from the fanbase for getting nothing for McCarthy and probably raising a few eyebrows among ownership as well. Doing so would add almost $4 million to this year’s salary cap in the form of dead cap and offer no salary reduction or trade compensation compared to keeping him on the roster through next season. At that point, after four years in the league, McCarthy would be a free agent and could choose from whatever offers may come his way. But a trade could lead him to a poor situation for the next two seasons. A release now could do the same as he would have to clear waivers before becoming a free agent and any team could claim him. Another reason McCarthy may have declined to play in the last preseason game was because he wasn’t confident enough, despite being cleared medically, to play. He doubtless saw the reviews of his performance against the Ravens and perhaps was worried another performance like that would sink his career. Who knows. But at this point McCarthy at QB3 seems like a white elephant taking up a roster spot. It’s a sad situation without a good solution. The Vikings can cut bait on McCarthy and release him, which doesn’t do them any good from a salary cap or compensation perspective, to free up a roster spot for a quarterback with more potential, or they can hold on to him for another season, hope he isn’t needed and somehow improves with whatever reps QB3 gets in practice. Neither choice is ideal. Maybe a trade is still somehow possible. But the Vikings and new GM Nolan Teasley will need to decide how valuable McCarthy’s roster spot is to the team, whether McCarthy or someone else maximizes that…

(Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images More than two hours after the 11:00 AM Central time deadline, the National Football League has announced the waiver claims that teams around the NFL have made, and the Minnesota Vikings have been awarded two players off of the waiver wire, both of them offensive linemen. Per numerous reports, the team has claimed center Nick Samac and guard Trevor Keegan. Corresponding roster moves to put them on the 53-man roster have not been announced at the present time. Samac (pronounced SAY-mack) was a seventh-round pick of the Baltimore Ravens in the 2024 NFL Draft after playing his college ball at Michigan State. He spent the 2024 season on the Baltimore practice squad, and after being waived by the Ravens following camp in 2025 and signed to their practice squad, he was signed by the Carolina Panthers to their active roster. He appeared in 11 games for the Panthers in 2025, playing exclusively on special teams. Keegan was a fifth-round pick of the Philadelphia Eagles in the 2024 NFL Draft after his college career at the University of Michigan. A First-Team All-Big Ten Selection in 2022 and a Second-Team All-Big Ten Selection in 2023, Keegan was a part of the Eagles team that won the Super Bowl in 2024. (Yes, he only appeared in one game that season, but hey. . .rings is rings.) He was waived by the Eagles in August of 2025 and claimed by their division rivals, the Dallas Cowboys. He appeared in two games for the Cowboys before being placed on injured reserve with a neck injury. None of the players that the Vikings waived on Sunday as part of getting down to the 53-man roster were claimed by other teams. title: Minnesota Vikings Practice Squad Tracker and Practice Squad Rules
summary: While we’re still awaiting the results of the final cuts for the Minnesota Vikings, we’re going to go over the rules governing the practice squads for the upcoming season. Once the final cuts are completed, this post will also serve as our practice squad tracker, so we’ll be updating this post with any news of […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - SEPTEMBER 25: Marcus Sherels #35 of the Minnesota Vikings returns a punt for a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers during the game at Bank of America Stadium on September 25, 2016 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Grant Halverson/Getty Images) | Getty Images While we’re still awaiting the results of the final cuts for the Minnesota Vikings, we’re going to go over the rules governing the practice squads for the upcoming season. Once the final cuts are completed, this post will also serve as our practice squad tracker, so we’ll be updating this post with any news of signings to the practice squad for the purple as well. As we went over in the previous post about the roster cutdown rules, teams need to have their rosters trimmed to 53 players by 5:00 PM Central Time on Sunday, 30 August, which is today. After that, teams are allowed to claim any players who are subject to waivers. Those waiver claims will be processed by the league at 11:00 AM Central Time on Monday, 31 August. Once those claims are processed, any players who were not claimed on waivers are eligible to be signed by any team to their practice squad. An NFL practice squad will normally consist of sixteen players. The one exception to this is if a team brings on a player who is participating in the league’s International Player Pathway Program (IPPP), such as punter Brett Thorson, who has spent this offseason with the Vikings. If Thorson does not make the 53-man roster and clears waivers, the Vikings (or any other team) could bring him onto the practice squad as a 17th member with an exemption. Should that IPPP member get elevated to the main roster, he does not carry that exemption with him. He’s a regular member of the 53-man roster like anyone else. UPDATE : As you’ve seen by now if you’re following with our roster cut tracker (and you should be), Thorson made the 53-man roster for the Vikings. But the Vikings could sign a different IPPP participant to a 17th practice squad spot if they so chose. As far as the other sixteen players are concerned, at least ten of the sixteen spots must be occupied by players who have two or fewer accrued seasons of NFL experience. (An accrued season is one where a player spent at least six games in a full-pay status.) Any player can occupy any of the other six spots on a team’s practice squad, regardless of their experience level. During the regular season, a player can be “elevated” from the practice squad to the main roster up to three times. If the team wishes to bring a player up from the practice squad for a fourth time, they need to sign them to the active roster. During the postseason, player elevations are unlimited. In addition, if a team wants to sign a player from another team’s practice squad, it has to sign that player to its active roster. They can’t simply sign a player from one team’s practice squad to their practice squad. The signing team also has to keep that player on their active roster for a minimum of three weeks. A player also cannot sign with a team that is scheduled to play their current team in the upcoming week, unless they do so at least six days before the game (or ten days if the acquiring team is on a bye week). Those should be all of the rules that we need to be aware of when it comes to the practice squad. Again, once the final cuts are made, we’ll be using this post to track practice squad signings on Monday, so we’ll move it up to the top of the page so people can find it more easily. After all, if the Vikings are going to help people cash on a bet of +140 to win ten games or more (thank you, FanDuel Sportsbook ), some of the guys that end up on that practice squad are likely going to play a role at some point this season. UPDATE : The Vikings were awarded two offensive linemen from waiver claims , so they will have to waive or release two players from the 53-man roster to make room for them. None of the players they waived as part of Sunday’s final cuts were claimed by anyone.
