title: Vikings Keep Four QBs: 53-Man Roster Breakdown & Preseason Recap
summary: Vikings 53-Man Roster Breakdown: Four QBs, Rookies Rising, and a Preseason to Forget — The Minnesota Vikings finalized their 53-man roster after a dismal preseason featuring just one offensive touchdown, and the biggest headline is keeping four quarterbacks — Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz, J.J. McCarthy, and Max Brosmer — on the active roster. Darren Campbell […]
full_text: EAGAN, MINNESOTA - JUNE 10: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings participates in a drill during minicamp at Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center on June 10, 2026 in Eagan, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Vikings 53-Man Roster Breakdown: Four QBs, Rookies Rising, and a Preseason to Forget — The Minnesota Vikings finalized their 53-man roster after a dismal preseason featuring just one offensive touchdown, and the biggest headline is keeping four quarterbacks — Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz, J.J. McCarthy, and Max Brosmer — on the active roster. Darren Campbell and Dave Stefano broke it all down on the latest episode of Two Old Bloggers, a Vikings 1st & SKOL production, covering roster surprises, quarterback controversy, defensive line questions, and a trip down franchise history lane. The Friday night 34-6 loss to Denver was, as Darren put it, “another very miserable viewing experience for Vikings fans.” With McCarthy sitting out due to a sore ankle, the quarterback depth chart remains unsettled. “This was his one last chance before the season started to give me some confidence in him as the backup quarterback, and he did not do that because he did not play,” Darren said. Yet he supports keeping McCarthy: “I want J.J. McCarthy to stay on this team right now… at times, he showed ability to move the team and have the offense hopping.” Dave agreed, noting all four QBs “all have injury histories,” which justified the unusual four-quarterback approach. Key Points from the Episode: Four QBs kept: Murray, Wentz, McCarthy, and Brosmer all made the 53 — a rarity in the NFL. Darren called it “a surprising roster decision,” noting Brosmer’s spot could’ve gone to a special teams contributor. Punter change: Johnny Hekker was released in favor of rookie Brett Thorson. “It’s not a case where Hekker clearly outplayed him,” Darren noted, citing Thorson’s bigger leg and lower cost. Jacob Thomas steals the show: The undrafted safety from James Madison was the surprise of camp. “Brian Flores was giving him flowers in press conferences,” Dave said. Darren added Thomas was “telling other players, veteran players like Jay Ward, where to be on the field” — remarkable for a UDFA. Defensive line goes young: With Jonathan Allen and Javon Hargrave gone, Levi Drake Rodriguez and Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins step into starting roles backed by rookies Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange. “The bar that those two departed guys set isn’t that high,” Darren offered as a silver lining. Running game revamp: New OL coach Keith Carter and run game coordinator Frank Smith bring a physical philosophy. Darren remains cautious: “We’ve heard this before… and the results always seem to be the same.” Rivalries uniform revealed: The Vikings unveiled new alternate jerseys for the December 20 Lions game. Darren admitted “jersey fatigue” but liked the Nordic rune designs. Pro Bowl abolished: The NFL scrapped the Pro Bowl game entirely. “Just have a legit decision on who the best players are and announce them,” Darren said. Franchise firsts: Chuck Foreman was the first 1,000-yard rusher (1975), Warren Moon the first 4,000-yard passer (1994), and John Gilliam the first 1,000-yard receiver (1972) — all explored in a fun history segment. Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: The 2026 season kicks off in two weeks against the Packers, and questions abound. Can Kyler Murray master KOC’s offense? Will the youthful defensive line hold up? Is Jacob Thomas the real deal? For the full breakdown — including roster bubble analysis, injury updates, and a deep dive into Vikings franchise history — tune in to Two Old Bloggers with Darren and Dave, a Minnesota Vikings podcast on the Bleav Network. Like, subscribe, and SKOL. Fan With Us! We have your Minnesota Vikings talk amongst the Two Old Bloggers , Darren @KickassblogVike and Dave @Luft_Krigare . Join the conversation! Fan with us at Vikings 1st & SKOL @Vikings1stSKOL and the at the @BleavNetwork . Open Question for Readers: What’s your biggest concern heading into Week 1 — the quarterback situation, the defensive line, or the running game? Drop your thoughts below and join the conversation.

title: Instant analysis of the Patriots’ initial practice squad
summary: As the New England Patriots continued to tinker with their 53-man roster on Monday, they also began the process of putting together their practice squad. In total, New England added 12 players to their developmental team, 11 of which were with the team during training camp this past summer. Here are the top storylines regarding […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Cameron Dorner #88 of the New England Patriots runs against the Philadelphia Eagles during an NFL preseason football game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images As the New England Patriots continued to tinker with their 53-man roster on Monday, they also began the process of putting together their practice squad . In total, New England added 12 players to their developmental team, 11 of which were with the team during training camp this past summer. The Patriots announced 12 practice squad signings: S Mike Brown, WR Kyle Dixon, WR Cameron Dorner, DT Eric Gregory, RB Hassan Haskins, RB Lan Larison, T Lorenz Metz, DT Jeremiah Pharms Jr., OL Jacob Rizy, CB Kindle Vildor, LB Riley Wilson and P Mitch Wishnowsky — Brian Hines (@iambrianhines) August 31, 2026 Here are the top storylines regarding the team’s initial practice squad. Spaces remain New England’s initial developmental squad features 12 players, one being an International Pathway Player that does not count against the 16-man limit. That means the Patriots have five open spots on their practice — in addition to two spots on their 53-man roster. Vested veterans Ben Brown and K.J. Britt, who both were released on Monday after making the initial 53-man roster, are candidates to return to the team and fill two of the remaining spots. Punter contingency The Patriots placed punter Bryce Baringer on injured reserve, meaning the 27-year old will miss at least the first four weeks of the season. It’s a disappointing result for Baringer, who suffered the undisclosed lower body injury in the second preseason game, as he was having a strong camp. With Baringer sidelined, the Patriots signed veteran Mitch Wishnowsky to the practice squad. Wishnowsky spent the first six years of his career with the 49ers before punting in 13 games for the Bills last season. He is the only current member of the practice squad that did not spend the summer with the team. Offensive line depth The backup offensive line was struck with the injury bug this offseason, as Marcus Bryant will start the year on injured reserve while Ben Brown was also sidelined. New England is then keeping offensive tackle Lorenz Metz and center Jacob Rizy on the practice squad as additional depth. Rizy filled in this summer for Brown as the second-team center, while Metz has been with the team last January. Part of the International Pathway Program, the 6-foot-9 Metz does not count against the 16-player practice squad total. New England is set to then add even more depth up front, with Brown’s expected return and the reported signing of Jake Kubas from the New York Giants. Receiver replacements New England’s practice squad last season featured wide receivers John Jiles and Jeremiah Webb for the duration of the season. Jiles, however, was released earlier this offseason while Webb landed on injured reserve early in training camp. That led to a pair of UDFA’s in Kyle Dixon and Cameron Dorner signing with the practice squad this season. Dixon brings good size to the scout team while he impressed in the preseason finale. Dorner had several impressive moments this summer with his ability to separate and generate explosive plays. Backfield depth Elsewhere on offense, the Patriots kept both Hassan Haskins and Lan Larison at the running back position. The duo was competing for the RB3 spot behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson this summer before the Patriots traded for Corey Kiner. With Haskins’ power and Larison’s ability as a pass catcher, the duo brings a good variety of skillsets to the practice squad while both have special teams ability.

title: Patriots’ first practice squad for 2026 NFL season announced
summary: The New England Patriots have built their first practice squad of the 2026 season, and it includes several familiar faces. Of the 12 players officially announced to have been signed to their developmental roster, 11 were released by the Patriots just ahead of the NFL roster cutdown deadline. The lone exception is a free agency […]
full_text: Foxborough, MA - August 25: New England Patriots running back Lan Larison runs with the ball during practice at Gillette Stadium on August 25, 2026. (Photo by Danielle Parhizkaran/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images The New England Patriots have built their first practice squad of the 2026 season, and it includes several familiar faces. Of the 12 players officially announced to have been signed to their developmental roster, 11 were released by the Patriots just ahead of the NFL roster cutdown deadline. The lone exception is a free agency pickup who spent the summer in Buffalo but could end up playing fairly big role for the reigning AFC East champions early on in the season. Patriots’ initial practice squad Practice squad (11): RB Hassan Haskins, RB Lan Larison, WR Kyle Dixon, WR Cameron Dorner, OL Jacob Rizy, DT Eric Gregory, DT Jeremiah Pharms Jr., LB Riley Wilson, CB Kindle Vildor, S Mike Brown, P Mitch Wishnowsky Practice squad exempt (1): OT Lorenz Metz A look at the Patriots’ first practice squad shows that it features few surprises. Running backs Hassan Haskins and Lan Larison were both fringe roster players whose outlook changed for the worse due to the recent trade acquisition of Corey Kiner; Eric Gregory made a strong case for himself as a backup interior defensive lineman; Kindle Vildor looked like the team’s fourth or fifth cornerback at times this summer. Now, all of them plus other depth options have been retained via the practice squad. And with five spots still open — offensive tackle Lorenz Metz carries an exception due to his international status — it would not be a surprise if more players let go over the weekend are eventually brought back. Also expected to join the mix is interior offensive lineman Jake Kubas, who spent the last two seasons with the Giants and has started three games. He is reportedly set to be added in the near future, even though the signing was not yet part of Monday’s announcement. This leaves punter Mitch Wishnowsky as the only outside addition thus far. Wishnowsky, 34, originally entered the NFL as a fourth-round pick by the 49ers in the 2019 NFL Draft. The Utah product spent his first six seasons in San Francisco and later also had stints in Washington and Buffalo. In New England, he will help replace Bryce Baringer. Even though Baringer had made the initial 53-man roster , an injury suffered in preseason cast doubt over his availability for Week 1. The fourth-year punter has since been moved to injured reserve , knocking him out at least four weeks and opening the door for Wishnowsky to possibly fill his shoes during the early parts of the season.

summary: The dust from the NFL’s 53-man roster deadline continues to settle in Foxborough. full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA- JUNE 11: Bryce Baringer #17 of the New England Patriots ready for the snap during New England Patriots Minicamp on June 11, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Summer Lamont/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The dust from the NFL’s 53-man roster deadline continues to settle in Foxborough. The New England Patriots placed punter Bryce Baringer and linebacker Khalil Jacobs on injured reserve amid a series of moves announced Monday evening. Both will be eligible to return to the active roster after missing a minimum of four games to start the 2026 regular season. Should their 21-day practice windows open on schedule, October’s matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders at Gillette Stadium can be circled on the calendar. Baringer, 27, sustained an injury in the second game of the preseason that resulted in quarterback Behren Morton stepping on as the emergency punter. The Patriots closed out August with Matt Haack at the position and have since added veteran free agent Mitch Wishnowsky to the initial practice squad. Baringer, who landed in the sixth round of the 2023 draft at pick No. 192 overall, has appeared in all 51 games for New England since then and handled holding duties. The 6-foot-2, 215-pound incumbent out of Illinois and Michigan State has averaged 47.9 yards per punt with season longs of 79, 75 and 73 yards, respectively, during his tenure. Jacobs, 23, outlasted the 53-man cutdown as an undrafted rookie despite missing the preseason finale due to injury. Prior to then, the 6-foot-1, 227-pound linebacker had a hand in eight tackles and made one start off the ball in August action. Signed in May, Jacobs spent two years at South Alabama and two years at Missouri. He appeared in all 13 games for the Tigers in 2025 on the way to notching 47 tackles and three sacks. Tight end Cameron Latu and linebacker Darius Muasau were claimed off waivers by New England following the cutdown deadline. To make room on the active roster, the club released vested veterans in center Ben Brown and linebacker K.J. Britt. The Patriots also announced 12 signings to the initial practice squad as part of Monday’s moves.

The 6-foot-5, 313-pound interior lineman’s time in Foxborough dates back to the fall of 2024, when he was signed off the practice squad of the Las Vegas Raiders. Brown appeared in 27 games over the past pair of regular seasons, starting 14 between center and guard. He accrued 998 snaps on offense, 124 snaps on special teams as well as a contract extension last December. Undrafted in 2022, the Ole Miss alum has also made stops with Cincinnati Bengals, Seattle Seahawks and Arizona Cardinals. Britt, 27, signed a one-year deal with the reigning AFC champions in March. The 6-foot, 240-pound linebacker stands 76 games into an NFL run that began in the fifth round of the 2021 draft at No. 176 overall. An Auburn product who spent previous tours with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Miami Dolphins, Britt’s career spans 16 starts, 994 snaps on defense and 1,289 snaps in the kicking game. He has recorded 161 tackles along with one split sack, four stops for loss and three passes defensed. Both bypass the claiming period are now unrestricted free agents. title: Patriots claim tight end, linebacker off waivers following NFL roster deadline
summary: The New England Patriots stood No. 31 in the waiver priority after active rosters around the NFL reduced to 53. That standing still brought some movement. The reigning AFC champions claimed tight end Cameron Latu and linebacker Darius Muasau off waivers as the window closed Monday at 1 p.m. ET, according to the transaction wire. […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 26: New York Giants linebacker Darius Muasau #53 rushes the passer during the game between the New York Giants and the Philadelphia Eagles on October 26th, 2025 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots stood No. 31 in the waiver priority after active rosters around the NFL reduced to 53. That standing still brought some movement. The reigning AFC champions claimed tight end Cameron Latu and linebacker Darius Muasau off waivers as the window closed Monday at 1 p.m. ET, according to the transaction wire. Latu, 26, had been waived by the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday. The 6-foot-5, 244-pound tight end previously visited Foxborough for joint practices and preseason work earlier in the month. Entering the NFL in the third round of the 2023 draft at pick No. 101 overall out of Alabama, he began his career with the San Francisco 49ers and Cleveland Browns before signing a futures contract in the NFC East in 2025. The former national champion went on to appear in 15 games last season, including a pair of starts. Latu saw 102 snaps on offense to go with 257 snaps on special teams while having a hand in a blocked punt and 11 tackles. Muasau, 25, went to waivers via the New York Giants as part of the cutdown. The 6-foot, 234-pound off-ball linebacker had landed in East Rutherford in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL draft at pick No. 183 overall. A former transfer from Hawaii to UCLA, Muasau stands 27 games and 18 starts into his career. He has totaled 106 tackles, one sack and one interception across 890 snaps on defense and 341 snaps on special teams. To make room on the initial active roster , veteran linebacker K.J. Britt has become one of the corresponding moves for the Patriots, per ESPN’s Adam Schefter . The formation of the practice squad is also underway amid the musical chairs. But only one of the 28 non-vested veterans involved in the weekend cutdown at Gillette Stadium found a new home via waivers. The Miami Dolphins were awarded cornerback Marcellas Dial Jr. from the AFC East rival. Dial, 25, was among the first wave of cuts for New England. The 6-foot, 190-pound corner spent last year on injured reserve after suffering a torn ACL in training camp. By way of Georgia Military and South Carolina, Dial landed with the Patriots in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL draft at No. 180 overall. He appeared in all 17 games as a rookie, notching 12 tackles, one forced fumble and one start while handling 83.3 percent of the workload on special teams. Last year post-deadline, head coach Mike Vrabel’s contingent claimed quarterback Tommy DeVito and cornerback Charles Woods.

title: NFL roster cuts 2026: 6 waiver wire targets that would make sense for the Patriots
summary: The roster movement continues across the NFL on Monday after teams trimmed their rosters down to 53 players on Sunday. With hundreds of transactions across the league, a significant portion of them — those with fewer than four accrued seasons in the league — were placed on the waiver wire: where teams have until 1 […]
full_text: Aug 27, 2026; Orchard Park, New York, USA; Buffalo Bills defensive back Kani Walker (41) tackles Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Brandon Smith (87) during the second quarter at New Highmark Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The roster movement continues across the NFL on Monday after teams trimmed their rosters down to 53 players on Sunday. With hundreds of transactions across the league, a significant portion of them — those with fewer than four accrued seasons in the league — were placed on the waiver wire: where teams have until 1 p.m. ET on Monday to put in claims in order to add them to their 53-man rosters. The New England Patriots, who have the 31st spot in the waiver claim priority, have a full 53-man roster as of now. However, that roster will continue to be fluid over the upcoming days as they continue to search for depth upgrades. With that being said, let’s take a look at 6 potential targets that would make sense. WR/KR Charlie Jones The Patriots are set at wide receiver, but the team failed to find a kick returner this offseason. They rotated through several options in the preseason but did not have a return of at least 30 yards. Jones, meanwhile, has been a dynamic returner for the Bengals over the past three years, including a pair of kick return touchdowns. Is that enough to justify rostering seven wide receivers, or will the Patriots look to Kyle Williams to potentially fill the role? CB Kani Walker Six cornerbacks were kept on the 53-man roster, with Charles Woods and rookies Karon Prunty and Channing Canada making the team. But the group’s play was inconsistent throughout the summer, perhaps leading the Patriots to look for depth elsewhere. In the AFC East, Bills cornerback Kani Walker was a bit of a surprise cut after a strong preseason and brings good size (6’2) to the boundary. Edge Adisa Isaac New England’s pass-rush group remains the weakest on the roster, as the Patriots kept just Gabe Jacas and Quintayvious Hutchins to back up Dre’Mont Jones and Elijah Ponder. Adding pass-rush help should be on the to-do list, and Isaac is expected to draw interest around the league. The 2024 third-round pick has dealt with injuries to begin his career but showed his potential with a strong preseason. Edge Sam Williams Elsewhere along the edge, the 27-year-old Williams has recorded 9.5 sacks across three seasons as a rotational pass rusher for the Cowboys. Williams missed all of 2024 with a torn ACL and was suspended for three games for violating the league’s personal conduct policy. His physical, violent skill set should be appealing to New England, but he needs to improve his discipline. DL Joshua Weru and Uar Bernard The Patriots got a first-hand look at the Eagles’ roster this summer during a pair of joint practices and one preseason game. While Weru and Bernard are both project players as they are new to the game of football, the International Player Pathway Program players have intriguing skill sets and flashed at times this preseason. That included Weru recording a sack in the preseason game against New England, while Bernard is a freakish athlete along the interior of the defensive line.

title: Saints vs. Cowboys: Game MVP
summary: The Saints were able to finish the preseason with a check in the win column, giving a young locker room its first victory this year. While the game started off strong, with the Saints holding a big lead for the majority of the game, it did get close at the end, and the Saints needed […]
full_text: The Saints were able to finish the preseason with a check in the win column, giving a young locker room its first victory this year. While the game started off strong, with the Saints holding a big lead for the majority of the game, it did get close at the end, and the Saints needed a late field goal from Daniel Carlson to hold on for the win. There were several players who played really well throughout the game. Spencer Rattler had his best game of the preseason. Rattler finished 8-of-10 for 70 yards with zero turnovers. He was pressured four times and sacked once. Rattler also ran the ball twice for nine yards and a touchdown. Zach Wilson also played pretty well. Wilson finished 9-of-12 for 93 yards with zero turnovers. Wilson was also pressured seven times and sacked once. On the defensive side of the ball, safeties Terrell Burgess and Jordan Howden finished as the two highest-graded defenders on PFF. Isaiah Stalbird finished the game leading the team in tackles on defense with eight total tackles. There were several players who truly showed up and played well, but the overall game MVP was Ronnie Bell. Bell finished as the highest-graded player on PFF for the Saints with a 91.7 overall offensive grade. Bell was targeted seven times and had six receptions for 65 yards, with a long of 23 yards and an average of 10.8 yards per reception. Bell definitely made a statement with this game, but unfortunately, it was not enough to earn a spot on the Saints’ roster. Hopefully, scouts will see this tape and he will be able to get another opportunity in league.

title: Saints’ penalty problem could become costly in 2026
summary: The New Orleans Saints ended the preseason on a high note, defeating the Dallas Cowboys 27-24. After two ugly performances to begin the preseason, the victory provided plenty of reasons for optimism heading into the regular season. However, there is one issue from the preseason that shouldn’t simply be forgotten because of a better showing […]
full_text: The New Orleans Saints ended the preseason on a high note, defeating the Dallas Cowboys 27-24. After two ugly performances to begin the preseason, the victory provided plenty of reasons for optimism heading into the regular season. However, there is one issue from the preseason that shouldn’t simply be forgotten because of a better showing in the finale. Penalties. Through three preseason games, the Saints had 24 accepted penalties for 201 yards. That’s an average of eight penalties and 67 yards per game. The problem was especially noticeable in the first two games. New Orleans committed eight accepted penalties for 66 yards in its preseason-opening loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Things got considerably worse the following week against the Los Angeles Rams, when the Saints were hit with 12 accepted penalties for 96 yards in a 34-0 blowout loss. That’s a lot of self-inflicted damage, especially for a team trying to establish consistency heading into the regular season. The good news is the Saints cleaned things up against Dallas. They had just four accepted penalties for 39 yards, a significant improvement from the previous two games. That’s enough to make this feel more like a warning sign than a full-blown concern. Preseason games also come with plenty of variables. Young players are getting significant reps, different combinations are playing together and mistakes are more common. It’s reasonable to expect some of those issues to disappear once the regular-season starters are on the field together. But the Saints can’t afford for the penalty problems to follow them into the regular season. Penalties that stall drives, erase positive plays or give opponents extra opportunities can quickly determine the outcome of the game. New Orleans showed against Dallas that it can play a cleaner game. Now they need to make that the standard. So, is it an overreaction to be concerned? Probably, for now. But after 24 accepted penalties in three preseason games, it’s certainly something worth monitoring once the games start counting.

(Photo by Greg Fiore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New Orleans Saints ended the 2026 preseason on a high note, defeating the Dallas Cowboys 27-24 on Friday. This week’s breakout player had an eye-opening performance, though it ultimately wasn’t enough to save him from the chopping block: WR Ronnie Bell . Bell was released by the Saints on Saturday as the team begins trimming its roster down to 53 players. While that news is undoubtedly disappointing for the former seventh-round pick, his performance in the victory over the Dallas Cowboys was still worth highlighting and could ultimately earn him a spot on the practice squad. Bell finished the game with six receptions on seven targets for 65 yards, including a long of 23 yards. More importantly, he consistently moved the chains, recording four first-down conversions while also recording a contested catch. The 26-year-old posted a team-high 91.7 overall grade from Pro Football Focus, along with a 91.4 receiving grade. That makes his release a little more notable. Bell was competing for a roster spot in a crowded Saints receiver room, and while his performance against Dallas gave him a strong finish to the preseason, the Saints ultimately went in another direction. Still, Bell put some quality film on tape. Cuts like this don’t necessarily mean a player’s chances with the team are over, but the timing is certainly unfortunate. Now, he’ll have to wait for the next opportunity to prove it again.

title: What does C.J. Okoye bring to the NY Giants? Looking at the good, and the bad
summary: The New York Giants traded a 2028 seventh-round pick to the Baltimore Ravens for C.J. Okoye. The 6-foot-6, 365-pound defensive lineman was part of the International Pathway Program and spent much of the 2025 season on the Ravens’ active roster, where he played 214 snaps for John Harbaugh. New York had interest and ensured that […]
full_text: C.J. Okoye | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants traded a 2028 seventh-round pick to the Baltimore Ravens for C.J. Okoye . The 6-foot-6, 365-pound defensive lineman was part of the International Pathway Program and spent much of the 2025 season on the Ravens’ active roster, where he played 214 snaps for John Harbaugh. New York had interest and ensured that Okoye was a New York Giant prior to final cuts. As expected, Okoye was on the Giants’ 53-man roster. Here are some highlights of Okoye from the preseason: C.J. Okoye wears No. 97 and 91 in the plays below The #Giants trade a 2028 7th-round pick for #Ravens DT C.J. Okoye. Massive 6'6, 340+ pound IDL, a part of the International Player Pathway Program (Nigeria). He went undrafted in 2023. Here are some preseason highlights for Okoye, who played 214 snaps for BAL last season. pic.twitter.com/KYJt4HP9U8 — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) August 29, 2026 A few things are evident on tape. For starters, he’s massive. Some outlets have him listed at 370 pounds. He has long 33¾-inch arms and just under 10-inch hands. Okoye has some serious push at the point of attack, and he generates good force into his bull-rush. His rush repertoire is based on the bull-rush to push the pocket, which is his primary move, but he does a good job getting his eyes on the quarterback and adjusting mid-play. There’s no doubting his strength, especially when he keeps his hips and pads low. The combination he landed against Washington was mpressive for Okoye, who is still a young player learning the position. He landed a hump-move and transitioned it into a club swim against a reaching guard off the play-action. The pass was somehow completed, but the rush showed a finesse game that — if mastered — would make Okoye a dangerous threat on the defensive line. via GIPHY Here’s a play from the regular season where Okoye drew a holding penalty based on the aforementioned push and lower-body drive that he possesses. He’s also solid with his vision and awareness; he keeps his eyes open when rushing to cut angles off against mobile quarterbacks who try to escape the pocket. via GIPHY Okoye showed exceptional awareness by pushing the pocket and closing throwing lanes with his long wingspan. His eyes are an underrated trait, especially for a player who is relatively new to football. via GIPHY Okoye displayed a solid anchor against one-on-one blocks last year. Above, we watch him use his awareness and vision to locate Chase Brown (30) in the hole. The B-Gap opened up, and Okoye was able to close it from the A, while hand fighting the center. via GIPHY Okoye gets a good jump off the snap and catches, neutralizing the center’s blocking attempt, forcing the football to bounce inside and into a waiting defender. Okoye has solid regular-season reps on a talented team, and he’ll fit into the Giants rotation well. Concerns Okoye is a massive man who plays high at times, allowing blockers to control/steer him too frequently. When he plays low, though, he’s difficult to move. But that high nature can be a liability. The zone looks, specifically, where Okoye gets his feet moving laterally, have led to blocks where he gets displaced due to his high nature. It happened a few times versus the Bengals last season: via GIPHY via GIPHY Okoye can field double teams and anchor, but he was displaced a few times on tape due to the pad-level issue. via GIPHY via GIPHY via GIPHY Final thoughts Planet theory — the Giants traded for a massive human being with potential and familiarity to their coaching staff. When precise with his technique and pad level, Okoye is almost immovable in one-on-one blocks, with a solid ability to anchor in the ground, but staying low is an issue for the 6-6 defensive lineman. Still, he’s a high-processing player with excellent push into contact, and he’s flashed adroit hand usage and has strung some moves together, albeit I wouldn’t count on him being a pass-rushing specialist. Okoye will be a rotational defensive lineman for the Giants; one who will battle for snaps with Bobby Jameson-Travis and Darius Alexander. It’s not out of the realm of possibility that Okoye earns the number three defensive tackle role behind veterans D.J. Reader and Shelby Harris ( not including Chauncey Golston) . It was a good trade to get Harbaugh a familiar player at a position of need. Okoye is still only 24years old.

The offense is relatively young, especially the core pieces. Quarterback Jaxson Dart and running back Cam Skattebo both enter their second seasons while star wide receiver Malik Nabers is going into his third campaign in the NFL. On the defensive side of the ball, veterans like edge rusher Brian Burns, cornerback Greg Newsome II and safety Jevon Holland should provide some strong leadership for a young group of players including linebacker Arvell Reese and edge rusher Abdul Carter. 2014 OBJ vs. 2026 Odell "Maybe for the first time in his entire career, we'll get to learn who Odell Beckham Jr. is, instead of OBJ" 💙 Manti can't wait to see @obj 's impact on the @Giants 53-man roster pic.twitter.com/Vw4AqMu5b3 — Good Morning Football (@gmfb) August 31, 2026 Darius Slayton’s role on Giants remains unclear as he sticks on roster | New York Daily News Slayton is not far removed from leading the team in receiving yards in back-to-back seasons, with 724 yards in 2022 and 770 in 2023. He has been an invaluable shoulder for Nabers to lean on, clarifying responsibilities for the young receiver in the huddle at times so the Giants’ top wideout can play fast and free. He also is just one more Giant receiver injury away from this offense suddenly featuring him in the rotation again, and he has proven in the past that he can perform when he gets that opportunity. So the Giants’ 2019 fifth-round pick out of Auburn has been here before. It’s just a question of how much longer he’ll be here. Winners and Losers from Every NFL Team’s 2026 Roster Cuts | Bleacher Report Winner: CB Deonte Banks . By most estimations, Deonte Banks first three seasons in the NFL have been a massive disappointment. The 24th overall pick in the 2023 draft has made 35 starts over that span, but his passer rating against was over 120 each of the past two years. Banks appears to be taking full advantage of a fresh start under new head coach John Harbaugh and defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson. Wilson’s aggressive scheme calls for a lot of press coverage, and Banks has taken to it well. His offseason wasn’t flawless, but the youngster went from potentially being on the roster bubble to having a real shot to start in Week 1. Loser: OL Evan Neal. Evan Neal’s tenure with the Giants has fallen well short of expectations for a No. 7 overall pick. Since New York selected him in the 2022 draft, he has struggled to establish himself as a reliable starter at either tackle or guard. Neal spent much of the summer with the third-team offense, an indication that he has lost ground in the competition for a meaningful role. At this stage, he faces an uphill climb to revive his standing with the Giants. Giants 53-man roster breakdown: Odell Beckham Jr. is back; what comes next for NY? | The Athletic Schmitz, a second-round pick in 2023, is the only locked-in starter remaining from the 18 picks made in the 2022 and 2023 drafts. OLB Kayvon Thibodeaux, ILB Micah McFadden and CB Deonte Banks, who could start this season, are the only other players remaining from those two draft classes. The only intrigue at offensive line was the backup center battle between Hudson and Patrick. It seemed like Patrick was ahead in the competition since he was first up to replace Schmitz in the preseason finale. But the Giants elected to roll with the 25-year-old Hudson, who is eight years younger than Patrick. Hudson’s youth comes with inexperience — he has only played three career snaps — but there’s upside for the future, which is important as Schmitz enters the final year of his rookie contract. Patrick could return to the practice squad, but he may have opportunities elsewhere with center injuries striking around the league. Every NFL team’s highest-graded player from the 2026 preseason | PFF New York Giants: S Tyler Nubin, 91.4. The 47th selection of the 2024 NFL Draft started all three of the Giants’ preseason games this summer and excelled in the process. He recorded a 91.3 PFF coverage grade, with just one reception allowed on throws where he was the primary coverage defender. The only question is how much Odell Beckham on potentially wearing No. 13 pic.twitter.com/xqxRUfYGyj — Jared Schwartz (@jschwartz115) August 31, 2026 Top 10 breakout candidates for this NFL season | Yahoo Sports Giants QB Jaxson Dart. There was a weird stretch when people were questioning whether Dart was the answer for the Giants. It’s unclear what more he could have done as a rookie, aside from stay healthy. Dart looked good as a rookie, though the missed time was a concern. He had 2,272 passing yards, 15 touchdowns and five interceptions with 487 rushing yards and nine rushing touchdowns despite starting only 12 games. This season he should have Malik Nabers for most of the season and a better coaching staff to work with. Last year’s first-round draft pick can leave no doubt that he’s the Giants’ quarterback of the foreseeable future. title: Odell Beckham ‘earned his spot’ with Giants — now what will he do with it?
summary: Odell Beckham Jr. has a spot on the New York Giants’ 2026 roster, marking the first step in a comeback many did not see as realistic. Making the roster, though, is only part of the deal. Now the question is, how much can the 33-year-old Beckham, who has suffered a number of leg injuries throughout […]
full_text: Odell Beckham | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Odell Beckham Jr. has a spot on the New York Giants’ 2026 roster, marking the first step in a comeback many did not see as realistic. Making the roster, though, is only part of the deal. Now the question is, how much can the 33-year-old Beckham, who has suffered a number of leg injuries throughout a career than began when the Giants selected him 12th overall in the 2014 NFL Draft, help the Giants on the field? Beckham didn’t come back to be a nostalgia act. He didn’t come back to wave at fans from the sidelines on game days, get some polite cheers, and then watch other receivers catch passes from Jaxson Dart. He came back to show that he could still be a productive player. He came back, as he has said several times, to leave the game the way he wanted to leave it rather than having it taken from him before he was ready to go. When Beckham badgered Giants coach John Harbaugh into giving him a tryout, then a second tryout, and finally signing him, Harbaugh laid it out for him. “You can’t be just okay. You’re Odell Beckham,” Harbaugh said at the time. “You’ve got to come out here and you have to be performing at a high level in workout, you’ve got to be performing at a high level in practice. You got to be a guy capable that we can see would have a chance to make a difference in NFL games. You have to be that kind of player.” Beckham thinks he still can be. “I feel confident in my ability, and whatever it is that I need to provide, I’m looking to do that and more,” Beckham said on Monday. “I’ve never shied away from competition or anything like that. So, I feel that I can produce. I know that’s what I want to do and now it’s about putting the work in to be able to do that. “As far as what I feel like I can do on the field, I feel confident in that, and I’ve never allowed anything anyone says to shake that confidence.” Harbaugh said Monday that Beckham is not on the roster to be a spectator. “He’ll be in that receiver group,” Harbaugh said. “I mean, he’ll be rotating in in different personnel groups, and he’ll be playing.” Harbaugh said he “sensed accomplishment” from Beckham when the coach told Beckham after Sunday’s practice that he would be part of the initial 53-man roster. “I feel like he felt like he accomplished something, but not finished, and he said that,” Harbaugh said. “He wants to get – now it’s time to make it count, that’s where he’s at. “But I know he knows he accomplished a lot. It’s kind of unheard of, in some ways, to be away for so long to come back. I don’t know how many times this has actually been done. It would be interesting to see, but the odds were probably against him, I would say. He overcame the odds and did it. Now what do you do with it? And that’s what he’s focused on.” Beckham admitted to shedding tears when he knew he had made the roster. “I have an opportunity to rewrite some of the last bit of the chapter,” he said. “Don’t know, last year, whatever it is, I just know I’m going to give my all. But definitely had that moment where it was like you could let out some of the pain that I feel like I went through. It was just very healing, very emotional, something I was very happy about.” Beckham said “it’s everything” to make the roster for the team that drafted him. Making the roster, though, isn’t enough. “Nobody’s playing just to play – you all want to win,” Beckham said. “So, that was kind of the message I had to the group. It’s like, it’s one thing to get here. It’s an honor and a privilege, but how do you take that next step each and every day and find ways to level up?” Odell Beckham on potentially wearing No. 13 pic.twitter.com/xqxRUfYGyj — Jared Schwartz (@jschwartz115) August 31, 2026 ‘He earned his spot’ I have, at times, been accused of being a Beckham hater. I was even accused of that in the Monday morning roster review podcast I did with Tony DelGenio. I am not a Beckham hater. I did hate some of the self-serving, “look at me” things Beckham did as a young player with the Giants. Why? Because those things forced us to talk about stuff that had nothing to do with football, and how great Beckham was at playing it. As much as Beckham has often said he never wanted to leave New York, his own words, actions, and choices are what led to him being traded before the 2019 season. I have admitted to thinking that the Giants bringing Beckham back was not a good idea. I doubted both his ability to still play at a high enough level, and his willingness to accept without complaint a role where things did not revolve around him. The version of Beckham we have seen this summer has not sought adulation or attention, though fans shower him with plenty of both. He has only come to work every day, and done his best to show that he belongs on the football team. “He was one of the best guys, he earned it, he earned his spot,” Harbaugh said. “I mean, from beginning to end, he earned it. “There’s nobody in that locker room, I believe, or anywhere in the building, that questions Odell’s earning this. It’s clear cut, so that’s it.” Beckham, father to a young boy and a more spiritual person than he was as a younger man, has talked about his journey. “He has talked quite a bit about that. And I think it’s – what he says, I listen to what he says because it’s interesting to me. I’ve been in these conversations with him now for, over the years, a lot, but probably in the last six months a lot lot,” Harbaugh said. “And he’s been – this is what he’s been talking about, kind of the growth. I just think he’s going through some things in his life that have really made him take stock of certain things, and what’s important in his life, and it’s neat to see. We all go through that and hopefully continue to. “But he’s in a great place, he’s in a great place, he’s ready to compete. He’s ready to help the Giants be the best team they can be. He wants to make plays, he wants to make blocks, he wants to do whatever he can do to help the team.” Beckham has earned this second chance with the Giants. Let’s hope he does something good with it, and that he can live in peace with however it turns out.

title: NY Giants will keep WR Jalin Hyatt on their practice squad
summary: Former third-round pick Jalin Hyatt, cut on Sunday when the team reached the 53-man roster limit, will return to the New York Giants as part of their practice squad. The Giants traded up in the 2023 NFL Draft to select Hyatt after he won the Fred Belitnikoff Award as the nation’s top wide receiver as […]
full_text: Jalin Hyatt | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Former third-round pick Jalin Hyatt , cut on Sunday when the team reached the 53-man roster limit, will return to the New York Giants as part of their practice squad . The Giants traded up in the 2023 NFL Draft to select Hyatt after he won the Fred Belitnikoff Award as the nation’s top wide receiver as a member of the Tennessee Volunteers. Hyatt’s time with the Giants has been a disappointment. In three seasons, he has just 36 receptions for 470 yards and no touchdowns. Hyatt has barely played the past two seasons, catching just 13 balls. Hyatt suffered a leg injury during training camp in West Virginia when he was cut down by a defensive player. He has not practiced since that time. The Giants cut four draft picks on Sunday — Hyatt, Evan Neal, Darius Muasau, and Eric Gray. They also traded offensive lineman Josh Ezeudu to the Kansas City Chiefs last week. Thus far, Hyatt is the only one to be brought back. Muasau was claimed by the New England Patriots .

full_text: Ex-Giant Darius Muasau was claimed by the Patriots. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants were not awarded any players on waivers Monday as teams moved to acquire players dropped on Sunday when 53-man rosters had to be set for the regular season. The Giants were fifth in the waiver wire priority, but still did not add any players. The Las Vegas Raiders, New York Jets, Arizona Cardinals, and Tennessee Titans — in that order — were ahead of the Giants. The Raiders were awarded just one player, defensive back Darrell Luter. The Jets claimed kicker Blake Grupe and linebacker Trevin Wallace. The Titans claimed three, linebacker Owen Pappoe, defensive back Melvin Smith, and defensive tackle Nazir Stackhouse. Per Paul Schwartz, the Giants did not submit any waiver claims . Former Giants linebacker Darius Muasau , a 2024 sixth-round pick, was claimed by the New England Patriots. Ex-Giants defensive coordinator Shane Bowen is on the Patriots’ defensive staff. The Miami Dolphins, who had the 11th priority in the claim order, were awarded seven players. title: NY Giants will sign Braxton Berrios to their practice squad
summary: One day after somewhat surprisingly leaving him off their initial 53-man roster, the New York Giants are signing veteran wide receiver/return man Braxton Berrios to their practice squad. With Calvin Austin having suffered a season-ending torn ACL, Berrios figures to be the primary punt returner and part of the primary kickoff return duo with Deonte […]
full_text: Braxton Berrios against the Jets last Friday. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect One day after somewhat surprisingly leaving him off their initial 53-man roster, the New York Giants are signing veteran wide receiver/return man Braxton Berrios to their practice squad . With Calvin Austin having suffered a season-ending torn ACL, Berrios figures to be the primary punt returner and part of the primary kickoff return duo with Deonte Banks. Teams can elevate players from the practice squad three times before having to add them to their 53-man rosters, and the Giants figure to do that with Berrios. The Giants cut the 30-year-old Berrios on Sunday, enabling them to keep second-year tight end Thomas Fidone rather than exposing him to waivers in an effort to get him to the practice squad. Entering his eighth season, Berrios has averaged 11.3 yards on 100 career punt returns, 24.9 yards on 91 kickoff returns, and has 140 career pass receptions. Follow our practice squad tracker for all of the moves this afternoon as the Giants build their practice squad, and perhaps adjust their 53-man roster.

full_text: The New York Giants are currently 2.5-point underdogs to the Dallas Cowboys in their season-opening Sept. 13 Sunday Night Football meeting, per Fanduel Sportsbook . The over/under is 48.5. This will be the first regular-season game of the John Harbaugh era as Giants head coach. The last time the Giants and Cowboys met in a season-opening game came in 2023, a year after the Giants surprising run to the playoffs. Dallas embarrassed the Giants in that game, 40-0, setting the stage for a miserable 6-11 season and a 13-38 three-year stretch that led to Harbaugh’s hiring. Fanduel has the Cowboys as -120 to make the playoffs, with the Giants at +265. The Giants have not won a season-opener since defeating the Tennessee Titans 21-20 in 2022. They started 1-5 in 2023, 2-5 in 2024, and 1-4 last season. The Giants had a grueling summer training camp under Harbaugh’s direction. We will have to see how much that matters in Week 1.

title: Practice squad rules 2026, explained
summary: NFL teams including the New York Giants can start building their practice squads as soon as the waiver claim period for players released by Sunday’s 6 p.m. ET deadline to reach the 53-man roster limit is reached. That deadline this year is Monday at 1 p.m.. Practice squad rules How many players? NFL practice squads currently […]
full_text: Could dalen cambre be part of the Giants’ practice squad, or will he be claimed on waivers by another team? | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images NFL teams including the New York Giants can start building their practice squads as soon as the waiver claim period for players released by Sunday’s 6 p.m. ET deadline to reach the 53-man roster limit is reached. That deadline this year is Monday at 1 p.m.. Practice squad rules How many players? NFL practice squads currently consist of 16 players. Teams can carry 17 if one is an international player eligible for a practice squad exemption. For the Giants, that player will be Australian offensive lineman Jarrod Gray. Who is eligible? Here are the current eligibility rules: Players who do not have an accrued season of NFL experience. Free agent players who were on the Active List for fewer than nine games in their only accrued season. A maximum of 10 free agent players who have earned no more than two accrued seasons. A maximum of six free agent players with no limitations to their number of earned accrued seasons. When can teams start building practice squads? Once the waiver claim period ends teams can begin to sign players to their practice squads. This year, that means 1 p.m. ET on Monday. How much do practice squad players make? Per the Collective Bargaining Agreement, players with two accrued seasons or less will earn $13,750 for each week they are on a practice squad. Players with more than two accrued seasons will earn at least $18,350 per week with a maximum of $22,850. Poaching players: Teams can sign players off the practice squad of any other NFL team. That player must be added to the new team’s 53-man roster and be eligible for at least three games. COVID-era practice squad protections which enabled teams to designate four players each week who could not be signed by another team no longer exist. Waiver claim order The waiver claim order is based on the order of the most recent NFL Draft.. Throughout the preseason and the first three weeks of the regular season, the waiver wire order is based on that year’s original NFL Draft order (trades are irrelevant). After the first three weeks of the regular season, the waiver order is based on the standings at the time. The current order is: 1. Las Vegas Raiders 2. New York Jets 3. Arizona Cardinals 4. title: Jets awarded two off waivers, lose one
summary: The Jets were awarded two players off waivers today: kicker Blake Grupe and linebacker Trevin Wallace. They lost quarterback Brady Cook to a waiver claim by the Miami Dolphins. Waiver claims! pic.twitter.com/wLbrIJL54j — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) August 31, 2026 Blake Grupe was brought in because the Jets clearly were not sold on Jason Sanders as […]
full_text: CANTON, OHIO - AUGUST 06: Trevin Wallace #32 of the Carolina Panthers looks on during the first quarter of the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame Game against the Arizona Cardinals at Tom Benson Hall Of Fame Stadium on August 06, 2026 in Canton, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Jets were awarded two players off waivers today: kicker Blake Grupe and linebacker Trevin Wallace. They lost quarterback Brady Cook to a waiver claim by the Miami Dolphins. Waiver claims! pic.twitter.com/wLbrIJL54j — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) August 31, 2026 Blake Grupe was brought in because the Jets clearly were not sold on Jason Sanders as the Jets 2026 kicker. Grupe is a 27 year old kicker who has been in the NFL three years, with stints with the New Orleans Saints and the Indianapolis Colts. He has made 81.9% of his field goal attempts for his career, including 19 0f 27 from beyond 50 yards. A concerning note is that he has made just 75% of his attempts from 40 – 49 yards, a distance that has become almost automatic for the best kickers in the league. One would assume Jason Sanders will be cut to make room for Grupe on the roster. Trevin Wallace is a 23 year old, 6’ 1”, 244 pound linebacker out of Kentucky. He was drafted by the Carolina Panthers with the 72nd overall pick in the third round of the 2024 NFL draft. Wallace played in 25 games with the Panthers over the last two years, starting 20. He is a physical specimen, running a 4.51 40 yard dash with a 37.5” vertical at the 2024 NFL Scouting Combine. A 244 pound man with that kind of explosiveness is a rare commodity, but his lack of football instincts eventually led to the Panthers giving up on him. Now the Jets will try to develop a young linebacker with tremendous physical tools who needs a fresh start. Best case scenario here might be something like Quincy Williams, a young linebacker with great tools who struggled at the start of his career but blossomed into a star with the Jets. Waiver wire pickups are for the most part inconsequential. You are claiming somebody who couldn’t make the top 53 of another team. It’s unlikely that player will become a difference maker for your team. As an example, this time last year the Jets claimed three players off waivers: Cam Jones, Esa Pole and Jelani Woods. Jones and Pole are long gone. Woods is slated to be the team’s TE4 and unless there are injuries in front of him on the depth chart, he will rarely see the field on offense. However, there are occasional exceptions. As just one example, in 2019 the Los Angeles Rams cut little known defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers. The Jets claimed him on waivers. Franklin-Myers was out injured all of 2019, but in subsequent years he has developed into one of the better defensive linemen in the NFL, and is still playing at a high level seven years later. Chances of something like this happening with any one waiver claim are quite low, but you just never know.

summary: The Philadelphia Eagles signed 13 players to their practice squad on Monday afternoon, according to an official team announcement. Here’s a last name alphabetical order overview with analysis to follow. EAGLES PRACTICE SQUAD DT Uar Bernard LB Chance Campbell WR Britain Covey DT Gabe Hall EDGE Keyshawn James-Newby C/G Jake Majors T John Ojukwu RB […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 28: Uar Bernard #93 of the Philadelphia Eagles smiles after a preseason game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field on August 28, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles signed 13 players to their practice squad on Monday afternoon, according to an official team announcement. Here’s a last name alphabetical order overview with analysis to follow. EAGLES PRACTICE SQUAD DT Uar Bernard LB Chance Campbell WR Britain Covey DT Gabe Hall EDGE Keyshawn James-Newby C/G Jake Majors T John Ojukwu RB Dameon Pierce S Maximus Pulley OLB Mason Reiger RB Carson Steele EDGE Joshua Weru S Cole Wisniewski ANALYSIS In case you missed it : Myles Hinton, Cameron Williams, Kapena Gushiken, and Cameron Latu won’t be able to join the Eagles’ practice squad because they were claimed by teams on waivers. I’m surprised Hinton got claimed because he had a pretty bad summer but the Eagles did just play the Bengals in the preseason, so, Cincy must have seen something they liked. I had Williams making my final 53-man roster projection; I thought the Eagles would be reluctant to give up on his potential. Williams might’ve been able to stick if Markel Bell wasn’t injured, which probably prompted the Eagles to keep Fred Johnson around despite the fact he didn’t look good this summer. Gush didn’t play well enough to make the roster but he was the Eagles’ most expensive undrafted rookie free agent signing, which signaled that he previously had interest from other teams after the 2026 NFL Draft. Latu probably just isn’t much of an offensive contributor but he is a really good special teams guy, so, losing him hurts. Notable Eagles practice squad omissions thus far (subject to change): Deontae Lawson and Zion Wilson. They both showed some developmental promise in the preseason games. Would be good to get them on the PS. I didn’t think the Eagles would struggle to get Uar Bernard back on the practice squad, which is why I left him off my final 53-man roster projection. He’s clearly just not ready to play this year. Good to see he’s back, though. The Eagles’ official team site indicates that the team has not yet designated their international exemption slot but I would guess they’re going to use it on Bernard. By doing so, Bernard would be ineligible to play in a game this season … but he also wouldn’t count against their 16-player practice squad limit. Chance Campbell likely would’ve been the fifth off-ball linebacker on the roster if the Eagles kept more than four. Good veteran option to have around for even more depth and special teams help. Britain Covey is a contender to be temporarily elevated to the roster if the Eagles want to use him as their punt returner. It’s currently unclear how else they plan to go about returning punts. Covey also provides depth at slot receiver. Gabe Hall had a good summer relative to expectation. He’s roster-worthy but the Eagles already have five defensive tackles on the team ahead of him. He could get a call up if they deal with interior defensive line injuries. Keyshawn James-Newby missed a lot of practice time this offseason but he flashed just enough to warrant a practice squad spot. Good to be keeping the 2026 seventh-round pick in the building. Jake Majors might’ve made the roster if the Eagles didn’t already have Drew Kendall, Willie Lampkin, and Micah Morris stepping up to make the team. I wouldn’t be surprised if another team poached him from the Eagles’ practice squad this season if they run into offensive line injuries. John Ojukwu missed some time in camp due to injury but I feel like I generally liked what I saw out of him more than Fred Johnson this summer. Totally fine with keeping him around for even more tackle depth. Dameon Pierce popped early in camp before suffering an injury that caused him to miss most of the summer. He then showed some good signs upon returning. Pierce is likely the fourth running back in the team’s pecking order behind Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby, and Will Shipley. He’s an RB injury away from getting called up. Maximus Pullley has some developmental potential at a position where the Eagles are thin. Mason Reiger is the player the Eagles recently brought in for a tryout . Some thought he could be an earlyish Day 3 pick but he likely went undrafted due to medical history concerns. Seems like a good player to take a no-risk chance on with a practice squad spot. Carson Steele is back on the practice squad following some concern that another team might poach him after having a productive preseason with the Eagles. Joshua Weru did not get poached! Great news. Although wildly inexperienced, Weru flashed some real potential in both training camp practices and preseason games. He seems to be closer to contributing than Bernard is, relatively speaking. Interested to see what he looks like next offseason. Cole Wisniewski joins Bernard and KJN as 2026 Eagles seventh-round picks to return to the team on the practice squad. He might’ve had a chance to make the roster if he hadn’t missed most of the Eagles’ offseason practices due to injury issues. Stay tuned for more practice squad news in the coming days!

full_text: Chicago Bears offensive tackle Kiran Amegadjie (72) falls to the turf while trying to block Minnesota Vikings linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel (43) in the third quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis on Dec. 16, 2024. (Chris Sweda/Chicago Tribune/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) The Eagles made their final roster cuts on Sunday and are starting to build their practice squad, which includes Chicago Bears 2024 third-round draft pick Kiran Amegadjie . The 24-year-old blocker is someone new to Philly, but with the team having two offensive tackles claimed through the waiver wire on Monday — Cameron Williams and Myles Hinton —, they were able to bring in someone with long-term potential that they can develop at the position. Amegadjieis 6’5”, 324 pounds, and was drafted out of Yale with the 75th overall pick. Amegadjie played in six games for the Bears his rookie season, but did struggle a bit with his hands, drawing two holding calls and one false start, in addition to two false start flags that were declined. He ended up on IR in Sept. 2025 for an elbow injury, and missed the remainder of what would have been his second season. The Eagles have a strong group of OTs on the active roster, and Amegadjie will now get a chance to learn behind Lane Johnson and Jordan Mailata, and even rookie Markel Bell who has really impressed throughout training camp.

Jenkins had a good summer but was still considered a bubble player. Calcaterra has been dealing with injuries, and even though he’s had some big moments, he’s not a better option than Zach Ertz. Ertz has shown Philly nothing but love since he was traded away years ago, and never ruled out coming back. The TE did have a little dust-up with head coach Nick Sirianni after one of the Eagles-Commanders matchups , but neither seemed to harbor any ill-will about it afterward. Plus, he continues to celebrate his time with the Eagles, and one of the most special memories for him and the City of Philadelphia. One of the greatest catches I’ve ever seen in person! Set the tone for the rest of the game! Legendary https://t.co/XjgxUTNx0b — Zach Ertz (@ZERTZ_86) August 30, 2026 So, what do you think? title: Eagles News: Nick Sirianni listed among people who will define the 2026 NFL season
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … 26 people who will define the NFL in 2026 – SB NationNick Sirianni, Head Coach — Philadelphia Eagles. There is mounting pressure on Nick Sirianni, which is wild after winning the NFC twice and having a Super Bowl ring — but this is a “what […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 20: Head coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles speaks during a press conference during a joint practice with the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Billie Weiss/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … 26 people who will define the NFL in 2026 – SB Nation Nick Sirianni, Head Coach — Philadelphia Eagles. There is mounting pressure on Nick Sirianni, which is wild after winning the NFC twice and having a Super Bowl ring — but this is a “what have you done for me lately?” league, and the Eagles being routinely regarded as a Super Bowl favorite means they need to perform every single season. Sirianni has quickly become the man perceived to be the weak link in the process. A struggling offense has been a problem for each of the past two years, with offensive coordinators being blamed — but Sirianni’s public sideline run-in with A.J. Brown led to the top receiver being traded, and questions raised about whether or not the coach was losing control of the locker room. This is a statement year for Sirianni and the Eagles, who need to assert themselves as the top of the NFC East once more. [BLG Note: Can you guess the one Eagles player who also made this list? It’s not Jalen Hurts.] Eagles depth chart: First look at the initial 2026 roster – BGN The Eagles keeping four quarterbacks feels very silly. At the same time, it’s very on brand for how weird this QB2 situation has been every step of the way. Guess the Eagles holding onto both Dalton and McKee with the hope that a team will trade for one in the coming days? If so, great. But you can’t expect the return will be much. And it could’ve been nice to just actually focus on preparing QB2 for the season instead of doing a competition where the players split the reps and seemingly did not benefit from that setup. Not to mention trying to get Cole Payton developmental snaps in the preseason, which they didn’t really do outside of the first preseason game. Eagles Roster Cuts With BLG and a Phillies Check-In With Anthony Dabbundo! – The Ringer’s Philly Special Sheil is joined by Brandon Lee Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation to break down the Eagles’ final roster cuts and their 53-man roster. Which notable training camp names didn’t make the roster? Anthony Dabbundo then jumps on to discuss the Phillies’ recent hot streak. How are the guys feeling about the team now compared to earlier in the season? SB Nation Launches App Home for Its 200 Fan Communities – Sportico SB Nation is launching an app to pull together content and chats from its network of close to 200 team- and league-focused sports communities. The launch comes as artificial intelligence impacts the amount of web search traffic media publishers receive and algorithmic, video-heavy social media feeds alter how fans connect with each other on game days. The app’s home page will feature a personalized list of posts from a user’s preferred sites, with another tab dedicated to game threads. “People are exhausted by the toxicity of the conversation on social, but they’re also exhausted by feeling like AI worms its way into these conversations,” SB Nation’s head of network John Ness said. “What we supply to folks is like, I feel like I’m talking to real fans who care about what I care about, and it feels like once again I’m having an authentic conversation about the team that spends so much time in my brain overall.” Ness added that users currently talk about being a member of one of the company’s communities, such as the Philadelphia Eagles’ Bleeding Green Nation, but—until now—there was no formal way to signal that support. An audience of readers who go directly to a site is increasingly valuable as certain media leaders talk about a future in which Google potentially sends them close to zero referral traffic if AI answers become more popular. [BLG Note: Hey, a BGN mention AND an NFC East Mixtape mention in this article! Go download the SB Nation app!] Eagles’ Week 1 opponent will be missing several important players; waived players who make sense – PhillyVoice QB Will Levis: Levis is 6’4, 229, he has a big arm, and he can run around a little bit. There’s talent there, and he was not exactly drafted into the best situation in Tennessee. On the downside, he has had some of the more ridiculous lowlights of the last decade. The Eagles already have had a weird, non-sensical offseason in their handling of the backup quarterbacks, and they still have to get rid of one of them. I’m certainly not suggesting they add one to the mess they have on their active roster. But if Levis clears waivers is he worth a spot on the practice squad, just to get a look? Sure, why not? Roster Cuts – Lots of Curve Balls – Iggles Blitz While a lot of people have questions on some of these moves, it is important to note that the Eagles have one of the best rosters in the league. We’re discussing the fringe guys at the bottom of the roster. The backup QB situation remains confusing. If the team gets that sorted out in the coming days, it could be a good thing. It will help if someone can be the clear #2 and focus on that role, not competition. As long as Jalen Hurts stays healthy, this isn’t time sensitive. Backup WBs have mostly been needed late in the season. You can’t count on that, but it is worth noting. I’ve talked about how Howie does a good job of building rosters with one eye on the present and one on the future. This roster feels more like it was built for the present. There are 5 rookies (Lemon, Stowers, Bell, Morris and Payton), but a couple of them could be playing this season. Keeping guys like Moore and Jones makes this feel more about today than tomorrow. Facts and figures, notes and numbers on the Eagles’ 53-man roster – NBCSP The Eagles released all three of their 7th-round picks as part of the roster cutdown to 53 – safety Cole Wisniewski, defensive tackle Uar Bernard and edge Keyshawn James-Newby. Last time the Eagles cut three rookie draft picks at roster cutdown was 2011, when Roseman – in his second year as general manager – released 5th-round pick Julian Vandervelde and 7th-round picks Greg Lloyd and Stanley Havili. Vandervelde and Havili made their way back to the practice squad and both wound up playing for the Eagles – 18 games for Vandervelde and 15 for Rolle. We’ll learn Monday whether Wisniewski, Bernard and James-Newby clear waivers and find their way back to the Eagles’ practice squad. Who made the cut? A player-by-player breakdown of the Eagles’ 53-man roster – The Athletic Eli Stowers: The Eagles selected Stowers in the second round, and it always seemed like a pick with 2027 and beyond in mind, and Stowers did not showcase playmaking skills in the passing game this summer. Unless he sees a spike in his progress behind the scenes, it might be unrealistic to expect much from Stowers this season. How to bet the 2026 NFL season: Three bets to make on each team – ESPN Philadelphia Eagles. 1) OVER 9.5 wins (-156) … 2) Division finishing position: 2 (+230) … 3) Jalen Hurts rushing yards UNDER 424.5 (-110). Philadelphia seems like a team with a lot to prove. With a dominant defense, I like the Eagles to go over their wins projection but finish second in the division. The under on Hurts’ rushing yards total can cash if the Eagles protect their franchise quarterback and reduce designed rushing opportunities. Plus, Hurts seems less enthusiastic about running the ball each and every year. With a deep roster and strong running game, Philadelphia doesn’t need Hurts to accumulate massive rushing numbers to succeed. Four NFL teams keep four QBs on initial 53-man rosters – NFL.com For most of the offseason, we’d discussed the Pittsburgh Steelers’ plan to keep four quarterbacks as an anomaly. It turns out the Steel City footballers weren’t the only club to play the 4-QB card this offseason. Following cutdown day, four NFL…

(Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of a handful of surprises from the Steelers on cutdown day was the team placing starting safety DeShon Elliott on injured reserve — guaranteeing he’ll miss at least the first four games of the regular season. Talking to the media on Monday, Pittsburgh general manger Omar Khan claimed that Elliott had no setbacks recovering from his knee injury despite playing last week, saying it just the “right thing to do” after the safety wasn’t 100%. Already seen as one of the thinnest position groups on the roster, Pittsburgh’s initial safety depth chart has just three names: Jaquan Brisker, Rayshawn Jenkins and rookie Robert Spears-Jennings. To make things more interesting, Brisker has had a quiet summer, never playing in the preseason and missing the last several weeks of practice with an injury. He’s expected to go Week 1, but his level of readiness — and how he’ll look in general — is difficult to gauge from the outside. But assuming Brisker is good to go against the Falcons who will start opposite him? It’s worth throwing veteran cornerback Jalen Ramsey into the mix, who filled in at safety for the secondary-needy Steelers last year. It’s apparent the team still views Ramsey as a nickel defender first and foremost, but starting him at safety to open the season might allow Pittsburgh to field its best 11 on defense with Brandin Echols also being a capable name defending the slot. However, I’d guess the Steelers start Jenkins Week 1. The veteran started nine games in 2023 and has 92 career starts under his belt. In the preseason, his strengths had some clear similarities to Elliott, with Jenkins looking comfortable in the box and being used as a blitzer in Patrick Graham’s aggressive scheme with general success. This stop by Rayshawn Jenkins 😮‍💨 NYJvsPIT on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/4I63pxpt6x — NFL (@NFL) August 21, 2026 Spears-Jennings deserves mention after a strong preseason himself, but the rookie seventh-rounder will almost certainly be starting his NFL career primarily on special teams. And with two safeties on the practice squad currently in Sebastian Castro and Juanyeh Thomas, Pittsburgh will be able to make some elevations to further bolster the depth, although it will mainly be more special teams contributors. The secondary should be able to survive the expected four weeks without Elliott. It’s a big loss, but Jenkins can provide Elliott-esque play, and Ramsey’s versatility means he could rotate in as a safety when the team is in base defense, or if Jenkins just isn’t the right player for the situation. That said, Pittsburgh’s defensive backfield had coverage issues in the preseason, and while it wasn’t a disaster as the team was down most of its starters, there is reason to wonder how those top players will look with little time to gel together before the regular season. Joey Porter Jr. didn’t practice leading up to cutdown day, staying on the PUP list and waiting for a new contract. Ramsey never played in the preseason and missed time with injury, as did Brisker. And now Elliott will miss the opening stretch of the year. There are plenty of talented names on paper, but the Steelers secondary is still a mystery headed into Week 1. What are your thoughts on the Steelers’ safety room? Join the BTSC community and let us know in the comments!

summary: The Seattle Seahawks took care first part of their roster-building process for the 2026 season. full_text: Aug 23, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Seattle Seahawks cornerback Andre Fuller (35) chases down Tennessee Titans tight end Joel Wilson (83) during the second half at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Seattle Seahawks took care first part of their roster-building process for the 2026 season. Seattle begins its Super Bowl repeat push on Sept. 9 against the New England Patriots, a familiar opponent after the Seahawks defeated New England to win Super Bowl 60 . The defending champions are currently 3.5-point favorites over the Patriots at FanDuel Sportsbook . After finishing the preseason, Seattle must reduce its roster to a maximum of 53 players by 3 p.m. PT on Sunday, August 30 . But the initial 53-man roster is only part of the process. Once the waiver wire process is completed, the Seahawks will begin assembling their practice squad, which can provide additional developmental players and emergency depth throughout the season. The claiming period for players placed on waivers during the final roster reduction expires at 10 a.m. PT on Monday, August 31 . After the league distributes the subsequent Personnel Notice confirming the results of the waiver process, teams can begin forming their practice squads. Seattle enters the waiver process with the 32nd and final priority , meaning all 31 other teams will have an opportunity to claim a player before the Seahawks. The waiver order is based on the 2025 regular-season standings through the first three weeks of the 2026 regular season, with Seattle at the bottom after winning the Super Bowl. That makes the Seahawks’ own collection of players particularly important. Several young players who don’t make the initial 53-man roster could potentially return to Seattle after clearing waivers, while veteran players who are not subject to waivers can immediately negotiate with teams or sign with a practice squad. We’ll track every Seahawks practice squad addition, as well as Seattle’s waiver claims, throughout the process. Practice squad formation rules Teams can begin forming their practice squads after the waiver period expires at 1 p.m. ET on Monday, August 31. The NFL will send a subsequent Personnel Notice confirming the results of the waiver process, and teams can begin signing practice squad players after receiving that notice. A player claimed off waivers cannot go directly to a practice squad. A successful waiver claim means that player goes onto the claiming team’s 53-man roster. The player must first clear waivers before becoming eligible to sign with a practice squad. A standard practice squad consists of 16 players. Teams can have a 17th player if that player qualifies for and is designated under the NFL’s International Player Pathway Program. It is worth mentioning that Seahawks have Federico Maranges, iOL that is part of this program. Players who are not subject to waivers can immediately sign with another team or join a practice squad. Players with four or more accrued seasons are unrestricted free agents when released and are not subject to waivers. Players with three or fewer accrued seasons are subject to the waiver process. As such, players like Eric Saubert and Noah Igbinoghene could be cut and brought back to the team later, just as the Seahawks have done in other years with other veterans. For purposes of an accrued season, a player generally needs to be on full pay status for at least six regular-season games. That includes time on a club’s active/inactive list or certain reserve lists like IR and PUP.
