summary: The Seattle Seahawks added a few more players to injured reserve after they cleared Monday’s waiver claims period. Fullback Brock Lampe, offensive tackle Amari Kight, and inside linebackers Aaron Smith and Power Echols were all waived on Sunday with an injury designation. None of them was claimed, which means by rule they revert to Seattle’s […]
full_text: Sep 25, 2025; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Seattle Seahawks tackle Amari Kight (79) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Seattle Seahawks added a few more players to injured reserve after they cleared Monday’s waiver claims period. Fullback Brock Lampe, offensive tackle Amari Kight, and inside linebackers Aaron Smith and Power Echols were all waived on Sunday with an injury designation. None of them was claimed, which means by rule they revert to Seattle’s injured reserve. Unless those players receive an injury settlement to become a free agent (like cornerback Shemar Jean-Charles did) then the next time they’re on the field is 2027. Lampe was brought in after Robbie Ouzts was placed on IR with a season-ending neck injury. Seattle ultimately is rolling with Brady Russell as its main fullback. Meanwhile, Kight had some first-team snaps last year in relief of an injured Josh Jones and Charles Cross during their two wins over the San Francisco 49ers, but struggled in camp and missed the last two games of preseason. Seattle’s injured reserve list is now 10-strong: Bud Clark, Mason Richman, Jake Bobo, Power Echols, Brock Lampe, Amari Kight, Aaron Smith, Robbie Ouzts, Chris Paul Jr, and Irv Charles. Only Charles is designated for return.

Defensive lineman Jared Ivey, who stayed on Seattle’s active roster as an undrafted rookie throughout last year, was claimed by the Atlanta Falcons. summary: It’d be easy to argue the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks were disrespected on the NFL’s hottest offseason ranking, but their superstar wideout certainly wasn’t. Jaxon Smith-Njigba was ranked 5th on the NFL’s Top 100 Players of 2026 list, marking his first career appearance and the highest of any wide receiver this year. He […]
full_text: It’d be easy to argue the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks were disrespected on the NFL’s hottest offseason ranking, but their superstar wideout certainly wasn’t. Jaxon Smith-Njigba was ranked 5th on the NFL’s Top 100 Players of 2026 list, marking his first career appearance and the highest of any wide receiver this year. He also joined Russell Wilson (No. 2, 2020) Richard Sherman (No. 7, 2014) and Marshawn Lynch (No. 9, 2015) as the only Seahawks to ever be placed in the Top 10. No. 5 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/cttIMrAnWn — NFL (@NFL) August 31, 2026 In regards to this season, linebacker LB Ernest Jones IV (No. 97) and quarterback Sam Darnold (No. 21) were previously the only two players from Seattle’s roster to be featured. The four players ranked above JSN (in a TBA order) are Bijan Robinson, Josh Allen, Matthew Stafford, and Myles Garrett. Although Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (No. 7) was also included in the Top 10 when the list’s final players were released on August 21, there was little doubt Smith-Njigba would earn the edge on the ranking and be the top-ranked receiver on this list. Following an offseason where the Seahawks moved on from longtime receivers DK Metcalf and Tyler Lockett, Smith-Njigba was given the lead duties and took advantage of them, accumulating 119 receptions for a league-leading 1,793 receiving yards en route to winning the Offensive Player of the Year award . His historic season landed him a much deserved four-year, $168.6 million extension , making him the highest paid wide receiver in league history — and perhaps slightly less notably, earning himself a spot in the NFL Top 100. So, while several Seahawks such as defensive tackle Leonard Williams, cornerback Devon Witherspoon and safety Nick Emmanwori may have missed the cut and the respect they deserved, it’s good to know Smith-Njigba didn’t.

title: Kyle Shanahan says plan for newly acquired OL is ‘to get him in the group right away’
summary: The San Francisco 49ers had a busy weekend as they cut down to 53 players on a day that always has a degree of roster politics around. While a majority of the team’s moves were expected, there was one surprise: the release of veteran guard Robert Jones, who signed a one-year deal in the offseason. […]
full_text: Sep 29, 2024; Houston, Texas, USA; Houston Texans center Jarrett Patterson (54) during the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at NRG Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The San Francisco 49ers had a busy weekend as they cut down to 53 players on a day that always has a degree of roster politics around. While a majority of the team’s moves were expected, there was one surprise: the release of veteran guard Robert Jones, who signed a one-year deal in the offseason. Jones had been a part of the competition at left guard, but that had been shifting towards rookie Carver Willis as training camp continued. Still, he could’ve been a depth piece for the 49ers after spending the whole offseason with the team. Well, questions were quickly answered as the 49ers traded for Houston Texans offensive lineman Jarrett Patterson, who was a sixth-round pick in 2023. Patterson, 27, has played in 39 games for the Texans, starting 21, with time at both center and guard. He played in all 17 games in 2025, starting five. San Francisco still hasn’t decided on a Week 1 starter at guard, but could also use some center depth with Willis now clearly being in the guard mix this season. What’s the plan for Patterson as he arrives in San Francisco, with Week 1 just over a week away? “To get him in the group right away,” head coach Kyle Shanahan said on Tuesday. “We love that he has some flex at center and guard. It’s still fluid in all our positions in there, so I want to see where he fits in the group in these three days. “That is the hard thing with not just going to Australia, but just not opening on a Sunday. The time that we’re usually used to making some of these decisions have all been sped up. So, I want to get him in the group, see where he fits, just see him in person, see how he can help us at guard, how he can help us at center, and how he stacks up to the other guys.” So, it seems the plan is to test Patterson out at both guard and center, although there isn’t much time to figure that out ahead of Week 1. Shanahan did add that he ‘does not know yet’ who the 49ers Week 1 starter at left guard is, pointing out that it’s fluid following the addition of Patterson. “Nope, [I don’t know the starter at left guard],” Shanahan said. “It’s the truth. Usually, we get all three of these practices, and then by that Monday is like when we come in and usually do leadership council, captains and, ‘all right, this is who we’re rolling with.’ But we haven’t had those three practices yet, and we just added a new guy to the group too. So, it’s truly fluid.”

title: 49ers Practice Squad Tracker: The potential Week 1 punt returner signs
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are starting to make some moves, trimming the 90-man roster to 53. Those that don’t make the 53 have a chance of being placed on the practice squad. The practice squad is important: players on it can travel with the team and do much of the work that any other active […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 13: Buffalo cornerback Brandon Codrington (29) warms up prior to the start of the NFL game between the Buffalo Bills and the Atlanta Falcons on October 13th, 2025 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are starting to make some moves, trimming the 90-man roster to 53. Those that don’t make the 53 have a chance of being placed on the practice squad. The practice squad is important: players on it can travel with the team and do much of the work that any other active player does. They just don’t suit up on game day. That means they can help the 49ers prepare for their Week 1 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams. The 49ers sit as 3.5-point underdogs over at FanDuel Sportsbook . The game is in Melbourne, Australia, with the Rams as the designated home team. Without the Rams’ field to help (which usually gets invaded by 49ers fans), the playing field is severely leveled. An NFL practice squad consists of 17 players. One of which is part of the NFL International Pathway Program, six can be veterans with no cap on experience, and the final 10 must be rookies or second-year players. As of this writing, the full 17 spots are available, so the 49ers have lots of flexibility. Of that practice squad, the 49ers get to designate four protected players, which means they can’t be placed on another team’s active roster (basically to stop poaching). Two players can be promoted to the active roster for one week and return to the squad. If they play an additional consecutive week, then the 49ers have to offer the player a one-year deal. In other words, the 49ers want both young talent they can develop over the season and players who can be absolute backups when injuries occur. Some of these players will be protected and won’t even sniff the field for a year while they develop. Others are chances the 49ers take to hold onto unless they sign to another team’s active roster. Isaac Alarcon will be the International Player Pathway exemption following his release, per Matt Maiocco. That allows the 49ers to have 17 on their practice squad. Maiocco also hinted that running back Khalil Herbert, wide receiver KhaDarel Hodge, and edge rusher Ogbo Okoronkwo would be on the plane for Australia on Wednesday. Whether those are “handshake deals” after being released, or they make the initial 53-man roster remains to be seen. We’ll update this thread in the meantime with any rumors or reports of who the 49ers plan to use to fill out the 17 spots on the squad. Kyle’s update, 9:42 a.m. PT: The Ravens released Adisa Isaac, a former third-round pick from the 2024 NFL Draft. The #Ravens are expected to release OLB Adisa Isaac. A former third-round pick who has been hampered by injuries, Isaac is expected to draw interest from teams looking for a young pass rusher. — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) August 30, 2026 Isaac has a long list of injuries in his short career. He only played four games as a rookie due to a hamstring injury that lingered into the season after sustaining it during training camp. Last August, Isaac dislocated his elbow in the preseason. That elbow injury cost Isaac his 2025 season after he underwent surgery in November. Isaac entered the NFL as a raw, toolsy pass rusher. He has elite traits. While he’s only listed at around 247 pounds, Isaac had a broad jump in the 83rd percentile, while his height, arm length, 40, and vertical jump were all in the 60th percentile. The 49ers could buy low on a player like Isaac and hopefully develop him into a role player. Isaac can also contribute on special teams. He’d be a better fit in Raheem Morris’s scheme, as Isaac could play from a two-point stance. The cupboard is bare at the position after Nick Bosa, Mykel Williams, Sam O, and Romello Height. You’re unlikely to have Williams healthy to begin the season. Isaac gives you a power rusher who can drop in coverage with traits to build on. Why not roll the dice on a former third-rounder to see if he can give you more than what Ogbo Okoronkwo can? Kyle’s update, 10:59 a.m. PT: A couple of other former draft picks at edge rusher have been waived. Jose Ramirez is undersized, listed at 6’1 7/8″ and 242 pounds. He had elite shuttle times with a 3-cone in the 88th percentile and a 20-yard shuttle in the 78th percentile. If the 49ers are looking to add speed on the roster or practice squad, Ramirez is worth a look. Trice tore his ACL in the first preseason game of his rookie year. He hurt the same knee last preseason. Injuries are brutal. Some had high hopes for Trice. It’s unlikely even Raheem Morris, somebody familiar with Trice, would roll the dice on him after multiple injuries. Kyle’s update, 11:16 a.m. PT: The 49ers released Quinton Bell. That’s the first of many moves to come today. Kyle’s update, 12:37 p.m. PT: The 49ers waived tight end Khalil Dinkins. According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, the team plans to bring him back to the practice squad if he clears waivers. Dinkins is an intriguing project at tight end. He was an impressive blocker in the preseason finale. Pat’s Update 1:33 p.m PT: The 49ers have waived LB Jalen Graham . That’s a possible practice squad candidate. As Matt Barrows points out , Jalen’s height + background at safety could be something the 49ers could use. Pat’s Update 1:42 p.m. PT: The 49ers have waived WR Will Pauling . That’s another practice squad candidate. Pat’s update 1:50 p.m. PT: Per Matt Maiocco, the 49ers have waived tight end Hayden Rucci . Things are going a bit quicker now as the deadline approaches. Pat’s update 1:51 p.m. PT : The 49ers have waived defensive back Patrick McMorris. That’s another practice squad candidate. Kyle’s update, 2:15 p.m. PT : Jalen Stroman has been waived, per Maiocco. The 49ers intend to bring him back to the practice squad. Kyle’s update, 2:57 p.m. PT: Any minute now, the 49ers’ full roster should be out. Until then, the team released wide receiver KhaDarel Hodge. Depending on how they feel about the rest of the receiver room, Hodge would be a candidate to return to the practice squad and be elevated on game day to cover kicks. Kyle’s update, Monday, 10:36 a.m. PT: The 49ers are building their practice squad. According to Matt Barrows, edge rusher Ogbo Okoronkwo, tight end Khalil Dinkins, and wide receiver Wesley Grimes will all sign with the practice squad. Kyle’s update, 11:17 a.m. PT: Linebacker Jalen Graham and defensive tackle Sebastian Valdez will also join the practice squad, according to Barrows. Mike Garafolo tweeted that wide receiver Will Pauling will also join the practice squad. Vic Tafur tweeted that running back Sincere McCormick will also sign to the practice squad. That brings the practice squad to 7 members. Pat’s update 12:07 p.m. PT : For those of you hoping to see Darrell Luter or Bryson Eason coming to the 49ers practice squad, you will be disappoited. Both have been claimed off waivers. Easeon was claimed by the Kansas City Chiefs and Darrell Luter was claimed by the Las Vegas Raiders. title: 49ers expect to get a few positive reinforcements back at practice this week
summary: The San Francisco 49ers will get Nick Bosa and George Kittle back at practice this week. Kyle Shanahan explained what the workload would look like for both: “With three days before we go, we’re balancing it out with both of them. We don’t want them to go three days in a row, so we’re going […]
full_text: GLENDALE, AZ - JANUARY 5: Nick Bosa #97, George Kittle #85, Fred Warner #54 and Kyle Juszczyk #44 of the San Francisco 49ers on the sideline before the game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on January 5, 2025 in Glendale, Arizona. The Cardinals defeated the 49ers 47-24. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers will get Nick Bosa and George Kittle back at practice this week. Kyle Shanahan explained what the workload would look like for both: “With three days before we go, we’re balancing it out with both of them. We don’t want them to go three days in a row, so we’re going to do a little on some of these days, and more on one. Both of them are on a little different schedule. It’s a little different now. Usually, we have these three-day practices, then we get three days off. And then we kind of settle everything that bonus Monday of the week. We already had our three days off because of our travel deal. Now we have these three bonus practices. Then we’ll get on our plane and go. Our Monday where we kind of settle everything will be our Saturday in Australia.” Shanahan said this coming Saturday will be Monday for the team, just because they’re creatures of habit and because the schedule is generally the same as in most years. When Kittle spoke a couple of Sundays ago, he said if he wasn’t going to play in Melbourne, it would make more sense for him to stay back. Shanahan was asked if the team felt like they needed to decide between Kittle playing over the next couple of days, to determine whether he’d travel with the team: “I don’t think you have to do anything. I think if we didn’t think he was going to play, though, and it was looking that way, I think it’d be much nicer to make that decision before we left instead of having him go through all that. It’s also a long time that we’re out there. So to be away from the team for a week, not for camaraderie or anything, but just the training staff and things like that, and being away from meetings is also a big deal too. But, hopefully these three days that we have, these three practices will go the right way and make it an easy decision to get him on the plane.” As for Nick Bosa, Shanahan said he initially was missing practice due to tendinitis. But more recently, it’s more of a maintenance thing where the team is being smart with their star defensive player: “I mean, you guys see him on the field working out. He’s feeling great. We’re deciding how much we want to do in team settings going against people and stuff before we get out there. And that’s what we’ve kind of put out for these three days. Again, they’re not going to go all of them, but we’re going to get them in in these three days. And hopefully that continues what we’ve seen when they haven’t been out there, and then we’ll be on to Australia with them.” And here’s John Lynch on Bosa: “Nick’s pretty blessed with tremendous genes and was going along great. So, the intention when he came back was that he was right. When he upped the activity, he got sore. And so he backed off. And we put together a really good plan that thinks that we believe will have him ready for Australia. And I always believe that the athlete knows their body better than anyone, and Nick certainly takes that to the nth degree. He knows his body extremely well and knows what it takes to have him ready. We saw him one year in a contract year come in here like on a Thursday and play pretty well on Sunday. So, got a lot of faith in his ability to do that.” Shanahan would not name who the starting left guard is or the backup running back, saying he doesn’t know and that was the truth. He added that adding Jarrett Patterson makes the offensive line fluid, and the team will use the three practices to figure that out. Here’s more from Shanahan on his expectations and the plan for Patterson: To get him in the group right away. We love that he has some flex at center and guard. It’s still fluid in all our positions in there, so I want to see where he fits in the group in these three days. That is the hard thing with not just going to Australia, but just not opening on a Sunday. The time that we’re usually used to making some of these decisions have all been sped up. So, I want to get him in the group, see where he fits, just see him in person, see how he can help us at guard, how he can help us at center, and how he stacks up to the other guys.” Drew Greenlaw will be on a maintenance schedule all year. He won’t practice three days in a row. The team is still getting to know Mike Evans. Shanahan said he’s never practiced three days in a row. He’ll be on a similar schedule that Trent Williams and Christian McCaffrey have been on: “Mike’s still coming back from his injury. We should, I think we’ll get him down there the first Saturday, which I look at as a Monday, but possibly on one of these three days but he’s ahead of schedule, doing good. But, we know with Mike and where he is at in his career, we’ll definitely have to treat him differently.” Safety Malik Mustapha returns to practice for the first time in over a month. The same is true for Dominick Puni, Vederian Lowe, Kurtis Rourke, and Kyle Juszczyk. According to The Athletic’s Matt Barrows, Mike Evans, Gracen Halton, Renardo Green, Brayden Willis, Luke Gifford, Jacob Cowing, and Nate Hobbs were all working on the side. Nick Bosa, Romello Height, and Ephesians Prysock were not seen. But they may have made an appearance once the media left practice after the first 15 minutes or so.

full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 13: Ashtyn Davis #29 of the San Francisco 49ers defends in coverage during the first quarter of a preseason NFL football game against the Tennessee Titans at Levi's Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers announced the re-signing of safety Ashtyn Davis and punter Corliss Waitman to one-year deals. To make room for them on the roster, cornerback Nate Hobbs ( groin ) and linebacker Nick Martin ( hamstring ) were placed on the Injured Reserve. Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports said Martin is expected to return at some point during the middle of the season. He added that Hobbs will return and contribute at some point this year, but didn’t note when. It was unlikely that Martin would contribute defensively, even before he was hurt. The IR may have been an option for Martin, regardless, so the team can keep him on the roster without using a roster spot. As for Hobbs, the team must feel good about what he can potentially bring to the table when healthy. Any player who lands on the Injured Reserve can be brought back. The difference between Martin and Hobbs, compared to Austen Pleasants and Christian Kirk , is that the former two, along with anybody else the team places on the IR, don’t need to be designated to return. Davis will live on special teams. Whenever you see a safety signing, you’re going to wonder whether it means Malik Mustapha is further away from returning than expected. But then you remember that the 49ers only kept a couple of safeties and the depth is next to nothing, even when you count Mustapha. A few teams released their punter on Sunday, in a procedural move that is becoming the norm. You don’t have to worry about somebody else signing your punter after everyone else has submitted their roster. We’ll see if this becomes an annual transaction for the Niners.

title: 3 takeaways from the 49ers’ initial 53-man roster: Deebo Samuel’s versatility helps everybody
summary: The San Francisco 49ers submitted the 53-man roster, down from 90, on Sunday afternoon. As far as surprises go, there weren’t many, but there are takeaways from the roster and how the 49ers are going to operate with certain position groups. Here are three takeaways from the 49ers’ 53-man roster: Deebo Samuel allows the 49ers […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 20: Deebo Samuel Sr. #19 of the San Francisco 49ers looks on before the preseason game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers submitted the 53-man roster , down from 90, on Sunday afternoon. As far as surprises go, there weren’t many, but there are takeaways from the roster and how the 49ers are going to operate with certain position groups. Here are three takeaways from the 49ers’ 53-man roster: Deebo Samuel allows the 49ers to carry three RBs and Kyle Juszczyk The 49ers placed Isaac Guerendo on the reserve/PUP list , but the 49ers usually carry four running backs and their fullback. 49ers rookie Kaelon Black impressed during the preseason, and the return of Jordan James instilled enough confidence in the organization to carry three running backs initially. Deebo Samuel will operate as the fourth running back and mix in with Christian McCaffrey. Sincere McCormick made a push to crack the roster, but in a pinch, he can be called right back to Santa Clara. It remains to be seen if Black will spell McCaffrey more in 2026, but Samuel is a part of the plan at running back and allows the team flexibility. The great left guard debate If you wanted clarity on who will start at left guard in Australia against the Rams, the 53-man roster didn’t provide any. Carver Willis and Connor Colby were locks to make the roster, but the trade for interior offensive lineman Jarrett Patterson from Houston throws another option in the mix. With the week leading up to the season opener, Patterson is here as a veteran presence. So who will it be? Will the 49ers start the rookie Willis, the second-year Colby, or opt for the veteran in Week 1? A week of practice will likely determine the starter. Which linebacker(s) are headed to IR? The 49ers have to create two spots for punter Corliss Waitman and long snapper Jon Weeks. It’s assumed that one or both, Luke Gifford or Nick Martin, will be placed on IR . Seven linebackers made the 53-man roster, but the 49ers are doing some gymnastics to fill all the spots. Could Deion Jones make it back to the practice squad, or Jalen Graham (Editor’s note: Jalen Graham has signed to the practice squad)? The team will need options on special teams at linebacker. Fred Warner, Dre Greenlaw, Jaden Dugger, Tatum Bethune, and Garrett Wallow are a deep group of players, but it will be interesting to see the roster moves with the group.

title: 49ers lose UDFA Bryson Eason to the Chiefs; 2 players the Niners should add to the practice squad
summary: It’ll be another busy day. Teams have until 10 a.m. PT to claim players off waivers. We’ll also find out about the practice squad as the day goes along. Lastly, we’ll hear more about any potential Injured Reserve moves and potential designations to return later this afternoon. Darrell Luter didn’t look great in the preseason. […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - JULY 27: Bryson Eason #67 of the San Francisco 49ers works out during training camp practice at SAP Performance Facility on July 27, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’ll be another busy day. Teams have until 10 a.m. PT to claim players off waivers. We’ll also find out about the practice squad as the day goes along. Lastly, we’ll hear more about any potential Injured Reserve moves and potential designations to return later this afternoon. Darrell Luter didn’t look great in the preseason. That didn’t stop the Raiders from claiming him . Bryson Eason failed to build on a strong Week 1. But he still played well. That was enough for the Chiefs to claim him. Kansas City was 9th on the waiver wire. Eason fell to a numbers game at defensive tackle. It’s an unfortunate loss. He looked the part. Was a smart player who held his own against the run. There wasn’t much to offer in the passing game, but you could argue that’s true for the majority of the defensive tackles on the 49ers roster. I’d love to be a fly on the wall to see how much draft status played a part in this decision. Eason outplayed Alfred Collins in the preseason. You could argue he was just as good, if not better, than CJ West during the games. But those were draft picks and you’re not going to cut ties with the players you invested in the draft just a year ago. I wrote about three players below, but one was claimed. You’re never going to complain about being 28th on the waiver wire. It means you’re coming off a season where you won a playoff game. But being low on the totem pole meant the 49ers were mostly stuck with what’s already on the roster when it’s time to make moves on the waiver wire. Perhaps the 49ers didn’t want to add any player to their immediate roster, which would’ve meant more immediate changes to the roster. But you can still poach players from the practice squad, or sign them before another team does, once they’ve cleared waivers. That’s the case with the final two players. S Kapena Gushiken Vic Fangio gave Gushiken the nickname “Gush” in OTAs. He’s an undrafted rookie free agent out of Ole Miss who worked with the Eagles starters at times during training camp. He’s undersized, listed at 5’9″, 189 pounds, but is a superb athlete. Gushiken ran a 4.35 40, had a vertical jump of 41″, and a broad jump of 11′ at Ole Miss’s Pro Day last spring. He registered the third-fastest GPS time in college football in 2024. It seemed as though Gushiken was a lock to make the roster up until the final preseason game. Fangio said it would be a big game for him. However, he missed three tackles, gave up a first-down reception, and allowed a touchdown, which likely sealed his fate. He was an aggressive tackler in the two games prior and gave up next to nothing in coverage. In every game, Gushiken was active on special teams. One of the misses occurred on special teams. And you can see where his size would be an issue as a gunner, but the closing speed and overall athleticism give you value on special teams and something to work with at safety. Update: Gushiken was claimed by the Colts . Indianapolis was 16th on the waiver wire. OT Christian Jones Jones is a right tackle who cross-trained on the left side, which likely hurt his development. Jones, 6’5″, 320 pounds, was drafted in the fifth round of the 2024 NFL Draft. He didn’t play more than 70 snaps as a rookie and was on the Injured Reserve until December of last season due to a knee injury. The arm length, hand size, and athleticism are there. He only played 10 snaps at left tackle in the Hall of Fame Game before playing right tackle in every other game. At 26, Jones is still green enough to develop into a swing tackle. The former Texas Longhorn is not a bad player. He needs to refine his technique, but the strength and movement skills are there. On the practice squad, Jones could continue to develop as a player in hopes of impressing enough to land as a backup next year. Update: Jones was claimed by EDGE Isaiah Foskey Foskey played edge rusher for the Bengals. He was a second-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft. He had a strong preseason, recording 11 pressures. His tackling was shoddy, but Foskey showed enough as a pass rusher and was comfortable dropping into coverage, where it’s worth a waiver claim — especially for a team struggling to generate a pass rush. Foskey has good size and length at nearly 6’5″, 264 pounds, with 34″ arms. He ran a 4.58 40 and had a broad jump in the 89th percentile, so the get-off should be there. The 49ers would be banking on the second-round pedigree, Notre Dame’s all-time sack leader, and a player who plays hard. The idea is to upgrade your depth at edge rusher. Foskey allows you to get younger and more athletic.

title: Raiders expected to claim former 49ers CB with top waiver spot
summary: The San Francisco 49ers had a bevy of cuts on Sunday as they trimmed down to their 53-man roster. As always, roster politics is a factor, hence why the team cut both their starting long snapper and punter, but there were some interesting decisions made overall. San Francisco went with just four running backs, including […]
full_text: Dec 17, 2023; Glendale, Arizona, USA; San Francisco 49ers cornerback Darrell Luter (28) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The San Francisco 49ers had a bevy of cuts on Sunday as they trimmed down to their 53-man roster. As always, roster politics is a factor, hence why the team cut both their starting long snapper and punter, but there were some interesting decisions made overall. San Francisco went with just four running backs, including Kyle Juszczyk, with Isaac Guerendo going on PUP. While expected, that puts a lot of faith on rookie Kaelon Black and second-year pro Jordan James to carry the load behind Christian McCaffrey. The 49ers kept their youngsters at receivers, as Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins both made the roster. Christian Kirk went on IR, while the team elected to cut players like undrafted free agent Will Pauling. San Francisco kept their standard four tight ends, while having nine offensive linemen make the team, not including Austen Pleasants (IR, to return). That included Jarrett Patterson, whom the 49ers traded for with the Houston Texans just before the deadline. On defense, the 49ers kept nine defensive linemen, including undrafted free agent rookie James Thompson Jr., and seven linebackers, as Nick Martin, Garrett Wallow, Luke Gifford, and Jaden Dugger all made the team. In the secondary, the 49ers had some camp battles, but kept six cornerbacks, with rookie Ephysians Prysock making the team over former fifth-round pick Darrell Luter Jr. Luter was a candidate for the practice squad, but it appears he won’t make it there. According to Adam Schefter, Luter is expected to be among the players claimed by the Las Vegas Raiders, who have the top claim spot on the waiver wire. The Raiders kept five cornerbacks on their 53-man roster: Taron Johnson, Hezekiah Masses, Jermod McCoy, Darien Porter, Decamerion Richardson, and Eric Stokes. Luter will join a group without much experience, so he could earn some early playing time in the cornerback room there. The 49ers also cut Eli Apple and Jakob Robinson from the room, and both could be candidates to return on the practice squad. We’ll see what other roster moves the 49ers make with a number of players currently injured, but they may have to look elsewhere for additional corner depth now.

title: Which 49ers player landing on the IR would be the worst-case scenario?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers’ 53-man roster is finalized — until they make another five or so moves today. With the team parting ways with long-snapper Jon Weeks and punter Corliss Waitman temporarily, there are a couple of roster spots that are up for grabs. Unfortunately, the 49ers have several options on the roster to place […]
full_text: The San Francisco 49ers’ 53-man roster is finalized — until they make another five or so moves today. With the team parting ways with long-snapper Jon Weeks and punter Corliss Waitman temporarily, there are a couple of roster spots that are up for grabs. Unfortunately, the 49ers have several options on the roster to place on the Injured Reserve. We don’t know how severe some of these injuries are. What we do know is that you can designate up to eight players to return in the regular season — two of those were used on Christian Kirk and Austen Pleasants. Let’s take the linebackers, for example. Luke Gifford and Nick Martin are both dealing with hamstring injuries. Martin’s happened in the second preseason game, while Gifford sustained his injury early on in training camp. Keeping seven linebackers makes it feel like at least one of these players is destined to land on the IR. In the secondary, the 49ers have a pair of players who were in line to start nursing hamstring injuries. Renardo Green’s injury happened in the second preseason game, while Malik Mustapha has been out since the end of July . The team has been mum on both injuries. The lack of depth paired with the importance of both positions in Raheem Morris’s defense makes for a scary proposition if either were to miss time. The unknown for seemingly every injury leads to speculation. Kyle Shanahan said Vederian Lowe was an IR candidate along with Kirk. Lowe has missed a month with a high-ankle sprain. If he goes on the IR, that would mean rookie Enrqiue Cruz is the swing tackle, unless the team would shuffle the deck enough where the rookie wouldn’t see the field. Lowe isn’t the only player dealing with an ankle injury. Rookie Romello Height has had two ankle injuries in the past month. Height could return to practice on Monday. But he didn’t play in the preseason finale, making you wonder if it’s an injury that’ll linger into the regular season. There are six IR candidates, and we left out a couple. Rookie Ephesians Prysock (shoulder) and Nate Hobbs (groin) could easily be on the list. Which 49ers player landing on the IR would be the worst-case scenario? My answer: The obvious answer is Renardo Green. He’s the closest “matchup cornerback” the team has. Height would be a big blow to the 49ers’ pass-rushing depth. The options at edge are thin as it is, and that’s under the assumption that Nick Bosa will be ready to roll for Week 1 — which is a dangerous game to play, knowing it’s unlikely he plays 80% of the snaps. But I’ll go with Malik Mustapha. You have Ji’Ayir Brown, Marques Sigle, and that’s the depth chart. The only defensive snaps Siran Neal played in the preseason were at cornerback. I’m sure Upton Stout could play safety in a pinch, but that would mean you move Deommodore Lenoir inside and Jack Jones has to play on the outside — moves most fans would probably root for. The point is the depth at the position is shaky. You’re one injury away from needing to uproot everything. Mustapha could stabilize that if he’s healthy. While Mustapha isn’t a lock to start, he has the best sample size as a pro (he was quite good as a rookie) and has the highest ceiling of the three safeties. In my mind, Mustapha is one of the wild cards on the 49ers’ defense this season and a player who could really help unlock the ceiling of this defense. Not having him early in the season would be detrimental to the defense. Who is your answer? Scroll down and let us know in the comments.

title: Buccaneers bring back Sean Murphy-Bunting
summary: Earlier today, we speculated that there may be a potential reunion between Tampa Bay and one of its Super Bowl champion defensive backs. The “Grave Diggers” was Tampa’s moniker during the team’s dominant playoff run in 2020. At the forefront of the team’s success was their pass defense. The pass-rush, led by Shaq Barrett, J.P.P., […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - JANUARY 17: Sean Murphy-Bunting #23 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers stiff arm Michael Thomas #13 of the New Orleans Saints as he runs with the ball after intercepting a pass thrown by Drew Brees #9 of the New Orleans Saints during the second quarter in the NFC Divisional Playoff game at Mercedes Benz Superdome on January 17, 2021 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Earlier today, we speculated that there may be a potential reunion between Tampa Bay and one of its Super Bowl champion defensive backs. The “Grave Diggers” was Tampa’s moniker during the team’s dominant playoff run in 2020. At the forefront of the team’s success was their pass defense. The pass-rush, led by Shaq Barrett, J.P.P., Ndamukong Suh, Vita Vea, and co., feasted on offensive lines while the team’s young defensive backfield of Carlton Davis, Jamel Dean, Antoine Winfield Jr., Jordan Whitehead, Mike Edwards, and Sean Murphy-Bunting feasted on quarterbacks. Amidst the unit’s generational run through some of the league’s most iconic all-time passers (Brees–Rodgers–Mahomes), few ate more than Sean Murphy-Bunting. In four playoff games, Murphy-Bunting snagged himself three interceptions— Including the interception that set up one of the most legendary plays in team history, Scotty Miller’s Hail Mary touchdown catch. Across four seasons in the red and pewter, SMB wore a good amount of hats. He flipped between starter over as well as back up behind Jamel Dean, he played games inside at nickel, and also as an outside corner. In his Buccaneer career, he totaled six interceptions, four forced fumbles, and scooped up a loose ball as well. SMB left Tampa Bay in 2023, signing with the Tennessee Titans. After just one season in Tennessee, he moved out west joining the Arizona Cardinals. Murphy-Bunting did not play in 2025, however, in his two healthy seasons away from Todd Bowles the former Buccaneer stayed productive pulling in five interceptions, four forced fumbles, and a fumble recovery. While he is only joining the Bucs’ practice squad, he could certainly find his way to the active roster sooner rather than later— especially considering the team’s questionable depth at defensive back. It’s very unlikely the Bucs will be getting back the Sean Murphy-Bunting of old, but there will always be value in a defensive player who has a nose for the ball and comfort in the scheme. Sean Murphy-Bunting has proven to be a ball hawk that comes with a résumé of success in Todd Bowles’ defense.

Quarterback Easton Stick joins the club’s practice squad after being waived by the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, August 30. Tampa Bay’s practice squad currently sits at 16 out of a possible 17 players. Stick (6-1, 224) has appeared in six career games for the Los Angeles Chargers, making four starts and completing 112-of-175 passes (64.0%) for 1,133 yards and three touchdowns against one interception for an 85.7 passer rating. He originally entered the league as a fifth-round selection (No. 166 overall) by the Chargers in the 2019 NFL Draft and spent six seasons with the organization before joining the Atlanta Falcons in 2025 and Colts in 2026. He played collegiately at North Dakota State University (2014-18), starting 52-of-55 games and finishing as the FCS’s all-time winningest quarterback with a 49-3 record as a starter. Stick concluded his career as NDSU’s all-time leader in passing yards (8,693), passing touchdowns (88), total offense (11,216) and touchdowns responsible for (129). He helped the Bison win four FCS national championships, including three as the starting quarterback. As a senior in 2018, he earned first-team Associated Press All-America honors and was named the Missouri Valley Football Conference Offensive Player of the Year. The Omaha, Nebraska, native will wear No. 16 for Tampa Bay. (Courtesy of the Buccaneers Communications Department.)

summary: Tampa Bay has loved reunions in the past, could another one be featured in the near future? Jason Licht and co. passed down their final decisions and the roster is set (for now). full_text: Football: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Jordan Whitehead (33) and Mike Edwards (32) during game vs New York Giants at Raymond James Stadium. Tampa, FL 11/22/2021 CREDIT: Simon Bruty (Photo by Simon Bruty/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images) (Set Number: X163871 TK1) Tampa Bay has loved reunions in the past, could another one be featured in the near future? Jason Licht and co. passed down their final decisions and the roster is set (for now). Noteworthy oddities, would be some of the lack of depth in pockets of the roster— Namely the safety postion. The Buccaneers chose to equip themselves with just three safeties— Tykee Smith, Antoine Winfield Jr., and Miles Killebrew. One backup… Tampa Bay fans can clench up and cross their fingers that Winfield Jr. and Tykee Smith remain completely healthy and don’t miss any time. A three-safety depth chart is not the standard and aside from leaving the Buccaneers vulnerable, it is a relevant talking point because it carries the implications that there may be more moves to come. What moves are the Buccaneers in position to make? The Buccaneers do have some former players at the position available, fan favorites at that. Both Mike Edwards and Jordan Whitehead are without a team. Neither is the player that they were when both they and Tampa Bay’s defense were at their peak at the beginning of the decade, but as depth pieces each represent interesting options. Whitehead and Edwards are very different players stylistically, however, both can bring value to a team that’s safety position has the depth of the shallow end of the pool— Making a reunion a genuine possibility. Would you like to see a return of one of Tampa’s Super Bowl champions?

full_text: NASHVILLE, TN - AUGUST 29: Tennessee Titans quarterback Hendon Hooker (16) throws a pass from the end zone in front of Chicago Bears defensive lineman Jeremiah Martin (69) during a preseason game between the Tennessee Titans and Chicago Bears, August 29, 2026 at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tennessee. They are allowed to have 17. My assumption is that they are holding that last spot for Xavier Restrepo, who was released today. They have to wait until he clears waivers tomorrow to officially add him. Of course, there is a chance that another team will claim him. They went heavy on receivers, which makes sense considering they only have five receivers currently on the active roster. They can elevate two players each week to the active roster. As long as they only have five receivers on the active roster, I would expect one of the players elevated to be a receiver. full_text: Tennessee Titans center Pat Coogan (79) and tackle Austin Deculus (76) run drills during mandatory minicamp at Vanderbilt Health Football Center in Nashville, Tenn., Wednesday, June 17, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Tennessee Titans named their initial 53-man roster on Sunday evening . Among the bigger surprises, veteran guard Cordell Volson and wide receiver Bryce Oliver got cut. Fan favorite Xavier Restrepo was among the inclusions, and defensive end Truman Jones was another surprise. The roster isn’t finalized. The Titans own the fourth spot in the waiver wire priority. Transactions will be processed on Monday at 12 noon ET. We’ve identified three Titans players at risk of immediately losing their roster spot. Austin Deculus, OT Titans fans were disappointed to see Austin Deculus make the initial roster. The veteran swing tackle was absolutely dreadful throughout training camp and the preseason. Despite playing against backups, Deculus allowed three sacks and was terrible in pass protection. Imagine if he had to play against regular-season starters. The Titans desperately need to find an upgrade via the waiver wire process. Former Titan Oli Udoh and Tank Lichtenhan qualify as potential options. Garrett Dellinger, IOL Analyzing the entire 53-man roster, Garrett Dellinger is arguably the biggest surprise inclusion. He garnered little-to-no fan hype during training camp and the preseason. The Titans even kept him over Volson, who plays the same guard position and had guaranteed money on his contract. It’s a heartwarming story for Dellinger, but the Titans could be considering him a placeholder for an upcoming waiver claim at cornerback. Do they need him, Jackson Slater, and Pat Coogan? Probably not. Jerrick Reed II, S Jerrick Reed II was among the slightly surprising defensive backs. He made the roster over guys like Keydrain Calligan, Mario Goodrich III, and Bishop Fitzgerald. Kendell Brooks was waived-injured, and could have taken this roster spot if he was healthy. Reed is an experienced special teams player, and he’s currently the fourth safety. We might be wrong by including him on this list. Perhaps Mike Borgonzi will identify a safety upgrade via waivers.

title: Commanders takeaways from Dan Quinn, Adam Peters press conference
summary: The Commanders formally set their initial 53-man roster on Sunday and then made some tweaks to it. Expect that pattern to continue over the next two weeks, as Washington prepares to play the Philadelphia Eagles on Sept. 13 in the regular-season opener.   Monday afternoon marked the first time head coach Dan Quinn and general […]
full_text: The Commanders formally set their initial 53-man roster on Sunday and then made some tweaks to it. Expect that pattern to continue over the next two weeks, as Washington prepares to play the Philadelphia Eagles on Sept. 13 in the regular-season opener. Monday afternoon marked the first time head coach Dan Quinn and general manager Adam Peters spoke publicly since the weekend’s roster cuts, and they explained why actions were taken and how this team was formed. Here are some key takeaways from that session with on-site reporters: Commanders confidence in Nick Allegretti The Commanders have been stress-tested at the center spot. Nick Allegretti suffered a calf strain in Washington’s first training camp practice and aggravated it two practices into his return. Julian Good-Jones and rookie Matt Gulbin proved to be insufficient backups – Good-Jones was since released and is on the practice squad – at that position, which the Commanders did not address via waiver claims or a free-agent signing. That has led to major concerns, considering the value placed on centers as a cerebral hub within coordinator David Blough’s system. Quinn delivered some positive news on Monday, relaying to reporters that Allegretti returned to practice. There’s also a great deal of internal confidence in the veteran despite a lack of preseason or camp. If Allegretti validates such faith and is available all season, all this center talk will be rendered moot. “Not having Nick for most of camp was something we had to work through, but we have a ton of confidence in him,” Peters said. “He has played 3,000-some odd snaps in this league, and he has played good football for us before. He went through the whole offseason, so we’re really confident. “He’s not a guy who needs a ton of reps, especially from a mental standpoint.” While Quinn stated that the Commanders are still working through the center situation and are not afraid to add to it, they also believe that Gulbin can step into a game and play. “I feel the strength with him in the pocket,” Quinn said. “He’s not someone who repeats a lot of mistakes. Is he going to make some? Hell yeah. That’s part of training camp and learning from them. …To see him not repeat those, that’s a sign of a mature player who is making a lot of progress.” Jayden Daniels’ heavy workload Jayden Daniels played just three snaps during the Commanders preseason slate, but the third-year quarterback still got tons of work in over the summer. His accuracy, leadership and poise were lauded by many throughout the course of camp, and the Commanders believe he’s all set to have a huge year following a 2025 campaign plagued by injury . He’s healthy now and ready to go. “I love Jayden’s readiness,” Quinn said. “He took over 500 snaps this training camp. That’s almost like a half season’s worth of reps. His timing with Stef (Diggs) and Terry (McLaurin) is invaluable. With a new system, to put that kind of work in – he’s elite with the ball in his hands. He’s decisive in this system.” Why Trey Amos went on IR The Commanders consider Trey Amos their top cornerback. The second-year pro hasn’t practiced but twice since fracturing his fibula last year, with soft-tissue soreness and then an ankle sprain preventing his return to regular action. Washington placed him on injured reserve with a designation to return on Sunday, meaning he’ll miss the first four games at least. After all that time missed, the Commanders want to be cautious about his return to prominence. “Not having Trey, he hasn’t played since midseason last year, so we want to take it slow with him,” Peters said. “That’s why we put him on IR. Could he have come back in a few weeks? Maybe. But, with the advances in sports science and what it will take for him to get ready to play after not having played since midseason last year, we wanted to take that a little bit slower. We’re confident he’ll be ready when it’s time for him to come out.” The Commanders are happy with the Rasul Douglas and Fabian Moreau additions to this point, which will help the team survive until Amos returns. Seven receivers, Adam? The Commanders went heavy on receivers Sunday, keeping seven of them on their 53-man roster. That’s an unorthodox number to be sure, but Washington didn’t want to let several of them go in what might be the deepest position group on the team. “It ended up being a really deep room,” Peters said. “All of those guys have a little bit different skill set and different ways they can help our team. Some of them are better on special teams. Some of them are better inside or outside. “We wanted to keep a mix of all those guys, and we thought more than who we kept are NFL players, and so we wanted to keep all the guys that could help us this year. Seven is probably — you usually keep maybe six; five, six or seven, you can keep any of those numbers — whatever you do, you’re taking away from another position. You try to balance that out to get the best 53 you can get. We certainly felt we had seven really capable NFL players at that position.” Better news on the injury front Quinn and Peters announced some positive news regarding Washington’s difficult bout with injuries over the second half of training camp, with Allegretti, defensive lineman Daron Payne, quarterback Marcus Mariota, tight end Ben Sinnott and linebacker Jordan Magee all returning to practice. There’s also optimism, per ESPN reporter John Keim , that running back Bill Croskey-Merritt and edge rusher K’Lavon Chaisson (knee) will be able to return next week. The outlook on top pass rusher Odafe Oweh is murkier, with his availability for the season opener in minor doubt. On Odafe Oweh: Dan Quinn said he won't practice today but he's "making a lot of progress. As we get into next week, thrilled he's making this kind of progress to get ready." Did not say he'll play in the opener, but will know more when he returns. — John Keim (@john_keim) August 31, 2026

title: Washington Commanders re-sign Fabian Moreau, Shy Tuttle after roster cuts
summary: The Commanders announced their initial 53-man roster on Sunday evening, but we all knew it was never built to last.   It contained two players destined for injured reserve, with some glaring gaps in important position groups.   The team got right in some ways on Monday afternoon, with two veterans returning to the mix. […]
full_text: The Commanders announced their initial 53-man roster on Sunday evening, but we all knew it was never built to last. It contained two players destined for injured reserve, with some glaring gaps in important position groups. The team got right in some ways on Monday afternoon, with two veterans returning to the mix. Washington re-signed cornerback Fabian Moreau and defensive lineman Shy Tuttle, the team announced. Left tackle Laremy Tunsil and defensive lineman Johnny Newton headed to IR as corresponding moves. We have made the following roster moves: – Placed DT Jer’Zhan Newton and T Laremy Tunsil on the Reserve/Injured List – Re-signed CB Fabian Moreau and DT Shy Tuttle — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) August 31, 2026 Tunsil ( torn triceps ) and Newton ( torn pec ) suffered long-term injuries during training camp that required surgery to repair. They’ll be out for months, with no guarantee that either player will return to action this season. Waiting until after the initial 53-man roster was set to place them on IR ensures they don’t burn a one of eight designations to return should Tunsil and/or Newton not be able to come back in 2026. The Commanders used the two return designations at initial cuts on cornerback Trey Amos (ankle) and running back Jeremy McNichols (quad). Letting Moreau and Tuttle go on Sunday was clearly done with a handshake deal that they would return the following day. As veterans, they are not subject to waivers and can therefore re-sign with the team. There were surely full-season guaranteed money involved here, considering that base salaries become guaranteed when making the 53-man roster. Moreau was a mid-camp signing designed to bolster depth. The UCLA product did exactly that in his return to the team that drafted him, and he’ll become the fourth cornerback behind Mike Sainristil, Rasul Douglas and Amik Robertson. With four players in that position group and safeties in Quan Maritn and Tyler Owens who can play the slot, the secondary seems better suited to play a game. Tuttle’s return gives Tim Settle a true backup at the nose tackle spot, with six guys in a rotational front.

summary: The Washington Commanders announced their initial practice squad on Monday afternoon. Receiver Jaden Bradley is a notable addition, someone who received high praise throughout the course of camp. Terry McLaurin has mentored the […]
full_text: The Washington Commanders announced their initial practice squad on Monday afternoon. It included several standout players from training camp and the preseason, with talent that will surely support game-day efforts throughout the year. Receiver Jaden Bradley is a notable addition, someone who received high praise throughout the course of camp. Terry McLaurin has mentored the undrafted UNLV product, who proved a hard worker in practices and a dynamic playmaker in preseason games. The Commanders have a bloated receiver corps right now, but it’s still possible Bradley sees the field at some point during the regular season. Washington also signed veteran defensive lineman Byron Cowart, a relatively late addition who is an effective run stopper up front. The Commanders also added fan favorite Robert Henry Jr., a running back and big-play threat. Craig Reynolds was also kept in that position group, and could be the first rusher elevated with just three backs on the active roster. Despite having a rough training camp at the center spot, the Commanders retained Julian Good-Jones on the practice squad. Linebacker Ale Kaho was kept around as well, a smart move that serves to increase the team’s depth among the off-the-ball linebackers. The Commanders also went outside their offseason roster to reportedly sign offensive tackle Esa Pole, per the Kansas City Star a player who started four games for the Kansas City Chiefs last year. He’s a massive human at 6-foot-7 and 319 pounds , and could be a factor down the road on the offensive line. They also reportedly added cornerback Reddy Steward, per Jordan Schutlz, who played in 17 games, with five starts, for the Dallas Cowboys in 2025. He’s someone who might be called upon early as an elevation. Those reported moves put the practice squad at 14 players, with three spots remaining, with Jeffery M’Ba receiving an exemption as part of the International Player Pathway. Also of note: The Commanders had the seventh slot in the NFL’s waiver order, which is based on the draft slots (excluding trades) form the 2026 selection. That order will remain through the season’s first three weeks, until 2026 regular-season results start dictating the waiver wire. They didn’t use it on anyone.That doesn’t mean there won’t be roster moves in free agency to fortify the squad. It just didn’t come with a waiver claim. title: Players the Washington Commanders could pursue after the roster deadline
summary: The preseason schedule is complete, and NFL teams trimmed their rosters to 53 players on Sunday afternoon. Both rookies and veterans alike were released, with different rules applying for each. Players with fewer than four accrued seasons must pass through the waiver wire to become unrestricted free agents. An accrued season is defined as six […]
full_text: The preseason schedule is complete, and NFL teams trimmed their rosters to 53 players on Sunday afternoon. Both rookies and veterans alike were released, with different rules applying for each. Players with fewer than four accrued seasons must pass through the waiver wire to become unrestricted free agents. An accrued season is defined as six or more games on either a team’s roster, injured reserve, or physically unable to perform list. Players that have four or more accrued seasons are immediately free agents and don’t have to go through waivers. Commanders GM Adam Peters continues to build the talent of the roster in his third year at the helm, but some positions are still deficient as quarterback Jayden Daniels enters a critical third season. The following is a list of players that Peters could consider following the cutdown deadline. Some are subject to waivers. Keep in mind that relatively few players are claimed during this period, and last year Washington submitted no claims . This year may be different, as the team finds themselves with obvious needs, especially along the offensive line. The Commanders hold the seventh spot on the waiver order by virtue of last season’s 5-12 finish, so they should have an opportunity to add some talent if they see the right fit. Any player claimed on waivers needs to go directly on the 53-man roster. Center We start with the most obvious area of need. Nick Allegretti has missed the majority of training camp and preseason. Julian Good-Jones looked the part of a perennial practice-squad player and was cut after taking first-team reps through out camp. Sixth-round rookie Matt Gulbin made the final 53-man roster but appeared to need more development. A center is currently the most pressing issue for the team, but Washington did not acquire an additional one before the roster-cuts deadline. Fans have been waiting for this list for a couple of weeks now, but it was projected to be much longer just a mere 24 hours ago. Lucas Patrick (Free Agent) A 33-year-old NFL veteran, Lucas Patrick was originally an undrafted free agent signed by the Green Bay Packers. After spending a few years with the team, he continued his career with several different teams, including the Chicago Bears (2022-2023), New Orleans Saints (2024), and Cincinnati Bengals (2025). Lucas Patrick versus Philadelphia pic.twitter.com/FLGRHcCpl6 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) August 9, 2025 Patrick has started 28 games at center, 19 games at left guard, and 18 games at right guard in his career, with over 1,000 snaps played at all three spots while being credited with allowing just eight total sacks on 2,607 pass block snaps across his nine NFL seasons, according to Pro Football Focus. Lucas reportedly had a good training camp with no sacks or pressures in 28 pass-blocking snaps this season but found himself caught in the numbers game after the Giants traded for Joshua Ezeudu. Injuries are a concern, but if they are looking for an immediate, experienced, and reliable backup over Matt Gulbin, the Commanders should consider signing him. Nick Dawkins (Waivers) With limited veteran experience available, the Commanders may choose to look for a newer, high-upside addition. An undrafted free agent acquisition of the Baltimore Ravens, Dawkins originally came out of Penn State and has already caught the eye of Hogs Haven writer MattInBrisVegas. He included the Penn State graduate in his pre-draft center roundup , citing Dawkins’ plus athleticism and blocking metrics. In 2025, he split rushing between gap and zone concepts. According to Williams, he thrives on inside zone runs, where he generates movement, with length and mobility to reach, seal, and climb effectively to the second level. The blocking performance metrics show him to be significantly above average in both phases. His Pressure Rate in pass protection ranked 7 th among consensus-ranked centers and was at the 87 th percentile among FBS centers. His Run Blocking Grade ranked 10 th out of 22 consensus ranked centers and was at the 78 th percentile in the FBS. Nick Dawkins is a OC prospect in the 2026 draft class. He scored a 9.77 RAS out of a possible 10.00. This ranked 18 out of 735 OC from 1987 to 2026. https://t.co/PMTG2dWzg7 pic.twitter.com/sd3VTCAUbD — RAS.football (@MathBomb) April 12, 2026 Dawkins received plenty of run in the preseason behind Ethan Pocic, as Danny Pinter went out early with a knee injury and last year’s backup Corey Bullock missed time during the preseason. Nick’s draft profile indicates he is a high IQ player that GM Adam Peters and head coach Dan Quinn seem to look for in a player. Functional strength and experience are needed, but the upside is there. Penn State's OL imposed their will on Oregon's DL. Checkout Nick Dawkins blocking 2 guys at one time ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/ph3uvyMwC4 — LandonTengwall (@LandonTengwall) December 9, 2024 Guard Sam Cosmi has the starting right guard position locked down, but Chris Paul won the left guard spot by default after Brandon Coleman took over left tackle for Laremy Tunsil. He has reportedly struggled in camp this season, but the team has yet to field a legitimate contender for the starting role. At a minimum the team needs to upgrade the depth at the position. The team kept undrafted guard Tanoa Togiai, but will most certainly look for an upgrade. Evan Neal (Free Agent) Peters may need to get creative and try to convert a tackle to acquire a starting-level talent. Originally drafted as tackle prospect, the Giants switched No. 7 overall selection Evan Neal to guard during the 2025 season, but the project never got off the ground due to setbacks from an offseason ankle surgery. New Giants head coach John Harbaugh saw something in Neal and offered him a one-year contract to stay with the team in 2026, and while he has reportedly shown some progress this offseason, Neal was cut by the Giants on Sunday. Fans may be skeptical of his potential, but a film review of his play at guard by SB Nation’s Big Blue View is encouraging. Guard seems to agree with Neal when it comes to pass protection. His feet are much more controlled, which translates to improved hand usage. Neal tended to let his hands drift high and wide as he used them for balance while mirroring speed at tackle. He’s able to keep his punch loaded without as much ground to cover, which allows him to fire his punch into defenders’ chest plates and win inside leverage……Neal’s power and play strength leap off the screen in both run blocking and pass protection. His height demands that he plays with good hip and pad level, but he’s the type of blocker who can take a defender out of the play once he latches on. It is not all positive, as his height works against him when trying to create leverage, he tends to lunge at times, and his overall game is inconsistent. Still, for a player available in late August, Neal represents potential the Washington Commanders do not currently have at the position. The team had some success reclaiming Ereck Flowers in 2019; perhaps Evan Neal could be the next Giants tackle to succeed for them at the guard position. Pin-pull Evan Neal to the play side to lead. Skip, square to target, and hit to the inside of No. 41 behind the blocks of J.C. Davis and Thomas Fidone II. pic.twitter.com/vxtFtjbfeK — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) August 29, 2026 Elijah Klein (Waivers) A sixth-round selection of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2024, Elijah Klein is profiled with NFL length and power but average athleticism. He offers the desired versatility with 55 collegiate starts, including right guard, tackle, and guard/center flexibility. . @UTEPFB @ElijahKlein79 has game experience; versatility; length; good raw strength; and he enjoys hitting people.
