title: 2026 NFL Rank: Predicting top 100 players for this season
summary: We predicted the top 100 NFL players for 2026. Which defender came in at No. 1? How many QBs made the list? Which team had the most players included?
full_text:
As we approach the start of the NFL season , it's time for our annual ranking of the league's top 100 players. Which players do we project to be the best in 2026?

 To create our list, we asked 12 NFL analysts and reporters -- Aaron Schatz, Ben Solak, Dan Graziano, Eric Moody, Field Yates, Jeff Legwold, Liz Loza, Matt Bowen, Mina Kimes, Mike Clay, Nick Wagoner and Seth Walder -- to rank players based on expected performance for the 2026 season. Their rankings are based on predicting potential greatness rather than past performance. We used those 12 sets of votes to come up with our consensus list.

 The Eagles lead the pack in players included (eight) for the second straight year , and the Lions and 49ers are next up with six players each. The Jets, meanwhile, are the only team without a single representative. By position, quarterbacks dominated the list with 16 mentions. Edge rushers followed with 13.

 Along with the top-100 ranking, our NFL Nation reporters weighed in on every player's outlook for the season, ESPN Research provided a stat to know and fantasy analyst Mike Clay projected 2026 stats. Here's our list, starting at No. 100 and working our way to No. 1.

 Note: Commanders offensive tackle Laremy Tunsil was not considered for this exercise due to his recent triceps injury ; again, this is predicting 2026 play. Rams defensive tackle  Aaron Donald , who came out of retirement Sunday, also was not considered. 

 

 Jump to: 
 100-76 | 75-51 | 50-26 | 25-1 

 More on NFL Rank: 
 Execs and scouts name snubs 

 

 

 100. Sam Darnold 
 QB | Seahawks 
Age: 29 
2025 rank: NR 

 No quarterback has more wins over the past two seasons than Darnold, who has 31 with the Vikings and Seahawks. He'd be higher on this list if not for his league-high 20 turnovers in 2025, though he went the final four games without one. One reason Darnold could be better in 2026: This is the first time since 2020 that he returns to the same team as its unquestioned starter. -- Brady Henderson 

 Signature stat: Last season, Darnold went 14-3 as a starter with the Seahawks after finishing the 2024 season with a 14-3 record for the Vikings. Darnold joined Tom Brady (2003-04) as the only QBs to record back-to-back 14-win seasons.

 2026 projections :  4,013 passing yards, 24 TDs, 12 INTs; 44 carries, 126 rushing yards, 1 TD

 
 

 99. Jessie Bates III 
 S | Falcons 
Age: 29 
2025 rank: 62 

 One of the premier ball hawks in the NFL, Bates has 27 interceptions and 11 forced fumbles (fifth most among defensive backs) since he entered the league in 2018. He's the unquestioned leader of the Falcons' defense and could be part of one of the best 2026 safety duos alongside Xavier Watts (five interceptions as a rookie in 2025). -- Marc Raimondi 

 Signature stat: Bates' 27 interceptions over the past eight seasons is the third most in the NFL behind Kevin Byard and Justin Simmons (both 28).

 2026 projections :  96 tackles, 6 PDs, 2 INTs, 1 FF

 
 

 98. Antoine Winfield Jr. 
 S | Buccaneers 
Age: 28 
2025 rank: 85 

 The Bucs were really intentional about bringing in some new players on defense who fit their type of attitude and instinct. Having linebacker Alex Anzalone -- one of the best cover inside linebackers in the league -- patrolling the middle of the field will be a huge assist to Winfield. So will another year of experience for Winfield's fellow safety Tykee Smith , as well as a revamped pass rush with rookie Rueben Bain Jr.   -- Jenna Laine 

 Signature stat: Winfield leads all safeties in forced fumbles (12) and fumble recoveries (10) since entering the league in 2020.

 2026 projections :  95 tackles, 8 PDs, 2 sacks, 2 INTs, 1 FF

 
 

 97. Jalen Hurts 
 QB | Eagles 
Age: 28 
2025 rank: 38 

 Hurts is coming off an up-and-down year and is now at the controls of a brand-new scheme designed by offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. Hurts has found ways to maneuver around obstacles in the past, though. He has a 57-25 record as a starting QB and ranks second to only Josh Allen in total touchdowns (138) since 2022. -- Tim McManus 

 Signature stat: Hurts recorded his fourth straight season with 30-plus combined passing and rushing touchdowns, the fourth-longest active streak behind Allen (six). That included his fewest rushing TDs (eight) since becoming the full-time starter in 2021.

 2026 projections :  3,779 passing yards, 24 TDs, 12 INTs; 106 carries, 438 rushing yards, 9 TDs

 
 

 96. Trevor Lawrence 
 QB | Jaguars 
Age: 26 
2025 rank: NR 

 It can't be coincidence that Liam Coen coached quarterback  Baker Mayfield and Lawrence to their best seasons in back-to-back years. Unlike 2025, Lawrence isn't learning a new offense or changing his footwork. So, it shouldn't take half of the season for him to get rolling the way he did over the final eight games of 2025 (19 TD passes and five rushing TDs). -- Michael DiRocco 

 Signature stat: Lawrence set a franchise record with 38 total touchdowns last season. He also finished fifth in MVP voting, which was the highest finish ever by a Jaguar.

 2026 projections :  3,932 passing yards, 25 TDs, 13 INTs; 73 carries, 335 rushing yards, 5 TDs

 
 

 95. Rashawn Slater 
 OT | Chargers 
Age: 27 
2025 rank: NR 

 Slater missed all of last season with a ruptured patellar tendon in his left knee. Through training camp, he looks like the Pro Bowl version of himself at left tackle, but the true determination will be when the season starts. Slater has already missed practice time this offseason due to a flare-up, so it will be something to watch as he tries to reestablish himself as one of the best players at his position. -- Kris Rhim 

 Signature stat: In 2024, Slater finished 10th in run block win rate (78.6%) and 22nd in pass block win rate (90.7%) among qualifying tackles.

 
 

 94. Jaycee Horn 
 CB | Panthers 
Age: 26 
2025 rank: NR 

 Horn will be more fluid in the defensive backfield in 2026. This summer, he has been used in the slot, which should take advantage of his blitzing ability. While he was sent at the quarterback just 16 times over the past two seasons, according to NFL Next Gen Stats, he created pressure on 25% of those opportunities (including two sacks and four QB hits). -- Mike Kaye 

 Signature stat: All five of Horn's interceptions last season came on passes at least 20 yards downfield, the most in the NFL.

 2026 projections :  50 tackles, 10 PDs, 1 INT

 
 

 93. DeVonta Smith 
 WR | Eagles 
Age: 27 
2025 rank: NR 

 Philadelphia is highly confident Smith can take his game to another level as the clear-cut No. 1 receiver after  A.J. Brown 's departure. A 100-catch season certainly seems within reach; he already came close with 95 catches for nearly 1,200 yards in 2022. -- Tim McManus 

 Signature stat: Smith is one of five players to win the Heisman Trophy, NCAA title and Super Bowl. The others are Tony Dorsett, Marcus Allen, Reggie Bush and Charles Woodson.

 2026 projections :  91 receptions, 1,130 receiving yards, 6 TDs

 
 

 92. Jack Campbell 
 LB | Lions 
Age: 26 
2025 rank: NR 

 Campbell is fresh off a first-team All-Pro season in 2025. So naturally, his confidence is at an "all-time high," according to coach Dan Campbell. Over the offseason, Campbell inked a four-year, $81 million extension . Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard is now giving him more leeway to run the defense in Year 4. "You've got to earn it every year," Campbell told ESPN. "No matter what, it's just my mindset to try to get a little better every single year." -- Eric Woodyard 

 Signature stat: Campbell is one of five players with at least 375 tackles and four forced fumbles since entering the league in 2023, joining Zaire Franklin , Bobby Okereke , Patrick Queen and Germaine Pratt .

 2026 projections :  156 tackles, 4 PDs, 3 sacks, 2 FFs, 1 INT

 
 

 91. Kamari Lassiter 
 CB | Texans 
Age: 23 
2025 rank: NR 

 Lassiter would be the No. 1 cornerback on a lot of teams, but he just happens to share a defense with Derek Stingley Jr.…

title: Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett learning quickly under Mike LaFleur
summary: After an extended holdout/hold-in, Brissett is learning a new system and picking it up quickly.
full_text:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- During the early days of  Jacoby Brissett 's return to the field on July 26 after a contract standoff, he was just trying to survive.

 When the  Arizona Cardinals  quarterback first took the field early in training camp and started running new coach Mike LaFleur's offense for the first time, Brissett would stand in the huddle and tell the offense which play they were going to run based on what he called last season.

 "This is what we did last [year]," Brissett would say, according to tight end Trey McBride . "This is what we called it last year."

 Weeks later, those days are gone.

 It's been more than five weeks since Brissett returned from a monthslong holdout and hold-in as he waited for a reworked contract, and every day since has been one step closer toward mastering the offense.

 With Week 1 against the Los Angeles Chargers on the horizon, Brissett's grasp of the offense has grown by the day. At one point during camp, the 33-year-old described his progress as "leaps and bounds" beyond what his understanding of the scheme was when he first returned from his holdout.

 "I feel like it's significantly better than when he first started," McBride said. "Obviously he's played a lot of football in his career and you can only make so many football plays up. We're running the same stuff. Maybe it's called a little bit different.

 "He's kind of getting into the new terminology, and he's a fast learner. He's a smart guy. He spends a lot of time learning the game. So, it's been no issue for him. And I feel like right now he's very comfortable. He knows exactly what to do. And we're running and operating as a very good offense."

 

 How Brissett learned the offense was an example of his maturity as NFL veteran heading into his 11th season.

 Quarterbacks coach Matt Schaub didn't start from scratch when Brissett was ready to take the field for the first time in training camp after watching from the sidelines for the first three days as the final details of his new contract were hammered out.

 "We really didn't hold back with slowing things down or trying to go back to the beginning of camp or even OTAs with everything," Schaub said. "It's just like, we're just going to keep going and he's done a great job of extra meetings, extra time in the room, talking through things, extra walk-throughs to be able to just catch up, if you will."

 To get himself caught up as fast as he could, Brissett employed a variety of techniques to learn all the verbiage and information the coaches have thrown at him. The specific plays weren't necessarily new to Brissett, as LaFleur had proclaimed time and time again throughout Brissett's holdout. Everything else was, though.

 Brissett would go through the playcalls in his head whenever LaFleur was presenting in front of the offense or the team during camp. Then there were all the opportunities to run through the plays physically through walk-throughs, pre-practice walk-throughs and then in practice.

 "As you say it more and more and more, you get more comfortable with it and you kind of beat him to the punch on some of the plays," Brissett said. "So, it's finding new ways to learn the same stuff."

 A lot of that falls on Schaub, the 45-year-old in his first year of coaching who played 16 seasons for the Falcons, Texans, Raiders and Ravens.

 Schaub's approach to Brissett is quite different than if he were preparing rookie quarterback Carson Beck . Since Brissett has spent a decade in the NFL, Schaub talks things through with him more than younger quarterbacks, whom he would typically give a framework to and tell them to work within that.

 

 With Brissett, Schaub would ask him: "Hey, what have you done? What are you comfortable with? How do you see this?" Their conversations are more discussions with a heavy dose of give-and-take, from footwork to concepts and beyond. With all their conversations, Schaub said, the end goal is to find "common ground in what we're actually trying to get done."

 When Brissett takes the field at SoFi Stadium on Sept. 13, his work still won't be done. That'll be largely due to his still budding relationship with LaFleur. That's a work in progress.

 The two have been working overtime to get to know each other since they didn't spend a second on the field together during OTAs or minicamp. Yet, from the moment that head coach-playcaller-quarterback relationship began in earnest on July 28, Brissett has been all in on building a rapport with LaFleur.

 But like Brissett is still learning the nuances of the offense, he is still learning LaFleur. Brissett has picked up the most about his coach in specific practice situations such as first down, second down, third down and red zone.

 Every day, Brissett said he learns something new about LaFleur.

 "We're still learning each other and what he likes to call, what do I like and stuff like that," Brissett said. "So, being able to be vulnerable enough to say like, 'Man, I don't like that.' And him say like, 'Oh, I messed up,' or, 'I like this right here because of this.' And that part of the learning part of the relationship I think is cool.

 "I wouldn't say we're best friends because that'll be a lie. But I do like where our relationship is and his willingness and my willingness to merge our relationship and what he's doing with all the players on the team. He's building his own relationship with guys and it's been a joy to work with him."

title: How many different Week 1 starting QBs has each NFL team used?
summary: Since the NFL expanded to 32 teams in 2002, no team has used more Week 1 starting quarterbacks than the Browns.
full_text:
Since the NFL expanded to 32 teams in 2002, no team has used more Week 1 starting quarterbacks than the Browns with 18. While the Browns aren't expected to add to that total this year with the announcement that  Deshaun Watson will start Week 1 , several teams are adding to their totals.

 Here's a look at how many different starting quarterbacks each team has utilized in Week 1 since 2002.

 Cleveland Browns - 18 
 Most Starts: Baker Mayfield (3) 
 Deshaun Watson will make his third opening-day start for the Browns in 2026, which will tie him with Baker Mayfield for the most by a Browns quarterback since the team returned to the NFL in 1999.

 Cleveland is 3-23-1 in openers since 1999. Watson has the chance to become the first Browns quarterback to win multiple openers in that time.

 Washington Commanders - 15 
 Most Starts: Jason Campbell (3), Robert Griffin III (3) and Kirk Cousins (3) 
 If Jayden Daniels makes his third straight opening-game start as expected, he'll match the most by a Washington quarterback since 2002. If he's able to continue the streak in 2027, he'll become the first Washington quarterback to start four straight since Mark Rypien from 1989 to 1993.

 Minnesota Vikings - 13 
 Most Starts: Kirk Cousins (6) 
 Kyler Murray has the most Week 1 starts for the Cardinals since 2002 and will now be the fourth different Week 1 starter in five seasons under coach Kevin O'Connell.

 

 Arizona Cardinals - 12 
 Most Starts: Kyler Murray (6) 
 Jacoby Brissett is expected to make his fourth opening-game start for his fourth different franchise (Browns, Colts, Patriots). That would be the most opening-game starts in the Super Bowl era without having multiple with any one team.

 Las Vegas Raiders - 12 
 Most Starts: Derek Carr (9) 
 The Raiders are adding a new starter to their total regardless of who gets the nod in Week 1, which will make it five straight years with a different Week 1 starter. It's either Kirk Cousins, who is 3-7 in his career on opening day, or Fernando Mendoza , who'd be making his NFL debut.

 New York Jets - 12 
 Most Starts: Mark Sanchez (4) and Chad Pennington (4) 
 Geno Smith is expected to make his third Week 1 start for the Jets, but his first since the 2014 season. No quarterback in the Super Bowl era has had a longer gap between opening-day starts for a single franchise. Currently the largest is by Brad Johnson, who started the 1998 and 2006 openers for the Vikings.

 Denver Broncos - 12 
 Most Starts: Peyton Manning (4) and Jake Plummer (4) 
 Since John Elway retired, no Broncos quarterback has started more than four season openers. Bo Nix is slated to start his third straight this season.

 Tampa Bay Buccaneers - 11 
 Most Starts: Josh Freeman (4) and Jameis Winston (4) 
 *Includes 2017, when Buccaneers started their season in Week 2 due to Hurricane Irma 
 Baker Mayfield is 3-0 with the Buccaneers in Week 1 after going 0-4 in such games with the Browns and Panthers. No Buccaneers quarterback has ever won four season openers.

 San Francisco 49ers - 11 
 Most Starts: Alex Smith (5) 
 Brock Purdy will be looking to improve to 4-0 in Week 1 games as the 49ers' starting quarterback. Maybe no surprise, but Steve Young (6-3) and Joe Montana (5-5) are the only Niners quarterbacks with more season-opening wins in the Super Bowl era.

 Chicago Bears - 10 
 Most Starts: Jay Cutler (8) 
 The first two Week 1 starts by Caleb Williams  came at home, but he'll make his first road start in an opener this season. The Bears are 4-15 in season openers on the road in the Super Bowl era.

 Houston Texans - 10 
 Most Starts: Matt Schaub (7) 
 C.J. Stroud will make his fourth opening-day start, trailing only Matt Schaub (7) and David Carr (5) for most in franchise history. Stroud is 1-2 in Week 1 games.

 Jacksonville Jaguars - 10 
 Most Starts: Trevor Lawrence (5) 
 Trevor Lawrence is expected to make his sixth straight opening-day start for the Jaguars. That would tie Mark Brunell for the longest streak in franchise history.

 Indianapolis Colts - 10 
 Most Starts: Peyton Manning (9) 
 Since Andrew Luck's retirement ahead of the 2017 season, the Colts are tied for the most season-opening starting quarterbacks with the Commanders (8 each). Daniel Jones is projected to make his second straight opening day start for the Colts.

 Miami Dolphins - 10 
 Most Starts: Ryan Tannehill (6) 
 *Includes 2017, when Dolphins started their season in Week 2 due to Hurricane Irma 
 Malik Willis is entering his fifth NFL season but will be making his first Week 1 start. He'll be the 11th opening-day starting quarterback for the Dolphins since Dan Marino retired.

 Pittsburgh Steelers - 9 
 Most Starts: Ben Roethlisberger (15) 
 Aaron Rodgers could be making his 19th and final opening-day start. That would tie Drew Brees for second most in the Super Bowl era and put him one shy of Tom Brady (20).

 Carolina Panthers - 9 
 Most Starts: Cam Newton (8) 
 Bryce Young is making his fourth opening-day start for the Panthers, but he's still searching for his first Week 1 win. The last quarterback to lose his first four opening-day starts? Baker Mayfield.

 Tennessee Titans - 9 
 Most Starts: Marcus Mariota (5) 
 The Titans have lost five straight season openers, the longest active streak in the NFL and the longest streak in franchise history. Cam Ward , the 2025 No. 1 pick, is slated to make his second straight opening-day start for Tennessee.

 Buffalo Bills - 9 
 Most Starts: Josh Allen (7) 
 Josh Allen has the most opening day starts for the Bills since 2002, but he still has some work to do to catch the Bills' franchise leaders. Joe Ferguson (12) and Jim Kelly (11) each have more.

 Los Angeles Rams - 8 
 Most Starts: Marc Bulger (6) 
 Reigning MVP Matthew Stafford  is slated to make his 18th opening-game start, which would tie him with Brett Favre for fourth most in the Super Bowl era.

 Stafford will also tie Marc Bulger for the most opening-day starts by a Rams quarterback since 2002.

 Atlanta Falcons - 8 
 Most Starts: Matt Ryan (14) 
 Tua Tagovailoa would be the sixth different Week 1 starting quarterback for the Falcons in the past six years if he gets the nod. If it's Michael Penix Jr ., he'd be the first repeat Week 1 starter for Atlanta since Matt Ryan started 14 straight openers (2008-21).

 Philadelphia Eagles - 7 
 Most Starts: Donovan McNabb (8) 
 Jalen Hurts is 5-0 in season-opening starts. The last quarterback to win his first six season openers? Roger Staubach, who went 9-0 in his career in opening games.

 New England Patriots - 6 
 Most Starts: Tom Brady (17) 
 The Patriots are only 2-4 in season openers since Tom Brady left for Tampa, including a loss in 2025 under Drake Maye .

 Kansas City Chiefs - 6 
 Most Starts: Patrick Mahomes (8) 
 Patrick Mahomes started his career 5-0 in season openers but is 1-2 in his past three, including a loss last season to the Chargers.

 His next Week 1 start will break a tie with Len Dawson for most by a Chiefs quarterback in the Super Bowl era.

 Cincinnati Bengals - 5 
 Most Starts: Andy Dalton (9) 
 Carson Palmer (7), Andy Dalton (9) and Joe Burrow (7) are the only Week 1 starters for the Bengals since 2004. Burrow is 2-4 in season openers and 3-9 in the first two games of the season.

 Seattle Seahawks - 5 
 Most Starts: Russell Wilson (10) 
 The reigning Super Bowl champions are 21-5 in Week 1 games this century but are just 2-2 in their past four.

 Sam Darnold is 3-3 in his career in six opening-game starts.

 Detroit Lions - 5 
 Most Starts: Matthew Stafford (12) 
 Jared Goff will be making his sixth straight opening game start, picking up where Matthew Stafford left off (12 straight). The last time the Lions had player who wasn't  the No. 1 pick of a draft start in Week 1 was Jon Kitna in 2008.

 Dallas Cowboys - 5 
 Most Starts: Dak Prescott (10) 
 Dak Prescott is expected to make his 11th season-opening start for the Cowboys. He'd be one shy of matching Troy Aikman (12) for the most…

title: How to bet the 2026 NFL season: Three bets to make on each team
summary: Will your NFL team beat its projected win total? What props should you target? Tyler Fulghum offers his three favorite bets for each team.
full_text:
The NFL season offers an almost unlimited amount of betting opportunities, from seasonlong win totals to individual player props and everything in between. It can be daunting.

 Don't worry. I've got you covered.

 Here are three wagers for each of the 32 franchises. Some picks look at the big picture, such as Super Bowl futures or division odds. Others zoom in on specific players, highlighting yardage totals, touchdown props or award chances. And for those who like long shots, we have a few of those too.

 Whether you're a futures-focused bettor mapping out the entire season or someone who prefers to target specific markets, this guide gives you a broad menu of options for every team. Consider it your all-in-one starting point for betting the 2026 NFL season.

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change .

 Jump to: ARI  | ATL  | BAL  | BUF  | CAR  | CHI 
 CIN  |  CLE  | DAL  | DEN  | DET  | GB  | HOU 
 IND  |  JAX  | KC  | LAC  | LAR  | LV  | MIA 
 MIN  |  NE  | NO  | NYG  | NYJ  | PHI  | PIT 
 SEA  |  SF  | TB  | TEN  | WAS 

 

 

   Arizona Cardinals 
 •  UNDER 4.5 wins (-186)  
•  Trey McBride  receiving yards UNDER 999.5 (-110) 
•  Jeremiyah Love rushing TDs UNDER 5.5 (+100) 

 The Cardinals have the hardest schedule in the league this year, and I expect their record to reflect that. If Arizona struggles to stay competitive, McBride's receiving prop becomes difficult to clear because of statistical regression and a likely lack of consistent quarterback play. The under on Love adds another attractive fade of touchdown production. The rookie running back already suffered an ankle injury in training camp.

 

 
   Atlanta Falcons 

 • UNDER 6.5 wins (+130) 
• Fewest regular-season wins (15-1) 
• Bijan Robinson rushing TDs UNDER 8.5 (+100) 

 

 Atlanta could struggle to find consistency because of questions at quarterback and a suspect defense. Under 6.5 wins is the primary value play, while a bet on the fewest regular-season wins provides significant upside if the Falcons completely bottom out. The Robinson play complements the team unders by fading Atlanta's ability to consistently finish drives. Robinson can still post strong yardage numbers while falling short of this touchdown threshold.

 

 
   Baltimore Ravens 
 •  UNDER 11.5 wins (-140) 
•  Zay Flowers receiving TDs UNDER 5.5 (-120) 
•  Trey Hendrickson sacks UNDER 12.25 (-125) 

 The under on wins doesn't require a disastrous season, it simply requires the Ravens to fall short of an extremely high bar. Flowers' under on receiving touchdowns fits that thesis. He has been a productive receiver but has never scored more than five receiving TDs in a season, as his size limits his chances in the red zone. The Hendrickson under is another bet against elite individual production for a really good player. That's just a massive number to clear, even if he does stay healthy the entire season.

 

 
   Buffalo Bills 

 •  OVER 10.5 wins (-120) 
•  Win AFC East (-136) 
•  James Cook III rushing yards UNDER 1,224.5 (-110) 

 Buffalo is lined as the co-AFC favorite with Baltimore, and I agree that the team is going to be very good this season. I'm comfortable with the pricing on over 10.5 wins and an AFC East title. Those bets are closely correlated. If the Bills reach 11 or more victories, they're in excellent position to take back the division from the Patriots. The under on Cook's rushing yards is a bet against a massive number. Buffalo should have an elite rushing attack, but missing even one or two games makes this a difficult threshold to clear.

 

 
   Carolina Panthers 
 •  OVER 6.5 wins (-166) 
• OVER 2.5 division wins (-165) 
• Bryce Young passing TDs UNDER 20.5 (-110) 

 After last season's playoff appearance, Carolina feels poised to take a meaningful step forward. Over 6.5 wins is the anchor wager, while over 2.5 division wins suggests Carolina can capitalize on a mediocre NFC South and a solid home-field advantage. The under on Young's passing touchdowns can coexist with both bets if the Panthers lean on their running game and defense, which I fully expect Dave Canales to do, following the script from a season ago.

 

 
   Chicago Bears 

 • OVER 9.5 wins (+105) 
• Highest-scoring team in NFL (+900) 
•  Caleb Williams 30+ TD passes (+275) 

 Chicago's three bets are built around an offense that coach Ben Johnson has openly said he wants to break scoring records this year. The price betting the over on wins provides value on a team that could make a significant leap, while a bet on highest-scoring team in the NFL offers a much bigger payoff if Johnson's proclamations prove prophetic. Williams throwing 30-plus touchdown passes directly correlates with that outcome. If Williams takes a jump alongside Luther Burden III , Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland , watch out.

 

 
   Cincinnati Bengals 
 •  OVER 9.5 wins (-160) 
•  Win AFC North (+184) 
• Zac Taylor to win Coach of the Year (28-1) 

 

 Cincinnati feels like a sleeper team in the AFC. The bets on wins and the AFC North depend on the Bengals remaining healthy on offense, while Taylor winning Coach of the Year at these odds provides substantial upside if the revamped defense helps the Bengals become a more complete contender in the conference. The additions of DT Dexter Lawrence II , DT Jonathan Allen and DE Boye Mafe should pay immediate dividends on that side of the ball.

 

 
   Cleveland Browns 
 

 • UNDER 5.5 wins (+115) 
•  Fewest regular-season wins (+1050) 
•  Deshaun Watson passing yards UNDER 1,749.5 (-120) 

 Cleveland's portfolio of wagers is a straightforward assessment that this team is bad . The under bet on wins provides value if the Browns struggle to find stability, while a play on the fewest regular-season wins offers significant leverage on a true collapse. The under on Watson's passing yards prop fits particularly well because the number can be threatened simply by injury and/or ineffectiveness. Stocked up with bonus draft capital for 2027 and beyond, the Browns are actually incentivized to quietly tank this season.

 

 
   Dallas Cowboys 

 •  OVER 9.5 wins (+100) 
•  Division finishing position: 1 (+235) 
• Earn No. 1 seed in NFC (+1550) 

 On paper, Dallas looks like a legit contender entering this season. Bets on wins and winning the division are particularly attractive. We know the offense should be capable, but the upgraded personnel on the defensive side of the ball has me really intrigued with the ceiling of this team. That's why I'm willing to sprinkle a little on Dallas earning the NFC's No. 1 seed. That requires everything to break right, but the price is super attractive given the talent on this roster.

 

 
   Denver Broncos 
 •  OVER 9.5 wins (-110) 
•  AFC champions (+1025) 
• Jonah Coleman to win OROY (55-1) 

 After hosting the AFC Championship Game without its starting QB last season, Denver feels a little undervalued in the market. Over on wins is the core position, reflecting confidence that the Broncos can remain among the AFC's better teams. Bo Nix is back and healthy to start the season, and Denver should once again have an elite defensive unit, so the number to win the AFC feels mispriced. Coleman winning Offensive Rookie of the Year is the lottery ticket. It requires a major breakout, but Coleman has looked incredible in the preseason, with coach Sean Payton raving about his play.

 

 
 Check out the latest odds and lines for Week 1   . 

 -->
   Detroit Lions 
 •  UNDER 10.5 wins (-105) 
• MISS playoffs (+180) 
• Jared Goff to record 400-yard passing game (-105) 

 

 Detroit could be headed for some regression in 2026 thanks to a defense that is already beat up and playing in a difficult division. The under on wins and missing the playoffs both play into this thesis. Goff recording 400-plus passing yards in a game also relates to my belief that this team could play in a lot of shootouts. Dan Campbell is a great coach and the offense should be one of the most dangerous in…

title: Preseason NFL Power Rankings 2026: How all 32 teams stack up
summary: How do all 32 NFL teams stack up with under 10 days to go until the regular season? Plus, we picked out statistical milestones on the horizon for each team.
full_text:
With all 32 NFL teams making their final cuts Sunday night, it's the perfect time to size up the league in our Power Rankings just days away from the 2026 season .

 To form the list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another, ranking them from No. 1 to 32.

 In addition to our 1-32 ranking, NFL Nation reporters picked a milestone to watch for each franchise this season. From 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan becoming the longest-tenured coach in 49ers history to Ravens running back Derrick Henry moving up to No. 6 on the career rushing list, there's plenty at stake beyond who wins  Super Bowl LXI . Let's dive into the record books, starting with two NFC West teams.

 Previous rankings: Post-Super Bowl , Postdraft 

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI |  ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 

 1. Los Angeles Rams 
 Postdraft ranking: 2 

 Milestone to watch: Quarterback Matthew Stafford  surpassing Philip Rivers for the sixth-most touchdown passes in NFL history during the regular season.

 Stafford has quickly climbed several career lists in recent years, including becoming the 10th quarterback to hit the 60,000 passing yards  milestone in Week 1 of 2025. He could check off another box with three more touchdown passes, eclipsing Rivers' career mark of 425. Given that Stafford averaged 2.7 touchdown passes per game in 2025, he could reach the milestone as early as Week 1 or Week 2 . Brett Favre is fifth on the list with 508 touchdowns. -- Sarah Barshop 

 

 
 

 2. Seattle Seahawks 
 Postdraft ranking: 1 

 Milestone to watch: Jaxon Smith-Njigba becoming the fourth player with at least 100 receptions in three of his first four seasons.

 Smith-Njigba had 100 receptions in 2024 before setting a franchise record with 119 last season on his way to winning AP Offensive Player of the Year . So his catch count will be worth watching come December. Brandon Marshall, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Michael Thomas are the only three players who've accomplished the feat -- though Rams star receiver Puka Nacua can also join the list in 2026. -- Brady Henderson 

 

 
 

 

 3. Buffalo Bills 
 Postdraft ranking: 4 

 Milestone to watch: Josh Allen  surpassing  Patrick Mahomes  for the most combined passing and rushing yards by a quarterback in his first nine NFL seasons.

 This would take Allen close to the end of the season, but it is well within reach. Allen is 3,782 yards away from eclipsing Mahomes (38,604), and Allen has not missed a start since his rookie season. He averages 590.1 rushing yards and 3,762.8 passing yards per season, so he could pass Mahomes with multiple games to spare. Breaking records is a common occurrence for Allen, and with new No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore added to the mix, he's primed to set many marks yet again. -- Alaina Getzenberg 

 

 
 

 4. Denver Broncos 
 Postdraft ranking: 3 

 Milestone to watch: Sean Payton moving into top 10 for career coaching wins.

 Payton, now in his fourth season with the Broncos, could move into the top 10 if the team plays at even a wild-card level. The Broncos, who were tied for a league-best 14 wins last season, would move Payton from the No. 13 spot (184) to No. 9 with at least nine wins. Currently, Hall of Famer Chuck Noll and Mike Tomlin are tied at No. 9 with 193. Marty Schottenheimer is No. 8 with 200 wins. -- Jeff Legwold 

 

 
 

 5. Philadelphia Eagles 
 Postdraft ranking: 5 

 Milestone to watch: Jalen Hurts becoming the third quarterback with at least 75 career rushing touchdowns.

 Hurts has 63 rushing TDs. He would join Allen (79) and Cam Newton (75) as the only signal-callers to reach 75. Last season, he had a career low since becoming the full-time starter in rushing attempts (105), yards (421) and touchdowns (eight). But he looked faster this summer when breaking from the pocket or executing designed runs. -- Tim McManus 

 

 
 

 6. New England Patriots 
 Postdraft ranking: 6 

 Milestone to watch: Wide receiver A.J. Brown totaling 1,000 receiving yards for the seventh season of his career.

 Brown has had four straight 1,000-yard seasons and has hit 1,000 in six of his seven NFL seasons. He could become one of seven WRs to have seven or more 1,000-yard seasons in his first eight years in the league, joining Mike Evans (eight), Lance Alworth (seven), Torry Holt (seven), Brandon Marshall (seven), Jerry Rice (seven) and Randy Moss (seven). -- Mike Reiss 

 

 
 

 7. Green Bay Packers 
 Postdraft ranking: 7 

 Milestone to watch: Edge rusher Micah Parsons becoming the first player to record at least 12 sacks in each of his first six NFL seasons since the metric became official in 1982.

 Parsons is likely to start the year on the physically unable to perform list while recovering from last season's torn ACL . He could be targeting a Week 6 return, which would give him 13 games to hit the dozen sack mark. He played in exactly that many games in 2024. If Parsons gets to at least 10 sacks, he would join Reggie White as the only players since 1982 to reach that mark in their first six seasons. -- Rob Demovsky 

 

 
 

 8. Baltimore Ravens 
 Postdraft ranking: 10 

 Milestone to watch: Derrick Henry surpassing four Hall of Fame running backs to move to No. 6 on the career rushing list.

 Henry, who ranks 10th on the league's career rushing list, needs 995 yards to move up four spots. He would surpass Eric Dickerson (ninth), Jerome Bettis (eighth), LaDainian Tomlinson (seventh) and Curtis Martin (sixth). Based on Henry's average rushing yards per game (85.1), he would likely move into No. 6 by the Nov. 29 game at the Texans. Henry would need 1,811 yards rushing to surpass Adrian Peterson and climb into the top five. -- Jamison Hensley 

 

 

 
 

 9. San Francisco 49ers 
 Postdraft ranking: 8 

 Milestone to watch: Kyle Shanahan surpassing Bill Walsh for most games in charge of the 49ers and total wins.

 Shanahan has coached the Niners in 141 regular-season games, compiling 82 wins in the process. The legendary Walsh owns the franchise record for games coached (152) and won 92 of those (second most in franchise history). Shanahan can pass the games coached record at home in Week 12 against the Vikings, and he can move to second in wins with 11. The Niners would have to go a spectacular 17-1 for Shanahan to also pass George Seifert (98 wins) as the winningest coach in team history, but that's a record within striking distance over the next two seasons. -- Nick Wagoner 

 

 
 

 10. Houston Texans 
 Postdraft ranking: 13 

 Milestone to watch: Quarterback C.J. Stroud becoming second in multiple Texans passing categories.

 If Stroud throws for 3,663 passing yards in 2026, he'll pass Deshaun Watson (14,539) and move into second place in Texans' history. Stroud (10,876) currently sits behind David Carr (13,391) at fourth overall, while Matt Schaub is well ahead at No. 1 (23,221). Another category to watch is passing touchdowns in franchise history. Stroud is third with 62, but if he goes nuclear and tosses at least 43 touchdown passes, he'll also pass Watson (104) for second. Schaub leads with 124. -- DJ Bien-Aime 

 

 
 

 11. Detroit Lions 
 Postdraft ranking: 11 

 Milestone to watch: Wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown posting the most receptions through first six seasons all time.

 The fourth-round pick from the 2021 draft will try to continue to add to his record-breaking start as he enters this season with 547 career receptions. St. Brown can surpass Justin Jefferson (579) for the most receptions by a player in his first six NFL seasons, which could happen near midseason. The "Sun God" can also become the first player with at least 100 receptions in five of his first six seasons. -- Eric Woodyard

title: 2026 NFL roster cuts: Biggest moves, more for all 32 teams
summary: Sunday was the deadline for NFL teams to finalize their 53-man rosters ahead of the 2026 season. We have full lists of cuts and big moves for all 32.
full_text:
We're less than two weeks from the start of the 2026 NFL season , when the Seahawks and Patriots meet in a Super Bowl rematch Sept. 9 . And with the preseason play wrapped up, front offices and coaching staffs have been busy around the league getting the rosters ready.

 The deadline for each team to finalize its 53-man roster was Sunday at 6 p.m. ET. Teams can still make moves, of course, before the opener, but getting down to 53 players by the deadline meant a lot of cuts and trades. Of note, the Cowboys released second-year running back Jaydon Blue , while the Colts retained quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr .

 Our NFL Nation reporters have the official releases and other moves for all 32 teams as news trickles out. Plus, they broke down the biggest moves to know.

 
 Jump to a team:

 NE  |  NO  |  NYG  |  NYJ |  PHI  |  PIT  |  SF 
 SEA |  TB |  TEN |  WSH 

 
 

 AFC East 
 

 

 Buffalo Bills 
 Biggest move: Cutting undrafted cornerback Kani Walker . Walker had a strong training camp and preseason, but this move is more impactful because of where it leaves the initial 53-man roster. The Bills have only three dedicated cornerbacks -- starters Christian Benford and Maxwell Hairston , and rookie backup Davison Igbinosun . General manager Brandon Beane stressed the importance of nailing down the position after the draft and having depth. The team also moved on from seventh-round cornerback  Toriano Pride Jr ., and Walker will likely be on the practice squad if he is not claimed. But how the Bills address the position moving forward will be key for the defense. -- Alaina Getzenberg

 Reserve/suspended : DT Phidarian Mathis

 Miami Dolphins 
 Biggest move: Trading Quinn Ewers and acquiring  Kyle McCord . The Dolphins' backup quarterback situation was untenable after a cumulatively underwhelming preseason from Cam Miller , Mark Gronowski and Ewers. Swapping Ewers for McCord is still risky; McCord is yet to play an NFL game, while Ewers has three starts. But McCord was one of the top preseason performers and is young enough to qualify as a developmental passer for a young Miami team. On the other side of the ball, the Dolphins released linebacker Tyrel Dodson , clearing a starting job for second-round pick Jacob Rodriguez . -- Marcel Louis-Jacques

 Reserve/suspended : DT Kenneth Grant , LB Trey Moore , CB Darrell Baker Jr ., CB Storm Duck 

 

 

 

 New England Patriots 
 Biggest move: This was a straightforward cut-down weekend for the Patriots, with arguably the biggest surprise coming with the sixth cornerback spot as undrafted Channing Canada (TCU) got the nod over veteran Kindle Vildor , who had been praised by coach Mike Vrabel after the second preseason game. Trades involving late-round draft picks to improve depth with T/G Walter Rouse and RB Corey Kiner were notable but not headline-grabbing, which made the team's injury-based decisions the biggest news: Veteran OLB Harold Landry III is starting on the physically unable to perform list, special teams captain Brenden Schooler starts on the non-football injury list and reserve OT Marcus Bryant begins on injured reserve. title: NFL execs pick snubs in ESPN's 2026 top 100 player rankings
summary: Only 100 players can make our list of the top NFL players for this season. Here are nine who league insiders believe should have been there.
full_text:
The NFL Rank project celebrates 100 players expected to have a terrific season. One problem: More than 100 qualify.

 ESPN's NFL experts rated players based on performance expectations for the 2026 season. Though the players who made the cut are deserving, at least nine marquee players could be classified as snubs -- the most important part of any list, right?

 This project arrives about a month after we finalized our annual positional top 10s project , in which NFL executives, coaches and scouts rank the top players at each position. A review of both rankings shows plenty of similarities in order -- but also a bunch of differences. So, we asked league personnel evaluators to peek at our rankings and nominate players who deserved to be included -- but weren't.

 Note: Commanders offensive tackle Laremy Tunsil was not considered for this exercise due to his recent triceps injury -- again, this is predicting 2026 play. Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald , who came out of retirement Sunday, was also not considered. 

 
 See the full NFL Rank list 

 
 

 

 Baker Mayfield , QB, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 
 Sixteen quarterbacks made this year's top 100, and Mayfield was not one. 

 Mayfield ranks third in passing yards (12,237) and second in touchdown passes (95) since 2023. He has had some success in Tampa Bay, so much so that he turned down a two-year extension of over $100 million in hopes of more long-term security with his team. Mayfield is poised for another big year, which should help his standing on the list.

 "When he's healthy, he's a top-10 quarterback," an NFL personnel evaluator said. "I don't think he was healthy last year. He should have a big season."

 
 

 

 Denzel Ward , CB, Cleveland Browns 
 Ward is, quite comfortably, a top-seven cornerback. This list pushes him out of the top 10.

 "I think durability and the fact he plays in Cleveland keeps him out of the top cornerback discussion, but he's so good," an AFC executive said. "One of the smoothest athletes in all of football."

 Ward typically misses a few games per season because of injury, but his production is undeniable. He has 18 interceptions and 74 pass deflections over eight seasons.

 
 

 Malik Nabers , WR, New York Giants 
 Recovery from a torn ACL affects Nabers' standing. He was limited to 18 catches for 271 yards in four games last season. But when he's healthy, the 23-year-old is easily a top-10 receiver. The top-100 list featured 12 receivers, with Nabers noticeably absent.

 Nabers is one of 10 players all time to record 1,200-plus receiving yards as a rookie (2024).

 "He completely changes the [Giants'] offense if he's healthy this year," an NFC executive said. "It might take him some time, but he moves differently than most receivers when he's full tilt."

 
 

 Kenneth Walker III , RB, Kansas City Chiefs 
 Walker is squarely in his prime (25 years old) without much wear and tear (821 carries in four seasons). He's coming off a dominant three-game playoff stretch, including 313 rushing yards with four touchdowns and a Super Bowl MVP award . And Walker tied for third last season with 10 rushes of at least 20 yards. The other three backs with at least that many -- Jahmyr Gibbs , Derrick Henry and  De'Von Achane  -- ranked in the top 65 of this list.

 "If Andy Reid commits to running the ball, [Walker] is in a position to be a true bell cow who can use his vision to dictate the line of scrimmage," an AFC scout said.

 
 

 

 Brian Branch , S, Detroit Lions 
 Often an underappreciated position, five safeties were featured in this year's NFL Rank. Left off the ballot was Branch, who has established himself as a premier player over the past two seasons with a 1.9% pass breakup percentage that ranks third among safeties. In 2025, Branch was one of two defensive backs with at least five passes defended, five tackles for loss and 2.5 sacks.

 His Achilles tear late last season doesn't help his cause. But the 24-year-old's skill set is undeniable.

 "Really versatile, can put him in the slot or in open space, physical," an AFC personnel evaluator said. "Definitely a top-100 player."

 
 

 Milton Williams , DT, New England Patriots 
 The game is loaded with star defensive tackles -- many of whom make more than $30 million per year. Williams makes $26 million a year, which is a relative bargain for his ability to change games.

 Nine defensive tackles made the top 100 here, and Williams should have been in that group. New England's run defense was drastically improved  with Williams in the lineup. And he had 3.5 sacks and eight tackles for loss over 12 games in 2025.

 "He's a player that's gotten better every year, and he was clearly comfortable being a focal point for the defense," an NFC scout said.

 
 

 Peter Skoronski , G, Tennessee Titans 
 Skoronski is the NFL's highest-paid guard at $25 million annually. But according to NFL Rank, he's not a top-five guard. Chicago's Joe Thuney , Denver's Quinn Meinerz , Indianapolis'  Quenton Nelson , Atlanta's Chris Lindstrom and Dallas'  Tyler Smith round out the top 100 at that position.

 Skoronski has played his way into this conversation and should be on the list next year. He ranked fourth among guards with a 96.0% pass block win rate in 2025.

 "He wasn't a finished product when he came into the league, but he's probably Tennessee's best player on offense, a guy you can build around up front," an NFC exec said. "He's gotten more powerful."

 Kansas City's  Trey Smith was another notable snub at guard.

 
 

 

 Zack Baun , LB, Philadelphia Eagles 
 Baun became an All-Pro and consensus top-five linebacker over the past two seasons in Philadelphia. San Francisco's Fred Warner was the only off-ball linebacker to crack the top 75, and only four made the top 100. Baun has 273 tackles over the past two seasons, along with seven sacks and three interceptions.

 "He's got range. He can play the run close to the box or can cover in space, has great awareness," an NFC executive said. "One of the best at his position."

 
 

 Tucker Kraft , TE, Green Bay Packers 
 Several young tight ends deserve consideration, from Detroit's Sam LaPorta to Indianapolis' Tyler Warren . Let's go with Kraft here because of his upside after  ACL surgery .

 He's a vertical threat who can also block. And by Week 1, he might be the NFL's first $20 million-per-year tight end; the Packers and Kraft are discussing a contract extension.

 "He gives that offense so much juice, and Jordan Love obviously trusts him," an AFC scout said. "If he's healthy, he's primed for a big year."

title: Will Packers coach Matt LaFleur let Jordan Love cook in '26?
summary: LaFleur recently said Love is "the best I've been around in terms of protections and adjustments."
full_text:
"He's got to be the best I've been around in terms of protections and adjustments, and rarely does he get out-schemed." 

 -- Matt LaFleur, Aug. 10, 2026, on NFL Network 

 GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Aaron Rodgers . Jared Goff . Matt Ryan . Between those quarterbacks, they have five NFL MVPs and three Super Bowl appearances.

 Throw in Kirk Cousins , Robert Griffin III and Marcus Mariota , and you see a group of Matt LaFleur-coached QBs who have had more success than failure -- which is why on more than one occasion LaFleur was given the opportunity to recant his statement about Jordan Love being the best he has been around when it comes to protections and adjustments at the line of scrimmage.

 Each time, whether it was in the moment on the NFL Network set during Packers training camp or in his next news conference, LaFleur held his ground.

 If that's truly how LaFleur feels about his quarterback, then perhaps the 2026 season will prove transformative for the Packers' offense -- because in Love's three seasons as the starting quarterback, LaFleur has been about as run-heavy of a playcaller as there has been in the NFL.

 LaFleur has called designed runs on 43.8% of his plays since the start of the 2023 season. Only two teams, the Baltimore Ravens (45.7%) and Philadelphia Eagles (44.8%), have been more run-heavy by design.

 Put that up against LaFleur's four seasons with Rodgers, when the Packers ranked higher than 15th in designed run percentage only once (ninth in 2020), and it's fair to wonder whether LaFleur is really ready to turn Love loose in 2026.

 The quarterback thinks so.

 "I definitely believe Matt fully trusts me," Love said.

 This summer, LaFleur let Love do something he had never done before: call the offensive plays for one of the backups in a preseason game. There was Love with the headset on and the call sheet in hand during the second half of the preseason finale against the Arizona Cardinals , telling Kyle McCord what to run.

 "Just to hear his demeanor on the headset and how calm, cool and collected he was throughout the entire game, especially in those critical moments," LaFleur said. "It's not a surprise to me because that's what we see on the field too."

 
 

 TRUST DOESN'T DEVELOP overnight. Sometimes, it doesn't develop in a season or two -- even for Rodgers.

 While Rodgers sat for three years behind Brett Favre, it took another three for him to feel like he had earned coach Mike McCarthy's trust.

 "Me and Mike got to that, but it wasn't early," Rodgers recalled recently. "It was years of working through things and having success.

 "And I felt like by the third year, he trusted me enough -- because that was our fifth year together -- that if I said something, it wasn't just [that] I was trying to push back against them, or I was trying to do some sort of measuring. It was because I firmly believed that this is what was going to help us win or be the best on this play."

 That doesn't mean it was always congenial.

 Sometimes, Rodgers said, McCarthy would let things slide.

 Other times, it would turn contentious.

 

 Rodgers recalled times when McCarthy would call him into his office on a Monday morning with a list of 10 plays that Rodgers had changed in the previous game -- and for each and every one of them, McCarthy wanted to know why.

 "We'd talk it out, and he'd see my side and I'd see his side, and we always kind of met back in the middle," Rodgers said. "I think that was the beauty in the success that we had, it was a lot of push and pull. He gave me the latitude. I proved that I deserve latitude and could make it work. And when I went too far, he would rein me back in."

 It didn't take as long for LaFleur to trust Rodgers. He was a first-time head coach, and Rodgers had a pair of MVPs, a Super Bowl title and 14 years of starting experience to his credit. The 39-year-old coach was only four years older than his quarterback.

 Even so, there was the early issue of whether LaFleur would allow Rodgers the freedom to change plays willy-nilly like he could under McCarthy. In fact, to audible or not to audible was the dominant story in the early months after LaFleur was hired in 2019.

 Rodgers had a good year in 2019 with 4,002 yards, 26 touchdowns and four interceptions. He followed that up with MVP seasons in 2020 (4,299 yards, 48 TDs, five INTs) and 2021 (4,115 yards, 37 TDs, four INTs).

 He credited the offseason of 2020, when COVID restrictions forced all meetings to go virtual, for helping he and LaFleur to connect on another level.

 "I think the biggest jump for us was in the '20 offseason, when we had all those phone calls and Zoom calls," Rodgers said. "You start to take that ownership of the offense and tell them exactly what you want. As a young player, it's natural where you feel like I can't maybe put my stamp on this one or push too hard, there's still that balance of the authority figure and the peer relationship. 

 "I think that's the beauty in the league, is that you are peers. There's still that hierarchy, and you have to respect that, but the more you can use your voice to tell them exactly what you want when you want it, the smoother it ultimately goes."

 Rodgers believes that Love, after three years as the starter and three straight playoff appearances (1-3 record), has reached that point.

 "This is his fourth year starting now," Rodgers said. "I think with every year you get a little more confidence. Obviously your body of work is a chip on your shoulder to kind of use at any time, to say, 'Look, I've done this. I've made plays. I've won in the playoffs. I've played at a high level.' It just comes down to the communication part."

 
 

 IT MAY BE a false -- or at least misguided -- premise that LaFleur hasn't turned Love loose yet.

 Despite his run-heavy playcalls, LaFleur hasn't made Love into a dink-and-dunk quarterback. In fact, it's the opposite. When the Packers have passed, they've aired it out. Since 2023, Love has the third-highest average air yards per attempt (8.3) in the NFL, right behind the Baltimore Ravens' Lamar Jackson and Jacksonville Jaguars ' Trevor Lawrence , both at 8.4.

 And when the game is on the line, Love has delivered his share of comebacks. He has led eight fourth-quarter comebacks since becoming the starter, tied for most in the league during that span, according to ESPN Research.

 

 If that's not evidence that Love is ready to take on more in the offense, then maybe this is: The only players with a better QBR than Love's mark of 67.1 among quarterbacks who have made at least 40 starts over the past three seasons are the Buffalo Bills' Josh Allen (70.3) and Jackson (68.5). Both Allen and Jackson have won MVPs in that time.

 "There's not a place on the field that's a weakness for him," former quarterback and 2002 NFL MVP Rich Gannon said of Love. "I just think there's three or four plays typically that you're watching a Packers game, you go, 'What the hell is that? What happened there?' And that's really what he's got to get cleaned up.

 "We're not talking about a guy that has eight or nine of them, but there's a couple, and he just has to eliminate some of the inconsistency."

 To that end, LaFleur wanted Love to focus on one specific fundamental this offseason: footwork.

 Love was raw coming out of Utah State in 2020, and not having a normal offseason before his rookie year because the pandemic slowed his development. In 2023 and 2024, his first two seasons as a starter, Love's accuracy was an issue.

 Last season, Love posted his highest completion percentage (66.3) in any season as a starter, college or pro. LaFleur believes that number could go even higher.

 "I think one of the things he's been really focused and conscious of throughout the course of the offseason and on his own in the summer is just trying to play with as much balance in the pocket as he can," LaFleur said, "knowing that there's going to be times you get moved off the spot.

title: 49ers, Chargers top sports world poking fun at man who posed as 49ers player
summary: Since two men were arrested with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud, the story has dominated social media, with even athletes and sports teams chiming in.
full_text:
Days after news broke that federal authorities charged and arrested two men -- one of which posed as a San Francisco 49ers player -- with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud, various sports organizations have poked fun at the situation. Even a member of the 49ers.

 

 According to the U.S. Attorney's office in the District of Oregon and court documents, the FBI arrested Daejon Love and Taylor Jamie Chan on Aug. 24 in Boise, Idaho. The two defrauded more than two dozen women out of about $1.3 million.

 A part of Love's alleged scheme was posing as a member of the 49ers. Authorities say he posted images and videos of himself on social media websites with 49ers gear on, acting like he was a wide receiver for the team.

 When Love would meet people on dating apps and social media, he created "fictitious personas" as a 49ers wide receiver or as a wealthy real estate investor. Authorities say Love and Chan then created fictitious investments to defraud women.

 The scheme came to a halt and last Monday, Love and Chan were handcuffed. Since then, the story has dominated social media, with even athletes and sports teams chiming in.

 Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley posted an image of himself on X, similar to one that Love shared on his Instagram, with the caption: "Believe it or not I'm in the NFL." The Chargers reposted it and wrote: "can confirm."

 

 Pittsburgh Steelers defensive tackle Cameron Heyward took it a step further. He used an AI-generated image of himself and Love in the Steelers' locker room. Love rocked Steelers gear as Heyward quipped on the post: "Bro... he was JUST at the facility."

 

 49ers wide receivers coach Leonard Hankerson, who likely would have been Love's coach if he were actually on the roster, also chimed in.

 Hankerson posted a collage on Instagram with the second photo being an AI-generated photo of himself and Love at a 49ers practice. In the image, Hankerson was looking at paper, seemingly coaching Love. Former 49ers wide receiver Kendrick Bourne commented on Hankerson's post: "Man I knew you was coaching him," with laughing emojis.

 

 Even the MLB's Cleveland Guardians referenced the Love situation.

 Ahead of their game last Saturday, the Guardians' lineup graphic on X included an image of Love with Guardians baseball gear. Cleveland wrote in one of the replies under the post: "Daejon is locked in."

 

 San Francisco has yet to acknowledge the saga. But one thing seems apparent: There is no San Francisco jersey with "Love" on the back.

title: Do NFL superteams usually win the Super Bowl? Will the Rams?
summary: The Rams are loaded this season, and basically everyone is picking them to win the Super Bowl. But preseason darlings of the past 35 years haven't always met expectations.
full_text:
Editor's note: This story originally published on Aug. 10 but has been re-published after news of  Aaron Donald 's return to the Rams . Los Angeles' Super Bowl odds have shifted from +550 to +500 over the past three weeks at DraftKings. 

 The 2026 Rams are the closest thing we've had to a preseason superteam in several years. Sean McVay's group was already a popular pick to win Super Bowl LXI before the offseason began. But then L.A. traded for Trent McDuffie and signed Jaylen Watson , shoring up the secondary at the expense of a potential Super Bowl opponent in the Chiefs. The move to draft Ty Simpson as Matthew Stafford 's successor struck a curious tone, but general manager Les Snead responded with the mother of all high-stakes moves, trading Jared Verse and three picks to the Browns for reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett .

 Unsurprisingly, the Rams have become prohibitive favorites to win the Super Bowl after their aggressive moves this offseason. Picking any other team to win the Lombardi Trophy at this point would almost require coming up with some sort of explanation for what happened to the Rams along the way.

 And yet, we have to look back only one year to remind ourselves how NFL seasons can play out entirely differently once players get on the field. In 2025, 68 ESPN personalities picked  their AFC and NFC champions, along with an eventual Super Bowl winner, before the season kicked off. Not a single person picked the Seahawks or Patriots. I predicted the  Chiefs and Packers , who combined for exactly zero playoff wins. Preseason darlings like the Chiefs, Lions and Commanders each missed the playoffs altogether.

 Was 2025 just a weird year? And how often do heavily favorited superteams such as the 2026 Rams actually win the Super Bowl? I decided to take a more comprehensive look through history to get a sense of how confident we can be that Los Angeles will be the last team standing come Feb. 14 .

 
 Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' 

 
 To do so, I'm going to look at the 15 largest preseason favorites since 1990 and see how their seasons played out. I'll be using the preseason odds compiled at Pro Football Reference from 1990 to 2025 and compare them with the odds posted for this season's Super Bowl at  DraftKings . The Rams have odds of +550 at DraftKings to win the Super Bowl, while nobody else in the league is shorter than +1000. After we adjust for the vigorish and convert the betting lines into probabilities, the Rams have an implied 12.5% chance of winning this season's Super Bowl, putting them 5.1 percentage points ahead of the second-placed Bills and Ravens.

 While the absolute number might be a better sense of how the market views a particular team, I'm going to use the latter figure to sort through our top 15 teams (well, 16, if we're including the 2026 Rams). There were plenty of seasons in the 1990s where two or three superteams -- such as the 49ers and Cowboys -- were seen as significantly better than the rest of the competition. I want to get a sense of what it was like for the teams that truly separated from the pack before the season began, as appears to be the case for this Rams squad.

 Did those teams hold up to their preseason expectations? Was the market overconfident about their chances? Let's go team by team before using the lessons from those 15 earlier cases to talk about what it means for the 2026 Rams and their chances of winning McVay and Stafford their second title.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 2026 Rams | 2021 Chiefs | 2019 Patriots 
 2018 Patriots | 2017 Patriots | 2009 Patriots 
 2008 Patriots | 2007 Patriots | 2002 Rams 
 2001 Rams | 1998 Packers | 1997 Packers 
 1996 49ers | 1995 49ers | 1994 49ers | 1990 49ers 
 Can this season's Rams win the Super Bowl? 

 
 

 

 2017 New England Patriots 
 Implied odds: 19.8% 
 Gap to the rest of the NFL: 11.5% 
 Result: Lost Super Bowl LII to the Eagles, 41-33 

 I wouldn't have guessed that the 2017 Patriots stood out in terms of Super Bowl odds more than any other New England team from the Tom Brady-Bill Belichick era, but let's contextualize this. The Pats were coming off that legendary 34-28 win over the Falcons in Super Bowl LI . Brady was getting Rob Gronkowski back from injury after the star tight end missed the playoff run with a back ailment , while Belichick added a new star receiver to the mix in Brandin Cooks . After a 14-2 season and with Brady motivated by the four-game suspension he took for the Deflategate scandal, you could understand why the Patriots were heavy favorites to repeat as champs.

 

 Some things went as expected. Brady won the league MVP award. Cooks and Gronkowski each topped 1,000 yards. The Pats went 13-3 and took home the top seed in the AFC.

 Others did not. Belichick's team started 2-2 and needed a last-minute comeback win over a 4-12 Texans team to avoid opening the season 1-3. The Pats righted the ship quickly, but they were trailing by 10 points in the fourth quarter of the AFC title game and were down nearly three scores to the Jaguars, only for Myles Jack 's fumble recovery touchdown to be overturned. Two late touchdown passes to Danny Amendola controversially pushed the Pats into the Super Bowl.

 There, well, nothing went as planned. The Patriots defense had quietly been a mess all year, finishing the regular season ranked 31st in DVOA. The offense covered up the weakness by holding on to the ball and getting out to early leads. The Eagles were heavy underdogs with backup quarterback Nick Foles in for the injured Carson Wentz , and you know what happened next. Brady threw for 505 yards and three touchdowns, still the record for an NFL quarterback in a losing effort, but the defense couldn't stop Foles & Co. The Pats fell 41-33.

 

 
 

 2007 New England Patriots 
 Implied odds: 20.9% 
 Gap to the rest of the NFL:  10.5% 
 Result: Lost Super Bowl XLII to the Giants, 17-14 

 Are you sensing a trend? This was another Patriots team that rode offseason optimism about its offensive additions to high hopes before falling short in the Super Bowl. The 2006 Pats had blown a 21-3 lead to the Colts in the AFC Championship Game , but they also weren't far removed from winning three titles between 2001 and 2004. Brady had improved as a quarterback over that time, and during the offseason, Belichick had rebuilt the offense by trading for Randy Moss and Wes Welker and signing Donte' Stallworth.

 What happened next is one of the more notable seasons in NFL history. The Pats were caught spying on the Jets during a 38-14 blowout victory in Week 1, turning a team that had been the underdog favorites during their win over the Rams in 2001 into the villains of the NFL. On the field, the Patriots blew defenses away with their spread attack, as Brady produced arguably the greatest season in league history under center. The Patriots went 16-0 in the regular season, winning their average game by nearly 20 points.

 By the time the postseason came around, though, the cracks were beginning to show. Brady threw three picks in the AFC title game , but with Philip Rivers playing through a torn ACL and LaDainian Tomlinson limited by injury to three touches, the Chargers couldn't take advantage in a 21-12 defeat. And in the Super Bowl, again as heavy favorites, the Patriots were upset by a Giants team that was able to control Brady in the pocket with its pass rush.

 

 

 
 

 1996 San Francisco 49ers 
 Implied odds: 19.2% 
 Gap to the rest of the NFL:  9.6% 
 Result: Lost in divisional round to the Packers, 35-14 

 The 49ers were the preseason favorites to win the Super Bowl in 1994, 1995 and 1996. Their status as the third team on this list might have more to do with a lack of competition in the AFC than anything else. The Bills were among the Super Bowl favorites earlier in the decade, but after a 7-9 season in 1994 and a 10-6 campaign in 1995, they had fallen back to the pack. The Steelers had advanced to the Super Bowl the…

title: From Knicks to Yankees, Nick Jonas finds the perfect song
summary: The Jonas Brothers are longtime New York sports fans and have a song that can speak to their favorite teams.
full_text:
First, it was the New York Knicks ' first NBA title in 53 years. Then it was the "American royal wedding" between pop star Taylor Swift and Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce  keeping the historic Madison Square Garden busy this summer. However, summer at the world's most famous arena isn't over yet. 
 
 

 The Jonas Brothers' three-night stint at MSG for the "Burnin' Up Tour All Over Again" kicks off Aug. 20. Raised in New Jersey, the three brothers, who are featured in the new Disney film "Camp Rock 3," are New York sports fans and have been unwavering supporters of the Knicks, so the venue just seems fitting, especially during a summer like this. 
 
 

 "Going back to last year, the run [the Knicks] made in the playoffs, I was in New York at the time doing a show on Broadway and was around it every day, feeling the energy in the city. It was electric," Jonas told ESPN. "Cut to this year, and just to see them complete the journey during the finals and what that meant to the city as a whole ... it was pretty incredible to see."

 On the crest of a historic New York summer and ahead of performing at halftime of the NFL Week 1 game between the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia, ESPN spoke with Nick Jonas and he assigned songs to his favorite teams. Jonas and comedian Kevin Hart headline DraftKings' "Take Your Game Anywhere" campaign that launches on Sept. 2.

 

 

 New York Knicks: 'Love Bug' 

 Again, the Knicks are still the moment after winning their first NBA championship in more than 50 years. This sweet ballad from the Jonas Brothers, released in 2008, perfectly sums up how Nick Jonas feels about his team.

 "It just feels right for them," he said.

 

 

 New York Giants : 'Sucker' 

 The NFL regular season is right around the corner, and many New York sports fans are loyal to "Big Blue." The Giants also have a humongous fanbase, just like "Sucker." In 2019, the group's comeback single struck the top of the Billboard charts -- the Jonas Brothers'  first-ever No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 .

 "I'm probably going to go with 'Sucker' because it's the biggest one, the most important [song], to some," Jonas told ESPN.

 

 

 New York Yankees : 'Burnin' Up' 

 Just like the Yankees, there's so much nostalgia that comes with "Burnin' Up." The song, released in 2008, was one of the first smash hits for the Jonas Brothers. As for the Yankees, they are one of the most revered franchises in sports. 

 "[The Yankees are] more like legacy," Jonas said.

summary: With Zach Charbonnet set to miss the first four weeks on the PUP list, Seattle will turn to its first-round pick.
full_text:
RENTON, Wash. -- Rookie Jadarian Price is ready to lead the Seattle Seahawks ' backfield while it waits for Zach Charbonnet to return. Or at least as ready as he can be.

 Except for the week he missed with a minor injury, Price has had a strong summer, displaying the vision, decisiveness and athleticism that made him the Seahawks' choice with the 32nd pick in April's draft. He has looked as good as advertised -- and in some ways better.

 But that all comes with the caveat that when Price steps onto Lumen Field for Seattle's Sept. 9 opener against the New England Patriots , the team's presumed RB1 will be making his NFL debut having not played a single snap in the preseason. Getting Price as prepared as possible for actual football has been trumped by the Seahawks' desire to preserve him for the long haul.

 "He's done a great job. He really has -- all three downs," coach Mike Macdonald said last week. "He's a rookie in terms of, there's going to be things that we're going to attack in his game that will show itself in games. We haven't been afforded the luxury of having the bodies right now at running back to give him the reps in a [preseason] game that we would normally give to a rookie runner."

 

 The best guess is that the Seahawks are planning, for now, to roll with Price as their lead back while mixing in a heavy dose of George Holani , whose receiving and pass-blocking skills seem perfectly suited for third-down work.

 Emanuel Wilson will be the power complement to those two, though the free agent addition is on the mend from an undisclosed injury that sidelined him for the last couple of weeks and kept him out of Seattle's preseason finale Friday against the Kansas City Chiefs . Wilson has been running off to the side with trainers during practice, suggesting he won't be out for long.

 Whatever plan Seattle has going into Week 1 will start to change once Charbonnet returns.

 Last year's co-starter appears to be in the closing stretch of his recovery from February surgery to repair an ACL tear he suffered in January. He's still on the physically unable to perform list, meaning he will miss the first four games of the season at a minimum.

 Whenever Charbonnet is all the way back, it's easy to envision the Seahawks splitting the work in their backfield fairly evenly between him and Price the way they did last season with Charbonnet and Kenneth Walker III .

 

 Price may not have the same fifth gear as Walker, but he looks like he can replicate at least some of the explosiveness Seattle's backfield lost when the Super Bowl LX MVP signed with Kansas City in free agency.

 "He's good, man," linebacker Ernest Jones IV  said early in camp. "Mature for his age, you can tell. You don't get too many words out of him, but he's working. He got me today, man. He had a hell of a route on me today. ... I think he's going to help us. He's doing everything right and he's got a great group of backs in front of him that's kind of teaching him the way."

 Jones was referring to how Price had beaten him for a touchdown during a 7-on-7 rep, getting open behind the 2025 second-team All-Pro before making an over-the-shoulder catch on a deep ball from Sam Darnold . Price's ability to contribute in the passing game was one of the biggest questions about his skill set after he finished his Notre Dame career with only 15 receptions over three seasons as a backup. But he's answering it.

 "He's a special player," Darnold said after the Seahawks' Aug. 21 joint practice in Nashville, Tennessee. "He's a really special player. He brings a different facet to the offense that only a guy like him can bring. Whether it's catching passes out of the backfield, catching screens, running in between the tackles, outside the tackles. He can really do it all, and I know he's just going to continue to get better and learn."

 Holani got much of the work with the No. 1 offense that day, with Price still ramping back up. The cautious, long-game approach the Seahawks have taken with their top pick could mean even more growing pains out of the gate than they'd usually expect from a rookie. But they seem willing to live with that for the trade-off of keeping him healthy.

 "He's shown that we're really confident in him going into Week 1," Macdonald said. "He's earned that decision for us to feel good about it. Even though in just about any other circumstance, you'd definitely want really any rookie to get preseason exposure and experience."
